name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.globalJacobiOperator
doc:
The concrete deterministic Fock operator obtained by lifting the local
Jacobi multiplication matrices at the two distinct sites.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.VacuumMoment`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.globalJacobiOperator_eq_smul_rawMultiplication {m n d b : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.globalJacobiOperator b F =
    (1 / ↑m) • NLAlib.SparseSketch.rawMultiplication m (fun i a => (F.u i).ofLp a) √(↑b - 1)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.globalJacobiOperator_eq_smul_rawMultiplication
doc:
The global Jacobi operator from the exact vacuum moment is the normalized
physical multiplication matrix from `GlobalBands`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.ConcreteLadder`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection {d m n : ℕ} (nu : ℕ) : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FullOp d m n
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection
doc:
The diagonal orthogonal projection onto total grade `nu`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_apply {d m n : ℕ} (nu : ℕ) (out inp : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu out inp = if out = inp ∧ out.2.grade = nu then 1 else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_apply
doc:
An exact-grade projection has unit diagonal precisely on the selected grade.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_mulVec {d m n : ℕ} (nu : ℕ) (x : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n → ℝ)
  (a : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) :
  Matrix.mulVec (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu) x a = if a.2.grade = nu then x a else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_mulVec
doc:
Multiplication by the grade projection simply keeps coordinates in the
specified grade.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_mul_gradeProjection {d m n mu nu : ℕ} (h : mu ≠ nu) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection mu * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu = 0
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_mul_gradeProjection
doc:
Projections onto distinct exact grades have zero product.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_mul_self {d m n : ℕ} (nu : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu =
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_mul_self
doc:
Each exact-grade projection is idempotent.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_normSq {d m n : ℕ} (nu : ℕ) (x : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.sumSq (Matrix.mulVec (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu) x) =
    ∑ a with a.2.grade = nu, x a ^ 2
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_normSq
doc:
Projecting to one grade retains exactly the energy in that grade.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_normSq_le {d m n : ℕ} (nu : ℕ) (x : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.sumSq (Matrix.mulVec (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu) x) ≤ NLAlib.SparseSketch.sumSq x
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_normSq_le
doc:
Grade projections are Euclidean contractions, stated in exact coordinate
energy form.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_norm_le_one {d m n : ℕ} (nu : ℕ) : ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤ 1
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_norm_le_one
doc:
Every exact-grade projection has Euclidean operator norm at most one.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_transpose {d m n : ℕ} (nu : ℕ) :
  Matrix.transpose (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection_transpose
doc:
Each exact-grade projection is symmetric.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeZ_eq_cast_grade {m n : ℕ} (p : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n) : p.gradeZ = ↑p.grade
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeZ_eq_cast_grade
doc:
The integer grade used by homogeneous matrices is the cast of the natural
occupation grade.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeZ_sub_eq_pair {m n : ℕ} {s t : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Site m n}
  {out inp : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Pattern m n} (hst : s ≠ t) (h : NLAlib.SparseSketch.agreesOutsidePair s t out inp) :
  out.gradeZ - inp.gradeZ =
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.weightZ (out s) - NLAlib.SparseSketch.weightZ (inp s) +
      (NLAlib.SparseSketch.weightZ (out t) - NLAlib.SparseSketch.weightZ (inp t))
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeZ_sub_eq_pair
doc:
Patterns agreeing outside a distinct pair differ in grade by the two site occupation changes.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteSiteOperators`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeZ_sub_eq_site
doc:
Patterns agreeing outside one site differ in grade exactly by that site's occupation change.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteSiteOperators`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.grade_envelope_le_betaEnvelope {d q nu : ℕ} {m s : ℝ} (hnu : nu ≤ 2 * q) (hm : 0 < m) (hs : 0 < s) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandConstant *
      (NLAlib.SparseSketch.aTerm (↑d) (↑nu) m + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm (↑d) (↑nu) m +
        NLAlib.SparseSketch.cTerm (↑nu) s) ≤
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandEnvelope d q m s
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.grade_envelope_le_betaEnvelope
doc:
Monotonicity from a grade `nu ≤ 2q` to the uniform ladder parameter
`bandEnvelope d q m s`.  This is the exact scalar bridge from the concrete
band proposition to ladder iteration.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.BandEnvelope`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError.{u_1} {k : Type u_1} [Fintype k] {n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (S : Matrix k (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError
doc:
The Gram error `Uᵀ SᵀS U - I_d`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseStackModel`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_entry_hasLocalDegree_two {s b n d : ℕ} (hs : 0 < s) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (a c : Fin d) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.HasLocalDegree 2 fun z =>
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) a c
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_entry_hasLocalDegree_two
doc:
Every scalar entry of the pointwise SparseStack Gram error has local
interaction degree at most two.  The proof uses the exact hollow identity,
so no independence is involved.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseStackLimitedIndependence`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_eq_block_first {s b n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (Z : NLAlib.SparseStackSample s b n) (hs : 0 < s) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix Z) = fun a c =>
    1 / ↑s *
      ∑ g,
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
            inner ℝ (NLAlib.SparseSketch.signedBasis Z g i) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.signedBasis Z g j) * (F.u i).ofLp a *
              (F.u j).ofLp c
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_eq_block_first
doc:
Paper-form statement of the hollow identity, with the block sum outermost.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseStackModel`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_eq_hollow {s b n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (Z : NLAlib.SparseStackSample s b n) (hs : 0 < s) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix Z) = NLAlib.SparseSketch.hollowGram F Z
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_eq_hollow
doc:
The exact hollow identity (paper (2.2)): the Parseval diagonal cancels from
`UᵀΠᵀΠU-I`, leaving only ordered pairs `i ≠ j`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseStackModel`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_frameOfMatrix.{u_1} {k : Type u_1} [Fintype k] {n d : ℕ} (U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin d) ℝ)
  (hU : U.transpose * U = 1) (S : Matrix k (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError (NLAlib.SparseSketch.frameOfMatrix U hU) S =
    U.transpose * (NLAlib.SparseSketch.sketchGram S * U) - 1
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_frameOfMatrix
doc:
Consequently the formal Gram error is exactly the displayed matrix in the
main probability event.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.MatrixFrameBridge`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_isHermitian.{u_1} {k : Type u_1} [Fintype k] {n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (S : Matrix k (Fin n) ℝ) : (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F S).IsHermitian
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_isHermitian
doc:
The Gram error is real symmetric.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.MatrixTail`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_pow_entry_hasLocalDegree {s b n d : ℕ} (hs : 0 < s) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (r : ℕ) (a c : Fin d) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.HasLocalDegree (2 * r) fun z =>
    (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) ^ r) a c
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError_pow_entry_hasLocalDegree
doc:
An entry of the `r`-th Gram-error power has interaction degree at most
`2r`.  This recursive noncommutative expansion is the formal word count.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseStackLimitedIndependence`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.half_pow_sparseMomentOrder_le {d : ℕ} {delta : ℝ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdelta : 0 < delta) :
  (1 / 2) ^ NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta ≤ delta / ↑d
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.half_pow_sparseMomentOrder_le
doc:
Equivalently, `2⁻q ≤ delta/d`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.PaperParameters`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.hollowGram {s b n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) (Z : NLAlib.SparseStackSample s b n) :
  Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.hollowGram
doc:
The exact hollow sum.  `j ∈ univ.erase i` is the literal finite encoding of `i ≠ j`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseStackModel`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.hollowGram_block_first {s b n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (Z : NLAlib.SparseStackSample s b n) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.hollowGram F Z = fun a c =>
    1 / ↑s *
      ∑ g,
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
            inner ℝ (NLAlib.SparseSketch.signedBasis Z g i) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.signedBasis Z g j) * (F.u i).ofLp a *
              (F.u j).ofLp c
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.hollowGram_block_first
doc:
The same hollow sum with the block index written first, matching the paper's
literal order `Σ_g Σ_{i≠j}`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseStackModel`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.homogeneous_add
doc:
Adding matrices with the same grade shift preserves that shift.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.homogeneous_grade_relation
doc:
A concrete matrix is grade homogeneous iff every nonzero entry has the
advertised casted occupation shift.  This is a convenient natural-grade form
of `IsFullGradeShift`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.homogeneous_smul {d m n : ℕ} {delta : ℤ} {A : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FullOp d m n}
  (hA : NLAlib.SparseSketch.IsFullGradeShift delta A) (c : ℝ) : NLAlib.SparseSketch.IsFullGradeShift delta (c • A)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.homogeneous_smul
doc:
Scalar multiplication preserves a matrix's grade shift.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw {b : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (s n : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.FiniteLaw (NLAlib.SparseSketch.YArray b s n)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw
doc:
The literal product law of all iid ternary vectors `Y_(g,i)`.  Each vector
itself has the literal product law of its `b` ternary coordinates.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseIIDUnconditional`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw_expect_flatten_eq_iidLaw_expect {s b n : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b)
  (f : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Configuration (s * b) n → ℝ) :
  ((NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw ⋯ s n).expect fun y => f (NLAlib.SparseSketch.flattenY y)) =
    (NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidLaw b hb (s * b) n).expect f
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw_expect_flatten_eq_iidLaw_expect
doc:
Every observable has exactly the same expectation under the nested iid
array law and the flattened product-Fock law.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.DistributionBridges`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw_weight {b : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (s n : ℕ) (y : NLAlib.SparseSketch.YArray b s n) :
  (NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw hb s n).weight y = ∏ z, (NLAlib.SparseSketch.yVectorLaw b hb).weight (y z)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw_weight
doc:
The iid-array law is the product of its coordinate vector masses.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseIIDUnconditional`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw_weight_eq_iidLaw_weight {s b n : ℕ} (hb : 1 < b)
  (y : NLAlib.SparseSketch.YArray b s n) :
  (NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw ⋯ s n).weight y =
    (NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidLaw b hb (s * b) n).weight (NLAlib.SparseSketch.flattenY y)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidArrayLaw_weight_eq_iidLaw_weight
doc:
Pointwise probability masses are preserved by flattening.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.DistributionBridges`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidGramError {m n d : ℕ} (b : ℕ) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (omega : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Configuration m n) : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidGramError
doc:
The normalized iid-coordinate Gram error
`m⁻¹ Σ_r Σ_{i≠j} eta_{ri} eta_{rj} u_i u_jᵀ`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.VacuumMoment`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidGramError_apply {m n d : ℕ} (b : ℕ) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (omega : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Configuration m n) (a c : Fin d) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidGramError b F omega a c =
    1 / ↑m *
      ∑ r,
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
            NLAlib.SparseSketch.etaCoordinate b (r, i) omega * NLAlib.SparseSketch.etaCoordinate b (r, j) omega *
                (F.u i).ofLp a *
              (F.u j).ofLp c
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidGramError_apply
doc:
An iid hollow Gram-error entry is the explicit off-diagonal ternary-coordinate sum.
Source: ported sparse-Fock shared-leg/vacuum proof, commit
`b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b`; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidLaw (b : ℕ) (hb : 1 < b) (m n : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.FiniteLaw (NLAlib.SparseSketch.Configuration m n)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidLaw
doc:
The iid product law on all sites.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.ProductFock`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidLaw_weight (b : ℕ) (hb : 1 < b) (m n : ℕ) (omega : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Configuration m n) :
  (NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidLaw b hb m n).weight omega = ∏ s, NLAlib.SparseSketch.mass b (omega s)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidLaw_weight
doc:
The iid finite Fock-law weight is the product of its coordinate weights.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.ProductFock`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError {b s n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (y : NLAlib.SparseSketch.YArray b s n) : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError
doc:
The iid-vector hollow Gram error before multiplying by `c_b²`.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseIIDTransfer`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError_eq_flattened_iidGramError {s b n d : ℕ} (hs : 0 < s) (hb : 1 < b)
  (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) (y : NLAlib.SparseSketch.YArray b s n) :
  NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError F y = NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidGramError b F (NLAlib.SparseSketch.flattenY y)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError_eq_flattened_iidGramError
doc:
The iid-vector error before coupling scaling is exactly the flattened
product-Fock iid Gram error.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.DistributionBridges`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError_symmetric {b s n d : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (y : NLAlib.SparseSketch.YArray b s n) :
  (NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError F y).transpose = NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError F y
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.iidVectorError_symmetric
doc:
The literal iid-vector Gram error is symmetric.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.SparseIIDTransfer`,

signature:

  {q : ℕ} {beta : ℝ} (hbeta : 0 ≤ beta)
  (hband :

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.independent_frame_operator_failure_of_band_bounds.{u_1} {Omega : Type u_1} [Fintype Omega] {n d : ℕ}
  {delta eps : ℝ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdelta0 : 0 < delta) (hdelta1 : delta ≤ 1) (heps0 : 0 < eps) (heps1 : eps ≤ 1)
  (frameLaw : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FiniteLaw Omega) (frames : Omega → NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (hband :
    ∀ (omega : Omega) (shift : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift),
      ∀ nu ≤ 2 * NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta,
        ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand (NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) (frames omega)
                (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) shift *
              NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandEnvelope d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta)
            ↑(NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            ↑(NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)) :
  (frameLaw.product
          (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n ⋯)).prob
      {outcome |
        eps < ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError (frames outcome.1) (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix outcome.2.toSample)‖} ≤
    delta
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.independent_frame_operator_failure_of_band_bounds

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.independent_frame_ose_success_of_band_bounds.{u_1} {Omega : Type u_1} [Fintype Omega] {n d : ℕ}
  {delta eps : ℝ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdelta0 : 0 < delta) (hdelta1 : delta ≤ 1) (heps0 : 0 < eps) (heps1 : eps ≤ 1)
  (frameLaw : NLAlib.SparseSketch.FiniteLaw Omega) (frames : Omega → NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (hband :
    ∀ (omega : Omega) (shift : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift),
      ∀ nu ≤ 2 * NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta,
        ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand (NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) (frames omega)
                (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) shift *
              NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandEnvelope d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta)
            ↑(NLAlib.sparseRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            ↑(NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)) :
  1 - delta ≤
    (frameLaw.product
          (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw (NLAlib.sparseColumnSparsity (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps)
            (NLAlib.sparseBlockRows d (NLAlib.sparseMomentOrder d delta) eps) n ⋯)).prob
      {outcome |
        NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix outcome.2.toSample)
          (NLAlib.SparseSketch.rowMatrix (frames outcome.1).u) eps}

    ‖((1 / ↑m) • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Lplus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      a + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m)
  (hmixed :
    ‖(1 / ↑m) •

                NLAlib.SparseSketch.Yplus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + 3 / 2 * c)
  (hheavy :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • √(↑b - 1) ^ 2 • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Hplus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      c)
  (hbTerm : 0 ≤ NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m) :
  ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand m F b NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift.plus * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandConstant * (a + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + c)

  (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) {q : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) {beta : ℝ} (hbeta : 0 ≤ beta)
  (hband :
    ∀ (delta : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift),
      ∀ nu ≤ 2 * q,
        ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand (s * b) F b delta * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤ beta)
  {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
  (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n ⋯).prob
      {z | ¬NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.rowMatrix F.u) eps} ≤
    ↑d * (3 * NLAlib.SparseSketch.cB b ^ 2 * beta / eps) ^ (2 * q)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.sparseStack_failure_tail_of_band_bounds
doc:

signature:

  (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
  (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n hb).prob
      {z | ε ≤ ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample)‖} ≤
    ((NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n hb).expect fun z =>
        (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) ^ (2 * q)).trace) /
      ε ^ (2 * q)

doc:
The concrete finite-law Markov tail for the actual independent uniform
signed-hash SparseStack distribution.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.sparseStack_ose_failure_tail {s b n d : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) (q : ℕ)
  (hq : 0 < q) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
  (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n hb).prob
      {z | ¬NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.rowMatrix F.u) ε} ≤
    ((NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n hb).expect fun z =>
        (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) ^ (2 * q)).trace) /
      ε ^ (2 * q)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.sparseStack_ose_failure_tail
doc:
Failure of the vector OSE property is contained in the concrete norm-tail
event, so it obeys the same trace-moment bound.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.MatrixTail`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseSketch.sparseStack_ose_success_probability {s b n d : ℕ} (hb : 0 < b) (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d)
  (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (δ : ℝ)
  (hmoment :
    ((NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n hb).expect fun z =>
          (NLAlib.SparseSketch.gramError F (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) ^ (2 * q)).trace) /
        ε ^ (2 * q) ≤
      δ) :
  1 - δ ≤
    (NLAlib.sparseStackSelectorLaw s b n hb).prob
      {z | NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding (NLAlib.sparseStackMatrix z.toSample) (NLAlib.SparseSketch.rowMatrix F.u) ε}

doc:

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.sumSq
doc:
The squared Euclidean norm `∑ i, x i ^ 2` of a finitely indexed real vector.

This is the single sum-of-squares spelling of the sparse-sketch proof: it replaces the
former copies `LightSectorConcrete.energy`, `LightSectorConcrete.coordinateEnergy`,
`HeavyBandsConcrete.coordNormSq` and `HeavyBandsConcrete.fockNormSq`. It is an interim
definition (decision D9 of `docs/SPARSE_INTEGRATION.md`): it equals `x ⬝ᵥ x`
(`sumSq_eq_dotProduct`) and is to be replaced by that expression.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.FiniteHilbert`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.sumSq_eq_dotProduct
doc:
The interim sum of squares is the self dot product.

NLAlib.SparseSketch.zero_band_envelope_of_components {d m n b : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseSketch.Frame n d) (nu : ℕ) {c : ℝ}
  (hc : 0 ≤ c)
  (hlight :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Lzero m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      3 * NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m)
  (hmixed :
    ‖(1 / ↑m) •
            √(↑b - 1) •
              ((((NLAlib.SparseSketch.Xzero m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                    NLAlib.SparseSketch.XzeroAdj m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                  NLAlib.SparseSketch.Yzero m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                NLAlib.SparseSketch.YzeroAdj m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + (1 + √2) * c)
  (hheavy :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • √(↑b - 1) ^ 2 • NLAlib.SparseSketch.Hzero m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      2 * c)
  (hbTerm : 0 ≤ NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m) (ha : 0 ≤ NLAlib.SparseSketch.aTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m) :
  ‖NLAlib.SparseSketch.normalizedBand m F b NLAlib.SparseSketch.Shift.zero * NLAlib.SparseSketch.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
    NLAlib.SparseSketch.bandConstant * (NLAlib.SparseSketch.aTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + NLAlib.SparseSketch.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + c)
name: NLAlib.SparseSketch.zero_band_envelope_of_components
doc:
Exact operator-level assembly for the grade-preserving band.

name: NLAlib.abs_compressionQuadratureEstimate_inv_sub_hutchinsonEstimate_le
doc:
**SLQ quadrature error for `f(x) = 1/x`.** If `A` is symmetric with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, each `Q_k` has orthonormal columns with `K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q_k`, then
`|SLQ(1/x) − tr_m(f(A))| ≤ 2 (2/a) ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^{2q} · tr_m(I)` with `f(A) = cfc (1/x) A`
(`= A⁻¹`). Source: Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], Thm 4.1 and §4.2 (inverse); the rate is the
CG/Chebyshev rate of `inverse-polynomial-approx`. Atlas: `slq-error`; uses
`lanczos-gauss-quadrature`, `inverse-polynomial-approx`.
atlas: slq-error (partial)

name: NLAlib.abs_compressionQuadratureEstimate_sub_hutchinsonEstimate_le
doc:
**SLQ quadrature error, deterministic.** If `A` is symmetric with spectrum in `[a, c]`,
each `Q_k` has orthonormal columns with `K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q_k`, and `|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`
for a polynomial `p` of degree `< 2q`, then `|SLQ − tr_m f(A)| ≤ 2E · tr_m(I)`, where `tr_m` is
the Hutchinson estimator with the same test vectors and `tr_m(I) = (1/m) ∑ₖ ‖g_k‖²`.
Source: Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], proof of Thm 4.1 (Lemma 4.2). Atlas: `slq-error`;
uses `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`.
atlas: slq-error (partial)

`2q` above the approximation degree `exponentialApproxDegree b δ`,
`|vᵀ exp(−A) v − (Qᵀv)ᵀ exp(−QᵀAQ) (Qᵀv)| ≤ 2δ ‖v‖²`.

`|vᵀ g(A) v| ≤ E (v ⬝ v)`. Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper; the `cfc` form of
`polynomial-spectral-bound`).

`chebyshev-minimax` (κ-form).

The derivative of `T_q` is bounded by `q²` on `[-1, 1]`: `|x| ≤ 1 → |T_q'(x)| ≤ q²`.

`chebyshev-second-kind`.
atlas: chebyshev-second-kind

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : |x| < 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q * M / √(1 - x ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Bernstein's inequality** for algebraic polynomials. If `p` has degree at most `q` and
`|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q M / √(1 − x²)` for `|x| < 1`.

Source: Bernstein (1912); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7; Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
Proof (algebraic form of the trigonometric argument): with `a = x = cos θ₀`, `b = √(1 − x²)`, the
odd part of `θ ↦ p(cos(θ₀ + θ))` is `sin θ · r(cos θ)` for a polynomial `r` of degree `< q` (built
from Hasse derivatives of `p`), `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, and `r(1) = −b p'(x)`; Schur's
inequality `abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` at `y = 1` gives
`b |p'(x)| ≤ q M`.
atlas: bernstein-polynomial-inequality

signature:

  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q ^ 2 * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality** (the first Markov inequality, sharp constant). If `p` has
degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q² M` for all `x ∈ [−1, 1]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), Thm 2.24 / §2.7;
Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
Proof: Bernstein's inequality `abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le` gives
`√(1 − y²) |p'(y)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`, and Schur's inequality
`abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` applied to `p'` (degree `< q`) gives
`|p'(x)| ≤ q · q M`. The equality case (`p = ±M T_q`, `x = ±1`) is not formalised.
atlas: markov-brothers

name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_two_mul_sq_div_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le

**Markov brothers' inequality on an interval.** If `p` has degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on
`[a, b]` (`a < b`), then `|p'(x)| ≤ 2 q² / (b − a) · M` for all `x ∈ [a, b]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (affine
rescaling of `abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le`). Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
atlas: markov-brothers

signature:

name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_abs_eval_T_real_of_forall_abs_le
doc:
Scaled form of Chebyshev's extremal growth bound: if `P` has degree at most `q` and
`|P| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|P(x)| ≤ M |T_q(x)|` for every `|x| ≥ 1`. No sign condition on `M`
(for `M ≤ 0` the hypothesis forces `P = 0`).
Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (1990), Thm 2.20 (case `k = 0`);
Atlas: `chebyshev-extremal`.
atlas: chebyshev-extremal

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {r : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q)
  (hr : r.degree < ↑q) (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, √(1 - y ^ 2) * |Polynomial.eval y r| ≤ M) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x r| ≤ ↑q * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Schur's inequality.** If `r` has degree `< q` and `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then
`|r(x)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`.

Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (Schur's lemma); Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Proof: for `|x| ≤ cos(π/(2q))` directly from
`√(1 − x²) ≥ sin(π/(2q)) ≥ 1/q`; for `x ≥ cos(π/(2q))` by Lagrange interpolation at the zeros
`ξ_k` of `T_q`, where all partial nodal products are nonnegative and the weights satisfy
`|r(ξ_k)| / |T_q'(ξ_k)| ≤ M/q`, so `|r(x)| ≤ (M/q) T_q'(x) ≤ q M`; the case `x ≤ −cos(π/(2q))` by
reflection. Atlas: auxiliary for `markov-brothers` and `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
atlas: schur-polynomial-inequality

signature:
NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_inverseIterate_sub_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ≠ μ) {i₀ : Fin (Fintype.card n)} {u : n → ℝ}
  (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ • u) (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {d D : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d)
  (hdJ : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ i₀ → d ≤ |hA.eigenvalues₀ i - μ|)
  (hD : ∀ (i : n), |hA.eigenvalues i - hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀| ≤ D) {x₀ : n → ℝ} (hx₀ : u ⬝ᵥ x₀ ≠ 0) (k : ℕ) :
  |NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A (NLAlib.inverseIterate A μ x₀ k) - hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀| ≤
    D * ((|hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ - μ| / d) ^ (2 * k) * NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x₀)
name: NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_inverseIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Inverse iteration, Rayleigh quotient.** Under the hypotheses of
`overlapTangentSq_inverseIterate_le`, with `|λᵢ − λ_{i₀}| ≤ D` for all `i` and `u ⬝ x₀ ≠ 0`:
`|ρ(x_k) − λ_{i₀}| ≤ D (|λ_{i₀} − μ|/d)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Thm 27.2 (second bound).
atlas: inverse-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_powerIterate_sub_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₀ : Fin (Fintype.card n)} {u : n → ℝ} (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ • u)
  (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) (hl : hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ ≠ 0) {ρ D : ℝ}
  (hρ : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ i₀ → |hA.eigenvalues₀ i| ≤ ρ)
  (hD : ∀ (i : n), |hA.eigenvalues i - hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀| ≤ D) {x₀ : n → ℝ} (hx₀ : u ⬝ᵥ x₀ ≠ 0) (k : ℕ) :
  |NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A (NLAlib.powerIterate A x₀ k) - hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀| ≤
    D * ((ρ / |hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀|) ^ (2 * k) * NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x₀)
name: NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_powerIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Power iteration, Rayleigh quotient.** For real symmetric `A`, a unit eigenvector `u` of
`λ₁ = λ_{i₀} ≠ 0`, `|λᵢ| ≤ ρ` at the other sorted positions, `|λᵢ − λ₁| ≤ D` for all `i`, and
`u ⬝ x₀ ≠ 0`: `|ρ(A^k x₀) − λ₁| ≤ D (ρ/|λ₁|)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`, the squared rate of the
angle. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 27.1; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
Thm 8.2.1. Deviation: explicit constant `D` (T&B: `O(|λ₂/λ₁|^{2k})`).
atlas: power-iteration

name: NLAlib.abs_rayleighQuotient_sub_le_mul_overlapTangentSq
doc:
**Rayleigh quotient error from the angle.** For real symmetric `A`, a unit eigenvector `u`
for the eigenvalue `λ₁ = λ_{i₀}` at sorted position `i₀`, `D` with `|λᵢ − λ₁| ≤ D` for every
`i` (e.g. `D = λ_max − λ_min`), and `x` with `u ⬝ x ≠ 0`: `|ρ(x) − λ₁| ≤ D tan² ∠(u, x)`.
Proof: split `x = (u ⬝ x) u + w` with `w ⟂ u`; then
`ρ(x) − λ₁ = (wᵀAw − λ₁ ‖w‖²)/‖x‖²` and `|wᵀAw − λ₁ ‖w‖²| ≤ D ‖w‖²`. Source:
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 27.1 (second bound) and Lect. 27 (`ρ(x) − λ = O(‖x − u‖²)`);
Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §4.1. Deviation: explicit constant `D` instead of `O(·)`; two-sided.
atlas: power-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.abs_sub_eval_interpolate_chebyshevZero_le {f : ℝ → ℝ} {q : ℕ} {M : ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Set.Ioo (-1) 1))
  (hM : ∀ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo (-1) 1, |iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ| ≤ M) (x : ℝ) :

    |f x -

            ((Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ (NLAlib.chebyshevZero (q + 1))) (f ∘ NLAlib.chebyshevZero (q + 1)))| ≤
      M / (2 ^ q * ↑(q + 1).factorial)

on `[−1, 1]`).

        NLAlib.matrixLog (μ[fun ω => NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) | m] ω) ≤

signature:

**Raw Gaussian Nyström exact recovery in the rank-deficient sketch regime.**

A standard Gaussian vector of positive dimension is almost surely nonzero:

signature:

        (nhds (NLAlib.singularValues G.transpose (Fintype.card (Fin r) - 1) ^ 2 + ε)) ∧

          (nhds (4 * NLAlib.singularValues G.transpose (Fintype.card (Fin r) - 1) ^ 2)) ∧

doc:
The Gaussian regularized soft minimum converges to the true squared
smallest singular value plus the regularizer, while its gradient energy
and Euler contraction converge to four and two times the unregularized
value. Source: operator hard-edge proof; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail`.
All simple-spectrum and unique-max conditions are discharged almost surely.

converge almost surely to the exact smallest squared Gaussian singular

signature:

Complex rectangular Gram polynomials intertwine through the original matrix.
Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, its complex `A A*`/`A* A` identity. The polynomial
has real coefficients, as in the manuscript.

name: NLAlib.aeval_conjGram_mul_mul_eq_of_block_decomposition
doc:
A polynomially filtered block SVD has the corresponding filtered diagonal blocks.
Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, the intertwining step before `sa:filter-theorem`.
The blocks need not be diagonal, so their squared singular blocks are written as Grams.

signature:

doc:
A polynomial of a diagonal matrix is the diagonal matrix of the polynomial values:
`p(diag d) = diag(p ∘ d)`. Atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_diagonal_ofReal.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ι → ℝ)

doc:
A real polynomial of a real diagonal matrix cast to `𝕜` is the diagonal of the values:
`p(diag (d : 𝕜)) = diag (p(d) : 𝕜)`.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_gram_diagonal_mul_diagonal_inv_eq_one.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]

The polynomial filter of the Gram matrix of a square diagonal is invertible by the diagonal
of reciprocals: `p(Sᴴ S) · diag (p(s i²)⁻¹) = 1` when `p` does not vanish on the squared
entries. Halko–Martinsson–Tropp 2011, §10.

A polynomially filtered block SVD has the corresponding filtered diagonal blocks.

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_mul_eq_mul_aeval_of_mul_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

the shifted matrices, written as the polynomial `∏_{j<k} (X − μ_j)` evaluated at `A`).

(2013) [`gvl13`], §7.5.

doc:
Every reflector vector of the reduction has first entry `0` (so every reflector fixes
`e₀`). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 26.

signature: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis
doc:
The **Arnoldi basis** `q_0, q_1, …`: Gram–Schmidt orthonormalisation of `b, A b, A² b, …`
(`gramSchmidtNormed` over `ℕ`); `q_j = 0` from the grade on (breakdown). Column `j` does not
depend on how many columns are taken. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Alg. 6.1;
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33. Atlas: `arnoldi-def`.

name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_dotProduct
doc: Orthonormality of the Arnoldi vectors below the grade: `q_i ⬝ q_j = δ_ij`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_dotProduct_of_ne.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)
  {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≠ j) : NLAlib.arnoldiBasis A b i ⬝ᵥ NLAlib.arnoldiBasis A b j = 0
name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_dotProduct_of_ne
doc:
Distinct Arnoldi vectors are orthogonal, `q_iᵀ q_j = 0` for `i ≠ j`, with no grade hypothesis
(past the grade the vectors are `0`). Helper for `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (b : n → ℝ) {j : ℕ} (hj : NLAlib.krylovGrade A b ≤ j) : NLAlib.arnoldiBasis A b j = 0
name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
The Arnoldi vectors vanish from the grade on: `arnoldiBasis A b j = 0` for
`krylovGrade A b ≤ j` (breakdown). Helper for `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.6.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)

name: NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_mem_krylovSpace

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiBasis_zero_dotProduct_pos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)

The first canonical Arnoldi vector is `b/‖b‖`: `q_1 ⬝ b = ‖b‖ > 0` (for `b ≠ 0`, i.e.
`0 < krylovGrade A b`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Alg. 6.1. Atlas: `arnoldi-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ)

  ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ ≤ NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ ^ 2 / 2 / (1 - θ * L / 3)) • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ^ 2 ∂μ) ∧
    NLAlib.matrixLog (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ) ≤ (θ ^ 2 / 2 / (1 - θ * L / 3)) • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ^ 2 ∂μ

signature:

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.borderedMatrix {n : ℕ} (a : ℝ) (r c : Fin n → ℝ) (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.borderedMatrix
doc:
The **bordered matrix** `[[a, rᵀ], [c, M]]` on `Fin (n + 1)`: pivot `a`, first row `r`,
first column `c`, trailing block `M`. This is the `Fin.cons` form of the leading-pivot block
splitting `Matrix.fromBlocks` over `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin n` that every recursion of the direct methods
uses (Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20–23; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.2, §4.2).

    (Matrix.reindex (NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv n) (NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv n))
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a) (Matrix.of fun x j => r j) (Matrix.of fun i x => c i) M)

Bridge from the bordered (`Fin.cons`) splitting to Mathlib's `Matrix.fromBlocks` over

signature:
NLAlib.bordered_interlacing_converse_of_strict_cases
  (hstrict :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → ℝ) (b : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ),
      StrictMono d →
        Monotone b →
          (∀ (i : Fin n), b i.castSucc ≤ d i ∧ d i ≤ b i.succ) →
            ∃ v a,
              (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal d) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) v) (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) v)
                    (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly =
                ∏ j, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (b j)))
  (n : ℕ) (d : Fin n → ℝ) (b : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) :
  Monotone d →
    Monotone b →
      (∀ (i : Fin n), b i.castSucc ≤ d i ∧ d i ≤ b i.succ) →
        ∃ v a,
          (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal d) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) v) (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) v)
                (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly =
            ∏ j, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (b j))

A bordered converse construction for strictly increasing original
spectra extends to arbitrary weak interlacing with repeated roots.
The deleted target root is exactly the repeated original root, and its
coordinate is restored with zero coupling. Horn–Johnson 2013,
Theorem 4.3.21; empty and singleton cases are included.

name: NLAlib.card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_neg_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul
doc:
**Spectrum slicing by `LDLᵀ`.** If `A` is real symmetric and `A − xI = L D Lᵀ` with `L`
invertible (e.g. unit lower triangular, from symmetric Gaussian elimination) and
`D = diag(d)`, then the number of eigenvalues of `A` below `x` is the number of negative `dᵢ`.
Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.4.1 (Sylvester's law and `LDLᵀ`); Parlett (1998)
[`parlett98`], Ch. 3. Deviation: any invertible `L`.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:
NLAlib.card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_sign_changes {m : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {x : ℝ}
  (hp : ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → k ≤ m → NLAlib.leadingMinor (A - x • 1) k ≠ 0) :
  {i | hA.eigenvalues i < x}.card =
    {k | NLAlib.leadingMinor (A - x • 1) ↑k * NLAlib.leadingMinor (A - x • 1) (↑k + 1) < 0}.card
name: NLAlib.card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_sign_changes
doc:
SCAFFOLD: sylvester-inertia
**Eigenvalue count from the leading principal minors (Sturm / Jacobi).** Let `A : Fin m × Fin m`
be real symmetric and `p_k = det (A − xI)_{1:k, 1:k}` (`p_0 = 1`). If every `p_k` (`1 ≤ k ≤ m`)
is nonzero, then the number of eigenvalues of `A` below `x` equals the number of sign changes
in `p_0, p_1, …, p_m`, i.e. `#{k < m : p_k p_{k+1} < 0}`. For an unreduced symmetric
tridiagonal `A` the `p_k` obey the Sturm three-term recurrence
`p_{k+1} = (a_{k+1} − x) p_k − b_k² p_{k−1}`, and this count drives bisection.
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Thm 8.5.1 and §8.4.1; Parlett (1998) [`parlett98`], Ch. 3;
Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], §4.5. Proof sketch: nonzero leading minors give `LU` of `A − xI`
(`luSucceeds_iff_forall_det_ne_zero`, D-A's `Matrix/Factorizations/LU.lean`), symmetric so
`A − xI = L D Lᵀ` with `d_{k+1} = p_{k+1}/p_k` (`IsLU.det_leadingSubmatrix`); then
`card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_neg_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul` and `p_{k+1}/p_k < 0 ↔ p_k p_{k+1} < 0`.
Difficulty 3.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_diagonal_real.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ι → ℝ) :

doc:
Real functional calculus acts entrywise on a real diagonal matrix.
Arbitrary real functions are allowed because the diagonal spectrum is finite.
Source: the private `cfc_diag` proof in `JointTensorRepresentation`, via Mathlib's
diagonal algebra homomorphism and Pi CFC; Tropp 2015, §2.1.11;
atlas `golden-thompson`, `operator-monotone-convex` (helper).

signature:

doc:
`f(A)` is `p(A)` for the Lagrange interpolant `p` of `f` at the (distinct) eigenvalues of the
symmetric `A`. Standard (Higham 2008 [`higham08`], Def. 1.4). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error`
(helper).

name: NLAlib.cfc_eq_aeval_of_forall_eval_eq
doc:
A matrix function of a symmetric `A` equals the polynomial calculus of any polynomial that
agrees with `f` at the eigenvalues: `f(A) = p(A)` when `p(λᵢ) = f(λᵢ)` for all `i`.
Standard (Higham 2008 [`higham08`], Def. 1.4 and Thm 1.12). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_eq_eigenvectorUnitary_mul_diagonal_mul_conjTranspose.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2}

The Hermitian functional calculus in eigenbasis coordinates: `f(A) = U diag(f(λᵢ)) Uᴴ`

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_eq_sum_smul_eigenvectorProjector.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {d : Type u_2} [Fintype d]

**Spectral decomposition of the functional calculus**:

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_fromBlocks.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty κ] (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (B : Matrix κ κ ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian)
  (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 B).IsHermitian ∧
    spectrum ℝ (Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 B) = spectrum ℝ A ∪ spectrum ℝ B ∧
      cfc f (Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 B) = Matrix.fromBlocks (cfc f A) 0 0 (cfc f B)
name: NLAlib.cfc_fromBlocks
doc:
A block-diagonal matrix of Hermitian blocks is Hermitian, its spectrum is the union of the block
spectra, and the functional calculus acts blockwise.

Tropp 2015, proof of Thm 8.5.2. Atlas: `operator-monotone-convex`. Ported from the Prove2me
mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 8*.

Auxiliary; not a numbered result in the source.

signature: NLAlib.cgInit.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.CGState n
name: NLAlib.cgInit
doc:
The initial state `(x₀, r₀, r₀)` with `r₀ = c − A x₀`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Alg. 38.1. Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

signature: NLAlib.cgObjective.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x : n → ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.cgObjective
doc:
The conjugate-gradient objective `φ(x) = ½ xᵀ A x − cᵀ x`. Its minimiser over `ℝⁿ` (for
positive definite `A`) solves `A x = c`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], eq. (38.6).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (c u d : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c (u + d) = NLAlib.cgObjective A c u + d ⬝ᵥ (A.mulVec u - c) + NLAlib.quadForm A d / 2
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_add
doc:
Expansion of the CG objective along a direction: for symmetric `A`,
`φ(u + d) = φ(u) + dᵀ (A u − c) + ½ dᵀ A d`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], proof of
Thm 38.2. Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (z : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c z = NLAlib.cgObjective A c xs + NLAlib.quadForm A (z - xs) / 2
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub
doc:
The CG objective measures the `A`-norm error: if `A x⋆ = c` then
`φ(z) = φ(x⋆) + ½ ‖z − x⋆‖_A²`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], eq. (38.7).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A W : Matrix n n ℝ) (c y : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c (W.mulVec y) = NLAlib.cgObjective (W.transpose * A * W) (W.transpose.mulVec c) y
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_mulVec
doc:
The CG objective under a change of variables: `φ_{A,c}(Wy) = φ_{WᵀAW, Wᵀc}(y)`.
Helper for `preconditioned-cg`.

signature: NLAlib.cgRecurrence.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.CGState n
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence
doc:
The **conjugate-gradient recursion**: the state after `k` Hestenes–Stiefel steps from
`(x₀, r₀, r₀)`, as `Nat.iterate`. `(cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).x` is the CG iterate `x_k`
(`isCGIterate_cgRecurrence`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 38.1; Hestenes–Stiefel
(1952). Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_add_of_r_eq_zero
doc:
After a zero residual the recursion is constant: if `r_k = 0` then for every `m ≥ 1` the
state `k + m` is `(x_k, 0, 0)`. Atlas: `cg-recurrence` (totality).

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (k : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) k ∧
    (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).r ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) (k + 1) ∧
      (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).p ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) (k + 1)
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
**Krylov memberships**, for every `A` (no hypothesis): `x_k − x₀ ∈ K_k(A, r₀)` and
`r_k, p_k ∈ K_{k+1}(A, r₀)`. Induction on `k` with `mulVec_mem_krylovSpace_succ`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (the inclusion half).
Helper for `cg-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_p_eq_zero_of_r_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) {k : ℕ}
  (hk : (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).r = 0) : (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).p = 0
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_p_eq_zero_of_r_eq_zero
doc:
A zero residual forces a zero search direction: `r_k = 0 → p_k = 0` (for `k = 0`, `p_0 = r_0`;
otherwise `β_{k−1} = 0`). No hypothesis on `A`. Atlas: `cg-recurrence` (totality).

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).r = c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).x
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_eq
doc:
**The residual identity** `r_k = c − A x_k`, for every `A` and every `k` (no hypothesis).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 38.1 (the update of `r` is the update of
`c − A x`). Helper for `cg-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
**The residual vanishes from the grade on**: for `A ≻ 0`, `r_k = 0` when
`k ≥ ν(A, r₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1. Proof:
`cgRecurrence_x_eq_of_krylovGrade_le` with `x⋆ = A⁻¹ c` and `cgRecurrence_r_eq`.
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_ne_zero_of_lt_krylovGrade.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k < NLAlib.krylovGrade A (c - A.mulVec x₀)) : (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k).r ≠ 0
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_r_ne_zero_of_lt_krylovGrade
doc:
**No breakdown before the grade**: `r_k ≠ 0` for `k < ν(A, r₀)`, for every `A` (no
definiteness needed). With `cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le` this says that for `A ≻ 0`
the recursion stops (`r_k = 0`, the only case in which a denominator vanishes, since
`pᵀAp = 0 ↔ p = 0`) exactly at the grade. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (the
hypothesis "`r_{k−1} ≠ 0`" is automatic below the grade); Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.3.
Proof: if `r_k = 0` then `r₀ = A (x_k − x₀) ∈ A K_k`, so `K_{k+1} ≤ A K_k` and
`min (k+1) ν ≤ min k ν` (`finrank_krylovSpace`), forcing `ν ≤ k`.
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_succ.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ (k + 1) = NLAlib.cgStep A (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ k)
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_succ
doc: One more step of the recursion. Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_x_eq_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
**Finite termination of the recursion**: for `A ≻ 0` and `A x⋆ = c`, `x_k = x⋆` once
`k ≥ ν(A, r₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (CG converges in at most `n`
steps); Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.7. Proof: `isCGIterate_cgRecurrence` and
`eq_of_isCGIterate_of_krylovGrade_le` (atlas `cg-finite-termination`).
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.cgRecurrence_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ 0 = NLAlib.cgInit A c x₀
name: NLAlib.cgRecurrence_zero
doc: The recursion starts at `(x₀, r₀, r₀)`. Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

signature: NLAlib.cgStep.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (s : NLAlib.CGState n) : NLAlib.CGState n
name: NLAlib.cgStep
doc:
One Hestenes–Stiefel step: `α = rᵀr / pᵀAp`, `x' = x + α p`, `r' = r − α A p`,
`β = r'ᵀr' / rᵀr`, `p' = r' + β p`. Total: with `x / 0 = 0` a zero residual gives `α = β = 0`
(`cgStep_of_r_eq_zero`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 38.1; Saad (2011)
[`saad11`], Alg. 6.18. Atlas: `cg-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgStep_of_r_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {s : NLAlib.CGState n} (hs : s.r = 0) :
  NLAlib.cgStep A s = { x := s.x, r := 0, p := 0 }
name: NLAlib.cgStep_of_r_eq_zero
doc:
**A zero residual freezes the state**: if `r = 0` then `cgStep A s = (x, 0, 0)` (`α = 0`
and `β = 0/0 = 0`). Atlas: `cg-recurrence` (totality).

signature:
NLAlib.cgf_const_mul.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Y : Ω → ℝ} (a θ : ℝ) :
  ProbabilityTheory.cgf (fun ω => a * Y ω) μ θ = ProbabilityTheory.cgf Y μ (a * θ)
name: NLAlib.cgf_const_mul
doc: Scaling inside the CGF: `cgf (a • Y) θ = cgf Y (a θ)`. Atlas `hanson-wright` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.change_eigenbasis_apply_eq_zero_of_eigenvalues_ne.{u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {K : Type u_3} [Field K] {A V W : Matrix n n K} {d : n → K} (hV : IsUnit V) (hAV : A * V = V * Matrix.diagonal d)
  (hAW : A * W = W * Matrix.diagonal d) {i j : n} (hij : d i ≠ d j) : (V⁻¹ * W) i j = 0
name: NLAlib.change_eigenbasis_apply_eq_zero_of_eigenvalues_ne
doc:
An aligned change of eigenvector basis vanishes between distinct
eigenvalues, so it is block diagonal on the repeated eigenspaces.
Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 1.3.27; the vanishing itself needs only the first
eigenvector matrix to be invertible.
atlas: diagonalizable-def (partial)

signature: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (K : Set ℂ) : ℕ
name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn

signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_eq_card_filter.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (K : Set ℂ) (d : n → ℂ) (hd : A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i))) :
  NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn A K = {i | d i ∈ K}.card
name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_eq_card_filter

signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_eq_of_preconnected.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [TopologicalSpace Ω] [PreconnectedSpace Ω] (A : Ω → Matrix n n ℂ) (hA : Continuous A) (K L : Set ℂ) (hK : IsCompact K)
  (hL : IsCompact L) (hdisj : Disjoint K L) (hspec : ∀ (t : Ω), spectrum ℂ (A t) ⊆ K ∪ L) (s t : Ω) :
  NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn (A s) K = NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn (A t) K
name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_eq_of_preconnected
doc:
Along a continuous family over a preconnected parameter space, the
number of characteristic roots in either of two disjoint compact spectral
sets is constant, including algebraic multiplicities.
Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 6.1.1; the finite closed root-count fibers are
clopen, so no root tracking or analytic projector is required.

signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_gershgorinColumnUnion_eq_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (I : Finset n)
  (hdisj : Disjoint (NLAlib.gershgorinColumnUnion A I) (NLAlib.gershgorinColumnUnion A Iᶜ)) :
  NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn A (NLAlib.gershgorinColumnUnion A I) = I.card
name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_gershgorinColumnUnion_eq_card
doc:
A union of selected closed column discs, disjoint from the remaining
closed column discs, contains exactly as many algebraic eigenvalues as
selected columns. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 6.1.3; all degenerate
and repeated-root cases are retained by transpose and the root multiset.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_gershgorinRowUnion_eq_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (I : Finset n)
  (hdisj : Disjoint (NLAlib.gershgorinRowUnion A I) (NLAlib.gershgorinRowUnion A Iᶜ)) :
  NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn A (NLAlib.gershgorinRowUnion A I) = I.card
name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_gershgorinRowUnion_eq_card
doc:
A union of `|I|` closed row discs, disjoint from the remaining closed
row discs, contains exactly `|I|` eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 6.1.1; internal overlaps, repeated roots,
zero-radius discs, empty selections and empty matrices are included.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:
NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_le_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (K : Set ℂ) :
  NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn A K ≤ Fintype.card n
name: NLAlib.charpolyRootCountIn_le_card
doc:
A characteristic-root count is at most the matrix dimension, including
empty shapes. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 6.1.1.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_add_vecMulVec_mul_X_sub_C.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [Infinite K] {A : Matrix n n K} {x : n → K} {μ : K} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hAx : A.mulVec x = μ • x) (y : n → K) :
  (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C μ) * (A + Matrix.vecMulVec x y).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (μ + y ⬝ᵥ x)) * A.charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_add_vecMulVec_mul_X_sub_C
doc:
The rank-one eigenvalue update satisfies a polynomial cross-product
identity, including every value of the polynomial variable.
Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 2.4.10.1; the infinite-field proof extends the
determinant-lemma computation across the finite old spectrum.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_bordered_diagonal_insertNth {n : ℕ} (d : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (p : Fin (n + 1)) (v : Fin n → ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal d) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) (p.insertNth 0 v))
        (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) (p.insertNth 0 v)) (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d p)) *
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ p.succAbove)) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) v)
          (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) v) (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_bordered_diagonal_insertNth
doc:
Inserting a zero coupling in a bordered diagonal matrix restores an
uncoupled scalar characteristic factor. The border scalar is preserved.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.3.21; repeated-root restoration helper.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Field K]
  [Infinite K] (d v : n → K) :
  (Matrix.diagonal d + Matrix.vecMulVec v v).charpoly =
    ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i)) -
      ∑ i, Polynomial.C (v i ^ 2) * ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d j))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec
doc:
The characteristic polynomial of a diagonal matrix plus `v vᵀ` is its
diagonal product minus the sum of squared couplings times products with
one factor erased. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), converse interlacing;
no distinctness, nonzero-entry or invertibility assumption is required,
and the empty matrix has characteristic polynomial one.
atlas: interlacing-converse (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_insertNth {n : ℕ} (d : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (p : Fin (n + 1)) (v : Fin n → ℝ) :
  (Matrix.diagonal d + Matrix.vecMulVec (p.insertNth 0 v) (p.insertNth 0 v)).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d p)) * (Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ p.succAbove) + Matrix.vecMulVec v v).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_insertNth

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_reindex.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (e : n ≃ m) (d v : n → ℝ) :
  (Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ ⇑e.symm) + Matrix.vecMulVec (v ∘ ⇑e.symm) (v ∘ ⇑e.symm)).charpoly =
    (Matrix.diagonal d + Matrix.vecMulVec v v).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_add_vecMulVec_reindex
doc:
Relabeling a diagonal rank-one update leaves its characteristic
polynomial unchanged. Source: permutation similarity; helper for converse
interlacing on arbitrary finite matrix labels.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_arrowhead_reindex.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (e : n ≃ m) (d v : n → ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal (d ∘ ⇑e.symm)) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) (v ∘ ⇑e.symm))
        (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) (v ∘ ⇑e.symm)) (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly =
    (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal d) (Matrix.replicateCol (Fin 1) v) (Matrix.replicateRow (Fin 1) v)
        (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_arrowhead_reindex

signature: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_one_neg_one_eq : (Matrix.diagonal ![1, -1]).charpoly = Polynomial.X ^ 2 - 1
name: NLAlib.charpoly_diagonal_one_neg_one_eq
doc:
The diagonal matrix with entries one and minus one has characteristic
polynomial `X²-1`. This is the gap-coefficient counterexample in frontier
equation `herm:coefficient-correct`, correcting `sylvester-criterion`.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_orthogonal_compression.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {k : ℕ} (f : Module.End 𝕜 E) {u : E}
  (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) {μ : 𝕜} (hfu : f u = μ • u) (hk : Module.finrank 𝕜 E = k + 1) :
  LinearMap.charpoly f =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C μ) * (↑(𝕜 ∙ u)ᗮ.orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘ₗ f ∘ₗ (𝕜 ∙ u)ᗮ.subtype).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_orthogonal_compression
doc:
Compressing away a unit eigenvector removes exactly its characteristic
linear factor. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), proof of Theorem 2.3.1; no
normality or simplicity assumption is needed.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_submatrix_of_isolated_coordinate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [CommRing K] (M : Matrix n n K) (i : n) (μ : K) (hcol : ∀ (j : n), M j i = if j = i then μ else 0)
  (hrow : ∀ (j : n), M i j = if j = i then μ else 0) :
  M.charpoly = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C μ) * (M.submatrix (fun j => ↑j) fun j => ↑j).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_submatrix_of_isolated_coordinate
doc:
An isolated coordinate contributes exactly one characteristic linear
factor. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 1.4.7; the remaining block is
the principal submatrix on all other coordinates, including an empty block.
The special case of `charpoly_eq_mul_of_isolated_equiv` for the equivalence
`Fin 1 ⊕ {j // j ≠ i} ≃ n` (over any commutative ring).

name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_X_sub_C_mul_succ_submatrix
doc:
A first-column eigenvalue factors out of the characteristic polynomial.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §1.4; first-column Laplace expansion.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_eq_mul_of_isolated_equiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {K : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [CommRing K] (A : Matrix m m K) (e : Fin 1 ⊕ n ≃ m)
  (h : ∀ (j : n), A (e (Sum.inl 0)) (e (Sum.inr j)) = 0 ∧ A (e (Sum.inr j)) (e (Sum.inl 0)) = 0) :
  A.charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (A (e (Sum.inl 0)) (e (Sum.inl 0)))) *
      (A.submatrix (fun j => e (Sum.inr j)) fun j => e (Sum.inr j)).charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_mul_of_isolated_equiv
doc:
An uncoupled scalar coordinate contributes one linear characteristic
factor, with the other coordinates in any specified order. Horn–Johnson
2013, Section 1.2; converse-interlacing restoration helper.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_eq_prod_of_eval_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (d : n → ℂ)
  (h : ∀ (j : Fin (Fintype.card n + 1)), Polynomial.eval (↑↑j) A.charpoly = ∏ i, (↑↑j - d i)) :
  A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_eq_prod_of_eval_eq

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_fromBlocks_diagonal_replicate.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Field K] [Infinite K] {l : Type u_3} [Unique l] [Fintype l] [DecidableEq l] (d v : n → K) (a : K) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.diagonal d) (Matrix.replicateCol l v) (Matrix.replicateRow l v)
        (Matrix.of fun x x_1 => a)).charpoly =
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) * ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i)) -
      ∑ i, Polynomial.C (v i ^ 2) * ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d j))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_fromBlocks_diagonal_replicate
doc:
The characteristic polynomial of a real or infinite-field diagonal
arrowhead is the diagonal product times its last linear factor, minus the
sum of squared couplings times the products with one factor erased.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), converse interlacing; the formula is
unconditional, including repeated diagonal entries and empty leading blocks.
atlas: interlacing-converse (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_inverse_mul_eq_prod_of_congruence.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A B S : Matrix n n ℝ} {d : n → ℝ} (hS : IsUnit S) (hA : A = S * S.transpose)
  (hB : B = S * Matrix.diagonal d * S.transpose) : (A⁻¹ * B).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_inverse_mul_eq_prod_of_congruence
doc:
The diagonal of a definite-pair congruence enumerates the relative
operator's eigenvalues with full characteristic multiplicity.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.6.1;
helper for `simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence`.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_mul_mul_transpose_of_hasOrthonormalCols.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (Q A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) : (Q * A * Q.transpose).charpoly = A.charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_mul_mul_transpose_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
Orthogonal conjugation preserves the characteristic polynomial.
Source: similarity invariance, used by the converse-interlacing transports.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_neg_eq_prod_of_isHermitian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (d : n → ℝ) (hd : A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i))) :
  (-A).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (-d i))
name: NLAlib.charpoly_neg_eq_prod_of_isHermitian
doc:
Negating a real symmetric matrix negates every entry of any complete
characteristic-root list, including multiplicities. Source: the spectral
theorem; helper for the negative rank-one converse-interlacing construction.

signature:
NLAlib.charpoly_nonsing_inv_mul_mul_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]
  (A S : Matrix n n K) (hS : IsUnit S) : (S⁻¹ * A * S).charpoly = A.charpoly
name: NLAlib.charpoly_nonsing_inv_mul_mul_eq
doc:
Nonsingular similarity preserves the characteristic polynomial.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §1.3; this is the cyclic characteristic identity.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex (N k : ℕ) : ℕ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex
doc:
Frequency folding into the degree range of the canonical Chebyshev extrema grid.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.1 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_le {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex N k ≤ N
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_le
doc:
Every folded frequency has degree at most the grid cutoff.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.1 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier
doc:
The gap-amplifying polynomial `chebyshevAmplifier α γ q = T_q(X/α) / T_q(1 + γ)`: equal to
`1` at `α(1 + γ)`, increasing beyond it, and exponentially small on `[−α, α]`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4–5; Atlas: `chebyshev-amplifier`.
atlas: chebyshev-amplifier

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier α γ q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + γ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C (1 / α) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff
doc:
The real Chebyshev coefficients are the real parts of the standard contour coefficients.
For a function real on `[-1,1]` these are the usual real Chebyshev expansion coefficients.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_eq_chebyshevCoeff {F : ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (hF : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, F ↑x = ↑(f x)) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k = NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_eq_chebyshevCoeff
doc:
A continuous real restriction identifies the real contour coefficient with the
weighted real Chebyshev coefficient. No holomorphic extension is needed for this equality.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant (F : ℂ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant
doc:
The Lagrange interpolant on the `(N+1)`-point canonical Chebyshev extrema grid.
Mathlib totalizes the `N=0` grid at the point `1`; this convention is made explicit.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 2 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, definition).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc (F : ℂ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc
doc:
The degree-`N` truncation of the canonical real Chebyshev coefficients.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, definition).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : ℂ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction
doc:
Pull back a complex function on the Bernstein ellipse to the additive circle.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_coe_eq_cos (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : ℝ) : NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F ↑θ = F ↑(Real.cos θ)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_coe_eq_cos
doc:
The circle pullback evaluated at a real angle is exactly `F(cos θ)`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_neg (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F (-θ) = NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F θ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_neg
doc:
The circle pullback is even, by the inversion symmetry of the Joukowski transform.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff
doc:
Real Chebyshev coefficient with zeroth normalization `1/π` and positive normalization
`2/π`, using the arcsine weight. Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 3.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_cosine_integral (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k =
    (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) / Real.pi * ∫ (θ : ℝ) in 0..Real.pi, f (Real.cos θ) * Real.cos (↑k * θ)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_cosine_integral
doc:
The weighted coefficient is the usual cosine coefficient, including the zeroth
normalization. Source: the cosine substitution for the Chebyshev weight.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_weighted_integral (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k =
    (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) / Real.pi *
      ∫ (x : ℝ) in -1..1, f x * Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k) * √(1 - x ^ 2)⁻¹
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff_eq_weighted_integral
doc:
The arcsine-measure coefficient is the classical weighted integral on `[-1,1]`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 3.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) : ℂ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff
doc:
Complex Chebyshev coefficients in their Joukowski contour form. The zeroth coefficient
has normalization `1/(2πi)`; positive coefficients have normalization `1/(πi)`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff F k = (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) * fourierCoeff (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F) ↑k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff
doc:
The contour definition agrees exactly with the standard Fourier definition of the
Chebyshev coefficients, including the distinct zeroth normalization.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_ofReal_chebyshevCoeff {F : ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (hF : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, F ↑x = ↑(f x)) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff F k = ↑(NLAlib.chebyshevCoeff f k)
