doc:
The complex contour coefficient itself is the real weighted coefficient when the
restriction is real and continuous. Source: even-real Fourier symmetry and the contour bridge.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (a b : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate
doc:
The Chebyshev iterate for spectrum in `[a, b]`: the polynomial method whose residual
polynomial is `chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`,
i.e. iteration polynomial `(1 − chebyshevResidual a b q) /ₘ X`. Source: Saad (2003)
[`saad03`], §12.3; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`]. Deviation: defined by its polynomial; the
recurrence of Saad Alg. 12.1 is the theorem `chebyshevIterate_add_two`.
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_add_two.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ (q + 2) =
    (Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑(q + 2)))⁻¹ •
      ((4 / (b - a) * Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑(q + 1))) •
          (((b + a) / 2) • NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ (q + 1) +
            (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ (q + 1)))) -
        Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) • NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_add_two
doc:
**The Chebyshev three-term recurrence** (Saad Alg. 12.1 in three-term form): for `0 < a < b`,
with `τ_k = T_k(σ)`, `σ = (b + a)/(b − a)`, `θ = (b + a)/2`, `δ = (b − a)/2` and
`r_k = c − A x_k`,
`τ_{q+2} x_{q+2} = (2τ_{q+1}/δ)(θ x_{q+1} + r_{q+1}) − τ_q x_q`, i.e.
`x_{q+2} = τ_{q+2}⁻¹ ((4τ_{q+1}/(b − a)) (θ x_{q+1} + r_{q+1}) − τ_q x_q)`.
No hypothesis on `A` and no solution is needed (a polynomial identity applied to `r₀`).
Saad's two-term form with `ρ_k = τ_k/τ_{k+1}` and `d_k = x_{k+1} − x_k`
(`d_k = ρ_kρ_{k−1} d_{k−1} + (2ρ_k/δ) r_k`) is a rearrangement of this identity together with
`τ_{q+2} = 2σ τ_{q+1} − τ_q`. Proof: `Polynomial.funext` after cancelling `X`, using
`Chebyshev.T_add_two` at `σ − 2t/(b − a)` and at `σ`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3, Alg. 12.1; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`].
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ 1 = x₀ + (2 / (b + a)) • (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_one
doc:
**First Chebyshev step**: `x_1 = x₀ + r₀/θ`, `θ = (b + a)/2`, for `0 < a < b`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Alg. 12.1 (`d_0 = r_0/θ`).
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
  (hab : a < b) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
The Chebyshev iterate lies in `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)` (its iteration polynomial has degree
`< q`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3.

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (a b : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ 0 = x₀
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_zero
doc:
`chebyshevIterate` at `q = 0` is the starting point. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
Alg. 12.1. Atlas: `chebyshev-iteration`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual
doc:
The shifted, scaled Chebyshev polynomial normalised to `1` at `0`:
`chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2 X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`. For `0 < a < b`
it has the smallest maximum modulus on `[a, b]` among polynomials of degree at most `q` with
value `1` at `0` (the residual polynomial of Chebyshev iteration and the model for CG).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.
atlas: chebyshev-minimax

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C ((b + a) / (b - a)) - Polynomial.C (2 / (b - a)) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevUSequence : Polynomial.Sequence ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevUSequence
doc:
Chebyshev second-kind polynomials form a degree-indexed polynomial sequence.
Source: Rivlin, Chebyshev Polynomials, Chapter 1; helper for sharp `jackson-lipschitz`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevZero (q : ℕ) (k : Fin q) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevZero
doc:
The Chebyshev zeros `chebyshevZero q k = cos((2k + 1)π/(2q))`, `k < q`: the `q` roots of
`T_q`, in decreasing order. Source: Trefethen (2019) [`trefethen19`], Ch. 2 ("Chebyshev points
of the first kind"); Mathlib `Polynomial.Chebyshev.roots_T_real`.
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`.
atlas: chebyshev-interpolation-error

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_injective (q : ℕ) : Function.Injective (NLAlib.chebyshevZero q)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_injective
doc:
The Chebyshev zeros are distinct (from Mathlib's `roots_T_real_nodup`).
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_mem_Icc (q : ℕ) (k : Fin q) : NLAlib.chebyshevZero q k ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1
name: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_mem_Icc
doc: The Chebyshev zeros lie in `[−1, 1]`. Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshev_node_injOn (N : ℕ) : Set.InjOn (Polynomial.Chebyshev.node N) ↑(Finset.range (N + 1))
name: NLAlib.chebyshev_node_injOn

Canonical Chebyshev grid nodes are injective on their index range.
Source: Mathlib `strictAntiOn_node`; helper for `chebyshev-approx-analytic`.

signature: NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient (L θ : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient
doc:
The Chernoff cgf coefficient `(e^{θL} - 1)/L`, equal to `θ` when `L = 0`. Tropp 2015, Lemma 5.4.1.
Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature: NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail (dimension : ℕ) (a L ε : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail
doc:
The matrix Chernoff lower tail `d · (e^{-ε}/(1-ε)^{1-ε})^{a/L}`, equal to `d` when `L = 0`. Tropp
2015, eq. (5.1.5). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature: NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail (dimension : ℕ) (a L ε : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail
doc:
The matrix Chernoff upper tail `d · (e^{ε}/(1+ε)^{1+ε})^{a/L}`, equal to `d` when `L = 0`. Tropp
2015, eq. (5.1.6). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature:
NLAlib.chernoff_matrix_mgf_cgf_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L)
  (hMeas : Measurable X) (hHerm : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X ω).IsHermitian)
  (hBound : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, 0 ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMin (X ω) ∧ NLAlib.lambdaMax (X ω) ≤ L) (θ : ℝ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ ≤ NLAlib.matrixExp (NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient L θ • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ) ∧
    NLAlib.matrixLog (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ) ≤ NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient L θ • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ
name: NLAlib.chernoff_matrix_mgf_cgf_le
doc:
For a random positive semidefinite `X` with `λmax X ≤ L`, `𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼ matrixExp (g(θ) •
𝔼 X)` and `matrixLog 𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼ g(θ) • 𝔼 X`, where `g = chernoffCgfCoefficient L`.

Tropp 2015, Lemma 5.4.1. Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 5*.

Stated for all real `θ`; `L = 0` is handled by the piecewise definition of
`chernoffCgfCoefficient`.

signature: NLAlib.cholesky {n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.cholesky
doc:
**The Cholesky recursion** on the leading pivot: for `A = [[a, cᵀ], [c, C]]`,
`L = [[√a, 0], [c/√a, L']]` with `L' = cholesky (C − c cᵀ/a)` (`pivotSchur`; for a symmetric
`A` the first row and column agree). Total: a nonpositive pivot gives `√a = 0` and junk, never
an error. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 23.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.5 (outer-product form).
atlas: cholesky-algorithm

signature: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (t : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace
doc:
Expected residual trace is the finite weighted sum over adaptive pivot histories.
Source: manuscript `sa:rpcholesky`, `u_t = E tr R_t`.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_antitone.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) : Antitone (NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A)
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_antitone
doc:
The expected trace is nonincreasing along the actual finite-history process.
Source: manuscript `sa:rpcholesky`, bounded finite moments and monotonicity.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_eq_zero_of_rank_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) {t : ℕ} (ht : A.rank ≤ t) : NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A t = 0
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_eq_zero_of_rank_le
doc:
The expected trace is exactly zero after at most the input rank positive pivots.
Source: manuscript `sa:rp-rank` and `sa:rp-theorem`, zero-tail branch.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_eq_zero_of_spectralTraceTail_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r k : ℕ} (ht : NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r = 0) (hk : r ≤ k) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A k = 0
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_eq_zero_of_spectralTraceTail_eq_zero
doc:
A zero optimal trace tail yields exact RPCholesky expected trace after at most
the target rank pivots, including a rank-zero input. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-theorem`.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_mul_spectralTraceTail.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hτ : 0 < NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r) {ε : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 < ε) (hbudget : ↑r / ε + ↑r * Real.log (A.trace / (ε * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r)) ≤ ↑k) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A k ≤ (1 + ε) * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_mul_spectralTraceTail
doc:
The actual RPCholesky expected trace reaches the precise relative-error target
under the manuscript's logarithmic pivot budget. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-theorem`;
CETW (2025). This is the positive-tail real-matrix branch, with all positive tolerances.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_mul_spectralTraceTail_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hτ : 0 < NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r) {ε h : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 < ε) (hh : 0 < h)
  (hbudget :
    ↑r * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r / (ε * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r + h) +
        ↑r * Real.log (A.trace / (ε * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r + h)) ≤
      ↑k) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A k ≤ (1 + ε) * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r + h
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_mul_spectralTraceTail_add
doc:
An additive tolerance has its own scale-correct pivot budget, distinct from the
relative optimal tail parameter. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-theorem`, additive corollary.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_of_relativeSpectralTraceTail.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hτ : 0 < NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r)
  {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hbudget : ↑r / ε + ↑r * Real.log (1 / (ε * NLAlib.relativeSpectralTraceTail A ⋯ r)) ≤ ↑k) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A k ≤ (1 + ε) * NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_le_of_relativeSpectralTraceTail

The relative parameter is exactly `eta = tau_*/tr A`, with the source's budget
`r/epsilon + r log(1/(epsilon eta))`. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-theorem`; CETW (2025).

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (t : ℕ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A t
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_nonneg
doc:
Every expected Cholesky residual trace is nonnegative.
Source: manuscript `sa:rpcholesky`, bounded finite moments.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_succ_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (t : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A (t + 1) =
    ∑ h,
      NLAlib.choleskyHistoryWeight A t h *
        ((NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A h).trace -
          (NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A h * NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A h).trace /
            (NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A h).trace)
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_succ_eq
doc:
The actual adaptive expected trace obeys the exact finite one-step averaging
formula before applying the scalar tail drift. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-recursion`.

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_succ_le_traceExcessDrift.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {r : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (t : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A (t + 1) ≤
    NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A t -
      NLAlib.traceExcessDrift (NLAlib.spectralTraceTail A ⋯ r) (NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace A t) / ↑r
name: NLAlib.choleskyExpectedTrace_succ_le_traceExcessDrift
doc:
The actual adaptive expected trace obeys the source's nonlinear relative-tail
recursion. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-recursion`; CETW (2025).
All matrix and probability inequalities are derived from the input PSD matrix.

NLAlib.choleskyPivotProbability.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (R : Matrix n n 𝕜)

The **RPCholesky pivot law** `Re rᵢᵢ / Re (tr R)`, uniform when `Re (tr R) = 0` (so it sums

signature: NLAlib.choleskyPivoted {n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Equiv.Perm (Fin n) × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.choleskyPivoted
doc:
**Cholesky with diagonal pivoting** as a total recursion: swap the largest diagonal entry
to the front (`diagPivotSwap`), take one Cholesky step, recurse on the Schur complement and
permute the computed column by the later pivots. Returns the pivot order `σ` and `L`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 4.2.4 (outer-product form with symmetric pivoting); Higham 2002,
§10.3. For PSD `A` a zero pivot means the remaining matrix is zero, and the recursion then
produces zero columns (`x / 0 = 0`), so it never fails.
atlas: cholesky-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyPivoted_apply_eq_zero_of_rank_le {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) (i j : Fin n)
  (hj : A.rank ≤ ↑j) : (NLAlib.choleskyPivoted A).2 i j = 0
name: NLAlib.choleskyPivoted_apply_eq_zero_of_rank_le
doc:
SCAFFOLD: cholesky-algorithm
**Pivoted Cholesky terminates at the rank**: for PSD `A`, the columns of the pivoted factor
with index `≥ rank A` vanish, so the factor has exactly `rank A` nonzero columns and
`P A Pᵀ = L₁ L₁ᵀ` with `L₁` its first `rank A` columns. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9;
Higham 2002, §10.3.
Proof sketch: as for `choleskyPivoted_apply_self_pos_iff_lt_rank`: after the first zero pivot
the remaining Schur complement is zero (zero maximal diagonal of a PSD matrix), so the
recursion produces zero columns.
atlas: cholesky-algorithm (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.choleskyPivoted_apply_self_pos_iff_lt_rank {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef)
  (i : Fin n) : 0 < (NLAlib.choleskyPivoted A).2 i i ↔ ↑i < A.rank
name: NLAlib.choleskyPivoted_apply_self_pos_iff_lt_rank
doc:
SCAFFOLD: cholesky-algorithm
**Pivoted Cholesky stops at the rank**: for PSD `A`, the diagonal of the pivoted factor is
positive exactly in the first `rank A` positions. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9; Higham 2002,
Thm 10.9.
Proof sketch: by diagonal pivoting, `lₖₖ² = max diag` of the `k`-th Schur complement, and a PSD
matrix with zero diagonal is zero; so once a pivot is zero all later columns vanish. The number
of nonzero columns of the lower triangular `L` with this staircase pattern is `rank L =
rank (L Lᵀ) = rank A` (`Matrix.rank_mul_transpose`-type lemma, `Matrix.rank_submatrix`).
atlas: cholesky-algorithm (partial)

name: NLAlib.completion_reduction
doc:
**Exact Gaussian completion, deterministic reduction** (Chen–Persson, Lemma
`lem:completion`; Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Thm 5.1).

Fixed `Q` (orthonormal columns, `q ≥ 1`), its orthogonal completion `Qp = Q⊥`
(`QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`), fixed `A`, random `Ψ` with `s ≥ q + 2`; `G₁ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q`,
`G₂ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q⊥`, `E = projResidual Q A = (I − QQᵀ)A`.
* `hG₁`: `G₁` has full column rank a.s. (so `G₁†G₁ = I`), the "almost surely" of the paper;
* `hG₂`: `E‖G₁†G₂(Q⊥ᵀE)‖_F² = E‖G₁†‖_F² · ‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F²` — `lem:moments` for `G₂` conditionally
  on `G₁` (independence of `G₁`, `G₂`) followed by the tower property;
* `hG₁m`: `E‖G₁†‖_F² = q/(s−q−1)` — `lem:invmom` (needs `s ≥ q+2`, `q ≥ 1`);
* `hGi`: integrability of the noise term.
Everything else in the paper's proof (`ΨᵀA = G₁QᵀA + G₂Q⊥ᵀE`, `X̂ = QᵀA + G₁†G₂Q⊥ᵀE`,
Pythagoras, `‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F = ‖E‖_F`) is proved in `SketchedRegression.lean` and used here.
Conclusion: `eq:completion`,
`E‖A − Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA‖_F² = (1 + q/(s−q−1)) ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²`.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (helper; uses `sketched-regression`, `orthonormal-completion`).
atlas: gn-expected-error

theorem. Four unitary factors have block sizes `p,p,q,q`; their cosines
are actual singular values. Every complex idempotent has its actual canonical
singular coefficients, range/kernel principal-angle secant at positive rank,
equal complementary norms at proper positive rank, and exact norm endpoints.

orthogonal and advertised complex unitary contracts without narrowing either.

derivations Section alg:cs. Empty spaces and zero/pi/2 CS angles are included.

Conjugate transposition preserves the condition number. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_eigenvalues₀_ratio.{u_3} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) :

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_eigenvalues₀_ratio
doc:
For a positive-definite `A` on a nonempty index type, `κ₂(A) = λ_max/λ_min`, the ratio of the
first and last sorted eigenvalues. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_ofReal_moorePenroseConditionNumber
doc:
The condition number of an invertible matrix is the pseudoinverse quantity
`moorePenroseConditionNumber A` (cast to `ℝ≥0∞`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_singularValues_ratio.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : IsUnit A) :
  NLAlib.conditionNumber A = ENNReal.ofReal (NLAlib.singularValues A 0 / NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card n - 1))
name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_singularValues_ratio
doc:
`κ₂(A) = σ₁/σ_n` for an invertible `A` (zero-indexed: `σ 0 / σ (card n - 1)`).
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2 and §5.5.2; Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (12.14).
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_top_iff.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) : NLAlib.conditionNumber A = ⊤ ↔ ¬IsUnit A
name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_eq_top_iff
doc:
The condition number is `⊤` exactly on singular matrices. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_inv.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) : NLAlib.conditionNumber A⁻¹ = NLAlib.conditionNumber A
name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_inv
doc:
Inversion preserves the condition number: `κ₂(A⁻¹) = κ₂(A)` (both `⊤` when `A` is singular,
where `A⁻¹ = 0`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_ne_top_iff.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) : NLAlib.conditionNumber A ≠ ⊤ ↔ IsUnit A
name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_ne_top_iff
doc: The condition number is finite exactly on invertible matrices.

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_of_isUnit.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
On an invertible matrix the condition number is `‖A‖₂ ‖A⁻¹‖₂`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_of_not_isUnit.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_of_not_isUnit
doc: A singular matrix has condition number `⊤`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_toReal_eq_moorePenroseConditionNumber
doc:
The real value of the condition number of an invertible matrix is
`moorePenroseConditionNumber A`.

signature:
NLAlib.conditionNumber_toReal_of_isUnit.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.conditionNumber_toReal_of_isUnit
doc:
The real value of the condition number of an invertible matrix is `‖A‖₂ ‖A⁻¹‖₂`; this is the
form the perturbation bounds are stated in. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.

signature:
NLAlib.conditionalMatrixSecondMoment.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype n]

The actual Bochner conditional second moment of increment `j`, conditioned at time
`j`. Integrability of the squared increment is supplied in the global-variance theorems.
Source: operator rederivations Section 3.1, `V_k`; atlas `matrix-freedman` (partial).

signature:
NLAlib.congruence_le_congruence_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B S : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hS : IsUnit S) : S * A * S.transpose ≤ S * B * S.transpose ↔ A ≤ B
name: NLAlib.congruence_le_congruence_iff
doc:
Invertible congruence preserves and reflects real matrix Loewner order.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.7; helper for relative-spectrum bounds.

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_complexVolumeSampleColumns_mul_eq_submatrix.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (S : Finset n) :

    (A.conjTranspose * A).submatrix Subtype.val Subtype.val
name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_complexVolumeSampleColumns_mul_eq_submatrix
doc:
Selected complex Gram matrices are the corresponding full Gram minors.
Source: `sa:volume`, principal-minor representation.

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_coordinateReflection.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι] (k : ι) :
  (NLAlib.coordinateReflection k).conjTranspose = NLAlib.coordinateReflection k
name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_coordinateReflection
doc:
A coordinate reflection is self-adjoint.
Bhatia 1997, IX.3; atlas `golden-thompson` (pinching helper).

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_leverageSamplingSketch_mul_self.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {d : ℕ}
  (U : Matrix n (Fin d) ℂ) (p : n → NNReal) {k : ℕ} (ω : Fin k → n) :
  (NLAlib.leverageSamplingSketch p ω * U).conjTranspose * (NLAlib.leverageSamplingSketch p ω * U) =

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_leverageSamplingSketch_mul_self
doc:
The sampled Gram matrix is the average of genuine inverse-probability
rank-one samples. Source: operator re-derivation `sa:leverage`.

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_mulVec_eq_zero_of_fromBlocks_posSemidef
doc:
A PSD block matrix kills every cross-block vector coming from the kernel of its leading
block: `A z = 0 ⟹ Bᴴ z = 0`. Albert 1969, Theorem 1; supports
`generalized-schur-complement-psd`.

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_eq_zero_comm.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_eq_zero_comm
doc:
`AᴴB = 0 ↔ BᴴA = 0`: orthogonality of column spaces is symmetric.
Atlas `projection-facts`.

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_eq_zero_of_completion.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_eq_zero_of_completion
doc:
If `Q`, `Qp` have orthonormal columns and `QQᴴ + QpQpᴴ = I`, then `QᴴQp = 0`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.4; atlas `orthonormal-completion`.

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_one_sub_mul_conjTranspose
doc: `Qᴴ (I − QQᴴ) = 0` for `Q` with orthonormal columns. Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_residual
doc:
The residual is orthogonal to `range Q`: `Qᴴ (I − QQᴴ) A = 0`. Atlas `projection-facts`.
atlas: projection-facts

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_self_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] {k : Type u_3}

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_self_apply
doc: `(Qᴴ Q)_ij = ⟨q_i, q_j⟩ = star q_i ⬝ q_j`. Helper for `arnoldi-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_self_of_orthonormalBasis.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  {ι : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (c : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 (EuclideanSpace 𝕜 m)) :

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_self_of_orthonormalBasis
doc:
The matrix whose columns are an orthonormal basis of `𝕜ᵐ`, indexed by any finite `ι`, has
orthonormal columns: `CᴴC = I`. Atlas `svd` (helper; belongs in a `Basic.lean`).

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_self_toEuclideanLin_symm.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (L : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ m) :

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_mul_self_toEuclideanLin_symm
doc:
A complex linear isometry has an isometric-column matrix in standard
Euclidean coordinates. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.1; complex CS helper.

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_rectDiag.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m n : ℕ} (σ : ℕ → ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.rectDiag σ).conjTranspose = NLAlib.rectDiag σ
name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_rectDiag
doc:
The conjugate transpose of a rectangular diagonal matrix (real diagonal) is rectangular
diagonal. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_rectDiag_mul_rectDiag.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m n : ℕ} (σ : ℕ → ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_rectDiag_mul_rectDiag
doc: `Σᴴ Σ` is diagonal with entries `σ_j²` for `j < m` and `0` beyond. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.conjTranspose_residual_mul_residual_eq_one_sub_overlap.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p : Type u_4} [Fintype p]
  [DecidableEq p] {P : Matrix m n 𝕜} {Q : Matrix m p 𝕜} (hP : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P)
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) :
  (NLAlib.projResidual P Q).conjTranspose * NLAlib.projResidual P Q =
    1 - (P.conjTranspose * Q).conjTranspose * (P.conjTranspose * Q)
name: NLAlib.conjTranspose_residual_mul_residual_eq_one_sub_overlap
doc:
The projection-residual Gram equals the identity minus the overlap Gram for frames with
orthonormal columns: `(projResidual P Q)ᴴ (projResidual P Q) = I − (PᴴQ)ᴴ(PᴴQ)`. The frame
widths may differ, and empty frames are allowed. Stewart–Sun 1990, §I.5 (Thm I.5.5).

signature:
NLAlib.contDiff_mul_of_tsupport_subset {n : WithTop ℕ∞} {η g : ℝ → ℝ} {U : Set ℝ} (hU : IsOpen U) (hη : ContDiff ℝ n η)

A multiplier smooth on an open neighborhood of the support preserves global
smoothness. This is the support-localization needed for the Gamma integrating factor.

Sine truncation preserves C1 smoothness. Source: Mathlib's

signature: NLAlib.continuousAt_Gamma_of_pos {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) : ContinuousAt Real.Gamma x

Real Gamma is continuous at every positive argument.
Source: Mathlib Gamma differentiability; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail`
(scalar endpoint helper).

The Fisher information is continuous at positive times on the C1
polynomial-growth domain. Source: two Gaussian dominated-convergence

At positive times, a continuous polynomial-growth function has a
continuous Mehler conditional expectation as a function of time.

Atlas: `ornstein-uhlenbeck`.

name: NLAlib.continuousOn_comp_joukowski_closed_annulus
doc:
A function holomorphic inside and continuous on the filled Bernstein ellipse pulls back
to a continuous function on the closed Joukowski annulus.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`, helper).

The Joukowski transform is continuous on the closed annulus of inner radius one.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`, helper).

from the proof-local helper of probabilistic Lieb.

signature:

The squared best-rank Frobenius error is continuous. This uses
only its value and does not require measurability of chosen singular vectors.
Atlas `eckart-young`, `rsvd-expected-error`.

The pullback of a function continuous on the filled Bernstein ellipse is continuous.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

Sorted signed eigenvalues of a symmetric affine pencil are continuous,
including at eigenvalue crossings. Bhatia 1997, Section III.4, Lidskii proof.

constant characteristic polynomial in dimension zero.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 6.3.12; simple-root persistence helper.

The Frobenius norm is continuous on finite matrix arrays.
Finite sums, products and the continuous square root; atlas `norm-lipschitz` (helper).

`GaussianMatrix.gordon_upper` (helper `gu_continuous_frobNorm`). Atlas: helper of `gordon`.

`G ↦ ⟨c, G⟩` is continuous. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.gordon_upper`
(helper `gu_continuous_lin`).

Matrix entries are continuous in the finite-dimensional operator topology.
Source: finite-dimensional linear maps; supports `haar-orthogonal`.

`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_lipschitz_entropy_bound`.

doc:
A fixed principal minor is continuous in its ambient matrix.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.8; immediate determinant continuity.

doc:
Each fixed-cardinality principal-minor product is continuous.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.8; immediate finite-product continuity.

signature:
NLAlib.cs_decomposition_properties.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {p : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype p] [Fintype q]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq p] [DecidableEq q] [DecidableEq n] (U : Matrix (p ⊕ q) (p ⊕ q) ℝ)
  (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) (hCard : Fintype.card p ≤ Fintype.card q) (P : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  (∃ e,
      have c := fun i => NLAlib.singularValues U.toBlocks₁₁ ↑((Fintype.equivFin p) i);
      (∀ (i : p), c i ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
        ∃ V₁ W₁ V₂ W₂,
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
            NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W₁ ∧
              NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧
                NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W₂ ∧
                  (Matrix.fromBlocks V₁ 0 0 V₂).transpose * U * Matrix.fromBlocks W₁ 0 0 W₂ =
                    NLAlib.csCanonicalMatrix c (Matrix.submatrix 1 id ⇑e)) ∧
    U.toBlocks₁₂.rank = U.toBlocks₂₁.rank ∧
      U.toBlocks₂₂.rank = U.toBlocks₁₁.rank + Fintype.card q - Fintype.card p ∧
        (∃ g ≤ min P.rank (Fintype.card n - P.rank),
            ∃ t,
              (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) ∧
                Antitone t ∧
                  (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < t i ↔ i < g) ∧
                    ∃ H,
                      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols H ∧
                        H * H.transpose = 1 ∧
                          H.transpose * P * H = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 (NLAlib.rectDiag t) 0 0 ∧
                            (∀ (i : ℕ), NLAlib.singularValues P i = if i < P.rank then √(1 + t i ^ 2) else 0) ∧
                              (∀ (i : ℕ), 1 < NLAlib.singularValues P i ↔ i < g) ∧
                                ∀ i < g, t i = √(NLAlib.singularValues P i ^ 2 - 1)) ∧
          (∀ (hr : 0 < P.rank),
              ∃ Q W,
                NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q ∧
                  NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W ∧
                    (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Q).range = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin P).range ∧
                      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin W).range = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin P).kerᗮ ∧
                        have θ := NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype W Q ⟨P.rank - 1, ⋯⟩;
                        (∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin P.rank))), NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype W Q i ≤ θ) ∧
                          θ < Real.pi / 2 ∧ NLAlib.specNorm P = 1 / Real.cos θ) ∧
            (0 < P.rank → P.rank < Fintype.card n → NLAlib.specNorm (1 - P) = NLAlib.specNorm P) ∧
              (P.rank = 0 → NLAlib.specNorm P = 0 ∧ NLAlib.specNorm (1 - P) = if Fintype.card n = 0 then 0 else 1) ∧
                (P.rank = Fintype.card n →
                  (NLAlib.specNorm P = if Fintype.card n = 0 then 0 else 1) ∧ NLAlib.specNorm (1 - P) = 0)
name: NLAlib.cs_decomposition_properties
doc:
The complete real CS and oblique-projection theorem. The CS factors have
one `p` and one `q` block on each side, with actual singular-value cosines and
literal coordinate inclusion. The oblique canonical coefficients have their
full actual singular-spectrum identities. The secant is asserted at positive
rank for the actual range and kernel-complement subspaces; complementary norm
equality requires proper positive rank and both rank endpoints are explicit.

derivations §alg:cs. Empty spaces and zero/pi/2 CS angles are included.

signature:
NLAlib.davis_kahan_bounds.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype k]
  [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq k] [DecidableEq r] {A E : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (hE : E.IsHermitian) {Q Qhat : Matrix n k ℝ} {R : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQhat : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qhat) (hR : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols R)
  (hcomp : Qhat * Qhat.transpose + R * R.transpose = 1) {L : Matrix k k ℝ} {M : Matrix r r ℝ} (hAQ : A * Q = Q * L)
  (hAR : (A + E) * R = R * M) :
  (∀ (a b δ : ℝ),
      0 < δ →
        (∀ (j : k), a ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues j ∧ ⋯.eigenvalues j ≤ b) →
          (∀ (i : r), ⋯.eigenvalues i ≤ a - δ ∨ b + δ ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues i) →
            NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles Q Qhat) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ∧
              NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (E * Q) / δ ∧
                NLAlib.specNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm E / δ ∧
                  NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles Q Qhat) ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ∧
                    NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ∧
                      NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm E / δ ∧
                        NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ √↑(Fintype.card k) * NLAlib.specNorm E / δ) ∧
    (∀ (j : ℕ) (hj0 : 0 < j) (hjN : j < Fintype.card n),
        0 < hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩ →
          have S := NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles (NLAlib.topEigenframe hA ⋯) (NLAlib.topEigenframe ⋯ ⋯);
          have δ := hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩;
          NLAlib.specNorm S ≤ NLAlib.specNorm E / δ ∧
            NLAlib.frobNorm S ≤ min (√↑j * NLAlib.specNorm E) (NLAlib.frobNorm E) / δ) ∧
      (∀ (j : ℕ) (hj0 : 0 < j) (hjN : j < Fintype.card n),
          0 < hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩ →
            have S := NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles (NLAlib.topEigenframe hA ⋯) (NLAlib.topEigenframe ⋯ ⋯);
            have g := hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩;
            NLAlib.specNorm S ≤ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / g ∧
              NLAlib.frobNorm S ≤ 2 * min (√↑j * NLAlib.specNorm E) (NLAlib.frobNorm E) / g) ∧
        ∀ (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ Fintype.card n),
          j = 0 ∨ j = Fintype.card n →
            NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles (NLAlib.topEigenframe hA hj) (NLAlib.topEigenframe ⋯ hj) = 0
name: NLAlib.davis_kahan_bounds
doc:
All requested Davis–Kahan bounds for invariant frames and sorted spectral subspaces. Davis–Kahan §6 and Yu–Wang–Samworth (2015),
Theorems 1–2. The generic interval theorem includes empty selected or
complementary frames and needs no endpoint-order assumption. The population
Frobenius minimum is unconditional and is proved by the finite trace deficit;
zero and full top-frame widths have zero sine matrices.
atlas: davis-kahan-sin-theta

signature:
NLAlib.davis_kahan_top_frame_bounds.{u_1, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n]
  [DecidableEq r] {A E : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hE : E.IsHermitian) {j : ℕ} (hj0 : 0 < j)
  (hjN : j < Fintype.card n) {Q Qhat : Matrix n (Fin j) ℝ} {R : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQhat : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qhat) (hR : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols R)
  (hcomp : Qhat * Qhat.transpose + R * R.transpose = 1) {L : Matrix (Fin j) (Fin j) ℝ} {M : Matrix r r ℝ}
  (hAQ : A * Q = Q * L) (hAR : (A + E) * R = R * M) (hmin : ∀ (t : Fin j), hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues t)
  (hmax : ∀ (t : r), ⋯.eigenvalues t ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩) :
  have S := NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles Q Qhat;
  have δ := hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩;
  have g := hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j - 1, ⋯⟩ - hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨j, hjN⟩;
  (0 < δ →
      NLAlib.specNorm S ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ∧
        NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm (E * Q) / δ ∧
          NLAlib.specNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm E / δ ∧
            NLAlib.frobNorm S ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ∧
              NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * E * Q) / δ ≤ NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ∧
                NLAlib.frobNorm (E * Q) / δ ≤ min (√↑j * NLAlib.specNorm E) (NLAlib.frobNorm E) / δ) ∧
    (0 < g → NLAlib.specNorm S ≤ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / g) ∧ (E = 0 → 0 < g → S = 0)
name: NLAlib.davis_kahan_top_frame_bounds
doc:
Supplied top invariant frames satisfy the exact mixed-gap residual
bounds and unconditional population spectral bound, including tied perturbed
choices and zero perturbations; Davis--Kahan, Section 6, and Yu--Wang--Samworth,
Theorem 2. The spectral hypotheses describe the selected/complementary cluster
and contain no angle or desired norm inequality.

signature:
NLAlib.definite_pair_congruence_characterizations.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
  (∃ S d,
      IsUnit S ∧
        A = S * S.transpose ∧
          B = S * Matrix.diagonal d * S.transpose ∧
            (A⁻¹ * B).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d i)) ∧
              spectrum ℝ (A⁻¹ * B) = Set.range d ∧
                NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable (A⁻¹ * B) ∧
                  NLAlib.inertiaPos (Matrix.diagonal d) = NLAlib.inertiaPos B ∧
                    NLAlib.inertiaNeg (Matrix.diagonal d) = NLAlib.inertiaNeg B ∧ (B.PosSemidef → ∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ d i)) ∧
    NLAlib.IsDiagonalizable (A * B) ∧ (B.PosSemidef → spectrum ℝ (A * B) ⊆ Set.Ici 0)
name: NLAlib.definite_pair_congruence_characterizations
doc:
The full definite-pair congruence clause gives the exact relative
eigenvalue list, its inertia and PSD signs, and real diagonalizability of
both relative and ordinary products. The general indefinite and PSD-pair
variants are separate parts of the atlas bundle.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.6.1 and Corollary 7.6.2.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence

signature:
NLAlib.deflatedTraceEstimate.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {r : Type u_2} [Fintype r]
  {κ : Type u_3} [Fintype κ] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (Q : Matrix n r ℝ) (Z : Matrix n κ ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.deflatedTraceEstimate
doc:
The deflated trace kernel with a supplied basis `Q` and Hutchinson test matrix `Z`:
`tr(QᵀAQ) + tr_m((I − QQᵀ)A(I − QQᵀ))`. Source: Meyer–Musco–Musco–Woodruff (2021) [`mmmw21`],
Alg. 1. Atlas: `hutchpp`, `hutchpp-unbiased`. `Q` is arbitrary here; unbiasedness requires orthonormality. The sketch-based
`hutchPlusPlusEstimate` below constructs its basis from `range (A S)`. An empty test family
has a zero residual average, leaving the compressed trace.

signature:
NLAlib.degree_le_and_abs_sub_chebyshev_approximations_le_of_open_ellipse {f : ℝ → ℝ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  (hmatch : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, F ↑x = ↑(f x)) (N : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc F N).degree ≤ ↑N ∧
    (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant F N).degree ≤ ↑N ∧
      ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1,
        |f x - Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc F N)| ≤ 2 * M / ρ ^ N / (ρ - 1) ∧
          |f x - Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant F N)| ≤ 4 * M / ρ ^ N / (ρ - 1)

doc:
Both canonical analytic Chebyshev approximations satisfy their exact source constants:
the coefficient truncation has error `2Mρ⁻ᴺ/(ρ-1)`, and the `(N+1)`-point grid
interpolant has error `4Mρ⁻ᴺ/(ρ-1)`. Both polynomials have degree at most `N`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 8.2; original open-ellipse assumptions, with the `N=0`
grid convention inherited explicitly from Mathlib's `node`.

**Residual polynomials of degree `≤ q`** are exactly the `1 − X s` with `deg s < q`:

(atlas `residual-polynomial`, helper).

  (hDen : ∀ (i j : n), x i + y j ≠ 0) :

    (Matrix.vandermonde (x ∘ ⇑(Fintype.equivFin n).symm)).det *
        (Matrix.vandermonde (y ∘ ⇑(Fintype.equivFin n).symm)).det /
      ∏ i, ∏ j, (x i + y j)
name: NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_eq_vandermonde_fintype
doc:
Cauchy's determinant formula on arbitrary finite labels, with the two
Vandermonde factors in the same finite coordinate ordering. The denominator
product is intrinsic. Empty labels and repeated parameters are included.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.
atlas: structured-matrices-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_pos_of_strictMono {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → ℝ) (hx : StrictMono x) (hy : StrictMono y)
  (hDen : ∀ (i j : Fin n), 0 < x i + y j) : 0 < (NLAlib.cauchyMatrix x y).det
name: NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_pos_of_strictMono
doc:
Ordered Cauchy parameters with positive denominators have positive
determinant, including the empty matrix. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.

signature:
NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_succ {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (hDen : ∀ (i j : Fin (n + 1)), x i + y j ≠ 0) :
  (NLAlib.cauchyMatrix x y).det =
    ((1 / (x 0 + y 0) * ∏ i, (x i.succ - x 0) / (x i.succ + y 0)) * ∏ j, (y j.succ - y 0) / (x 0 + y j.succ)) *
      (NLAlib.cauchyMatrix (fun i => x i.succ) fun j => y j.succ).det
name: NLAlib.det_cauchyMatrix_succ
doc:
One Schur elimination step gives the Cauchy determinant recurrence. The
only divisions are by the assumed nonzero denominators, so repeated x or y
values require no separate branch. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.

signature:

NLAlib.det_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_sum_norm_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {r : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype r]

The complex column-Gram determinant is the sum of squared absolute
values of all full-column minors. Too few rows, singular matrices and

Source: Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 0.8.1.

signature:
NLAlib.det_eq_iff_eq_of_posSemidef_le_posDef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}

on the larger matrix is essential. Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 7.7.4.

The determinant factors through the pivot: `det A = A₀₀ · det (pivotSchur A)` for a nonzero
pivot. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.2.10; Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.8.5.

signature:
NLAlib.det_eq_prod_diag_iff_isDiag_of_posDef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

Equality in positive definite Hadamard holds exactly for a diagonal
matrix. Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.8.1.

NLAlib.det_eq_prod_diag_iff_of_posSemidef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

PSD Hadamard equality holds exactly for a diagonal matrix or a zero
diagonal entry. The latter forces a zero row and column and both products
to vanish. Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.8.1; explicit singular equality
extension supporting the column-determinant bound.
atlas: hadamard-fischer-inequalities (partial)

The determinant of a triangular Cholesky factorization is the product of
the squared factor diagonals, including an empty product; no positivity of the diagonal is

Equality in Fischer's bound for a positive definite block matrix holds
exactly when its off-diagonal block is zero. Horn--Johnson (2013),

name: NLAlib.det_fromBlocks_le_mul_det_of_posSemidef
doc:
Fischer's determinant inequality for arbitrary PSD real blocks, including
singular and empty diagonal blocks. Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.8.5
and its semidefinite extension.
atlas: hadamard-fischer-inequalities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_fromCols_eq_mul_frobSq_sub_projector.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype k]

doc:
Appending one column multiplies the Gram determinant by its squared distance
from the existing column range. Source: manuscript `sa:volume-column`;
Deshpande--Rademacher--Vempala--Wang (2006), determinant-weighted projection identity.

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_fromCols_eq_mul_frobenius_norm_sq_sub_rangeProjector.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2}

doc:
Appending a genuine complex column multiplies its Gram determinant by
the squared Frobenius projection residual. Dependent starting columns and
empty shapes are included. Source: `sa:volume-column`.
atlas: volume-sampling (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_mul_eq_zero_of_det_gram_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} {k : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

A singular column Gram matrix stays singular after left multiplication.

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_mul_le_det_gram_mul_prod_sq_singularValues {m p k : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin p) ℝ)

A left image's Gram determinant is bounded by the original Gram determinant
times the product of the top squared singular values of the left multiplier.
Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 3.3.4, polar-compression step; singular inputs included.

doc:
The Gram determinant of the image of an orthonormal frame is bounded by the
product of the squared top singular values. Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 3.3.4,
compression-determinant step; all empty and rank deficient cases are included.

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_updateCol_eq_det_mul.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m]

doc:
The exact one-column Gram-volume exchange identity. Here `C t` is the
component in the selected column range and `d` is perpendicular to that range.
The inverse-Gram diagonal is the squared norm of the corresponding inverse
triangular-factor row in QR coordinates. No approximation or relaxed constant
is used. Gu–Eisenstat 1996, Theorem 3.2. Supports `rank-revealing-qr`.

Every Hilbert determinant is strictly positive, including the empty
determinant one. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.

NLAlib.det_inv_rpow_smul_eq_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)

definite matrix to determinant one. Positive dimension is essential.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.6; helper for determinant-root concavity.

Jacobi's inverse-minor formula in block coordinates: the determinant of
the complementary inverse block is the selected-block determinant divided
by the ambient determinant. The selected block can be singular and either
block can be empty. Horn–Johnson 2013, §§0.7.6 and 0.8.4.

signature:
NLAlib.det_inverse_complement_minor_eq_sign_mul_div.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3}

Jacobi's full inverse-minor identity for arbitrary ordered finite
coordinates. The first summand gives equal-sized selected row and column
sets; the second gives their complements. The sign is the relative
coordinate permutation sign, equal to the usual cofactor parity for the
increasing-coordinate convention. No selected minor is assumed invertible.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.8.4.
atlas: complementary-nullities (partial)

Determinant is monotone on the PSD cone. Horn--Johnson (2013),

Hadamard's inequality on the full PSD cone, with arbitrary finite

Cauchy–Binet for a square product of rectangular matrices, over every
commutative ring and arbitrary finite labels. All middle minors, including
empty and rank-deficient ones, are included. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.8.1.

Oppenheim's determinant lower bound for two PSD real matrices, including
singular and empty matrices and zero diagonal entries.

Similarity preserves the determinant polynomial `det(I+tG)` over any

signature:

Deleting one principal coordinate gives the determinant times the

signature:
NLAlib.det_principal_three_sets_eq_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)

        (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I) fun x => x ∈ I).det =
      (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I ∪ J) fun x => x ∈ I ∪ J).det *
        (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I ∪ K) fun x => x ∈ I ∪ K).det ↔
    ((A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ J) fun x => x ∈ K) -
        (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ J) fun x => x ∈ I) * (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I) fun x => x ∈ I)⁻¹ *
          A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I) fun x => x ∈ K) =
      0
name: NLAlib.det_principal_three_sets_eq_iff
doc:
Equality in the three-set overlapping determinant inequality holds exactly when the cross Schur block after eliminating the shared set vanishes. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.8.9.
atlas: hadamard-fischer-inequalities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_principal_three_sets_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)

  (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I ∪ (J ∪ K)) fun x => x ∈ I ∪ (J ∪ K)).det *
      (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I) fun x => x ∈ I).det ≤
    (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I ∪ J) fun x => x ∈ I ∪ J).det * (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ I ∪ K) fun x => x ∈ I ∪ K).det
name: NLAlib.det_principal_three_sets_le
doc:
Three pairwise disjoint principal index sets satisfy the overlapping determinant inequality. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.8.9.
atlas: hadamard-fischer-inequalities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_principal_union_eq_det_fromBlocks.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (s t : Finset n) (hst : Disjoint s t) :

    (Matrix.fromBlocks (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ s) fun x => x ∈ s) (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ s) fun x => x ∈ t)

name: NLAlib.det_principal_union_eq_det_fromBlocks
doc:
Splitting a principal set into two disjoint parts identifies its
determinant with the corresponding symmetric block determinant.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.8; helper for overlapping principal minors.

signature:
NLAlib.det_principal_union_mul_inter_eq_iff_of_posDef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosDef) (α β : Finset n) :

      (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ α) fun x => x ∈ α).det * (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ β) fun x => x ∈ β).det ↔
    ((A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ α \ β) fun x => x ∈ β \ α) -
        (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ α \ β) fun x => x ∈ α ∩ β) * (A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ α ∩ β) fun x => x ∈ α ∩ β)⁻¹ *
          A.toBlock (fun x => x ∈ α ∩ β) fun x => x ∈ β \ α) =
      0
name: NLAlib.det_principal_union_mul_inter_eq_iff_of_posDef
doc:
Equality in Koteljanski's inequality holds exactly when the cross block between `α \\ β` and `β \\ α`, after eliminating `α ∩ β`, vanishes. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.8.9.
atlas: hadamard-fischer-inequalities (partial)

signature:

doc:
**Koteljanski's inequality** for positive definite matrices: `det A[α ∪ β] · det A[α ∩ β] ≤ det A[α] · det A[β]`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.8.9.
atlas: hadamard-fischer-inequalities (partial)

signature:

doc:
Koteljanski's principal-minor inequality extends to all PSD matrices by
positive identity perturbation and determinant continuity. Its SPD equality

atlas: hadamard-fischer-inequalities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_rpow_inv_card_add_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)

signature:

NLAlib.det_rpow_mul_le_det_smul_add
doc:
**Multiplicative determinant Jensen inequality.** `det(A)^a det(B)^b ≤ det(aA + bB)` for positive definite `A`, `B` and `a + b = 1`, `a, b > 0`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.6.6.
atlas: log-det-concavity (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.det_scalar_block_eigenvalue_pencil_eq_schur.{u_1, u_2} {l : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Unique l] [Fintype n]

The scalar Schur function is the determinant factor in the separated
scalar/block eigenvalue pencil. Arbitrary finite trailing indices, including
empty blocks, are allowed. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 6.3.12; supports
`simple-eigenvalue-perturbation`.

name: NLAlib.det_smul_add_eq_rpow_mul_iff

Equality in the multiplicative determinant Jensen inequality holds exactly for `A = B`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.6.6.
atlas: log-det-concavity (partial)

name: NLAlib.det_smul_add_rpow_inv_card_eq_iff
doc:
Interior equality in determinant-root concavity is exactly positive
proportionality. The homogeneous statement allows arbitrary positive weights.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.6.10.

signature:
NLAlib.det_smul_one_sub_jacobiMatrix (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :

`det(x − J) = (x − a₀) det(x − J') − β₁² det(x − J'')` with `J'`, `J''` the trailing blocks
(shifted coefficients). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3.

signature:
NLAlib.det_smul_rpow_inv_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)

doc:
The positive-dimensional determinant root is homogeneous of degree one
under every nonnegative scalar, including scalar zero.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.6; helper for determinant-root concavity.

signature:

Two coordinate bijections change a determinant by their relative
permutation sign. This is the cofactor orientation convention for Jacobi's
identity. Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.8.4.

Cauchy–Binet for every selected minor of a rectangular product. Repeated

the product of the corresponding top eigenvalues. Poincaré separation,
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 4.3.37. The empty compression has determinant `1`.

minors, including the empty determinant and matrices with too few rows.

The Hermitian dilation of `A` is Hermitian, squares to `fromBlocks (A Aᴴ) 0 0 (Aᴴ A)`, and has
`λmax = ‖dilation A‖ = ‖A‖`.

Tropp 2015, Def. 2.1.5 and eqs (2.1.27–28). Atlas: `hermitian-dilation`. Ported from the Prove2me
mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype k]
  [Fintype k'] [DecidableEq k'] {𝕜 : Type u_4} [RCLike 𝕜] (Q : Matrix n k 𝕜) (X : Matrix n k' 𝕜) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap
doc:
The directed gap from the source subspace `range X` to the target subspace
`range Q`, represented by orthonormal frames: `‖(I − QQᴴ) X‖₂`. For arbitrary
blocks this definition is the residual norm. With orthonormal source and target
it lies in `[0, 1]` and depends only on their ranges. It is generally asymmetric
for unequal widths: a source contained in its target has gap zero, while the
reverse gap can be one. For equal widths it is the sine of the largest
principal angle (`directedSubspaceGap_eq_sin_principalAngles`).
Source: Stewart–Sun (1990), §I.5; Golub–Van Loan (2013), §2.5.3.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_comm.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {𝕜 : Type u_4} [RCLike 𝕜] {Q X : Matrix n k 𝕜} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hX : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols X) : NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q X = NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap X Q
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_comm
doc:
Equal-width orthonormal frames have symmetric directed gaps, equal to the
sine of their largest principal angle. This statement does not extend to
unequal-dimensional subspaces. Source: Stewart–Sun (1990), §I.5.

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_congr_right.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' = NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q''

doc:
The directed gap depends only on the source range `range Q'` among orthonormal frames: if `Q'`, `Q''` have
orthonormal columns and the same range then `‖(I − QQᵀ)Q'‖₂ = ‖(I − QQᵀ)Q''‖₂`. Proof:
`Q'' = Q' (Q'ᵀQ'')` with `‖Q'ᵀQ''‖₂ ≤ 1`, and symmetrically. Source: Stewart–Sun (1990)
[`ss90`], §I.5.

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_sin_principalAngles.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
`sin θ_max` is the sine of the largest principal angle: for frames `Q`, `Q'` of the same
positive width, `‖(I − QQᵀ)Q'‖₂ = sin θ_last`, `θ` the ordered principal angles
`principalAnglesFintype Q Q'`. (For unequal widths `0 < r' ≤ r` use
`directedSubspaceGap_eq_sqrt_one_sub_sq_singularValues`.) Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
§6.4.3; Stewart–Sun (1990) [`ss90`], Def I.5.3 and Thm I.5.5.

  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q X = NLAlib.specNorm (Qp.transpose * X)

doc:
With an orthonormal complement `Q⊥` (`Q⊥ᵀQ⊥ = I`, `QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`):
`sin θ_max = ‖Q⊥ᵀ X‖₂`. Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Thm 2.5.1; Stewart–Sun (1990)
[`ss90`], Thm I.5.5.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_sqrt_one_sub_sq_singularValues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {r r' : ℕ}
  {Q : Matrix n (Fin r) ℝ} {Q' : Matrix n (Fin r') ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q') (hr' : 0 < r') (hrr : r' ≤ r) :
  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' = √(1 - NLAlib.singularValues (Q.transpose * Q') (r' - 1) ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_eq_sqrt_one_sub_sq_singularValues
doc:
**Principal angles from the SVD.** For `Q : n × r`, `Q' : n × r'` with orthonormal columns and
`0 < r' ≤ r`: `sin θ_max = √(1 − σ_{r'−1}(QᵀQ')²)`, `σ` the zero-indexed singular values.
Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §6.4.3 and Thm 2.5.1; Stewart–Sun (1990) [`ss90`],
Def I.5.3. Proof: `specNorm_residual_sq_eq_one_sub_singularValues_last_sq` and
`σ_min(M) = σ_{r'−1}(M)` for `M : r × r'` with `r' ≤ r` (Courant–Fischer for `MᵀM`, the bridge
`singularValues` = `√` eigenvalues of `MᵀM`, `NLAlib.Matrix.Spectral.SVD`).

doc:
Containment of the source range in the target range makes the directed gap
zero. This permits different frame widths.

`range Z ⊆ range Y`, then `‖(I − QQᵀ)Z‖₂ ≤ ‖(I − QQᵀ)Y‖₂`, since `Z = Y (YᵀZ)` with

  NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' ≤ 1

doc:
The directed gap is at most one for `Q`, `Q'` with orthonormal columns. Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013)
[`gvl13`], §2.5.3. Atlas `principal-angles-def` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_lt_one_iff_isUnit.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

  (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q') : NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' < 1 ↔ IsUnit (Q.transpose * Q')
name: NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap_lt_one_iff_isUnit
doc:
**`QᵀQ'` is invertible iff `θ_max < π/2`.** For `Q`, `Q'` with orthonormal columns indexed by
the same `k`: `sin θ_max < 1 ↔ IsUnit (QᵀQ')`. Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
§2.5.3. Proof: by `specNorm_residual_sq_eq_one_sub_singularValues_last_sq` (`k` nonempty; the empty case
is trivial), `sin θ_max < 1 ↔ σ_min(QᵀQ') > 0 ↔` `QᵀQ'` injective `↔` invertible (square).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < 2 * ↑q) :
  b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b =
    Q.transpose.mulVec b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval (Q.transpose * A * Q)) p).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul
doc:
**Gauss (Lanczos) quadrature is exact for degree `< 2q`.** If `A` is symmetric, `Q` has
orthonormal columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, then for every polynomial `p` with
`deg p < 2q`, `bᵀ p(A) b = (Qᵀb)ᵀ p(QᵀAQ) (Qᵀb)`. Valid for every `q` (at `q = 0`, `p = 0`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6 and §7.1; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`],
Thm 2.1.
Deviation: any orthonormal `Q` whose range contains `K_q(A,b)`; with the Lanczos basis,
`Qᵀb = ‖b‖e₁` and the right side is `‖b‖² (p(T_q))₁₁`.

  ‖WithLp.toLp 2 ((cfc (fun x => Real.exp (-x)) A).mulVec v - NLAlib.krylovFunApprox A (fun x => Real.exp (-x)) v Q)‖ ^

    (2 * δ) ^ 2 * ‖WithLp.toLp 2 v‖ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_exp_neg_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le
doc:
**Lanczos-FA error for `exp(−x)`**: for a symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[0, b]` and
`q` above the approximation degree, `‖exp(−A) v − Q exp(−QᵀAQ) Qᵀ v‖² ≤ (2δ)² ‖v‖²`.
Source: Sachdeva–Vishnoi (2014) [`sv14`], Thm 4.1; Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4.
Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (exponential rate).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_inv_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le
doc:
**Lanczos-FA error for `f(x) = 1/x`** (the linear-system case): if `A` is symmetric with
every eigenvalue in `[a, c]`, `0 < a < c`, then
`‖A⁻¹ b − Q (QᵀAQ)⁻¹ Qᵀ b‖ ≤ 2 (2/a) ((√c − √a)/(√c + √a))^q ‖b‖` (squared form, with
`A⁻¹ = cfc (1/x) A`). Corollary of `dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le` and
`exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le` (atlas `inverse-polynomial-approx`).
Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8 (the rate).
atlas: lanczos-fa-error (partial)

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
Eigen-expansion of a quadratic form of a matrix function: for symmetric `A`,
`vᵀ f(A) v = ∑ᵢ f(λᵢ) (uᵢ ⬝ v)²` with `(λᵢ, uᵢ)` the eigenpairs of `A`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 7, eq. (7.1). Atlas: `spectral-measure`
(helper).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_self_eq_sum
doc:
Squared length after finite matrix functional calculus, in eigenbasis
coordinates. Parlett §4.5; bare functions are continuous on the finite spectrum.

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_self_le
doc:
**Spectral bound, `cfc` form.** If every eigenvalue of the symmetric `A` lies in `S` and
`|g| ≤ M` on `S`, then `‖g(A) v‖² ≤ M² ‖v‖²`. The `cfc` form of
`dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_self_le` (Saad 2003, §6.11). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper; the
`cfc` form of `polynomial-spectral-bound`).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le
doc:
**Lanczos-FA error bound.** Let `A` be symmetric with every eigenvalue in `[a, c]`, `Q` with
orthonormal columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, and `p` a polynomial with `deg p < q` and
`|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`. Then `‖f(A) b − Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b‖² ≤ (2E)² ‖b‖²`, i.e.
`‖f(A) b − Q f(T) Qᵀ b‖ ≤ 2E ‖b‖`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4 (with Lemma 3.1);
Druskin–Knizhnerman (1989) [`dk89`]; Higham (2008) [`higham08`], §13.2.
Deviation: an arbitrary approximant `p` in place of the best one (minimise over `p` to get the
printed form); squared norms; no `q ≥ 1` (at `q = 0`, `p = 0`).
atlas: lanczos-fa-error

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le_of_open_bernsteinEllipse
doc:
**Lanczos-FA error for an analytic function**: under the hypotheses of
`abs_dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_le_of_open_bernsteinEllipse`,
`‖f(A) v − Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ v‖² ≤ (4M ρ^{1−q}/(ρ − 1))² ‖v‖²`.
Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4; Trefethen (2019) [`atap`], Thm 8.2.
Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (analytic rate).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cgRecurrence_p_mulVec_eq_zero
doc:
SCAFFOLD: cg-recurrence
**Search directions are `A`-conjugate**: for `A ≻ 0`, `p_iᵀ A p_j = 0` for `i ≠ j`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (conjugacy of the search directions); Saad
(2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.20. Proof sketch: the joint induction of
`dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero` (the two invariants are proved together; for `j < k`,
`p_{k+1}ᵀ A p_j = r_{k+1}ᵀ A p_j + β_k p_kᵀ A p_j`, the first term is
`r_{k+1}ᵀ (r_j − r_{j+1}) / α_j = 0`, and for `j = k` the choice of `β_k` cancels the two terms).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero
doc:
SCAFFOLD: cg-recurrence
**Residuals are mutually orthogonal**: for `A ≻ 0`, `r_iᵀ r_j = 0` for `i ≠ j` (all `i, j`; after
the grade the residuals are `0`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1 (orthogonality
of the residuals); Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.19. Proof sketch: joint strong induction on
`k` for `∀ j < k, r_kᵀ r_j = 0 ∧ p_kᵀ A p_j = 0`, using `r_j ∈ span p_{≤j}` and
`p_j ∈ span r_{≤j}` (from the recurrence), the symmetry `uᵀ A v = vᵀ A u`, the identities
`r_kᵀ p_k = r_kᵀ r_k` and `p_kᵀ A p_k = r_kᵀ A p_k`, and `A p_j = (r_j − r_{j+1}) / α_j` when
`α_j ≠ 0`. Degenerate steps: `pᵀAp = 0 → p = 0` (`Matrix.PosDef.dotProduct_mulVec_pos`) and then
`r = 0` (from `r_kᵀ p_k = r_kᵀ r_k`), after which the state freezes
(`cgRecurrence_add_of_r_eq_zero`). Deferred: a long case analysis, not hard mathematics.

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero_of_mem
doc:
**Galerkin orthogonality of the recursion**: for `A ≻ 0`, `r_k ⟂ K_k(A, r₀)`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1; Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.19.
Proof: `K_k = span r_{<k}` (`span_cgRecurrence_r`) and `r_k ⟂ r_j` for `j < k`
(`dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero`). Helper for `cg-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_complement_eigenvalueProjector_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (ℓ : ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  (1 - NLAlib.eigenvalueProjector hA ℓ).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (1 - NLAlib.eigenvalueProjector hA ℓ).mulVec x =
    ∑ i, if hA.eigenvalues i = ℓ then 0 else ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ x) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_complement_eigenvalueProjector_eq_sum
doc:
The complementary eigenspace projector retains precisely the squared
coordinates outside the target eigenvalue. Parlett §11.7.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_eq_mul_dotProduct_of_forall_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {u v w : n → ℝ} {L : ℝ} (hu : A.mulVec u = L • u) {g : ℝ → ℝ}

  u ⬝ᵥ w = g L * u ⬝ᵥ v
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_eq_mul_dotProduct_of_forall_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eq
doc:
**A spectral multiplier commutes with an eigenvector**: if `uᵢ ⬝ w = g(λᵢ)(uᵢ ⬝ v)` for
every `i` (e.g. `w = g(A) v`) and `A u = L u`, then `u ⬝ w = g(L)(u ⬝ v)`. Helper for
`krylov-eigenvector-angle`, `power-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_eq_sum_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (v w : n → ℝ) :
  v ⬝ᵥ w = ∑ i, (hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v * (hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ w
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_eq_sum_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_mul
doc: Parseval for a pair: `v ⬝ w = ∑ᵢ (uᵢ ⬝ v)(uᵢ ⬝ w)`. Helper.

Left and right eigenvectors at different eigenvalues are biorthogonal.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Observation 1.4.6a; `y` denotes the left row,
which may be `star y₀` for a complex column eigenvector `y₀`.
atlas: left-right-eigenvectors

signature:

  [DecidableEq n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K] {A : Matrix n n K} {y z : n → K} {α μ : K} (hy : Matrix.vecMul y A = α • y)

A left eigenvector annihilates every generalized eigenspace at a
different eigenvalue. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), proof of Lemma 1.4.11;
the proof works over any field.
atlas: left-right-eigenvectors (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_fromBlocks_eq_generalizedSchurComplement_square.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m m 𝕜) (B : Matrix m n 𝕜) (C : Matrix n n 𝕜)

    star (y + (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec (B.mulVec x)) ⬝ᵥ
        A.mulVec (y + (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec (B.mulVec x)) +
      star x ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.generalizedSchurComplement A B C).mulVec x

doc:
**Square completion** with the Moore–Penrose inverse: for Hermitian `A` with
`A A⁺ B = B`,
`(y, x)ᴴ M (y, x) = (y + A⁺Bx)ᴴ A (y + A⁺Bx) + xᴴ (M / A) x`. Albert 1969, Theorem 1; supports
`generalized-schur-complement-psd`.

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_generalizedSchurComplement_mulVec_eq
doc:
**Variational characterisation, attainment**: for `M = [[A, B], [Bᴴ, C]] ⪰ 0` the minimum
over `y` of `(y, x)ᴴ M (y, x)` is attained at `y = −A⁺Bx` and equals `xᴴ (M / A) x`.
Albert 1969, Thm 1; cf. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.7.
Proof: the square completion `dotProduct_fromBlocks_eq_generalizedSchurComplement_square` with
`y + A⁺Bx = 0`.
atlas: generalized-schur-complement-psd (partial)

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_generalizedSchurComplement_mulVec_le
doc:
**Variational characterisation, lower bound**: for `M = [[A, B], [Bᴴ, C]] ⪰ 0`,
`xᴴ (M / A) x ≤ (y, x)ᴴ M (y, x)` for every `y`. Albert 1969, Thm 1; cf. Horn–Johnson 2013,
§7.7. The lower-bound half of `isLeast_generalizedSchurComplement_quadratic`.
atlas: generalized-schur-complement-psd (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_golubKahan_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {k : ℕ} (h : NLAlib.GolubKahanSucceeds A b k) :
  (∀ j ≤ k,
      (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b j).u ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b j).v =
        (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b j).alpha) ∧
    ∀ j < k,
      (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b (j + 1)).u ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b j).v =
        (NLAlib.golubKahanRecurrence A b (j + 1)).beta
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_golubKahan_eq
doc:
SCAFFOLD: golub-kahan-bidiagonalization
**The entries of `B` are the recursion's `α, β`.** Without breakdown through state `k`:
`u_{j+1}ᵀ A v_{j+1} = α_{j+1}` for `j ≤ k` and `u_{j+2}ᵀ A v_{j+1} = β_{j+2}` for `j < k`, so the
`B` of the realised decomposition has diagonal `α` and subdiagonal `β` (all positive). Source:
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Alg. 10.4.1 and eq. (10.4.4). Proof sketch: from the
recursion, `Aᵀu_{j+1} = α_{j+1}v_{j+1} + β_{j+1}v_j` and
`Av_{j+1} = α_{j+1}u_{j+1} + β_{j+2}u_{j+2}`, then orthonormality
(`isGradedKrylovBasis_golubKahanU_V`). Difficulty 2 given the realisation.
atlas: golub-kahan-recurrence

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_moorePenroseInverse_mul_mulVec_le_dotProduct_self.{u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (M : Matrix m n ℝ) (d : n → ℝ) : d ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse M * M).mulVec d ≤ d ⬝ᵥ d
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_moorePenroseInverse_mul_mulVec_le_dotProduct_self
doc:
The Moore–Penrose row projector is a contraction in the quadratic-form sense:
`dᵀ (M⁺M) d ≤ dᵀd`. Horn–Johnson §7.3; helper for `sketch-and-project`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_eq_of_apply_eq_zero.{u_2} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] (M : Matrix k k ℝ)

doc:
A quadratic form at a vector supported on one index: `c ⬝ M c = c_{i₀}² M_{i₀ i₀}`.
Helper for `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_eigenvalues₀_zero_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hcard : 0 < Fintype.card n) (x : n → ℝ) : x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x ≤ hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨0, hcard⟩ * x ⬝ᵥ x
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_eigenvalues₀_zero_mul
doc:
A symmetric quadratic form is bounded above by its largest eigenvalue.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.2.2; supports signed eigenvalue perturbation.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_mul_dotProduct_of_eigenvalues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {c : ℝ} (hc : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ≤ c) (x : n → ℝ) :
  x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x ≤ c * x ⬝ᵥ x
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_mul_dotProduct_of_eigenvalues
doc:
Upper Rayleigh bound from an eigenvalue enclosure: `xᵀ A x ≤ c ‖x‖²` if every eigenvalue is
at most `c`. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Thm 4.2.2. Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`
(helper).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_of_mem_range
doc:
Rayleigh quotients over `range Q` are bounded by any upper bound `θ` on the eigenvalues of
`QᵀAQ` (the Ritz values), for `Q` with orthonormal columns: `yᵀAy ≤ θ ‖y‖²` for `y ∈ range Q`.
Source: Parlett (1998), Thm 11.4.1 (Rayleigh–Ritz). Atlas: `ritz-value-bounds` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_pow_le_dotProduct_pow_mulVec.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m]
  {M : Matrix m m ℝ} (hM : M.PosSemidef) {y : m → ℝ} (hy : y ⬝ᵥ y ≤ 1) {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) :
  (y ⬝ᵥ M.mulVec y) ^ s ≤ y ⬝ᵥ (M ^ s).mulVec y
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_pow_le_dotProduct_pow_mulVec
doc:
**Jensen for a positive semidefinite quadratic form.** For `M ⪰ 0`, a vector `y` with
`y ⬝ y ≤ 1` and `s ≥ 1`, `(yᵀMy)^s ≤ yᵀM^s y`. With `y = Σᵢ cᵢuᵢ` in an eigenbasis this is
`(Σᵢ cᵢ²λᵢ)^s ≤ Σᵢ cᵢ²λᵢ^s`, convexity of `t ↦ t^s` on `t ≥ 0` with total weight `Σᵢ cᵢ² ≤ 1`.
HMT 2011, proof of Prop 8.6. Atlas `power-iteration-deterministic` (helper; belongs in
`Matrix/PolynomialCalculus.lean`).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2}
  [Fintype m] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {σlo σhi : ℝ} (hlo : 0 < σlo) (hlohi : σlo ≤ σhi)
  (hlow : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σlo ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v)
  (hup : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v ≤ σhi ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v) {b : m → ℝ} {x₀ xs x : n → ℝ}
  (hxs : A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec xs) = A.transpose.mulVec b) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate A b x₀ q x) :
  A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs) ≤
    (2 * ((σhi - σlo) / (σhi + σlo)) ^ q) ^ 2 * A.mulVec (x₀ - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate
doc:
**CGLS/LSQR convergence, `κ(A)` rate.** Let `A : ℝ^{m×n}` have all singular values in
`[σ_lo, σ_hi]`, `0 < σ_lo ≤ σ_hi`, stated as `σ_lo² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖² ≤ σ_hi² ‖v‖²` for all `v` (so `A`
has full column rank), let `x⋆` solve the normal equations `AᵀA x⋆ = Aᵀb`, and `x` be a `q`-th
CGLS iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖A(x − x⋆)‖² ≤ (2((σ_hi − σ_lo)/(σ_hi + σ_lo))^q)² ‖A(x₀ − x⋆)‖²`.
Proof: CG on `AᵀA` with spectrum in `[σ_lo², σ_hi²]` (`quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate`).

Deviation: squared norms; the singular-value hypothesis in Rayleigh form.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_chebyshevIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

`0 < a < b`, `‖c − A x_q‖² ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖r₀‖²`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3. Deviation: squared norms.
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_polyIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

    M ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_polyIterate_le
doc:
**Residual bound for a polynomial method.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `S` and
`|1 − x s(x)| ≤ M` on `S`, `‖c − A x‖² ≤ M² ‖r₀‖²`. No solution is needed.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_richardsonIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b ω : ℝ} (hω : 0 ≤ ω) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)

**Richardson contraction, residual norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]` and

atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:

Pythagoras separates the optimal Rayleigh residual and the shift error.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_shifted_residual_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_le_of_isCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2}
  [Fintype m] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {σlo σhi : ℝ} (hlo : 0 < σlo) (hlohi : σlo ≤ σhi)

  (hup : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v ≤ σhi ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v) {b : m → ℝ} {x₀ xs x : n → ℝ}

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

doc:
The least-squares objective is twice the CG objective of the normal equations plus a
constant: `‖b − Ay‖² = 2 φ_{AᵀA, Aᵀb}(y) + ‖b‖²`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3.
Helper for `cgls-lsqr-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq_add.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec xs) = A.transpose.mulVec b)

`AᵀA x⋆ = Aᵀb`, then `‖b − Ax‖² = ‖b − Ax⋆‖² + ‖A(x − x⋆)‖²` for every `x`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 11.1.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound (partial)

Interval/complement containment implies the pairwise separation used

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_eq_dotProduct_mulVec
doc:
An eigenvalue is the Rayleigh quotient of its unit eigenvector: `λᵢ = uᵢᵀ A uᵢ`.
Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper).

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_le_mul_overlapTangentSq
doc:
**Rayleigh–Ritz step of Kaniel–Paige–Saad.** Let `A` be real symmetric with every
eigenvalue `≥ a`, `u` a unit eigenvector for the eigenvalue `λ` at sorted position `i₀`, `Q`
with orthonormal columns, `θ₁ = θ_{j₁}` the largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`, and `x ∈ range Q`
with `u ⬝ x ≠ 0`. Then `λ − θ₁ ≤ (λ − a) tan² ∠(u, x)` (from
`λ − xᵀAx/xᵀx ≤ (λ − a) sin² ∠(u, x)`). Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], proof of Thm 6.4.
Helper for `kaniel-paige-saad`.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] [Nonempty n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {u : n → ℝ}
  (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 • u) (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c)
  (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues₀ 0) (hspec : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ 0 → hA.eigenvalues₀ i ∈ Set.Icc a c)
  {b : n → ℝ} (hb : u ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0) (q : ℕ) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1) ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {j₁ : k}
  (hj₁ : ∀ (j : k), ⋯.eigenvalues j ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues j₁) :
  hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - ⋯.eigenvalues j₁ ≤
    (hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - a) *
      (NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u b /
        Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues₀ 0 - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le
doc:
**Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound for the largest Ritz value.** Let `A` be real symmetric with top
eigenvalue `λ₁ = λ₀(A)` and unit eigenvector `u`, every other eigenvalue (sorted position `≠ 0`)
in `[a, c]` with `a < c < λ₁` (e.g. `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`), `u ⬝ b ≠ 0`, `Q` with orthonormal
columns and `K_{q+1}(A, b) ⊆ range Q` (e.g. a Lanczos basis after `q` matvecs), and `θ₁` the
largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`. Then
`λ₁ − θ₁ ≤ (λ₁ − a) tan² ∠(u, b) / T_q(1 + 2γ)²`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`; the lower bound
`0 ≤ λ₁ − θ₁` is `eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 6.4 (`i = 1`); Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4.
Deviation: Krylov dimension `q + 1` (Saad's `m`, so `T_{m−1} = T_q`); `[a, c]` any enclosure
of the other eigenvalues (Saad: `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`, factor `λ₁ − λₙ`); any orthonormal `Q`
whose range contains the Krylov space.
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le_of_poly
doc:
**Kaniel–Paige–Saad, polynomial form.** Let `A` be real symmetric with every eigenvalue
`≥ a`, `u` a unit eigenvector for the eigenvalue `λ` at sorted position `i₀`, `u ⬝ b ≠ 0`, `Q`
with orthonormal columns and `K_q(A, b) ⊆ range Q`, and `θ₁` the largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`.
For every polynomial `p` with `deg p < q`, `p(λ) ≠ 0` and `|p| ≤ M` at every other sorted
position: `λ − θ₁ ≤ (λ − a) (M/p(λ))² tan² ∠(u, b)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], proof of Thm 6.4 (`i = 1`).
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad (partial)

signature:

Eigen-coordinates of an eigenvector: `(λᵢ − L)(uᵢ ⬝ u) = 0` when `A u = L u`. Helper for
