name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le
doc:
The Ritz values are at most the top eigenvalue: `θⱼ ≤ λ₀(A)` for every eigenvalue `θⱼ` of
`Qᵀ A Q`, `Q` with orthonormal columns. This is the lower half `0 ≤ λ₁ − θ₁` of the
Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 6.4 (left inequality; Cauchy
interlacing).
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad (partial)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_mem_Icc
doc:
The eigenvalues of the compression `Qᵀ A Q` (`Q` with orthonormal columns) lie in any
interval `[a, c]` containing the eigenvalues of `A` (the Ritz values stay inside the spectral
interval). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4; Parlett (1998), Thm 10.1.1 (weak form).
Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper; Matrix-level, to move to `Matrix/Basic/QuadForm`).

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le_add_eigenvalues₀_zero
doc:
Weyl's signed eigenvalue perturbation bound, upper side.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.3.1. Indices are decreasing and zero-indexed.
atlas: eigenvalue-perturbation-symmetric

doc:
The eigenvector basis is orthonormal in dot-product form: `uᵢ ⬝ uⱼ = δᵢⱼ`.
Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`.

doc:
The resolvent shares the eigenvectors of `A`: if `μ` is not an eigenvalue,
`uᵢ ⬝ ((A − μI)⁻¹ v) = (λᵢ − μ)⁻¹ (uᵢ ⬝ v)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 27.
Helper for `inverse-iteration`.

name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_mul_eq
doc:
For an eigenvector `u` with `A u = L u`, `uᵢ ⬝ u` vanishes unless `λᵢ = L`, so any `g` acts
as `g(L)` on these coordinates: `(uᵢ ⬝ u) g(λᵢ) = (uᵢ ⬝ u) g(L)`. Helper.

name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_pow_mulVec_eq

Eigen-coordinates of powers of a spectral multiplier: if `uᵢ ⬝ (B y) = fᵢ (uᵢ ⬝ y)` for all
`y`, then `uᵢ ⬝ (B^k v) = fᵢ^k (uᵢ ⬝ v)`. Helper for `power-iteration`, `inverse-iteration`.

name: NLAlib.eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_sub_smul_mulVec
doc:
The shifted matrix in eigen-coordinates: `uᵢ ⬝ ((A − μI) y) = (λᵢ − μ)(uᵢ ⬝ y)`. Helper for
`inverse-iteration`.

signature:

onto its `i`-th eigenvector `uᵢ`, where `U = hA.eigenvectorUnitary` is Mathlib's chosen

basis-free object is the eigenspace projector `eigenspaceProjector hA ℓ` of

signature:
NLAlib.eq_eigenvectorUnitary_kronecker_mul_diagonal_mul_transpose.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
  Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) A B =
    (Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) ↑hA.eigenvectorUnitary ↑hB.eigenvectorUnitary *
        Matrix.diagonal fun ij => hA.eigenvalues ij.1 * hB.eigenvalues ij.2) *
      (Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) ↑hA.eigenvectorUnitary ↑hB.eigenvectorUnitary).transpose

doc:

Kronecker product with the pairwise eigenvalue products. Horn–Johnson 1991,
Theorem 4.2.12; the middle diagonal is not asserted to be sorted.

signature:
NLAlib.eq_eigenvectorUnitary_mul_diagonal_mul_transpose.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

Real spectral theorem in transpose form: `A = U diag(λ) Uᵀ` with `U = hA.eigenvectorUnitary`
and `λ = hA.eigenvalues`. Real specialisation of Mathlib's `Matrix.IsHermitian.spectral_theorem`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 4.1.5). Atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound` (helper).

**Finite termination of CG.** For positive definite `A` with `A x⋆ = c`, once `q` reaches the
grade `ν(A, r₀)` of the initial projResidual, every `q`-th CG iterate is the solution `x⋆`. The

minimiser is `0`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.3 and §6.7; Trefethen–Bau (1997)

Horn–Johnson (2013), §5.6; empty shapes are included.

eigenspace is already its ordinary eigenspace. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),

norms of all powers. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §5.6; the proof takes a
finite maximum over a basis and uses its explicit coordinate norm bound.

signature:

Lipschitz constant. They converge pointwise and satisfy `|fₙ|≤|f|+1`, so once `f` is

mollification. Ledoux 2001, proof of Theorem 5.3; atlas `herbst` (approximation helper).

signature:

doc:
A rank-one update along a nonzero right eigenvector replaces exactly one
occurrence of the eigenvalue: the unchanged polynomial factor is shared by
the old and updated characteristic polynomials. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),
Exercise 1.2.8 and Theorem 2.4.10.1. Over the complex field take `y = star v`
for the update `x v*`. Repeated eigenvalues and zero shifts are included;
the quotient is polynomial division, with no pointwise division at `μ`.
atlas: rank-one-eigenvalue-update

doc:
Circulants are exactly the ordinary Toeplitz matrices commuting with the
cyclic shift. Commutation alone already forces the circulant formula.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.7.
atlas: structured-matrices-def

Every commuting family on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space
over an algebraically closed field has a common nonzero eigenvector.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Lemma 1.3.19; arbitrary, infinite and empty
families are allowed.

specified nonzero eigenspace of one designated member. The family may be
infinite, and the eigenvalue may have any multiplicity. Horn–Johnson 2013,
Theorem 2.3.3; the prescribed-order strengthening in derivations gen:simultaneous.

doc:
An arbitrary commuting family of nonempty complex square matrices has
a common nonzero eigenvector. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Lemma 1.3.19;
infinite and empty families are allowed.
atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization

signature:

by four complex unitary factors of sizes `p,p,q,q`. The cosines are its
upper-left block's actual singular values; the right side is the complexified
real canonical CS matrix with the specified coordinate inclusion. Empty blocks
and zero/pi/2 angles are included. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.7.1.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

its actual range and kernel orthogonal complement. Their largest actual
principal angle is strictly below pi/2 and its secant is exactly the
Euclidean operator norm. Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; the identity
at positive dimension is included, and rank zero is excluded precisely
because it has no largest principal angle.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

The locally unique scalar Schur branch is continuous throughout a

Evaluating the finite first-kind expansion gives a finite cosine series.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_cs_decomposition.{u_1, u_2} {p : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} [Fintype p] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq p]

embedding's orthogonal complement. Coordinate inclusion gives the ordinary

atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

The full CS factorization with a literal coordinate inclusion into the

atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

the identity and a real diagonal, in factor form. The diagonal entries are
nonnegative whenever the second matrix is PSD.

atlas: simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence (partial)

Monomial approximation in the existential polynomial interface used by Krylov proofs.

The required sharp Jackson theorem on the unit interval: a degree-`n` algebraic
polynomial approximates every `L`-Lipschitz function with error at most `πL/(2(n+1))`.
Source: Arnold, *Numerical Analysis* lecture notes, §1.2 (Jackson's theorem).
Atlas `jackson-lipschitz` (unit-interval form).

        ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c,
          |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ 1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((L - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)

`p` of degree at most `q` with `p(L) = 1` and `|p| ≤ 1/T_q(1 + 2γ)` on `[a, c]`,
`γ = (L − c)/(c − a)`: namely `p(x) = T_q((2x − c − a)/(c − a))/T_q(1 + 2γ)`, the
`chebyshevAmplifier` with `α = (c − a)/2`, `γ' = 2γ`, shifted by `(c + a)/2`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1. Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle` (belongs in
`NLAlib.Polynomial.FunctionApproximation.Approximation` next to `chebyshev-amplifier`).

doc:
Polynomial approximation of `1/x` on `[a, b]`: for `0 < a < b` there is a polynomial `p` of
degree `< q` with `|p(x) − 1/x| ≤ (2/a)((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q` on `[a, b]`. The polynomial is
`p = (1 − r)/X` for the Chebyshev residual `r = chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8 (the CG error bound). Atlas:
`inverse-polynomial-approx`.
atlas: inverse-polynomial-approx

signature:

`x₀ + s(A) r₀ ∈ x₀ + K_q` has error `p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11
(the set `P_q^0`); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35. Promoted from the private CG lemma
`exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul` (atlas `residual-polynomial`, helper).

value `θ_j` (eigenvalue of `QᵀAQ`) satisfies
`λ₁ − θ_j ≤ ε λ₁ + λ₁ (2/(1 + √(2γ)))^{2q} ‖b‖²/(u ⬝ b)²`, `γ = ε/(1 − ε)`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Thm 1 (single-vector, gap-free); Kuczyński–Woźniakowski
(1992) [`kw92`] for the random-start analysis. The gap-dependent bound of Saad (2011), Thm 6.4,
is `eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le` (`kaniel-paige-saad`).
Deviation: `K_{q+1}` and the exponent `q` (the source counts the Krylov dimension).
atlas: ritz-value-bounds

Every congruence eigenvalue has a scaling factor in the closed interval
between squared extreme singular values, including singular transformations.

atlas: ostrowski-congruence-eigenvalues (partial)

signature:

Each eigenvalue of a real diagonal matrix is a diagonal entry.
Mathlib's diagonal spectrum theorem; supports spectral interval bounds.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_eq_mul_of_range_le.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {n : Type u_1} {a : Type u_4} {b : Type u_5} [Fintype a] [Fintype b]

If `range Y ⊆ range X` then `Y = X R` for some `R`. Helper for `principal-angles-def`

signature:
NLAlib.exists_eq_mul_transpose_of_posSemidef.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

finite index is `L Lᵀ` with `L` lower triangular with nonnegative diagonal (not unique in
general; on `Fin n` the witness is `cholesky A`, `eq_cholesky_mul_transpose_of_posSemidef`).
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.8; Higham 2002, Thm 10.9.
atlas: cholesky-decomposition

signature:

A lower-triangular factorization `A = L Lᵀ` transports along an order isomorphism of the
index type (with any predicate `P` on the diagonal).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_eq_transpose_mul_of_posSemidef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) : ∃ F, A = F.transpose * F

A real positive semidefinite matrix is a Gram matrix: `A = FᵀF` for some square `F`.
Mathlib `CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self`. Atlas `nystrom-structural`,
`partial-cholesky-nystrom` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_equiv_sum_extending_embedding.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {p : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype p]

Complete an embedding of finite types to an equivalence from a disjoint
sum, preserving every prescribed first-summand coordinate. The cardinality
identity supplies exactly the number of remaining coordinates.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_finset_net_specNorm_le.{u_3, u_4} (n : Type u_3) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε)
  (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  ∃ N,
    (∀ x ∈ N, x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) ∧
      ↑N.card ≤ (1 + 2 / ε) ^ Fintype.card n ∧
        ∀ (m : Type u_4) [inst : Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (M : ℝ),
          0 ≤ M → (∀ x ∈ N, √(A.mulVec x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x) ≤ M) → NLAlib.specNorm A ≤ M / (1 - ε)
name: NLAlib.exists_finset_net_specNorm_le
doc:
**ε-net bound for the spectral norm.** For `0 < ε < 1` there is a set `N` of at most
`(1 + 2/ε)^{card n}` unit vectors of `ℝ^n` such that for every real matrix `A` with `n` columns
and every `M ≥ 0`, `‖Ax‖₂ ≤ M` on `N` implies `‖A‖₂ ≤ M/(1-ε)`.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.2–5.3; Vershynin 2018, Cor 4.2.13 and Ex 4.4.3.
Atlas `epsilon-net-norm`. Deviation: the atlas states `(1-2ε)⁻¹`; the standard (and stronger)
operator form `(1-ε)⁻¹` is used here, the `(1-2ε)⁻¹` forms being
`specNorm_le_div_of_net_bilinear` and `specNorm_le_div_of_net_quadForm`.
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

signature:
NLAlib.exists_finset_sphere_net.{u_3} (ι : Type u_3) [Fintype ι] {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ N,
    (∀ x ∈ N, x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) ∧
      ↑N.card ≤ (1 + 2 / ε) ^ Fintype.card ι ∧ ∀ (y : ι → ℝ), y ⬝ᵥ y = 1 → ∃ x ∈ N, (x - y) ⬝ᵥ (x - y) ≤ ε ^ 2
name: NLAlib.exists_finset_sphere_net
doc:
**Volumetric ε-net of the sphere.** For `ε > 0`, the unit sphere of `ℝ^ι` (Euclidean) has an
`ε`-net contained in the sphere with at most `(1 + 2/ε)^{card ι}` points:
`∀ y` with `yᵀy = 1`, `∃ x ∈ N`, `(x - y)ᵀ(x - y) ≤ ε²`. For an empty index type the sphere is
empty and `N = ∅`. Proof: a maximal `ε`-separated subset of the sphere is an `ε`-net, and the
volumetric packing bound caps the size of every separated subset.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.2; Vershynin 2018, Cor 4.2.13. Atlas `epsilon-net-norm`
(covering half). Deviation: index type any `[Fintype ι]` (audit: `Fin n`).
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

name: NLAlib.exists_frame_projector_of_isHermitian_of_isIdempotentElem
doc:
An orthogonal projector (Hermitian idempotent) is the frame projector `QQᴴ` of an orthonormal
basis `Q` of its range; the frame has exactly `rank P` columns. Stewart–Sun 1990, §I.5.

signature:

doc:
For standard finite coordinates, full QR has its nonnegative
upper-triangular factor in the first rows and zero rows below that corner.
The ambient factor is orthogonal. Trefethen--Bau, Theorem 7.1;
Golub--Van Loan, Theorem 5.2.1.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:

doc:
Every thin QR extends to a full QR with the same triangular
factor in the specified coordinate corner and zero rows outside it. The
orthogonal completion agrees with the supplied frame in its chosen columns.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_full_qr_of_embedding.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

Full QR over arbitrary finite indices with the triangular corner located
by a specified column embedding. All rows outside the corner vanish, so this

signature:
NLAlib.exists_gamma_weighted_antitone_density_of_weak_inequality (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] (m : ℝ)
  (hweak :
    ∀ (ψ : ℝ → ℝ),
      ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) ψ →
        HasCompactSupport ψ →
          tsupport ψ ⊆ Set.Ioi 0 →
            (∀ (x : ℝ), 0 ≤ ψ x) → 0 ≤ ∫ (x : ℝ) in Set.Ioi 0, 4 * x * deriv ψ x + 2 * (m - x) * ψ x ∂μ) :
  ∃ h,
    Measurable h ∧
      AntitoneOn h (Set.Ioi 0) ∧
        (∀ x ∈ Set.Ioi 0, 0 ≤ h x) ∧
          μ.restrict (Set.Ioi 0) =

              ENNReal.ofReal (x ^ (m / 2 - 1) * Real.exp (-x / 2) * h x)

doc:
The weak scalar Wishart inequality produces a Gamma-weighted density
with a nonnegative antitone measurable factor. No density premise is assumed.
The original finite measure may have an atom at zero, which is removed by the
explicit restriction to the positive half-line.
Source: Edelman 1988; atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (helper).
atlas: gamma-weighted-antitone-density

signature:
NLAlib.exists_hasOrthonormalCols_of_card_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (hCard : Fintype.card n ≤ Fintype.card m) : ∃ J, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols J
name: NLAlib.exists_hasOrthonormalCols_of_card_le
doc:
An orthonormal coordinate frame exists whenever the column dimension does
not exceed the row dimension. Supports `qr-decomposition`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iInf_norm_mulVec_le_of_singularValues_last_le.{u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (s : ℝ)
  (hs : NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card n - 1) ≤ s) :
  ∃ j, ⨅ x, ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (A.mulVec ↑x)‖ ≤ √↑(Fintype.card n) * s
name: NLAlib.exists_iInf_norm_mulVec_le_of_singularValues_last_le
doc:
**Small `σ_min` forces a column close to the span of the others.** For `A : Matrix m n ℝ`
with `n` nonempty, if `σ_min(A) ≤ s` then for some column `j`,
`inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 } ≤ √|n| · s`; the left side is the distance from column `j` to the
span of the other columns. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Rudelson–Vershynin 2008,
Lemma 3.5 (the "invertibility via distance" step).
atlas: smin-small-ball

signature:
NLAlib.exists_idempotent_complement_norm_factor.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (P : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  ∃ a,
    1 ≤ a ∧
      (NLAlib.specNorm P = if P.rank = 0 then 0 else a) ∧

          (P.rank = 0 ∨ P.rank = Fintype.card n → a = 1)

doc:
An idempotent and its complement have a common norm factor at least one,
with the factor present exactly when the corresponding range is nonzero.
At either rank endpoint this factor is one, also in empty dimension.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; supports `cs-decomposition`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_injective_vecMulVec_le_of_posSemidef_rows_injective.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
A PSD matrix with pairwise distinct rows dominates a rank-one Gram
matrix whose defining coordinates are pairwise distinct. This deterministic
certificate allows singular input and a zero row.
Horn--Johnson (2013), proof of Theorem 7.5.9;
helper for strict entrywise exponential positivity.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_integral_domination_Ioi_of_weak_deriv_nonneg (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] (ℓ a : ℝ) (ha : ℓ < a)

doc:
A positive locally finite measure with nonpositive weak derivative has a
uniform integral domination bound to the right of every interior point. The
constant is finite because it is the integral of one fixed compactly supported
test. Source: Edelman 1988, interval alternative;
atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_invariant_line_or_real_schur_plane.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [Nontrivial E] (T : Module.End ℝ E) :

doc:
Every real endomorphism in positive dimension has an invariant real
line, or an invariant real plane with a canonical orthonormal Schur block.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_invariant_subspace_finrank_one_or_two.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [Nontrivial E] (T : Module.End ℝ E) :

doc:
A nonzero real endomorphism space contains an invariant subspace of
dimension one or two. The statement concerns the ambient dimension and
allows the zero endomorphism. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 2.3.1;
real Schur deflation helper.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isBestFrobRankApprox.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

name: NLAlib.exists_isBestFrobRankApprox
doc:
A Frobenius best rank-at-most-`k` approximation exists for every
finite rectangular matrix, including empty indices and every target rank.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.
atlas: eckart-young-frobenius

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) : ∃ x, NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x
name: NLAlib.exists_isCGIterate
doc:
**Existence of the CG iterate.** For positive definite `A`, every `c`, `x₀` and `q`, there
is a `q`-th CG iterate. It is the Galerkin solution: the bilinear form `(y, z) ↦ zᵀ A y` on `K_q`
is nondegenerate, hence `y ↦ (z ↦ zᵀ A y)` is a bijection `K_q → K_q*`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.2 (uniqueness and existence of the minimiser).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isCholesky_iff_posDef.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :

doc:
**Existence of the Cholesky factorization**: a real matrix on a linearly ordered finite index
has a Cholesky factorization iff it is positive definite; on `Fin n` the factor is `cholesky A`
(`isCholesky_cholesky_of_posDef`), and it is unique (`IsCholesky.unique`). Trefethen–Bau 1997,
Thm 23.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 4.2.7; Higham 2002, Thm 10.1.
atlas: cholesky-decomposition

signature: NLAlib.exists_isFullQR {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : ∃ Q R, NLAlib.IsFullQR A Q R

doc:
**Existence of a full QR** for every real `m × n` matrix, with no rank or shape hypothesis.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 7.1 (existence); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 5.2.1. Proof: induction on
`m`; one orthogonal step (`exists_transpose_mul_apply_succ_zero_eq_zero`) and
`isFullQR_mul_borderedUpper`. The constructive version with Householder reflectors is
`isFullQR_householderQR` (`NLAlib.Matrix.Factorizations.Householder`).
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isGMRESIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)

name: NLAlib.exists_isGMRESIterate
doc:
**Existence.** For every square `A`, right-hand side `c`, start `x₀` and `q` there is a
GMRES iterate (a least-squares problem over `A K_q`; no hypothesis on `A`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §2.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isGradedKrylovBasis_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : (∃ Q, NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis A b Q) ↔ q ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b

doc:
**Existence of graded bases**: a graded orthonormal Krylov basis with `q` columns exists iff
`q ≤ krylovGrade A b`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.4.
atlas: graded-krylov-basis-def (partial)

signature: NLAlib.exists_isHessenbergForm {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ∃ Q H, NLAlib.IsHessenbergForm A Q H
name: NLAlib.exists_isHessenbergForm

**Every square matrix is orthogonally similar to an upper Hessenberg matrix**; if `A` is
symmetric, to a symmetric tridiagonal one (`IsHessenbergForm.isTridiagonal`).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 26; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.3.
atlas: hessenberg-reduction

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isLU_iff_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

**Existence of LU for invertible matrices**: an invertible `A` has an LU factorization iff
all its leading principal minors are nonzero (and it is then unique, `IsLU.unique`).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.2.1; Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor. 3.5.6.
atlas: lu-decomposition

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isLU_iff_rowInclusion.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
  (∃ L U, NLAlib.IsLU A L U) ↔ NLAlib.HasRowInclusion A
name: NLAlib.exists_isLU_iff_rowInclusion
doc:
A singular real matrix admits a unit-lower LU factorization exactly when
it has row inclusion. Arbitrary finite ordered labels and empty matrices are
included. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 3.5.3.
atlas: lu-row-inclusion (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isLU_of_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (h : ∀ k < Fintype.card n, NLAlib.leadingMinor A k ≠ 0) : ∃ L U, NLAlib.IsLU A L U

doc:
**Existence of LU** when the leading principal minors of orders `1, …, n − 1` are nonzero (no
condition on `det A` itself), on any linearly ordered finite index; on `Fin n` the witness is
`lu A` (`isLU_lu_of_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.2.1;
Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor. 3.5.6.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isSVD.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

    | exact Fintype.card_fin _
    | rfl)

    first
    | exact Fintype.card_fin _
    | rfl) :
  ∃ U V, NLAlib.IsSVD A U V
name: NLAlib.exists_isSVD
doc:
**Singular value decomposition** (Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1): every
matrix `A : Matrix m n 𝕜` over `ℝ` or `ℂ`, with `m`, `n` arbitrary finite types, is
`A = U Σ Vᴴ` with `U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜`, `V : Matrix n (Fin q) 𝕜` unitary and
`Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)`, the singular values being nonnegative and non-increasing
(`singularValues_nonneg`, `singularValues_antitone`). The sizes `p = card m`, `q = card n` are
discharged automatically; for `Fin a`, `Fin b` this gives square `Fin a`, `Fin b` factors.
Atlas `svd`.

vectors `A vⱼ / σⱼ` with `σⱼ ≠ 0` are orthonormal and are completed to an orthonormal basis of
`𝕜ᵐ` (atlas `orthonormal-completion`) giving `U`.
atlas: svd

gives the source's inverse-adjoint column `y₀/(x* y₀)`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_card {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {s : Finset ℝ} (hs : s.card = q + 2)

  (hf' : ∀ k < q, ContinuousOn (iteratedDeriv (k + 1) f) (Set.Ioo a b)) (hz : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = 0) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ = 0
name: NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_card
doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem**, finset form: if `f` vanishes on a set of `q + 2` points of
`[a, b]` (hypotheses as in `exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono`), then `f^{(q+1)}`
vanishes somewhere in `(a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, proof of Thm 6.2. Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).
atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {v : Fin (q + 2) → ℝ}
  (hv : StrictMono v) (hva : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 2)), v i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b))
  (hf' : ∀ k < q, ContinuousOn (iteratedDeriv (k + 1) f) (Set.Ioo a b)) (hz : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 2)), f (v i) = 0) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ = 0
name: NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono
doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem.** If `f` vanishes at `q + 2` points `v 0 < ⋯ < v (q+1)` of
`[a, b]`, `f` is continuous on `[a, b]` and the derivatives `f', …, f^{(q)}` are continuous on
`(a, b)`, then `f^{(q+1)}(ξ) = 0` for some `ξ ∈ (a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, proof of Thm 6.2; Atkinson,
*An Introduction to Numerical Analysis* (2nd ed.), proof of Thm 3.2.
Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).
Deviation: stated with `q + 2` zeros and the `(q + 1)`-st derivative (so the conclusion is in the
open interval without a side condition); only continuity of `f^{(k)}`, `1 ≤ k ≤ q`, on `(a, b)`
is assumed — no differentiability, because `iteratedDeriv` is Mathlib's global derivative and
Rolle (`exists_deriv_eq_zero`) needs only continuity.
atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:
NLAlib.exists_least_squares_angle.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

  (hx : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) b ≠ 0) :
  have x := (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) b;
  have r := b - (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) x;
  ∃ θ,
    0 ≤ θ ∧
      θ < Real.pi / 2 ∧
        Real.cos θ = ‖(Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) x‖ / ‖b‖ ∧

doc:
The least-squares angle lies in `[0,π/2)` and has the fitted and
residual norm ratios as cosine and sine. Its tangent is their ratio.
Golub–Van Loan, Theorem 5.3.1; no angle relations are assumed.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_least_squares_angle_error_bound.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {A E : Matrix m n ℝ} {ε : ℝ} (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) (b f : EuclideanSpace ℝ m)
  (hx : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) b ≠ 0) (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
  (hE : NLAlib.specNorm E ≤ ε * NLAlib.specNorm A) (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ ε * ‖b‖)
  (hsmall : NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * ε < 1) :
  have x := (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) b;
  have y := (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A + E))) (b + f);
  have r := b - (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) x;
  ∃ θ,
    0 ≤ θ ∧
      θ < Real.pi / 2 ∧
        Real.cos θ = ‖(Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) x‖ / ‖b‖ ∧
          Real.sin θ = ‖r‖ / ‖b‖ ∧
            Real.tan θ = ‖r‖ / ‖(Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) x‖ ∧
              have C :=
                2 * NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A / Real.cos θ +
                  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A ^ 2 * Real.tan θ;
              ‖y - x‖ / ‖x‖ ≤ ε * C / (1 - NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * ε) ∧
                (ε ≤ 1 / (2 * NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A) →
                  ‖y - x‖ / ‖x‖ ≤ ε * C + 2 * NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * C * ε ^ 2)

doc:

coefficient and the explicit remainder `2κ C ε²` for `ε≤1/(2κ)`.
Golub–Van Loan, Theorem 5.3.1.
atlas: least-squares-perturbation (partial)

remaining coordinate blocks. Gu–Eisenstat 1996, Theorem 3.2; derivations
equations alg:rrqr-block through alg:rrqr-budget.

supports `rank-revealing-qr`.

some `y ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` has `x₀ + y − x⋆ = p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)`. No hypothesis on `A`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_overlapTangentSq_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]

    u ⬝ᵥ x ≠ 0 ∧
      NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x ≤
        NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u b /

doc:
**Angle between the top eigenvector and the Krylov space (Chebyshev bound).** Let `A` be
real symmetric with top eigenvalue `λ₁ = λ₀(A)` and unit eigenvector `u`, and suppose every other

an arbitrary enclosure `[a, c]` of the other eigenvalues instead of `[λₙ, λ₂]`.

        Antitone t ∧

where `t` is nonnegative, decreasing and positive exactly before `g`.

`card n - rank P - g`. Zero and full rank are included.

row and its independence from the regression). Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean` (helper). Ported
from the Prove2me solutions `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law` and
`GaussianMatrix.regression_residual_indep` (the two copies merged, keeping the stronger
statement).

name: NLAlib.exists_specNorm_le_one_frobInner_eq_nuclearNorm
doc:
A spectral contraction attains nuclear–spectral duality on arbitrary
finite index types, including empty shapes: the partial isometry `U Vᵀ` built from the
top singular frames. Horn–Johnson (1991), Corollary 3.4.4.

name: NLAlib.exists_sqrt_contraction_factor_of_fromBlocks_posSemidef
doc:
A PSD block matrix has a contraction factor between its diagonal square
roots. This holds without invertibility or rank assumptions.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.7.9.
atlas: psd-block-contraction (partial)

signature:

name: NLAlib.exists_sqrt_rowGram_mul_coisometry_eq
doc:
A wide real matrix has a coisometry on the right of its row-Gram square
root. Orthonormal rows are the dimensionally correct wide formulation.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.3.1.
atlas: polar-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_strong_rank_revealing_qr.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ A.rank) (f : ℝ) (hf : 1 ≤ f) :
  ∃ π Q R₁₁ R₁₂ R₂₂,
    NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q ∧
      Q * Q.transpose = 1 ∧
        IsUnit R₁₁ ∧
          R₁₁.IsUpperTriangular ∧
            NLAlib.IsUpperTrapezoidal R₂₂ ∧
              A.submatrix id ⇑π = Q * Matrix.fromBlocks R₁₁ R₁₂ 0 R₂₂ ∧
                (∀ i < k,
                    NLAlib.singularValues A i / √(1 + f ^ 2 * ↑k * (↑(Fintype.card n) - ↑k)) ≤
                      NLAlib.singularValues R₁₁ i) ∧
                  (∀ (j : ℕ),
                      NLAlib.singularValues R₂₂ j ≤
                        NLAlib.singularValues A (k + j) * √(1 + f ^ 2 * ↑k * (↑(Fintype.card n) - ↑k))) ∧
                    (∀ (i : Fin k) (j : Fin (Fintype.card n - k)), |(R₁₁⁻¹ * R₁₂) i j| ≤ f) ∧ (k = A.rank → R₂₂ = 0)
name: NLAlib.exists_strong_rank_revealing_qr
doc:
Strong rank-revealing QR exists with the exact constants
`sqrt(1 + f² k(n-k))` and interpolation bound `f`, for every `f ≥ 1`.
The column equivalence is a reordering of all input columns; the
full orthogonal factor has both Gram identities; the leading block is
invertible and upper triangular and the trailing block is upper trapezoidal.
Every leading and every zero-padded trailing singular value is controlled.

The necessary source repair is `k ≤ rank A`, since an ordinary leading
inverse is required. This theorem allows all such `k`, so applying it with
`k = rank A` proves the rank-adapted replacement when a requested rank is
too large; its last clause gives an exactly zero residual. At rank zero the
leading inverse is the valid empty inverse and the factorization reconstructs
the zero matrix. Gu–Eisenstat 1996, Theorem 3.2; Martinsson–Tropp 2020,
Section 13.2; derivations §alg:rrqr, maximum-volume proof.
atlas: rank-revealing-qr

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ}

  ∃ p, p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧ Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1 ∧ x - xs = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.exists_sub_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
**Error form of the residual polynomial.** If `A x⋆ = c` and `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)`, then
`x − x⋆ = p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)` for a residual polynomial `p`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11;
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (proof). Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial).
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b x : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ} (hab : a < b)
  (hv : Function.Injective v) (hva : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 1)), v i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Set.Ioo a b)) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b,
    f x - Polynomial.eval x ((Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ v) (f ∘ v)) =
      iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ / ↑(q + 1).factorial * Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ v)
name: NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq
doc:
**Interpolation remainder formula.** Let `v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ` be distinct nodes in
`[a, b]`, `f` continuous on `[a, b]` with `f, f', …, f^{(q)}` differentiable on `(a, b)`, and
`x ∈ [a, b]`. Then for the interpolating polynomial `L = Lagrange.interpolate univ v (f ∘ v)`
and the nodal polynomial `ω = ∏ (X − v i)` there is `ξ ∈ (a, b)` with
`f x − L(x) = f^{(q+1)}(ξ) / (q + 1)! · ω(x)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, Thm 6.2; Atkinson (2nd ed.),
Thm 3.2; Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas:
`interpolation-remainder`.
Deviation: `ξ` is in the open interval `(a, b)` (stronger than `[a, b]`), at the cost of the
hypothesis `a < b` (used only when `x` is a node).
atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hx : x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) :

doc:
**Residual-polynomial form of an affine Krylov iterate.** If `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)`,
`r₀ = c − A x₀`, then `c − A x = p(A) r₀` for a residual polynomial `p` (`deg p ≤ q`,
`p(0) = 1`). No hypothesis on `A`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11; Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 35. Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial: forward direction).
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_vecMulVec_charpoly_of_interlacing.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)

Any weakly interlacing negative rank-one target list is realized by
`A-vvᵀ` for a prescribed real symmetric matrix, with squared coupling norm
the original spectral sum minus the target sum. Source: Horn–Johnson
(2013), Theorem 4.3.26; reversal and negation reduce to the positive case,
without strictness assumptions or loss of multiplicities or empty cases.
atlas: interlacing-converse

signature:

name: NLAlib.exists_submodule_sq_singularValues_mul_le_mulVec_dotProduct
doc:
**Attaining subspace, max-min half (singular values)**: for `k < card n` there is a
subspace of dimension at least `k + 1` (spanned by the top `k + 1` right singular vectors) on
which `σ_k² ‖x‖² ≤ ‖Ax‖²`. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3
atlas `courant-fischer`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_subseq_eigenvalues₀_sum_difference_quotient_tendsto.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

        Filter.Tendsto (fun ν => (∑ j ∈ J, ⋯.eigenvalues₀ j - ∑ j ∈ J, hC.eigenvalues₀ j) / h (φ ν)) Filter.atTop
          (nhds c)
name: NLAlib.exists_subseq_eigenvalues₀_sum_difference_quotient_tendsto
doc:
Any positive perturbation sequence tending to zero admits a subsequence of
the selected eigenvalue difference quotients converging to a value bounded by
the exact top-`|J|` eigenvalue sum of the perturbation. The compact-eigenframe
argument treats repeated and negative eigenvalues without extra hypotheses.
Source: Bhatia 1997, Theorem III.4.1 proof route.

signature:

An eigenframe sequence along any real symmetric pencil has a convergent
orthogonal subsequence. Finite unit-vector compactness; Lidskii variation step.

At an ordered coordinate threshold, the top-coordinate upper bound is
attained. Every prefix from zero to full dimension is included.

NLAlib.exists_sum_smul_T_eq_of_degree_le {p : Polynomial ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑n) :

signature:
NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
  ∃ r U₁ U₂ V₁ V₂ S₂,
    A = U₁ * 1 * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose ∧
      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧ V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0 ∧ NLAlib.frobSq S₂ = NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq A k
name: NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks
doc:
Every real matrix has an SVD-derived right-space block split whose
tail is the optimal squared rank-`k` error. The head singular values
are absorbed into `U₁=A V₁`, as permitted by HMT's structural lemma.
Only `k≤n` is needed; `k>m` is handled by the padded zero singular values.
HMT 2011, Theorem 9.1; atlas `rsvd-expected-error`, `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks_specNorm {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
  ∃ r U₁ U₂ V₁ V₂ S₂,
    A = U₁ * 1 * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose ∧
      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧

name: NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks_specNorm
doc:
**SVD right blocks with spectral tail.** For `k ≤ n` every real `A` splits as
`A = U₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ` with `U₂`, `V₁`, `V₂` orthonormal, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`, `‖Σ₂‖ = σ_{k+1}` and

blocks are those of `exists_svd_right_blocks` (`U₁ = AV₁`, `U₂ = U`), with the spectral tail
identified through `IsSVD.specNorm_sub_truncatedMatrix`. HMT 2011, §2.1 and Thm 9.1.
Atlas `rsvd-spectral-expected` (helper; uses `svd`, `eckart-young`; belongs in
`Matrix/SvdBlocks.lean`).

Every size-`k+1` subset of zero-indexed finite labels contains a label at least

signature:

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_canonical.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (P : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  ∃ g ≤ min P.rank (Fintype.card n - P.rank),
    ∃ t,
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) ∧
        Antitone t ∧
          (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < t i ↔ i < g) ∧
            ∃ H,
              H.conjTranspose * H = 1 ∧
                H * H.conjTranspose = 1 ∧
                  H.conjTranspose * P * H = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 ((NLAlib.rectDiag t).map Complex.ofReal) 0 0
name: NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_canonical
doc:
Every complex idempotent is unitarily similar to the complexification
of `[I diag(t);0 0]`, where `t` is nonnegative, decreasing, and positive
exactly on the first `g` coordinates. These are the actual canonical
oblique planes `[1 tᵢ;0 0]`, with all remaining ones and zeros included.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; zero and full rank are allowed.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_canonical_spectrum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (P : Matrix n n ℂ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  ∃ g ≤ min P.rank (Fintype.card n - P.rank),
    ∃ t,
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 ≤ t i) ∧
        Antitone t ∧
          (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < t i ↔ i < g) ∧
            ∃ H,
              H.conjTranspose * H = 1 ∧
                H * H.conjTranspose = 1 ∧
                  H.conjTranspose * P * H = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 ((NLAlib.rectDiag t).map ⇑Complex.ofRealHom) 0 0 ∧
                    (∀ (i : ℕ), NLAlib.singularValues P i = if i < P.rank then √(1 + t i ^ 2) else 0) ∧
                      (∀ (i : ℕ), 1 < NLAlib.singularValues P i ↔ i < g) ∧
                        ∀ i < g, t i = √(NLAlib.singularValues P i ^ 2 - 1)
name: NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_canonical_spectrum
doc:
Every complex idempotent has its full unitary oblique canonical form,
and the actual singular values are `sqrt(1+tᵢ²)` on the range and zero
after the rank. Exactly the first `g` values exceed one, with canonical
coefficient `sqrt(σᵢ²-1)`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3;
all rank endpoints and the empty matrix are included.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_range_blocks.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (P : Matrix n n ℂ)

name: NLAlib.exists_unitary_idempotent_range_blocks
doc:
Complex orthonormal coordinates adapted to an idempotent's actual
range give the exact block form `[I T; 0 0]`, with identity size equal to
its actual rank. Both coordinate Gram identities are supplied.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3; includes rank zero, full rank and
empty dimension.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_unitary_mul_eq_of_gram_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

doc:
Two complex matrices of the same shape and with equal Gram matrices
differ by an ambient left unitary factor. Singular and empty matrices are
included. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.1; complex CS completion helper.

Source: Sachdeva–Vishnoi, Theorem 4.1 (`exp-polynomial-approx`).

signature: NLAlib.factorial_two_mul_div_factorial_le_succ_pow (m : ℕ) : ↑(2 * m).factorial / ↑m.factorial ≤ ↑(2 * m + 1) ^ m
name: NLAlib.factorial_two_mul_div_factorial_le_succ_pow
doc:
The factorial estimate `(2m)! / m! ≤ (2m + 1)ᵐ`, used to sum the square-exponential moment
series. Atlas `hanson-wright` (helper).

name: NLAlib.fderiv_sineTruncation_comp
doc:
The derivative multiplier of the smooth truncation has absolute value
at most one. Source: Mathlib's `HasFDerivAt.sin`.
Atlas: `gaussian-log-sobolev`.

signature: NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse (ρ : ℝ) : Set ℂ
name: NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse
doc:
The filled Bernstein ellipse is the Joukowski image of the closed annulus
`1≤|w|≤ρ`. For `ρ>1` this has semiaxes `(ρ+ρ⁻¹)/2` and `(ρ-ρ⁻¹)/2`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8; used by `bernstein-ellipse-approx` and
`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`.

signature:
NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse_subset_openBernsteinEllipse {r ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ) (hrρ : r < ρ) :
  NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse r ⊆ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ
name: NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse_subset_openBernsteinEllipse
doc:
Every strictly smaller closed Bernstein ellipse lies inside the larger open ellipse.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, radius-limit proof of Theorem 8.1
(`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.filterHeadMinAbs {κ : ℕ} [Nonempty (Fin κ)] (s : Fin κ → ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.filterHeadMinAbs
doc:
The smallest absolute leading polynomial value. Source: manuscript `sa:filter`,
its `c_phi`. A positive-dimensional leading block makes the minimum nonempty.

signature:
NLAlib.filterHeadMinAbs_le {κ : ℕ} [Nonempty (Fin κ)] (s : Fin κ → ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (i : Fin κ) :
  NLAlib.filterHeadMinAbs s p ≤ |Polynomial.eval (s i ^ 2) p|

The leading filter minimum bounds each leading filter value from below.
Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, definition of `c_phi`.

signature: NLAlib.filterTailMaxAbs (s : ℕ → ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (a b : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.filterTailMaxAbs
doc:
The largest absolute filtered singular tail entry, with value zero for an empty
tail. Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, its `t_phi`; zero-padded singular values are allowed.

signature: NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv (n : ℕ) : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin n ≃ Fin (n + 1)
name: NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv
doc:
The equivalence `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin n ≃ Fin (n + 1)` sending `inl 0 ↦ 0` and `inr i ↦ i.succ`,
used to transport Mathlib's `fromBlocks` lemmas to the bordered splitting.

signature: NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv_inl {n : ℕ} (i : Fin 1) : (NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv n) (Sum.inl i) = 0
name: NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv_inl

signature: NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv_inr {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) : (NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv n) (Sum.inr i) = i.succ
name: NLAlib.finOneSumEquiv_inr

signature: NLAlib.finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 1)) : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin n ≃ Fin (n + 1)
name: NLAlib.finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv
doc:
Isolate a chosen finite coordinate as the first singleton summand,
with every remaining coordinate in its original increasing order.
Supports the repeated-root restoration in converse interlacing.

signature:
NLAlib.finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv_inl {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin 1) :
  (NLAlib.finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv p) (Sum.inl i) = p
name: NLAlib.finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv_inl
doc:
The singled-out coordinate of `finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv` is the chosen
index. Supports repeated-root restoration in converse interlacing.

signature:
NLAlib.finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv_inr {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 1)) (i : Fin n) :
  (NLAlib.finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv p) (Sum.inr i) = p.succAbove i
name: NLAlib.finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv_inr
doc:
The remaining coordinates of `finOneSumSuccAboveEquiv` are exactly
`Fin.succAbove`. Supports repeated-root restoration in converse interlacing.

A finite sampling law is a probability measure. Source: the PMF construction;

The mass of a sampled index is precisely its specified probability.

name: NLAlib.finiteSamplingPMF
doc:
The probability mass function specified by a finite nonnegative vector
summing to one. Source: Drineas–Kannan–Mahoney 2006, §4.

signature:
NLAlib.finite_not_separable_charpoly_affine.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Field K] [CharZero K] (A D : Matrix n n K) (hD : D.charpoly.Separable) :

doc:
An affine matrix pencil ending at a separable characteristic polynomial
has only finitely many nonseparable parameters. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),
§2.3; the resultant of the characteristic polynomial and its derivative
is a nonzero scalar-parameter polynomial.

signature:
NLAlib.finrank_blockKrylovSpace_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

`dim K_q(A, Ω) ≤ q s` for `Ω` with `s` columns. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3.

signature:
NLAlib.finrank_ker_eq_card_eigenvalues_zero.{u_3} {k : Type u_3} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix k k ℝ}

signature:
NLAlib.finrank_ker_fromBlocks_eq_schur.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {C : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hAu : IsUnit A) (hC : C.IsHermitian)
  (B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  Module.finrank ℝ ↥(Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C).mulVecLin.ker =
    Module.finrank ℝ ↥(C - B.transpose * A⁻¹ * B).mulVecLin.ker
name: NLAlib.finrank_ker_fromBlocks_eq_schur
doc:
An invertible leading block leaves all nullity in its Schur complement.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Exercise 4.5.P21.
atlas: haynsworth-inertia-additivity (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.finrank_ker_mulVecLin_transpose_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {K : Type u_2} [Field K]
  (M : Matrix n n K) : Module.finrank K ↥M.transpose.mulVecLin.ker = Module.finrank K ↥M.mulVecLin.ker
name: NLAlib.finrank_ker_mulVecLin_transpose_eq
doc:
Transposition preserves the nullity of a square matrix over any field.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), §0.4; row rank equals column rank.

signature:
NLAlib.finrank_ker_toBlock_eq_finrank_ker_inverse_complement.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2}
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n K) (hA : IsUnit A.det) (p q : n → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
  [DecidablePred q] :
  Module.finrank K ↥(A.toBlock p q).mulVecLin.ker =
    Module.finrank K ↥(A⁻¹.toBlock (fun i => ¬q i) fun i => ¬p i).mulVecLin.ker
name: NLAlib.finrank_ker_toBlock_eq_finrank_ker_inverse_complement
doc:
Rectangular complementary submatrices of an invertible matrix have the
same right nullity. No equal-size condition is required: the inverse minor's
rows complement the original columns and its columns complement the original
rows. Holds over any field (generalised from `ℝ`, covering `ℂ`). Horn–Johnson 2013,
§§0.7.5–0.7.6.
atlas: complementary-nullities (partial), cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.finrank_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :

**Dimension of a Krylov space.** `dim K_q(A,b) = min q ν(A,b)`.

NLAlib.finrank_krylovSpace_le.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.finrank_krylovSpace_le
doc:
`dim K_q(A,b) ≤ q`. Source: [`gm10`], Ch. 4. Atlas: `krylov-subspace`.

doc:
A nonnegative subspace forces at least its dimension many nonnegative
eigenvalues. Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.2.12.

name: NLAlib.finrank_le_card_eigenvalues₀_pos
doc:
A positive subspace forces at least its dimension many positive
eigenvalues. Horn--Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.2.12.
atlas: eigenvalue-order-and-counting (partial)

NLAlib.finrank_le_finrank_comap_endomorphism.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]

Pullback by an endomorphism cannot lower a subspace's dimension.
Quotient rank--nullity; helper for `ostrowski-congruence-eigenvalues`.

NLAlib.first_order_reciprocal_bound_le {κ C ε : ℝ} (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) (hC : 0 ≤ C) (_hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hsmall : κ * ε ≤ 1 / 2) :

A half-size perturbation gives the explicit quadratic remainder

NLAlib.forall_invariantNorm_le_iff_weaklyMajorized.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

Fan dominance in both directions for all invariant norms on a fixed

signature: NLAlib.forwardSubst {n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → Fin n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.forwardSubst
doc:
**Forward substitution** for `L x = b`, as a total recursion on the leading pivot:
`x₀ = b₀ / L₀₀`, then solve the trailing system with right-hand side `b_{1:} − L_{1:,0} x₀`.
For a lower triangular `L` with nonzero diagonal this is the textbook loop
`xᵢ = (bᵢ − ∑_{j<i} Lᵢⱼ xⱼ) / Lᵢᵢ`; a zero pivot gives junk (`x / 0 = 0`), never an error.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 3.1.1 (column-oriented form); Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 17.
atlas: triangular-matrices-def

NLAlib.four_mul_card_powerset_filter_mem_notMem {n : ℕ} {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) :

Source-transport helper `four_mul_card_powerset_filter_mem_notMem` for Hanson–Wright.

NLAlib.fourierCoeff_chebyshevCircleFunction_eq_circleIntegral (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) :

signature:

The Fourier coefficients of the even Joukowski pullback are even.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.fourierCoeff_jacksonSquareWaveCircle_eq_zero {N k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (hkN : k < N) :

Low nonzero Fourier coefficients of the square wave vanish exactly.

signature: NLAlib.fourier_apply_add (k : ℤ) (x y : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : (fourier k) (x + y) = (fourier k) x * (fourier k) y

Fourier characters multiply under addition of their circle arguments.

signature: NLAlib.fourier_apply_neg (k : ℤ) (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : (fourier k) (-θ) = (fourier (-k)) θ

Reflecting a Fourier monomial in the circle reverses its frequency.
Source: Mathlib additive-circle Fourier definition; helper for `chebyshev-approx-analytic`.

Subtracting circle arguments reverses the Fourier frequency in the second argument.

signature:

A uniform `N`-grid step has the standard complex root-of-unity Fourier value.

The `N`-th character is one at a uniform `N`-grid step.
Source: roots of unity; used by sharp `jackson-lipschitz`.

A character with positive frequency below `N` is not one at a uniform `N`-grid step.

signature: NLAlib.fourier_nat_eq_pow (k : ℕ) (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : (fourier ↑k) θ = (fourier 1) θ ^ k

Natural Fourier frequencies are powers of the first unit-circle monomial.
Source: Mathlib additive-circle Fourier multiplication; helper for `chebyshev-approx-analytic`.

doc:
Fourier monomials of period `2π` equal the unit-circle parametrization at frequency one.
Source: Mathlib additive-circle Fourier definition; helper for `chebyshev-approx-analytic`.

`⟨X, E⟩_F ≤ √r ‖X‖_F ‖E‖₂`. Proof: with the orthogonal projector `P = X X⁺` onto `range X`,

`r` singular values; this is the `VonNeumannRankBound` hypothesis of the Chen–Persson LRA
formalization. Atlas `von-neumann-trace` (rank corollary); arbitrary finite index types, no
full-rank or nonemptiness condition.

`⟨X, E⟩_F = tr(XᵀE) ≤ ∑_{k < min (card m) (card n)} σ_k(X) σ_k(E)`. Horn–Johnson 2013,

principle for the diagonal of `UᵀEV` (through the weighted top-`k` inequality
`sum_mul_le_sum_ite_lt_of_antitone`) and Abel summation over `σ(X)`; no Birkhoff theorem is
needed. Stated over `ℝ` because the singular-value invariances `singularValues_isometry_mul`,
`singularValues_mul_unitary` are real.

if `range Q₁ ⊆ range Q₂`, written `Q₁ = Q₂ C`, then `‖(I − Q₂Q₂ᴴ)A‖_F² ≤ ‖(I − Q₁Q₁ᴴ)A‖_F²`.

by the formula `A − Q₁Q₁ᴴA`). Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset

case): if `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`, `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀΩ` has full row rank, `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀΩ`, `QᵀQ = I` and

Chen–Persson, Prop. `prop:hmt-struct`, second inequality (LRA `hmt_second_frob`).

hypotheses the proof uses (`U₂ᵀU₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₁ = I`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`; no diagonality,
no conditions on `U₁`); `P_Y` is `QQᵀ` for any orthonormal `Q` with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`
(HMT take `range Q = range(AΩ)`); index types are arbitrary `Fintype`s. Atlas
`hmt-9-1-frobenius`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r + 4 ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin r) (Fin k)).real {G | 12 * ↑r / (↑k - ↑r) * t < NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvR G)} ≤
    4 * t ^ (-((↑k - ↑r) / 2))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le
doc:
**Tail bound for the Frobenius norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `r + 4 ≤ k` and `t ≥ 1`,
`P[‖G†‖_F² > 12 r t/(k-r)] ≤ 4 t^{-(k-r)/2}`, with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Thm A.6 (used in Prop 10.4; HMT state it as `P[‖Ω₁†‖_F ≥ √(12k/p) t] ≤ 4 t^{-p}`
with `Ω₁` of size `k × (k+p)`, the same bound after `t ↦ √t`). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`.
Proof: each diagonal entry of `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹` is `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`
(`gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), whose `L^{(k-r)/2}` norm is at most
`3/(k-r+1)` (`integrable_and_integral_rpow_inv_sum_sq_gaussianReal_lt`, atlas
`chi-square-neg-moment`); Minkowski's inequality bounds `‖tr (G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖_{L^q}` and Markov's
inequality gives the tail. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.pinv_frobenius_tail`.
atlas: pinv-frob-tail

signature:

  μ.real {w | 12 * ↑r / (↑k - ↑r) * t < NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvR (X w))} ≤ 4 * t ^ (-((↑k - ↑r) / 2))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le_of_hasLaw
doc:
`gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le` for a random matrix `X` with
`HasLaw X (gaussianMatrix (Fin r) (Fin k)) μ`. Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_specNorm_pinvR_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin r) (Fin k)).real {G | t < NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.pinvR G)} ≤
    1 / √(2 * Real.pi * (↑k - ↑r + 1)) * (Real.exp 1 * √↑k / (↑k - ↑r + 1)) ^ (↑k - ↑r + 1) * t ^ (-(↑k - ↑r + 1))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_specNorm_pinvR_le
doc:
**Tail bound for the spectral norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `2 ≤ r ≤ k` and `t > 0`,
`P[‖G†‖ > t] ≤ (2π(k-r+1))^{-1/2} (e√k/(k-r+1))^{k-r+1} t^{-(k-r+1)}`,
with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Prop A.3; Chen–Dongarra 2005, Lemma 4.1. Atlas: `pinv-spectral-tail`. Proof:
`‖G†‖² = ‖(G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖ = 1/σ_min(Gᵀ)²` (`specNorm_pinvR_sq`,
`specNorm_inv_self_mul_transpose_eq`, atlas `pseudoinverse`), the `λ_min` lower tail
(`gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le`, atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail`, which uses the
proved operator bound (B.5)) and Stirling's formula. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.pinv_spectral_tail`.
atlas: pinv-spectral-tail

doc:

NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r ≤ k) (i : Fin r) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => (G * G.transpose)⁻¹ i i) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin r) (Fin k)) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (∑ j, x j ^ 2)⁻¹)
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self

**Law of a diagonal entry of the inverse Wishart matrix.** For an `r × k` standard Gaussian
matrix `G` with `r ≤ k` and any `i`, `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢᵢ` has the law of `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`, i.e. of
`(∑ⱼ xⱼ²)⁻¹` for a standard Gaussian vector `x ∈ ℝ^{k-r+1}`.

HMT 2011, proof of Prop A.5 / Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Lemma B.2 (each diagonal entry of an
inverse Wishart matrix is an inverse chi-square). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`,
`inverse-wishart-frob-moment` (helper). Proof: Schur complement
(`inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), conditioning on the other rows, which have full rank
a.s. (`gaussianMatrix_ae_rank_eq`, atlas `gaussian-full-rank-ae`), and the residual law
(`pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace`, atlas `block-law-indep`). Ported from Prove2me
solution `GaussianMatrix.inverse_wishart_diag_law`.

      ENNReal.ofReal

name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_one_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_eq
doc:
**The smallest Wishart eigenvalue for `r = 1`.** For a `1 × k` standard Gaussian matrix
`G` (`k ≥ 1`) and `t ≥ 0`, `σ_min(Gᵀ)² = ‖G‖² ∼ χ²_k`, and
`P[σ_min(Gᵀ)² ≤ t] = ∫₀ᵗ c(1,k) x^{(k-2)/2} e^{-x/2} dx` with
`c(1,k) = 2^{(k-2)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(1/2) Γ(k))` (`= 1/(2^{k/2} Γ(k/2))` by Legendre
duplication): the `χ²_k` CDF written in the shape of Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.5).

Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.5) in the case `r = 1` (where it is an equality); Edelman 1988.
Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (sanity case). Proof: polar coordinates for the standard
Gaussian vector and the substitution `y = √x`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.wishart_lambda_min_cdf_rank_one`.
atlas: wishart-lambda-min-tail

signature:

doc:
**Lower tail of the smallest Wishart eigenvalue.** For an `r × k` standard Gaussian matrix
`G` with `1 ≤ r ≤ k` and `t > 0`,
`P[λ_min(G Gᵀ) ≤ t] = P[σ_min(Gᵀ)² ≤ t] ≤ (1/Γ(k-r+2)) (t (k+r)/2)^{(k-r+1)/2}`.

Proof: the density bound (B.5)
(`gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le_lintegral`, proved here), the Gamma-ratio estimate
(`gammaRatio_le`) and `∫₀ᵗ x^a e^{-x/2} dx ≤ t^{a+1}/(a+1)` (`lintegral_rpow_mul_exp_le`, atlas
`tail-integral`). Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.wishart_lambda_min_tail`.
atlas: wishart-lambda-min-tail

            x ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-x / 2))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le_lintegral
doc:
**Density bound for the smallest Wishart eigenvalue** (Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.5); Edelman
1988, Chen–Dongarra 2005). For an `r × k` standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `1 ≤ r ≤ k` and
`t > 0`,
`P[σ_min(Gᵀ)² ≤ t] ≤ ∫₀ᵗ c(r,k) x^{(k-r-1)/2} e^{-x/2} dx` with
`c(r,k) = 2^{(k-r-1)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(r/2) Γ(k-r+1))`.

Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail`. Proof: Gaussian operator calculus gives a scalar
weak inequality; the scalar weighted-density theorem and quadratic-probe Mellin
endpoint recover the exact coefficient. No joint Wishart eigenvalue density or
Vandermonde Jacobian is used. The rank-one case holds with equality. The statement
is identical to the Prove2me density-bound theorem. The positive threshold hypothesis matches
the published statement and is not used by the proof.
atlas: wishart-lambda-min-tail

the classical Schur complement `C − Bᴴ A⁻¹ B` (`moorePenroseInverse` of an invertible matrix is
its inverse).

doc:
**Schur complement below the trailing block**: for `A ⪰ 0`, `M / A ⪯ C` (Loewner order),
since `C − M / A = Bᴴ A⁺ B = (A⁺B)ᴴ A (A⁺B) ⪰ 0`; only `A ⪰ 0` is needed.

name: NLAlib.generalizedSchurComplement_nonneg
doc:
The generalized Schur complement of a PSD block matrix is PSD: `0 ⪯ M / A` for `M ⪰ 0`
(Loewner order). Albert 1969, Theorem 1.

signature: NLAlib.givens.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] (i j : n) (c s : ℝ) : Matrix n n ℝ
name: NLAlib.givens
doc:
The **Givens rotation** `G(i, j, θ)` in the `(i, j)` plane with `c = cos θ`, `s = sin θ`:
`planeRotation eᵢ eⱼ c s`, the identity except for `G i i = c`, `G i j = s`, `G j i = −s`,
`G j j = c`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.8: `Gᵀ x` rotates `(x_i, x_j)` by `θ` and is used to zero
`x_j` (`givensRotation`). For `i = j` it is `planeRotation eᵢ eᵢ c s`, which is not a rotation.
atlas: givens-rotation-def

signature: NLAlib.givensCos (a b : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.givensCos
doc:
The cosine of the rotation zeroing `b` against `a`: `a / √(a² + b²)`, and `1` when
`a = b = 0` (so that the rotation is always orthogonal). Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 5.1.3.
atlas: givens-rotation-def

signature: NLAlib.givensCos_sq_add_givensSin_sq (a b : ℝ) : NLAlib.givensCos a b ^ 2 + NLAlib.givensSin a b ^ 2 = 1
name: NLAlib.givensCos_sq_add_givensSin_sq
doc: `givensCos² + givensSin² = 1` for all inputs. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.8.

signature: NLAlib.givensQR {n : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.givensQR
doc:
**Hessenberg QR by Givens rotations**: `(Q, R) = (G_0 ⋯ G_{n−2}, G_{n−2}ᵀ ⋯ G_0ᵀ H)`, using
`n − 1` rotations. Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 7.4.1, §7.4.2; Trefethen–Bau 1997, Ex. 10.4.
atlas: givens-rotation-def

signature: NLAlib.givensQRQ {n : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.givensQRQ
doc:
The accumulated orthogonal factor after `k` rotations: `Q₀ = I`, `Q_{k+1} = Q_k G_k`, i.e.
`Q_k = G_0 ⋯ G_{k−1}`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.2.
atlas: givens-rotation-def

signature:
NLAlib.givensQRQ_invariant {n : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.IsUpperHessenberg (NLAlib.givensQRQ H k) ∧
    ∀ (a b : Fin n), k < ↑b → NLAlib.givensQRQ H k a b = if a = b then 1 else 0
name: NLAlib.givensQRQ_invariant
doc:
SCAFFOLD: givens-rotation-def. The invariant of the accumulated Givens factor: `Q_k` is upper
Hessenberg and its columns beyond `k` are those of the identity. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.2.
Proof sketch (difficulty 2): induction on `k`; the step `Q_{k+1} = Q_k G_k` multiplies column-wise
by the rotation in the plane `(k, k+1)`: columns other than `k, k+1` are unchanged
(`givens_apply` off the plane), columns `> k + 1` stay identity columns by the second clause, and
the new columns `k, k+1` are combinations of the old columns `k, k+1`, which vanish below row
`k + 1` (identity column `k+1` and the Hessenberg clause for column `k`).

signature:
NLAlib.givensQRQ_mul_givensQRState {n : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.givensQRQ H k * NLAlib.givensQRState H k = H
name: NLAlib.givensQRQ_mul_givensQRState
doc: The invariant `Q_k H_k = H` of the Givens recursion (any `H`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.2.

signature:
NLAlib.givensQRQ_transpose_mul_self {n : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.givensQRQ H k).transpose * NLAlib.givensQRQ H k = 1
name: NLAlib.givensQRQ_transpose_mul_self
doc: The accumulated `Q_k` is orthogonal (any `H`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.2.

signature: NLAlib.givensQRState {n : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.givensQRState
doc:
The matrix after `k` rotations: `H₀ = H`, `H_{k+1} = G_kᵀ H_k`. Golub–Van Loan 2013,
Alg. 7.4.1.
atlas: givens-rotation-def

signature:
NLAlib.givensQRState_invariant {n : ℕ} {H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hH : NLAlib.IsUpperHessenberg H) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.IsUpperHessenberg (NLAlib.givensQRState H k) ∧
    ∀ (i j : Fin n), ↑i = ↑j + 1 → ↑j < k → NLAlib.givensQRState H k i j = 0
name: NLAlib.givensQRState_invariant
doc:
The invariant of the Givens recursion on an upper Hessenberg `H`: after `k` rotations the
matrix is still upper Hessenberg and its first `k` subdiagonal entries vanish.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.2.

signature: NLAlib.givensQRStep {n : ℕ} (W : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.givensQRStep
doc:
The rotation of step `k` of Hessenberg QR applied to the current matrix `W`: the Givens
rotation `G_k` in rows `k, k+1` with `G_kᵀ` zeroing `W (k+1) k`; the identity when `k + 1 ≥ n`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 7.4.1 (Hessenberg QR step).

signature:
NLAlib.givensQRStep_transpose_mul_self {n : ℕ} (W : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :

name: NLAlib.givensQRStep_transpose_mul_self
doc: Each step's rotation is orthogonal.

doc:
**Generalized Nyström expected error** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN`; Tropp–Webber 2023,
Thm 5.1). Output `Â ω = sketchedOutput (Q ω) (Ψ ω) A = Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA` with `Q ω = orth(AΩ ω)`
having `q` columns, `q ≤ t` (the paper's `q = rank(AΩ)`; here `q` is fixed, the generic case

  the Gaussian moment identity of the proof of `thm:RSVD`);

  the tower property: `E‖A − Â‖_F² = E[(1 + q/(s−q−1)) ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²]`. Its per-`Ω` content
  is `completion_reduction`; see `gn_main_of_completion` for a version whose hypothesis is the
  Gaussian noise moment instead;

**Generalized Nyström with Gaussian sketches** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN`; Tropp–Webber
2023, Thm 5.1). `Ω` (`n × t`) and `Ψ` (`m × s`) independent standard Gaussian matrices,
`t ≥ k + 2`, `s ≥ t + 2`; `Q ω = Qf(Ω ω)` with `q ≤ t` columns, `q ≥ 1`, `Qf` entrywise

`orth(AΩ)`). Output `Â = Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA`:
`E‖A − Â‖_F² ≤ (1 + t/(s−t−1)) (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.

`integrable_and_integral_frobSq_sub_sketchedOutput_le_rank_factor_gaussian` (factor
`1 + q/(s−q−1)`, needs only `s ≥ q + 2`) through `q ≤ t` and
`Assembly.completion_factor_mono`; it keeps the published constant `t/(s−t−1)`.

and `gaussianMatrix (Fin m) (Fin s)`); `q` is fixed (see `RSVD.lean`); `Q` must factor
measurably through `Ω`
(`hQ`, `hQf`), needed to apply Fubini.

doc:

signature:
NLAlib.golubKahanSucceeds_iff.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.GolubKahanSucceeds A b k ↔
    k + 1 ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade (A * A.transpose) b ∧ k + 1 ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade (A.transpose * A) (A.transpose.mulVec b)
name: NLAlib.golubKahanSucceeds_iff
doc:
SCAFFOLD: golub-kahan-bidiagonalization
**Breakdown.** The recursion runs without breakdown through state `k` iff both Krylov grades
are at least `k + 1`: `GolubKahanSucceeds A b k ↔ k + 1 ≤ grade(AAᵀ, b) ∧
k + 1 ≤ grade(AᵀA, Aᵀb)`. (In particular `b = 0` or `Aᵀb = 0` fails at once.) Source:
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §10.4.1; Paige–Saunders (1982), §3. Proof sketch: the
interleaved sequence `u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂, …` is the Lanczos basis of `[[0, A], [Aᵀ, 0]]` from
`(b, 0)`, whose Krylov space of dimension `2j` (resp. `2j + 1`) is
`K_j(AAᵀ, b) ⊕ K_j(AᵀA, Aᵀb)` (resp. `K_{j+1}(AAᵀ, b) ⊕ K_j(AᵀA, Aᵀb)`); Lanczos breaks down
exactly at the grade (`krylovGrade`, `finrank_krylovSpace`), and the norms `α, β` are the
Lanczos `β`'s. Difficulty 3.

`GaussianMatrix.gordon`.

`𝔼 (X_{u,t} - X_{u,s})² ≤ 𝔼 (Y_{u,t} - Y_{u,s})²` for all `u, t, s` and

`v_j = a_j − ∑_{i<j} (q_iᵀ a_j) q_i` (well-founded recursion on `j`). When `v_j = 0` (breakdown)

name: NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol_dotProduct_of_lt
doc:
**The Gram–Schmidt columns are pairwise orthogonal**, for every `A` (breakdowns included):
`q_iᵀ q_j = 0` for `i < j`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 7; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.7.
Proof: induction on `j`; `q_iᵀ v_j = q_iᵀ a_j (1 − q_iᵀ q_i) = 0` since `q_iᵀ q_i ∈ {0, 1}` and
`q_i = 0` when it is `0`.

signature:

doc:
SCAFFOLD: gram-schmidt
**Bridge to Mathlib**: `q_j` is Mathlib's `gramSchmidtNormed` of the columns of `A` (viewed in
`EuclideanSpace ℝ m`). Mathlib, `Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.GramSchmidtOrtho`
(`gramSchmidt f n = f n − ∑_{i<n} proj_{span(gramSchmidt f i)} (f n)`). Proof sketch: strong
induction on `j`; with `u_i = gramSchmidt (a) i` and `q_i = u_i / ‖u_i‖` (induction),
`(q_iᵀ a_j) q_i = (⟪u_i, a_j⟫ / ‖u_i‖²) u_i = (ℝ ∙ u_i).starProjection a_j`
(`Submodule.starProjection_singleton`), so `v_j = u_j` and `q_j = u_j / ‖u_j‖`. Difficulty 2.

  [DecidableEq κ] (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian
doc:
The coordinate Laplacian represented by the explicit Gram Hessian.
Source: operator tail proof; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).
atlas: inverse-power-gram-def

signature:
NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq ι]
  [DecidableEq κ] (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (hpd : (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G).PosDef) :
  have R := (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G)⁻¹;
  have T := (R ^ n).trace;
  NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian n ε G =
    2 * ↑(Fintype.card κ) * (NLAlib.inversePowerSoftMinWeight n (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G)).trace +
        4 * (↑n + 1) * T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 2) * (R ^ (2 * n + 2) * (G * G.transpose)).trace -
      T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 1) *
        ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          (2 * (R ^ (n + 2) * (G * G.transpose)).trace +
              (R ^ (n - a + 1)).trace * (R ^ (a + 1) * (G * G.transpose)).trace +
            (R ^ (a + 1)).trace * (R ^ (n - a + 1) * (G * G.transpose)).trace)
name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq
doc:
The exact finite resolvent Gram Laplacian in trace-power form. This
identity exposes the cancellations needed for the sharper limiting
Laplacian bound. Source: operator tail proof; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).

name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq_normalized
doc:
Factoring any positive reference inverse eigenvalue normalizes the
resolvent Gram Laplacian into power sums and a geometric kernel. Source:
operator tail proof; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq_spectral.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq ι]
  [DecidableEq κ] (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (hpd : (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G).PosDef) :
  have b := ⋯.eigenvalues;
  have l := fun i => (b i)⁻¹ - ε;
  have T := ∑ i, b i ^ n;
  NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian n ε G =
    2 * ↑(Fintype.card κ) * T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 1) * ∑ i, b i ^ (n + 1) +
        4 * (↑n + 1) * T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 2) * ∑ i, l i * b i ^ (2 * n + 2) -
      T ^ (-(↑n)⁻¹ - 1) *
        ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          (2 * ∑ i, l i * b i ^ (n + 2) + (∑ i, b i ^ (n - a + 1)) * ∑ i, l i * b i ^ (a + 1) +
            (∑ i, b i ^ (a + 1)) * ∑ i, l i * b i ^ (n - a + 1))
name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq_spectral
doc:
The Gram resolvent Laplacian is exactly a finite scalar expression
in the inverse eigenvalues and the corresponding Gram eigenvalues.
Source: spectral form of the operator tail proof; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).

name: NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_eq_spectral_offDiag
NLAlib.gramSoftMinLaplacian_unshifted_eq

The exact finite unshifted Gram Laplacian consists of its sharp
dimension term minus two nonnegative trace-product defects. Source: the
user's finite inverse-power refinement; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper).
The sum over `a < n` is the source's sum over exponents `1, ..., n`.
atlas: inverse-power-gram-laplacian

signature:
NLAlib.hanson_wright_mgf.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (X : ι → Ω → ℝ)
  (K : ℝ) (hK : 0 < K) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hmgf : ∀ (i : ι), ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (X i) ⟨K ^ 2, ⋯⟩ μ) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  μ.real {ω | t ≤ |(NLAlib.quadForm A fun i => X i ω) - ∫ (ω' : Ω), NLAlib.quadForm A fun i => X i ω' ∂μ|} ≤
    2 *
      Real.exp
        (-(1 / (256 * Real.exp 1 ^ 2)) *
          min (t ^ 2 / (K ^ 4 * NLAlib.frobNorm A ^ 2)) (t / (K ^ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm A)))
name: NLAlib.hanson_wright_mgf
doc:
**Hanson–Wright, MGF form.** Independent coordinates with sub-Gaussian
variance proxy `K²` satisfy the quadratic-form tail bound with the explicit
constant `1/(256 exp(1)²)`. The matrix is arbitrary, and zero matrix/dimension
cases use Lean's total real division convention. The MGF assumption also implies
coordinate centering; no quadratic-form MGF certificate is assumed.
Vershynin 2018, Theorem 6.2.1; Rudelson–Vershynin 2013, Theorem 1.1; atlas `hanson-wright`.
Deviation: the constant `1/(256 e²)` is explicit (the sources' `c` is unspecified); the index
type is an arbitrary `[Fintype ι]` (the leaf proof is over `Fin n` and is transported through
`Fintype.equivFin ι`). Ported from HighDimProb (Zhang–Lee–Liu, Apache-2.0).
atlas: hanson-wright

signature:
NLAlib.hanson_wright_of_lintegral_exp_sq_le_two.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (K : ℝ) (hK : 0 < K) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hX : ∀ (i : ι), AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hmean : ∀ (i : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X i ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hpsi : ∀ (i : ι), ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp ((X i ω / K) ^ 2)) ∂μ ≤ 2) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  μ.real {ω | t ≤ |(NLAlib.quadForm A fun i => X i ω) - ∫ (ω' : Ω), NLAlib.quadForm A fun i => X i ω' ∂μ|} ≤
    2 *
      Real.exp
        (-(1 / (20736 * Real.exp 1 ^ 2)) *
          min (t ^ 2 / (K ^ 4 * NLAlib.frobNorm A ^ 2)) (t / (K ^ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm A)))
name: NLAlib.hanson_wright_of_lintegral_exp_sq_le_two
doc:
**Hanson–Wright, exponential-square/ψ₂ form.** Independent centered
coordinates with nonnegative expectations `E exp((Xᵢ/K)²) ≤ 2` satisfy the
quadratic-form tail bound with explicit constant `1/(20736 exp(1)²)`.
The already-proved Orlicz-to-MGF bridge gives variance proxy `9K²`; the bound
therefore uses the common original ψ₂ scale with a conservative constant.
Vershynin 2018, Theorem 6.2.1; atlas `hanson-wright`. Deviation: the constant
`1/(20736 e²)` is explicit (Vershynin's `c` is unspecified); the index type is an arbitrary
`[Fintype ι]`.
atlas: hanson-wright

doc: Hanson-Wright MGF certificate for diagonal quadratic forms with sub-Gaussian coordinates.

name: NLAlib.hasHansonWrightMGF_of_bounded
doc:
A proved Hanson-Wright MGF certificate for bounded coordinates.

If each coordinate satisfies `|Xᵢ| ≤ K` almost surely, then the quadratic form lies
in the interval `[-K²‖A‖₁, K²‖A‖₁]`.  The centered quadratic form is therefore
bounded by `2K²‖A‖₁`; the local bounded MGF lemma above gives a quadratic CGF
estimate.  The explicit side condition compares this bounded-coordinate constant
with the Frobenius-scale constant used by the Hanson-Wright tail statement.

name: NLAlib.hasHansonWrightMGF_of_subgaussian
doc: Hanson-Wright MGF certificate from independent sub-Gaussian coordinates.

NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_logSobolev_of_bounded.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
