  (hLSI : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c) (f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (L : ℝ)
  (hLip : ∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |f x - f y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) (M : ℝ) (hM : ∀ (x : ι → ℝ), |f x| ≤ M) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (fun x => f x - ∫ (y : ι → ℝ), f y ∂μ) ⟨c * L ^ 2, ⋯⟩ μ
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_logSobolev_of_bounded
doc:
A bounded smooth Lipschitz observable under a measure satisfying a LSI has
the centered sub-Gaussian MGF with variance proxy `cL²`. Exponential integrability is
derived from boundedness. Ledoux 2001, Theorem 5.3; atlas `herbst`.

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_pi_of_coordinate_oscillation.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {S : ι → Type u_2} [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (S i)] (μ : (i : ι) → MeasureTheory.Measure (S i))
  [∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)] (f : ((i : ι) → S i) → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) (c : ι → ℝ)
  (hc : ∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ c i)
  (hcoord : ∀ (i : ι) (x : (j : ι) → S j) (y : S i), |f (Function.update x i y) - f x| ≤ c i) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (fun x => f x - ∫ (y : (i : ι) → S i), f y ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi μ)
    ⟨(∑ i, c i ^ 2) / 4, ⋯⟩ (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi μ)
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_pi_of_coordinate_oscillation
doc:
**Sharp bounded differences on a finite product.** Measurable globally
bounded coordinate oscillations give the centred MGF proxy `∑ cᵢ²/4`, with no
integrability hypotheses. All coordinate spaces may differ; no standard-Borel
assumption is used, and an empty product is included.
McDiarmid 1989, Lemma 3.3; Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart 2013, Theorem 6.2.
atlas: mcdiarmid (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_srhtNormalizedRow_dotProduct {n d : ℕ} [NeZero n] (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (hflat : ∀ (i j : Fin n), H i j ^ 2 = 1 / ↑n) (U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin d) ℝ) (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U)
  (j : Fin n) (u : Fin d → ℝ) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (fun ξ => NLAlib.srhtNormalizedRow H U j ξ ⬝ᵥ u) (‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖₊ ^ 2)
    (NLAlib.rademacherVector (Fin n))
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_srhtNormalizedRow_dotProduct
doc:
The primitive directional MGF condition for the literal one-sign SRHT row
is derived from flatness, the input isometry and the actual independent sign
vector law. Coordinates of the row may be dependent.
Source: operator re-derivation `sh:srht-quadratic`.

name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_sum_mul_rademacher
doc:
A Rademacher series `∑ᵢ aᵢ εᵢ` (`ε` a Rademacher vector) is sub-Gaussian with proxy
`‖a‖₂² = ∑ᵢ aᵢ²`. Vershynin 2018, Prop 2.6.1 with Example 2.5.8(ii). For independent signs given
as a family, build the vector law with `hasLaw_rademacherVector_of_iIndepFun`.
atlas: rademacher-khintchine

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T_cos_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  (θ : ℝ) :
  HasSum (fun k => NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k * Polynomial.eval (Real.cos θ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k))
    (F ↑(Real.cos θ)).re
name: NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T_cos_of_open_ellipse
doc:
The Chebyshev series on a real cosine argument reconstructs the original function's
real part from the open-ellipse holomorphy and bound assumptions.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 3.1(a), 8.1 and 8.2.
Atlas `chebyshev-approx-analytic` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  HasSum (fun k => NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k * Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k)) (F ↑x).re
name: NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T_of_open_ellipse
doc:
The Chebyshev series reconstructs the function on every point of `[-1,1]`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 3.1(a), 8.1 and 8.2.
Atlas `chebyshev-approx-analytic` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_interpolate_T_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  (N : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
  HasSum
    (fun k =>
      NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k *
        Polynomial.eval x
          ((Lagrange.interpolate (Finset.range (N + 1)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.node N)) fun j =>
            Polynomial.eval (Polynomial.Chebyshev.node N j) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k)))
    (Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant F N))
name: NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_interpolate_T_of_open_ellipse
doc:
The interpolant is obtained by interpolating the genuinely reconstructed
Chebyshev series term by term; there are only finitely many nodal values.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 3.1(a) and 4.2 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_fourier_chebyshevCircleFunction_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :
  HasSum (fun k => fourierCoeff (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F) k • (fourier k) θ)
    (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F θ)
name: NLAlib.hasSum_fourier_chebyshevCircleFunction_of_open_ellipse
doc:
The Fourier series of the circle pullback reconstructs the original function pointwise,
under the open-ellipse analytic assumptions.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 8.1 and 3.1(a); Mathlib's uniform Fourier reconstruction.
Atlas `chebyshev-approx-analytic` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_inv_factorial_smul_map_pow.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
  HasSum (fun k => (↑k.factorial)⁻¹ • A.map fun t => t ^ k) (A.map Real.exp)
name: NLAlib.hasSum_inv_factorial_smul_map_pow
doc:
The exponential power series converges entrywise as a matrix series.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.5; helper for exponential positivity.

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_matrix_pow_inv_of_spectralRadius_lt_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : spectralRadius ℂ A < 1) : HasSum (fun k => A ^ k) (1 - A)⁻¹
name: NLAlib.hasSum_matrix_pow_inv_of_spectralRadius_lt_one
doc:
The matrix geometric series has the stated inverse as its sum.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 5.6.13; combines absolute convergence
and the telescoping inverse identity.
atlas: matrix-power-convergence (partial)

signature: NLAlib.hasSum_pow_div_factorial_exp (x : ℝ) : HasSum (fun i => x ^ i / ↑i.factorial) (Real.exp x)
name: NLAlib.hasSum_pow_div_factorial_exp
doc:
The scalar exponential is the sum of its factorial power series.
Mathlib's general Banach-algebra theorem, specialized to reals; used by
Sachdeva–Vishnoi, Theorem 4.1 (`exp-polynomial-approx`).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_pow_inv_one_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {F : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hF : NLAlib.specNorm F < 1) : HasSum (fun k => F ^ k) (1 - F)⁻¹
name: NLAlib.hasSum_pow_inv_one_sub
doc:
The Neumann series as a `HasSum`: `∑ₖ Fᵏ` converges to `(1 - F)⁻¹` when `‖F‖₂ < 1`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Lemma 2.3.3.

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_real_matrix_pow_inv_of_complex_spectralRadius_lt_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : spectralRadius ℂ (A.map Complex.ofReal) < 1) : HasSum (fun k => A ^ k) (1 - A)⁻¹
name: NLAlib.hasSum_real_matrix_pow_inv_of_complex_spectralRadius_lt_one
doc:
The real Neumann series has the exact real inverse as its sum when the
complex spectral radius is below one. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),
Corollary 5.6.13; no real norm-below-one assumption is imposed.
atlas: matrix-power-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_smul_map_pow_of_hasSum_entries.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ)
  (h : ∀ (i j : n), HasSum (fun k => c k * A i j ^ k) (f (A i j))) :

name: NLAlib.hasSum_smul_map_pow_of_hasSum_entries

signature:
NLAlib.haynsworth_inertia_additivity.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {C : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hAu : IsUnit A) (hC : C.IsHermitian)
  (B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.inertiaPos (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C) =
      NLAlib.inertiaPos A + NLAlib.inertiaPos (C - B.transpose * A⁻¹ * B) ∧
    NLAlib.inertiaNeg (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C) =
        NLAlib.inertiaNeg A + NLAlib.inertiaNeg (C - B.transpose * A⁻¹ * B) ∧
      Module.finrank ℝ ↥(Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C).mulVecLin.ker =
          Module.finrank ℝ ↥(C - B.transpose * A⁻¹ * B).mulVecLin.ker ∧
        ((Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C).PosDef ↔ A.PosDef ∧ (C - B.transpose * A⁻¹ * B).PosDef)
name: NLAlib.haynsworth_inertia_additivity
doc:
Haynsworth inertia additivity gives the positive and negative counts,
the nullity identity, and the positive-definite Schur criterion.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Exercise 4.5.P21. Nullity is stated as kernel dimension,
which counts zero eigenvalues for a real symmetric matrix.
atlas: haynsworth-inertia-additivity

signature: NLAlib.headColumns.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} {n k : ℕ} (Q : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) (hk : k ≤ n) : Matrix m (Fin k) ℝ
name: NLAlib.headColumns
doc:
Select the first `k` columns of a matrix with `n` ordered columns.
Wedin (1972), leading singular-frame convention; zero columns are allowed.

signature:
NLAlib.headColumns_mul_transpose.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} {n k : ℕ} (Q : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
  NLAlib.headColumns Q hk * (NLAlib.headColumns Q hk).transpose =
    (Q * Matrix.diagonal fun i => if ↑i < k then 1 else 0) * Q.transpose
name: NLAlib.headColumns_mul_transpose
doc:
The head-column projector is the full frame with a diagonal prefix selector.
Wedin (1972), Section 3; this identity does not require an orthonormal frame.

signature:
NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) (Y : Ω → Matrix d d ℂ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment
doc:
The matrix variance statistic of a Hermitian random matrix: the spectral norm `‖𝔼 Y²‖`; `0` when
`Y²` is not integrable. Tropp 2015, eq. (2.2.4).
atlas: matrix-bernstein

signature:
NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment_dilation_eq_rectSecondMoment.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n]
  (Z : Ω → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ) (hL2 : MeasureTheory.MemLp Z 2 μ) :
  (NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment μ fun ω => NLAlib.dilation (Z ω - ∫ (ω' : Ω), Z ω' ∂μ)) =
    NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ fun ω => Z ω - ∫ (ω' : Ω), Z ω' ∂μ
name: NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment_dilation_eq_rectSecondMoment
doc:
The matrix variance of the Hermitian dilation of a centered rectangular random matrix equals its
rectangular variance statistic.

Tropp 2015, §2.2.8, eq. (2.2.10).
atlas: hermitian-dilation

signature:
NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment_hermitianSeries_eq.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (A : Fin N → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ)
  (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (g k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun g μ)
  (hSG : ∀ (k : Fin N), ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (g k) 1 μ)
  (hVar : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), g k ω ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) :
  (NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment μ fun ω => ∑ k, g k ω • A k) = NLAlib.specNorm (∑ k, A k ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment_hermitianSeries_eq
doc:
**Variance of a Hermitian series**: for independent centred unit-variance coefficients,
`hermitianSecondMoment μ (∑ k, g k • A k) = ‖∑ k, A k ^ 2‖`. Tropp 2015, eq. (4.6.1).
atlas: matrix-gaussian-series

signature:
NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment_sum_eq.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)
  (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (hL2 : ∀ (k : Fin N), MeasureTheory.MemLp (X k) 2 μ)
  (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ = 0) :
  (NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment μ fun ω => ∑ k, X k ω) = NLAlib.specNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ^ 2 ∂μ)
name: NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment_sum_eq
doc:
**Variance of an independent Hermitian sum**: for independent, centred, square-integrable
summands, `hermitianSecondMoment μ (∑ k, X k) = ‖∑ k, 𝔼 (X k)²‖`. Tropp 2015, eq. (6.2.1).
atlas: matrix-bernstein

signature: NLAlib.hessenbergH {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.hessenbergH
doc:
The Hessenberg matrix `H = QᵀAQ` of the reduction. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 26.1.
atlas: hessenberg-reduction

signature: NLAlib.hessenbergQ {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.hessenbergQ
doc:
The orthogonal factor of Hessenberg reduction: the product `P₁ P₂ ⋯ P_{n−2}` of the
reflectors. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 26.
atlas: hessenberg-reduction

signature:
NLAlib.hessenbergQ_mulVec_single_zero {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.hessenbergQ A).mulVec (Pi.single 0 1) = Pi.single 0 1
name: NLAlib.hessenbergQ_mulVec_single_zero
doc:
**`Q e₀ = e₀`**: the first column of the Householder `Q` is `e₀` (so `q₁ = e₁` in
Trefethen–Bau's numbering, which fixes `Q` up to signs by the implicit Q theorem).
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.3.
atlas: hessenberg-reduction

signature:
NLAlib.hessenbergQ_transpose_mul_self {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.hessenbergQ A).transpose * NLAlib.hessenbergQ A = 1
name: NLAlib.hessenbergQ_transpose_mul_self
doc: `QᵀQ = I` for the Hessenberg `Q` (proof-helper form of `hasOrthonormalCols_hessenbergQ`).

signature: NLAlib.hessenbergReduction {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.hessenbergReduction
doc:
**Hessenberg reduction** `A ↦ (Q, H)` by Householder reflectors. Trefethen–Bau 1997,
Alg. 26.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 7.4.2.
atlas: hessenberg-reduction

signature: NLAlib.hessenbergReflectors {n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → List (Fin n → ℝ)
name: NLAlib.hessenbergReflectors

signature: NLAlib.hilbertMatrix (n : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.hilbertMatrix
doc:
The Hilbert matrix in zero-based coordinates has entries
`1/(i+j+1)`, equivalent to the usual one-based `1/(i+j-1)`.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.
atlas: structured-matrices-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.hilbertMatrix_eq_cauchyMatrix (n : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.hilbertMatrix n = NLAlib.cauchyMatrix (fun i => ↑↑i + 1) fun j => ↑↑j
name: NLAlib.hilbertMatrix_eq_cauchyMatrix
doc:
Hilbert is a Cauchy matrix with shifted row and unshifted column labels.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §0.9.12.
atlas: structured-matrices-def

signature: NLAlib.householder.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (v : m → ℝ) : Matrix m m ℝ
name: NLAlib.householder
doc:
The **Householder reflector** `H_v = I − (2 / vᵀv) v vᵀ`. For `v = 0` it is the identity
(`2 / 0 = 0` in Lean; Trefethen–Bau set `H_0 = I` by convention as well).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10, eq. (10.4); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.2.
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature: NLAlib.householderQ {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ
name: NLAlib.householderQ
doc:
The orthogonal factor of Householder QR: the product `H₁ H₂ ⋯ H_k` of the reflectors.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10, eq. (10.2) and Alg. 10.3 (implicit `Q`).
atlas: householder-qr

signature: NLAlib.householderQR {m n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ → List (Fin m → ℝ) × Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.householderQR
doc:
**Householder QR** as a total recursion (Trefethen–Bau Alg. 10.1). On `A : (m+1) × (n+1)`:
`v = householderVector (A e₀) 0`, `B = H_v A`; recurse on the trailing block `B(1:, 1:)`; return
the reflector vectors `v, (0, v₂), (0, 0, v₃), …` (padded to length `m`) and
`R = [[B(0, :)], [0, R']]`. With no rows or no columns, no reflector and `R = A`. Exactly
`min m n` reflectors are produced (`length_householderQR_fst`; for `m = n` the last one is a
`1 × 1` sign flip, as in Trefethen–Bau). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 10.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013,
Alg. 5.2.1.
atlas: householder-qr

signature:
NLAlib.householderQ_mul_householderR {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.householderQ A * NLAlib.householderR A = A
name: NLAlib.householderQ_mul_householderR
doc:
**`QR = A` for Householder QR**, for every `A`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10
(eq. (10.1)–(10.2)); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.2.
atlas: householder-qr

signature:
NLAlib.householderQ_succ_succ {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.householderQ A =
    NLAlib.householder (NLAlib.householderVector (A.col 0) 0) *
      NLAlib.borderedUpper (Matrix.vecCons 1 0)
        (NLAlib.householderQ
          ((NLAlib.householder (NLAlib.householderVector (A.col 0) 0) * A).submatrix Fin.succ Fin.succ))
name: NLAlib.householderQ_succ_succ
doc:
One step of the recursion for `Q`: `Q(A) = H_v · diag(1, Q(B'))` with `B' = (H_v A)(1:, 1:)`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10, eq. (10.2).

signature:
NLAlib.householderQ_transpose_mul_self {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.householderQ A).transpose * NLAlib.householderQ A = 1
name: NLAlib.householderQ_transpose_mul_self
doc: `QᵀQ = I` for the Householder `Q` (proof-helper form of `hasOrthonormalCols_householderQ`).

signature: NLAlib.householderR {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.householderR
doc:
The triangular factor of Householder QR. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 10.1.
atlas: householder-qr

signature: NLAlib.householderSign (t : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.householderSign
doc:
The sign used by Trefethen–Bau: `sign t = 1` for `t ≥ 0` and `−1` for `t < 0` (so
`sign 0 = 1`). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10, eq. (10.5).
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature: NLAlib.householderSign_mul_self (t : ℝ) : NLAlib.householderSign t * t = |t|
name: NLAlib.householderSign_mul_self
doc: `sign t * t = |t|`.

signature: NLAlib.householderSign_sq (t : ℝ) : NLAlib.householderSign t ^ 2 = 1
name: NLAlib.householderSign_sq
doc: `sign t ^ 2 = 1`.

signature: NLAlib.householderVector.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (x : m → ℝ) (i₀ : m) : m → ℝ
name: NLAlib.householderVector
doc:
The **Trefethen–Bau Householder vector** `v = x + sign(x_{i₀}) ‖x‖ e_{i₀}`, whose reflector
maps `x` to `−sign(x_{i₀}) ‖x‖ e_{i₀}` (`householder_mulVec_householderVector`). The sign avoids
cancellation (both signs give valid reflectors in exact arithmetic). Trefethen–Bau 1997,
Lect. 10, eq. (10.5); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 5.1.1 (with the other sign convention).
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature:
NLAlib.householder_mulVec.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (v x : m → ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.householder v).mulVec x = x - (2 * v ⬝ᵥ x / ‖WithLp.toLp 2 v‖ ^ 2) • v
name: NLAlib.householder_mulVec
doc: `H_v x = x − (2 vᵀx / ‖v‖²) v`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10.

signature:
NLAlib.householder_mulVec_householderVector.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (x : m → ℝ) (i₀ : m) :
  (NLAlib.householder (NLAlib.householderVector x i₀)).mulVec x =
    -(NLAlib.householderSign (x i₀) * ‖WithLp.toLp 2 x‖) • Pi.single i₀ 1
name: NLAlib.householder_mulVec_householderVector
doc:
**The reflector maps `x` onto the axis**: `H_v x = −sign(x_{i₀}) ‖x‖ e_{i₀}` for the
Trefethen–Bau vector `v = householderVector x i₀`. No hypothesis (for `x = 0`, `v = 0`).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10 (eq. (10.5) and Fig. 10.2); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.2.
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature:
NLAlib.householder_mulVec_of_dotProduct_eq_zero.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] {v w : m → ℝ}
  (h : v ⬝ᵥ w = 0) : (NLAlib.householder v).mulVec w = w
name: NLAlib.householder_mulVec_of_dotProduct_eq_zero
doc:
`H_v` fixes the hyperplane `v^⊥`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10; Golub–Van Loan 2013,
§5.1.2.
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature:
NLAlib.householder_mulVec_self.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (v : m → ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.householder v).mulVec v = -v
name: NLAlib.householder_mulVec_self
doc:
`H_v v = −v`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.2.
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature:
NLAlib.householder_mul_self.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (v : m → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.householder v * NLAlib.householder v = 1
name: NLAlib.householder_mul_self
doc:
`H_v` is an involution, `H_v² = I`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10; Golub–Van Loan 2013,
§5.1.2.
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature:
NLAlib.householder_transpose.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (v : m → ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.householder v).transpose = NLAlib.householder v
name: NLAlib.householder_transpose
doc:
`H_v` is symmetric. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.2.
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature:
NLAlib.householder_transpose_mul_self.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (v : m → ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.householder v).transpose * NLAlib.householder v = 1
name: NLAlib.householder_transpose_mul_self
doc:
`H_v` is orthogonal, `H_vᵀ H_v = I`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10; Golub–Van Loan 2013,
§5.1.2.
atlas: householder-reflector-def

signature:
NLAlib.householder_vecCons_zero {m : ℕ} (w : Fin m → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.householder (Matrix.vecCons 0 w) = NLAlib.borderedUpper (Matrix.vecCons 1 0) (NLAlib.householder w)
name: NLAlib.householder_vecCons_zero
doc:
A reflector padded with a leading zero is `diag(1, H_w)`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10
(eq. (10.3): `Q_k = [[I, 0], [0, F]]`).

signature: NLAlib.householder_zero.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] : NLAlib.householder 0 = 1
name: NLAlib.householder_zero
doc: `H_0 = I`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10.

signature:
NLAlib.hutchPlusPlusBasis.{u_1, u_5} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {s : Type u_5} [Fintype s] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (S : Matrix n s ℝ) : Matrix n (Fin (Module.finrank ℝ ↥(A * S).mulVecLin.range)) ℝ
name: NLAlib.hutchPlusPlusBasis
doc:
The orthonormal sketch-image basis used by Hutch++.
Its columns span `range (A S)` exactly and their number is the rank of the sketch image.
Source: Meyer–Musco–Musco–Woodruff (2021), Alg. 1.

signature:
NLAlib.hutchPlusPlusEstimate.{u_1, u_3, u_5} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {κ : Type u_3} [Fintype κ]
  {s : Type u_5} [Fintype s] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (S : Matrix n s ℝ) (Z : Matrix n κ ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.hutchPlusPlusEstimate
doc:
Hutch++ with a basis constructed from the sketch image and a separate residual test matrix.
Source: Meyer–Musco–Musco–Woodruff (2021), Alg. 1. Rank-deficient and zero sketches use their
actual image dimension. This definition supplies the sketch-span relation; random-sketch
measurability, independence and complexity guarantees require separate theorems.

signature:
NLAlib.hutchinsonBlock.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
  Matrix (n × κ) (n × κ) ℝ
name: NLAlib.hutchinsonBlock
doc:
The block-diagonal matrix `(1/m) diag(A, …, A)` on `n × κ` whose quadratic form at
`vec(Z)` is the Hutchinson estimator. Atlas: `hutchinson-tail` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype κ] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (Z : Matrix n κ ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate
doc:
The `m`-sample Hutchinson estimator `(1/m) ∑ₖ zₖᵀ A zₖ`, with the samples `zₖ` the columns of
the test matrix `Z : Matrix n κ ℝ` and `m = |κ|`. Source: Hutchinson (1989) [`hutch89`];
Avron–Toledo (2011) [`at11`], §2.
atlas: trace-estimators-def

signature:
NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate_one.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq n]
  (G : Matrix n κ ℝ) : NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate 1 G = (∑ k, ‖WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => G i k‖ ^ 2) / ↑(Fintype.card κ)
name: NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate_one
doc: `tr_m(I) = (1/m) ∑ₖ ‖g_k‖²`. Atlas: `slq-error` (helper).

name: NLAlib.iIndepFun_centered_sq
doc:
Centring the squares of independent variables keeps them independent. Atlas
`hanson-wright` (helper).

NLAlib.iIndepFun_eval_gaussianVector.{u_1} (n : Type u_1) [Fintype n] :

NLAlib.iIndepFun_gaussianMatrix_entry.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] :

NLAlib.iIndepFun_gaussianMatrix_row.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] :

name: NLAlib.iIndepFun_gaussianMatrix_row

signature:
NLAlib.iIndepFun_uniform_sequence_comp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Fintype ι]

Coordinate compositions are independent under the
uniform finite sequence law. Source: product uniform law, `srht-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetConditionalWeight.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] {k : ℕ}
  (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α) (T : NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k) (I : Fin k → α) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetConditionalWeight
doc:
The conditional finite weights at a selected exact-size subset.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetConditionalWeight_invariant.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] {k : ℕ}
  (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α) (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (T : NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k) (I : Fin k → α) :
  NLAlib.iidSubsetConditionalWeight hk (NLAlib.permuteExactRowSubset σ T) (⇑σ ∘ I) =
    NLAlib.iidSubsetConditionalWeight hk T I
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetConditionalWeight_invariant
doc:
Conditional weights are equivariant under joint label permutations.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetConditionalWeight_nonneg
doc:
Conditional weights are nonnegative probability masses.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetExpectedCount.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] {k : ℕ}
  (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α) (T : NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k) (j : α) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetExpectedCount
doc:
The conditional expected multiplicity at one selected subset.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetExpectedCount_eq_of_mem
doc:
Every label inside the selected subset has the same expected count.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetExpectedCount_eq_one_of_mem
doc:
Each selected label has exact conditional expected count one. This is
proved by exchangeability and the fixed size, rather than assumed.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetExpectedCount_eq_zero_of_not_mem
doc:
Outside the selected subset, the conditional count is zero because the
literal coupling always contains the sequence support.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetExpectedCount_invariant
doc:
Expected multiplicities are invariant under relabeling.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] {k : ℕ}
  (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α) : PMF ((Fin k → α) × NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k)
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF
doc:
The joint iid/exact-subset coupling PMF.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF_toReal_eq_zero_of_not_subset.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
  {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α) (I : Fin k → α) (T : NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k)
  (h : ¬Finset.image I Finset.univ ⊆ ↑T) : ((NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF hk) (I, T)).toReal = 0
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF_toReal_eq_zero_of_not_subset
doc:
Pairs outside the literal support-extension relation have zero joint mass.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF_toReal_first_marginal
doc:
The sequence marginal of the explicit joint coupling is iid uniform,
with mass `1/n^k` for every sequence.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF_toReal_invariant.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] {k : ℕ}
  (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α) (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (I : Fin k → α) (T : NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k) :
  ((NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF hk) (⇑σ ∘ I, NLAlib.permuteExactRowSubset σ T)).toReal =
    ((NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF hk) (I, T)).toReal
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetJointPMF_toReal_invariant
doc:
Joint coupling probability masses are invariant under joint label permutations.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetMarginal.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α)
  (T : NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetMarginal
doc:
The subset marginal mass of the iid/subset coupling.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetMarginal_eq
doc:
Transitivity makes all exact-size subset marginal masses equal.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetMarginal_eq_uniform
doc:
The exact-size subset marginal is uniform, with the exact
finite uniform mass. Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetMarginal_invariant
doc:
The subset marginal is invariant under label permutations.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetOutcome.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α)
  (z : (Fin k → α) × Equiv.Perm α) : (Fin k → α) × NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetOutcome
doc:
One independent uniform permutation jointly symmetrizes the original
uniform iid sequence and its support extension.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetOutcome_act.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α)
  (σ : Equiv.Perm α) (z : (Fin k → α) × Equiv.Perm α) :
  NLAlib.iidSubsetOutcome hk ((NLAlib.iidSubsetSourceAct σ) z) =
    (NLAlib.iidSubsetPairAct σ) (NLAlib.iidSubsetOutcome hk z)
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetOutcome_act
doc:
The literal joint coupling is equivariant under every label permutation.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

name: NLAlib.iidSubsetOutcome_support_subset
doc:
The permutation coupling always places the sequence support inside
the selected subset. Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetPairAct.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] {k : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm α) :
  (Fin k → α) × NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k ≃ (Fin k → α) × NLAlib.ExactRowSubset α k
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetPairAct
doc:
The outcome action jointly permutes sequence labels and selected labels.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.iidSubsetSourceAct.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {k : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm α) :
  (Fin k → α) × Equiv.Perm α ≃ (Fin k → α) × Equiv.Perm α
name: NLAlib.iidSubsetSourceAct
doc:
The source action changes only its independent uniform permutation.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.im_fourierCoeff_of_even_real (g : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi) → ℝ)
  (heven : ∀ (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)), g (-t) = g t) (k : ℤ) : (fourierCoeff (fun t => ↑(g t)) k).im = 0
name: NLAlib.im_fourierCoeff_of_even_real
doc:
Fourier coefficients of an even real-valued circle function are real. Haar reflection
and complex conjugation give this without an assumed coefficient-reality certificate.
Source: elementary Fourier symmetry; used by sharp `jackson-lipschitz`.

signature: NLAlib.im_fourier_nat_coe_eq_sin (k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ((fourier ↑k) ↑t).im = Real.sin (↑k * t)
name: NLAlib.im_fourier_nat_coe_eq_sin
doc:
The imaginary part of the natural Fourier character at a real angle is its sine.
Source: Mathlib's additive-circle Fourier definition; used by sharp `jackson-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.image_univ_subset_sequenceSupportExtension.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ}
  (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card α) (I : Fin k → α) : Finset.image I Finset.univ ⊆ ↑(NLAlib.sequenceSupportExtension hk I)
name: NLAlib.image_univ_subset_sequenceSupportExtension
doc:
The extension contains every label that actually appears in the sequence.
Source: Hoeffding 1963, Theorem 4.

signature:
NLAlib.indepFun_mulVec_sq_dist_rowSpace {n k : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hH : H.rank = n) :
  ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (fun g => H.mulVec g)
    (fun g => g ⬝ᵥ g - H.mulVec g ⬝ᵥ (H * H.transpose)⁻¹.mulVec (H.mulVec g))
    (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
name: NLAlib.indepFun_mulVec_sq_dist_rowSpace
doc:
**Independence of Gaussian regression and residual.** Let `H` be a fixed `n × k` matrix of
full row rank and `g` a standard Gaussian vector in `ℝᵏ`. Then `H g` and the squared distance
`‖g‖² - (H g)ᵀ (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ (H g)` from `g` to the row space of `H` are independent.

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 (off-diagonal second moments of `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹`); the
classical independence of the least-squares fit and the residual sum of squares. Atlas:
`inverse-wishart-frob-moment` (helper); the proof uses Gaussian independence from zero
covariance. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.regression_residual_indep`.

signature:
NLAlib.indepFun_of_hasGaussianLaw_of_covariance_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} (U : Ω → ℝ) (W : ι → Ω → ℝ)
  (hUW : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω => (U ω, fun j => W j ω)) P)
  (hcov : ∀ (j : ι), ProbabilityTheory.covariance U (W j) P = 0) : ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun U (fun ω j => W j ω) P
name: NLAlib.indepFun_of_hasGaussianLaw_of_covariance_eq_zero
doc:
For a jointly Gaussian pair `(U, W)` with `U` real and `W` vector-valued, if `U` is
uncorrelated with every coordinate of `W` then `U` and `W` are independent. Atlas:
`gaussian-integration-by-parts` (helper).

signature: NLAlib.inertiaNeg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) : ℕ
name: NLAlib.inertiaNeg
doc:
The **negative index of inertia** of `A`: the largest dimension of a subspace on which
`x ↦ xᵀAx` is negative definite. For symmetric `A` it is the number of negative eigenvalues
(`inertiaNeg_eq_card_eigenvalues_neg`). Source: Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], §4.5.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaNeg_diagonal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (d : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.inertiaNeg (Matrix.diagonal d) = {i | d i < 0}.card
name: NLAlib.inertiaNeg_diagonal
doc:
The negative index of a diagonal matrix is the number of negative diagonal entries.
Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], §4.5.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaNeg_eq_card_eigenvalues_neg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) : NLAlib.inertiaNeg A = {i | hA.eigenvalues i < 0}.card
name: NLAlib.inertiaNeg_eq_card_eigenvalues_neg
doc:
For real symmetric `A`, `inertiaNeg A` is the number of negative eigenvalues.
Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], §4.5.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaNeg_fromBlocks_eq_add_schur.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {C : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hAu : IsUnit A)
  (hC : C.IsHermitian) (B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.inertiaNeg (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C) =
    NLAlib.inertiaNeg A + NLAlib.inertiaNeg (C - B.transpose * A⁻¹ * B)
name: NLAlib.inertiaNeg_fromBlocks_eq_add_schur
doc:
Haynsworth's negative inertia additivity at an invertible leading
block. Horn--Johnson (2013), Exercise 4.5.P21.
atlas: haynsworth-inertia-additivity (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaNeg_fromBlocks_zero.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {C : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hC : C.IsHermitian) :
  NLAlib.inertiaNeg (Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 C) = NLAlib.inertiaNeg A + NLAlib.inertiaNeg C
name: NLAlib.inertiaNeg_fromBlocks_zero
doc:
Negative inertia adds over a block direct sum. Horn--Johnson (2013),
Exercise 4.5.P21; helper for `haynsworth-inertia-additivity`.

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaNeg_sub_smul_one_eq_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (x : ℝ) : NLAlib.inertiaNeg (A - x • 1) = {i | hA.eigenvalues i < x}.card
name: NLAlib.inertiaNeg_sub_smul_one_eq_card
doc:
**Inertia from the spectrum (negative index).** For real symmetric `A` and any `x`,
`inertiaNeg (A − xI) = #{i : λᵢ < x}`. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], Thm 4.5.8;
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.4.1.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaNeg_transpose_mul_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  {X : Matrix n n ℝ} (hX : IsUnit X) : NLAlib.inertiaNeg (X.transpose * A * X) = NLAlib.inertiaNeg A
name: NLAlib.inertiaNeg_transpose_mul_mul
doc:
**Sylvester's law of inertia (negative index).** `inertiaNeg (XᵀAX) = inertiaNeg A` for
invertible `X`. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], Thm 4.5.8.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature: NLAlib.inertiaPos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) : ℕ

doc:

`x ↦ xᵀAx` is positive definite (Mathlib's `QuadraticForm.sigPos` of `A.toQuadraticForm'`).
For symmetric `A` it is the number of positive eigenvalues
(`inertiaPos_eq_card_eigenvalues_pos`). Source: Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], §4.5.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:

name: NLAlib.inertiaPos_add_inertiaNeg_eq_rank

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaPos_diagonal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (d : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.inertiaPos (Matrix.diagonal d) = {i | 0 < d i}.card
name: NLAlib.inertiaPos_diagonal
doc:
The positive index of a diagonal matrix is the number of positive diagonal entries.
Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], §4.5.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaPos_eq_card_eigenvalues_pos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) : NLAlib.inertiaPos A = {i | 0 < hA.eigenvalues i}.card
name: NLAlib.inertiaPos_eq_card_eigenvalues_pos
doc:
For real symmetric `A`, `inertiaPos A` is the number of positive eigenvalues.
Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], §4.5.
atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaPos_fromBlocks_eq_add_schur.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {C : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hAu : IsUnit A)
  (hC : C.IsHermitian) (B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.inertiaPos (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C) =
    NLAlib.inertiaPos A + NLAlib.inertiaPos (C - B.transpose * A⁻¹ * B)
name: NLAlib.inertiaPos_fromBlocks_eq_add_schur
doc:
Haynsworth's positive inertia additivity at an invertible leading
block. Horn--Johnson (2013), Exercise 4.5.P21.
atlas: haynsworth-inertia-additivity (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaPos_fromBlocks_zero.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

doc:
Positive inertia adds over a block direct sum. Horn--Johnson (2013),
Exercise 4.5.P21; helper for `haynsworth-inertia-additivity`.

signature:
NLAlib.inertiaPos_sub_smul_one_eq_card.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (x : ℝ) : NLAlib.inertiaPos (A - x • 1) = {i | x < hA.eigenvalues i}.card
name: NLAlib.inertiaPos_sub_smul_one_eq_card
doc:
**Inertia from the spectrum (positive index).** For real symmetric `A` and any `x`,
`inertiaPos (A − xI) = #{i : λᵢ > x}`; with `x = 0`, the number of positive eigenvalues.

atlas: sylvester-inertia

signature:

**Sylvester's law of inertia (positive index).** `inertiaPos (XᵀAX) = inertiaPos A` for

[`gvl13`], Thm 8.1.17. Uniqueness of the signature is Mathlib's
`QuadraticMap.Equivalent.sigPos_eq`.

signature:

  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun G => NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.pinvR G)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin (k + p))) ∧
    ∫ (G : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin (k + p)) ℝ),
        NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.pinvR G) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin (k + p)) ≤

`p ≥ 2`: Jensen and `E‖G†‖_F² = k/(p−1)`. HMT 2011, Prop 10.2 and proof of Thm 10.6.

signature:
NLAlib.integrable_and_integral_frobSq_inv_self_mul_transpose_gaussianMatrix {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r + 4 ≤ k) :
  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun G => NLAlib.frobSq (G * G.transpose)⁻¹) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin r) (Fin k)) ∧

doc:
**Frobenius moment of the inverse Wishart matrix.** For an `r × k` standard Gaussian matrix
`G` with `r + 4 ≤ k`, `‖(G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖_F²` is integrable and
`E‖(G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖_F² = r(k-1)/((k-r)(k-r-1)(k-r-3))`.

Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Lemma B.2 (second moments of the inverse Wishart matrix). Atlas:
`inverse-wishart-frob-moment`. Proof: sum of the diagonal
(`integrable_and_integral_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self_sq_gaussianMatrix`) and
off-diagonal (`integrable_and_integral_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_sq_gaussianMatrix`) second
moments, which use atlas `inverse-wishart-mean` and `chi-square-neg-moment`. Ported from
Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.inverse_wishart_frobenius_moment`.
atlas: inverse-wishart-frob-moment

signature:
NLAlib.integrable_and_integral_frobSq_pinvR_gaussianMatrix {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r + 2 ≤ k) :

doc:
**Frobenius moment of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** If `G` is an `r × k` standard Gaussian
matrix with `r + 2 ≤ k`, then `‖G†‖_F²` is integrable and `E ‖G†‖_F² = r / (k - r - 1)`, where

`k × (k+p)`). Atlas: `pinv-frob-moment`. Proof ported from the Prove2me solution
`Sol_GaussianMatrix_pinv_frobenius_moment`: `‖G†‖_F² = tr (G Gᵀ)⁻¹`
(`frobSq_pinvR_eq_trace_inv`, atlas `pseudoinverse`) and
`integrable_and_integral_inv_self_mul_transpose_gaussianMatrix` (atlas `inverse-wishart-mean`).
atlas: pinv-frob-moment

signature:

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n k t s : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t) (hqs : min A.rank t + 2 ≤ s) (Ω : Ωs → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ) (Ψ : Ωs → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin s) ℝ)
  (hΩ : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Ω (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin n) (Fin t)) μ)
  (hΨ : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Ψ (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin m) (Fin s)) μ)
  (hind : ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun Ω Ψ μ) :
  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => NLAlib.frobSq (A - NLAlib.rawGeneralizedNystrom A (A * Ω ω) (Ψ ω))) μ ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (A - NLAlib.rawGeneralizedNystrom A (A * Ω ω) (Ψ ω)) ∂μ ≤
      (1 + ↑(min A.rank t) / (↑s - ↑(min A.rank t) - 1)) * ((1 + ↑k / (↑t - ↑k - 1)) * NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq A k)

the actual raw Moore–Penrose output has integrable squared Frobenius error at most

no spectral decomposition, frame, rank, moment or completion certificate is supplied.
Tropp–Webber 2023, Theorem 5.1; atlas `gn-expected-error`.

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n r k t : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ}
  {F : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A = F.transpose * F) (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t) (Ω : Ωs → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ)
  (hΩ : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Ω (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin n) (Fin t)) μ) :
  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => (A - NLAlib.nystrom A (Ω ω)).trace) μ ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ωs), (A - NLAlib.nystrom A (Ω ω)).trace ∂μ ≤ (1 + ↑k / (↑t - ↑k - 1)) * NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq F k
name: NLAlib.integrable_and_integral_trace_sub_nystrom_le
doc:
**Randomized Nyström, expected trace error** (Gittens–Mahoney 2016, Thm 3 / §3;
Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1 specialised to Nyström; Martinsson–Tropp 2020, §19.2): if
`A = FᵀF` and `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix with `t ≥ k + 2`, then
`tr(A − A⟨Ω⟩)` is integrable and
`E tr(A − A⟨Ω⟩) ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) · ‖F − ⟦F⟧ₖ‖_F²`.

Proof: `tr(A − A⟨Ω⟩) = ‖(I − P)F‖_F²` (`trace_sub_nystrom_eq_of_eq_transpose_mul`); a.s.
the Gaussian range frame `Q` of `FΩ` has `min(rank F, t) = rank(FΩ)` columns, so `QQᵀ = P`;
then the Gaussian RSVD bound for `F`
(`integrable_and_integral_frobSq_residual_gaussianRangeFrame_le_bestRankFrobSq`).

Deviation: the right side is `bestRankFrobSq F k`; for `A = FᵀF` this equals
`∑_{i>k} λᵢ(A) = ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_*` (the atlas form), an identification not formalized here.
Index types are `Fin` (Gaussian law convention). Atlas `nystrom-randomized` (uses
`nystrom-structural`, `rsvd-expected-error`, `leverage-scores`).
atlas: nystrom-randomized (partial)

`integral_frobSq_mul_gaussianMatrix_mul` for a random matrix `X` with

signature:
NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gaussianMatrix_mul_sq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {p : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} [Fintype p]
  [Fintype m] [DecidableEq p] [DecidableEq m] {a : Type u_3} {n : Type u_4} [Fintype a] [Fintype n] (S : Matrix a p ℝ)
  (T : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  ∫ (G : Matrix p m ℝ), NLAlib.frobSq (S * G * T) ^ 2 ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix p m =
    (NLAlib.frobSq S * NLAlib.frobSq T) ^ 2 + 2 * NLAlib.frobSq (S.transpose * S) * NLAlib.frobSq (T * T.transpose)
name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gaussianMatrix_mul_sq
doc:
**Fourth moment of a Gaussian sandwich.** For a standard Gaussian `p × m` matrix `G` and
fixed `S : a × p`, `T : m × n`,
`E ‖S G T‖_F⁴ = (‖S‖_F² ‖T‖_F²)² + 2 ‖SᵀS‖_F² ‖T Tᵀ‖_F²`.

Isserlis formula applied to the entries `(S G T)_{ij} = ⟨S_i ⊗ T_j, G⟩`. Used for the variance of
Gaussian sketches (Tropp–Webber 2023, App. A; HMT 2011, Prop 10.1 second-moment companions).
Atlas: `gaussian-frob-fourth-moment`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.frobenius_fourth_moment`.
atlas: gaussian-frob-fourth-moment

name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gaussianMatrix_mul_sq_of_hasLaw
doc:
`integral_frobSq_mul_gaussianMatrix_mul_sq` for a random matrix `X` with
`HasLaw X (gaussianMatrix p m) μ`. Atlas: `gaussian-frob-fourth-moment`.

name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gaussian_mul_of_indepFun
doc:
**Sandwiched Gaussian second moment, conditioned.** If `Y` is a standard Gaussian
`p × m` matrix independent of `X`, then `E ‖S Y T(X)‖_F² = ‖S‖_F² E ‖T(X)‖_F²`.

No integrability hypothesis: both integrands are nonnegative and the identity holds for the
lower Lebesgue integrals (`lintegral_frobSq_mul_gaussian_mul_of_indepFun`); when the right side
is not integrable both Bochner integrals are `0`. Integrability of the left side is
`integrable_frobSq_mul_gaussian_mul_of_indepFun`.
HMT 2011 Prop 10.1 with the tower property (proof of Thm 10.5). Atlas `gaussian-conditioning`.
Measurability of `T` is stated entrywise.
atlas: gaussian-conditioning

signature:
NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gram_mul_transpose_sub {a b n t : ℕ} (ht : 1 ≤ t) (M : Matrix (Fin a) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (N : Matrix (Fin b) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  ∫ (Ω : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ),
        NLAlib.frobSq
          (M * (1 / ↑t) • (Ω * Ω.transpose) * N.transpose - M * N.transpose) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin n) (Fin t) =
      (NLAlib.frobSq M * NLAlib.frobSq N + NLAlib.frobSq (M * N.transpose)) / ↑t ∧
    (NLAlib.frobSq M * NLAlib.frobSq N + NLAlib.frobSq (M * N.transpose)) / ↑t ≤
      2 / ↑t * (NLAlib.frobSq M * NLAlib.frobSq N)
name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_mul_gram_mul_transpose_sub
doc:
**Gaussian approximate matrix multiplication.** For `M : a × n`, `N : b × n` and a standard
Gaussian `n × t` matrix `Ω` (`t ≥ 1`), the sketched product `M (Ω Ωᵀ / t) Nᵀ` has mean squared
error `E ‖M (Ω Ωᵀ / t) Nᵀ − M Nᵀ‖_F² = (‖M‖_F² ‖N‖_F² + ‖M Nᵀ‖_F²) / t`, and this is at most
`(2/t) ‖M‖_F² ‖N‖_F²`.

Drineas–Kannan–Mahoney 2006 / Sarlós 2006 (approximate matrix multiplication); Gaussian case
via the Isserlis formula, e.g. Martinsson–Tropp 2020, §6.3 / Woodruff 2014, Lemma 2.2.
Atlas: `gaussian-amm`. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.approx_multiplication`.
atlas: gaussian-amm

signature:
NLAlib.integral_frobSq_pinvL_block_mul_block_mul.{u_1, u_2} {Ωs : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ωs]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m s q rp : ℕ} {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  {Ψ : Ωs → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin s) ℝ} (hΨ : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Ψ (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin m) (Fin s)) μ)
  (Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin q) ℝ) (Qp : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin rp) ℝ) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hQp : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qp) (hQQp : Q.transpose * Qp = 0) (B : Matrix (Fin rp) ι ℝ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvL ((Ψ ω).transpose * Q) * ((Ψ ω).transpose * Qp) * B) ∂μ =
    (∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvL ((Ψ ω).transpose * Q)) ∂μ) * NLAlib.frobSq B
name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_pinvL_block_mul_block_mul
doc:
**Completion-step inverse-moment factorisation** (transposed form of
`integral_frobSq_mul_block_mul_pinvR_block`). If `Ψ` is an `m × s` standard Gaussian matrix and
`Q`, `Qp` have orthonormal, mutually orthogonal columns, then for every fixed `B`
`E ‖(ΨᵀQ)† (ΨᵀQp) B‖_F² = E ‖(ΨᵀQ)†‖_F² · ‖B‖_F²`.

Generalized Nyström / two-sided sketch analysis (hypothesis `hG₂` of `completion_reduction`);
the conditioning argument of HMT 2011 Thm 10.5 applied to the transposed sketch. Here
`(ΨᵀQ)† = pinvL (ΨᵀQ)`. Atlas `gaussian-conditioning`.
atlas: gaussian-conditioning

signature:
NLAlib.integral_frobSq_pinvR_block.{u_1} {Ωs : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ωs] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {n k t : ℕ}
  {Ω : Ωs → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ} (hΩ : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Ω (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin n) (Fin t)) μ)
  (V₁ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hV₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvR (V₁.transpose * Ω ω)) ∂μ =
    ∫ (G : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin t) ℝ), NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvR G) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin t)
name: NLAlib.integral_frobSq_pinvR_block
doc:
**Inverse moment of a Gaussian block.** If `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix and
`V₁` has orthonormal columns, then `E ‖(V₁ᵀΩ)†‖_F² = E_{G} ‖G†‖_F²` for `G` a `k × t` standard Gaussian matrix.
Combined with `integral_frobSq_mul_block_mul_pinvR_block` and the inverse moment of a Gaussian
matrix this closes hypothesis `hinv` of `NLAlib.rsvd_truncated_main`. HMT 2011 §10.2 (block law).
Atlas `gaussian-conditioning`.
atlas: gaussian-conditioning

              NLAlib.sampledRowMatrix B (NLAlib.columnRowProbabilities A B) ω -

signature:
NLAlib.integral_frobenius_average_sub_mean_sq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype ι]
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] (p : ι → NNReal) (hp : ∑ i, p i = 1)
  (Z : ι → Matrix m n ℂ) {c : ℕ} (hc : 0 < c) :
  (∫ (ω : Fin c → ι),
      ‖(1 / ↑c) • ∑ j, Z (ω j) - ∑ i, ↑(p i) • Z i‖ ^
        2 ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => NLAlib.finiteSamplingLaw p hp) =
    1 / ↑c * (∑ i, ↑(p i) * ‖Z i‖ ^ 2 - ‖∑ i, ↑(p i) • Z i‖ ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.integral_frobenius_average_sub_mean_sq
doc:
The squared Frobenius error of a finite matrix sample average is exactly
the one-sample variance divided by the sample count. Every expectation is
under the genuine independent product sampling law. Source: operator
re-derivation `sa:amm-variance`; helper for `amm-sampling`.

signature:
NLAlib.integral_frobenius_sampled_mul_sub_sq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {t : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype t] [MeasurableSpace n] [MeasurableSingletonClass n] (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (B : Matrix n t ℂ)
  (p : n → NNReal) (hp : ∑ i, p i = 1)
  (hsupport : ∀ (i : n), p i = 0 → (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun a => A a i) fun b => B i b) = 0) {c : ℕ} (hc : 0 < c) :
  (∫ (ω : Fin c → n),
      ‖NLAlib.sampledColumnMatrix A p ω * NLAlib.sampledRowMatrix B p ω - A * B‖ ^
        2 ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => NLAlib.finiteSamplingLaw p hp) =
    1 / ↑c * (∑ i, ((∑ a, ‖A a i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ b, ‖B i b‖ ^ 2) / ↑(p i) - ‖A * B‖ ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.integral_frobenius_sampled_mul_sub_sq
doc:
Exact Frobenius mean-square error for independently sampled, literally
rescaled columns and rows, with arbitrary admissible probabilities and
possibly zero probability on zero outer products. This includes complex
matrices and correlated entries of the deterministic factors.
Source: operator re-derivation `sa:amm-variance` and `sa:amm-theorem`.
atlas: amm-sampling (partial)

name: NLAlib.integral_frobenius_sampled_mul_sub_sq_le_of_probability_domination
doc:
Approximate column-row sampling probabilities give the exact complex
mean-square upper bound. Zero-mass support is derived from domination;
the estimator is the actual rescaled sampled column/row product.
Source: operator re-derivation `sa:amm-theorem`, approximate-law variant.
atlas: amm-sampling

signature:

              A * B‖ ^

      ((∑ i, NLAlib.columnRowWeight A B i) ^ 2 - ‖A * B‖ ^ 2) / ↑c ∧

product has exact mean-square error `(W² − ‖AB‖F²)/c`, bounded by

matrix `G` with `r + 4 ≤ k` and `i ≠ j`, with `N = (G Gᵀ)⁻¹`,

(`integrable_and_integral_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self_sq_gaussianMatrix`). Ported from

Standard Gamma-integral computation (e.g. HMT 2011, proof of Lemma A.10; Johnson–Kotz–
Balakrishnan, ch. 18). Proof: Euler representation of `S^{-q}` and of `(1 + 2v)^{-d/2}`, Tonelli,

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m' : Type u_8} {q' : Type u_9} [Fintype m']

  (hA : A = U₁ * S₁ * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose) (hU₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂)
  (hV₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁) (hV₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂) (hV : V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
  (hp : 2 ≤ p) (Ω : Ωs → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin (k + p)) ℝ)
  (hΩ : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Ω (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin n) (Fin (k + p))) μ) (Q : Ωs → Matrix m' q' ℝ)
  (hQo : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols (Q ω))
  (hQr : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, Q ω * ((Q ω).transpose * (A * Ω ω)) = A * Ω ω) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.projResidual (Q ω) A) ∂μ ≤
    (1 + √(↑k / (↑p - 1))) * NLAlib.specNorm S₂ + Real.exp 1 * √(↑k + ↑p) / ↑p * NLAlib.frobNorm S₂
name: NLAlib.integral_specNorm_residual_le_of_gaussian
doc:
**Expected spectral error of the randomized range finder** (HMT 2011, Thm 10.6): for a
block decomposition `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ` (hypotheses of
`specNorm_residual_sq_le_of_range_subset`), an `n × (k+p)` standard Gaussian test matrix `Ω`
with `k ≥ 1`, `p ≥ 2`, and any `Q ω` with a.s. orthonormal columns and `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`,
`E‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖ ≤ (1 + √(k/(p−1)))‖Σ₂‖ + (e√(k+p)/p)‖Σ₂‖_F`.

With the SVD blocks, `‖Σ₂‖ = σ_{k+1}` and `‖Σ₂‖_F = (Σ_{j>k} σ_j²)^{1/2}`, which is HMT's
printed form. Deviations: `k ≥ 1` instead of HMT's `k ≥ 2` (one-row endpoint, manuscript
`sa:expected-power`); the general block form (same hypotheses as `rsvd_main_gaussian`); no
measurability of `Q` is required (the left side is `0` if not integrable, and the bound is
nonnegative); `n`, `k`, `p`, `r`, `r'` are `Fin` sizes (Gaussian law convention).
Atlas `rsvd-spectral-expected` (new; uses `hmt-9-1-spectral`, `chevet`,
`pinv-spectral-expectation`, `pinv-frob-moment`, `gaussian-conditioning`,
`gaussian-full-rank-ae`).
atlas: rsvd-spectral-expected

    -(G.submatrix i.succAbove id * (G.submatrix i.succAbove id).transpose)⁻¹.mulVec

indexed by `Fin (n + 1)`, let `H` be `G` with row `i` removed and `g = G i`. If `H Hᵀ` is
invertible, then for every `a`, `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢ,ₛ₍ₐ₎ = -cₐ (G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢᵢ` with `s = i.succAbove` and

companion of `inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`. Atlas: `inverse-wishart-frob-moment`
(helper). Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.schur_offdiag_inv` (adjugate
computation).

Wall (1948), Ch. XI.

over `x₀ + K_k(A, r₀)`). No grade hypothesis: after the grade the state is frozen at the
solution. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1–38.2; Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.7;
KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.6. Proof: `cgRecurrence_mem_krylovSpace`, `cgRecurrence_r_eq` and
Galerkin orthogonality `dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero_of_mem`, then
`isCGIterate_of_forall_dotProduct_eq_zero`. Uses atlas `cg-convergence` (the predicate).
Deviation: the brief's form had `k ≤ krylovGrade A r₀`; the statement holds for all `k`.
atlas: cg-recurrence

signature:
NLAlib.isFullQR_householderQR {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsFullQR A (NLAlib.householderQ A) (NLAlib.householderR A)
name: NLAlib.isFullQR_householderQR
doc:
**Realisation of Householder QR**: `(householderQ A, householderR A)` is a full QR of every
real `m × n` matrix, with `Q` the product of `min m n` reflectors; no rank or shape
hypothesis (unlike Gram–Schmidt). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10, Alg. 10.1 and Thm 7.1
(existence via Householder); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 5.2.1. Proof: induction on `m`, each
step being `isFullQR_mul_borderedUpper` with `W = H_v` (symmetric, orthogonal), whose first
column condition is `householder_mulVec_householderVector`.
atlas: householder-qr

name: NLAlib.isFullQR_mul_borderedUpper
doc:
**One step of a full QR**: if `W` is orthogonal, `B = WᵀA` has zeros below the pivot in its
first column, and `B(1:, 1:) = Q'R'` is a full QR, then
`A = (W · diag(1, Q')) · [[B(0, :)], [0, R']]` is a full QR. This is the inductive step of every
orthogonal triangularisation (Householder, Givens, orthogonal completion).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 10, eq. (10.1)–(10.3); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.2.

name: NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_forall_dotProduct_eq_zero
doc:
**Petrov–Galerkin characterisation.** `x` is a GMRES iterate iff `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` and
the residual is orthogonal to `A K_q(A, r₀)`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 5.3 and
§6.5.1; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_isAffineMinimizer.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) :
  NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x ↔
    NLAlib.IsAffineMinimizer (fun y => NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Polynomial.X ^ 2)) (y - xs)) x₀

doc:
**MINRES is the class theorem's minimiser with weight `g = X²`.** For symmetric `A` and
`A x⋆ = c`, `x` is a GMRES iterate iff it minimises `‖· − x⋆‖²_{A²} = quadForm (A²) (· − x⋆)`
over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`; so `quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimizer` with `g = X²` applies.
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.2; KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `minres-bound` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.isGradedKrylovBasis_golubKahanU_V.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {k : ℕ} (h : NLAlib.GolubKahanSucceeds A b k) :
  NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis (A * A.transpose) b (NLAlib.golubKahanU A b (k + 1)) ∧
    NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis (A.transpose * A) (A.transpose.mulVec b) (NLAlib.golubKahanV A b (k + 1))
name: NLAlib.isGradedKrylovBasis_golubKahanU_V
doc:
SCAFFOLD: golub-kahan-bidiagonalization
**Realisation.** If the recursion does not break down through state `k`, then `[u₁ … u_{k+1}]`
is a graded orthonormal Krylov basis of `(AAᵀ, b)` and `[v₁ … v_{k+1}]` one of `(AᵀA, Aᵀb)`.
Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §10.4.1; Paige–Saunders (1982), §3. Proof sketch:
induction on `k` with the invariant "the two matrices are graded orthonormal bases"; membership
`u_{j+1} ∈ K_{j+2}(AAᵀ, b)` and `v_{j+1} ∈ K_{j+2}(AᵀA, Aᵀb)` from
`mulVec_mem_krylovSpace_mul_transpose`/`transpose_mulVec_mem_krylovSpace`; orthogonality of the
new `u` to `u_1..u_{j}` is the usual Lanczos short-recurrence argument
(`GolubKahanDecomp.B_apply_eq_zero_of_lt`/`…_of_add_one_lt` applied to the previous bases),
and `IsGradedKrylovBasis.of_mem`. Equivalently, it is Lanczos on
`[[0, A], [Aᵀ, 0]]` started at `(b, 0)` (D-E's `lanczosRecurrence`). Difficulty 3.
atlas: golub-kahan-recurrence

signature:
NLAlib.isGradedKrylovBasis_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}
  {Q : Matrix n (Fin q) ℝ} :
  NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis A b Q ↔
    NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q ∧ ∀ (j : Fin q), Q.col j ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (↑j + 1)
name: NLAlib.isGradedKrylovBasis_iff
doc: Characterisation of graded bases by membership. Atlas: `graded-krylov-basis-def`.

name: NLAlib.isGradedKrylovBasis_lanczosRecurrence
doc:
**The recursion produces a graded Krylov basis**: for symmetric `A` and `q ≤ ν(A, b)`, the
matrix with columns `q_0, …, q_{q−1}` of the recursion is a graded orthonormal Krylov basis (it
is `arnoldiMatrix A b q`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36; Saad (2011)
[`saad11`], Prop. 6.14. Uses atlas `graded-krylov-basis-def`.

Variational formula for the trace: for positive definite `M`, `tr M` is the greatest value of `tr

**Symmetry is preserved**: if `A` is symmetric then so is every `A_k`. Source:

Unitary conjugation preserves Hermitian matrices. Source: unitary functional
calculus, Tropp 2015, §2.1; atlas `golden-thompson` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.isHessenbergForm_hessenbergReduction {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :

**Realisation of Hessenberg reduction**: `(hessenbergQ A, hessenbergH A)` is a Hessenberg
form of every square `A`, with `Q` a product of `n − 2` Householder reflectors.

signature:
NLAlib.isLU_lu {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.LUSucceeds A) :
  NLAlib.IsLU A (NLAlib.lu A).1 (NLAlib.lu A).2
name: NLAlib.isLU_lu
doc:
**Realisation of Gaussian elimination**: if every pivot is nonzero, `lu` returns an LU
factorization. Proof: induction on `n`; the step is
`eq_borderedMatrix_mul_borderedMatrix_pivotSchur` with the factorization of the Schur
complement in the trailing blocks. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 20.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013,
Alg. 3.2.1.
atlas: lu-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.isLU_lu_of_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ}
  (h : ∀ k < n, NLAlib.leadingMinor A k ≠ 0) : NLAlib.IsLU A (NLAlib.lu A).1 (NLAlib.lu A).2
name: NLAlib.isLU_lu_of_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero
doc:
**Realisation of Gaussian elimination under the minimal hypothesis**: if the leading
principal minors of orders `1, …, n − 1` are nonzero, `lu A` is an LU factorization (the last
pivot is never divided by, so `det A` may vanish). Proof: induction on `n`; the `1 × 1` case is
trivial, otherwise the pivot is `det A(1:1,1:1) ≠ 0` and the Schur complement inherits the
hypothesis through `leadingMinor_succ_eq_mul_leadingMinor_pivotSchur`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.2.1; Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 20.1.
atlas: lu-algorithm

name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_eq_toEuclideanLin_pinv
doc:
Full column rank makes the Euclidean Moore–Penrose solution the
unique solution of the native least-squares predicate. Trefethen–Bau, Lecture 11.

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_dotProduct.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x ↔
    ∀ (y : n → ℝ), (b - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec x) ≤ (b - A.mulVec y) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec y)
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_dotProduct
doc: The dot-product form of `IsLeastSquaresSolution`: `x` minimises `(b - A y) ⬝ᵥ (b - A y)`.

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_eq_inv_mulVec_of_eq_mul.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A Q : Matrix m n ℝ} {R : Matrix n n ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hA : A = Q * R) (hR : IsUnit R) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x ↔ x = R⁻¹.mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_eq_inv_mulVec_of_eq_mul
doc:
**Least squares via thin QR.** If `A = Q R` with `QᵀQ = I` (`HasOrthonormalCols Q`) and `R`
square invertible, the least-squares solutions are exactly `x = R⁻¹ Qᵀ b`. Trefethen–Bau 1997,
Lecture 11, Algorithm 11.2; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.3.3. Stated with explicit hypotheses so that
any thin QR (Householder, Gram–Schmidt, `IsQR`) applies; invertibility of `R` is full column
rank. Proof: `AᵀA = RᵀR`, `Aᵀb = RᵀQᵀb`, cancel the invertible `Rᵀ`.
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_eq_moorePenroseInverse_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x ↔ x = (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_eq_moorePenroseInverse_mulVec
doc:
Under full column rank the least-squares solution is `A⁺ b`. Trefethen–Bau 1997,
Lecture 11 (eq. (11.10)).
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_eq_pinvL_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x ↔ x = (NLAlib.pinvL A).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_eq_pinvL_mulVec
doc:
Under full column rank the least-squares solution is `(Aᵀ A)⁻¹ Aᵀ b` (`pinvL`), the solution
of the normal equations. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11, eq. (11.9); Golub–Van Loan 2013,
§5.3.1.
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_euclidean_norm_min.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : EuclideanSpace ℝ m) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b.ofLp x.ofLp ↔
    ∀ (z : EuclideanSpace ℝ n), ‖b - (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) x‖ ≤ ‖b - (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) z‖
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_euclidean_norm_min
doc:
The native least-squares predicate is equivalent to Euclidean residual
norm minimization. Trefethen–Bau, Lecture 11; no rank assumption is needed.

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_forall_dotProduct_mulVec_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x ↔ ∀ (y : n → ℝ), (b - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec y = 0
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_forall_dotProduct_mulVec_eq_zero
doc:
A least-squares solution is exactly a vector whose residual is orthogonal to `range A`:
`(b - A x) ⬝ (A y) = 0` for all `y`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11, Thm 11.1 (the condition
`r ⟂ range(A)`).
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_mulVec_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x ↔ A.mulVec x = (A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_mulVec_eq
doc:
The fitted vector is unique: `x` is a least-squares solution iff `A x = A A⁺ b`, the
orthogonal projection of `b` onto `range A`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11, Thm 11.1
(`Ax = Pb`).
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_transpose_mulVec_mulVec_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b x ↔ A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec x) = A.transpose.mulVec b
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_iff_transpose_mulVec_mulVec_eq
doc:
**Normal equations.** `x` is a least-squares solution iff `Aᵀ A x = Aᵀ b`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11, Thm 11.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.3.1. Proof: `(⇐)` Pythagoras
(`dotProduct_sub_mulVec_eq_add_of_transpose_mulVec_eq_zero`); `(⇒)` perturb `x` along
`g = Aᵀ(b - A x)`: `‖b - A(x + t g)‖² = ‖r‖² - 2t‖g‖² + t²‖Ag‖²`, minimal at `t = 0` only if
`g = 0`.
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_moorePenroseInverse_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b)
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_moorePenroseInverse_mulVec
doc:
**Pseudoinverse solution.** `A⁺ b` is a least-squares solution for every `A` (any rank,
any shape, including empty dimensions). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lecture 11 (eq. (11.10)) and
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.5.2; proof by the normal equations and `Aᵀ A A⁺ = Aᵀ`.
atlas: least-squares-normal-equations (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_toEuclideanLin_pinv.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : EuclideanSpace ℝ m) :
  NLAlib.IsLeastSquaresSolution A b.ofLp ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) b).ofLp
name: NLAlib.isLeastSquaresSolution_toEuclideanLin_pinv
doc:
The Euclidean Moore–Penrose solution satisfies the native
least-squares predicate. Trefethen–Bau, Lecture 11; every rank is included.

name: NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_minimax
doc:
The Chebyshev minimax theorem on `[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`: the least possible bound `M` for
`|p|` on `[a, b]` over polynomials `p` of degree at most `q` with `p(0) = 1` is
`1 / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`, attained by `chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Trefethen–Bau (1997), Thm 38.5;
Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.
atlas: chebyshev-minimax

signature:
NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_monic_minimax (q : ℕ) :
  IsLeast {M | ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M} (1 / 2 ^ (q - 1))
name: NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_monic_minimax
doc:
The monic Chebyshev minimax theorem: over monic real polynomials of degree `q`, the least
possible bound for `|p|` on `[−1, 1]` is `1 / 2^(q−1)`, attained by `2^(1−q) T_q`.
Source: Trefethen (2013), Thm 2.2 / Rivlin (1990), Cor. 2.1.1; Atlas: `chebyshev-monic-minimal`.
Deviation: stated for all `q`, including `q = 0` (where the value is `1`).
atlas: chebyshev-monic-minimal

signature:
NLAlib.isLeast_frobSq_sub_orthogonal_mul.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) :

doc:
One-sided Procrustes has the advertised minimum, attained by an
orthogonal polar factor of the cross-product. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.4.
atlas: orthogonal-procrustes (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isLeast_frobSq_sub_orthogonal_mul_mul.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) :

doc:
Two-sided orthogonal Procrustes has the exact singular-value squared
distance as its minimum. SVD alignment supplies the attained rotations,
including rank-deficient and empty shapes. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.5.
atlas: orthogonal-procrustes (partial)

NLAlib.isLeast_frobSq_sub_scaled_orthogonal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)

name: NLAlib.isLeast_frobSq_sub_scaled_orthogonal
doc:
The scaled orthogonal Procrustes problem has its explicit attained
minimum at positive dimension, allowing positive or negative real scalars.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.6.
atlas: orthogonal-procrustes (partial)

NLAlib.isLeast_frobSq_sub_scaled_orthogonal_of_isEmpty.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [IsEmpty n]

doc:
In dimension zero the unique square matrix has scaled-orthogonal error
zero; no ordinary quotient by the dimension is used. Horn–Johnson §7.4.6,
frontier derivations' endpoint convention.
atlas: orthogonal-procrustes (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isLeast_generalizedSchurComplement_quadratic.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}

variable: `xᴴ (M / A) x = min_y (y, x)ᴴ M (y, x)` for `M ⪰ 0`. Albert 1969, Theorem 1.

signature:
NLAlib.isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A P W : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hW : W.transpose * P * W = 1) {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} :
  NLAlib.IsPCGIterate A P c x₀ q x ↔
    NLAlib.IsCGIterate (W.transpose * A * W) (W.transpose.mulVec c) (W⁻¹.mulVec x₀) q (W⁻¹.mulVec x)
name: NLAlib.isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate
doc:
**PCG is CG on the split-preconditioned system.** If `Wᵀ P W = I` (so `P⁻¹ = WWᵀ`), then `x`
is a PCG iterate for `(A, P, c, x₀)` iff `W⁻¹x` is a CG iterate for `WᵀAW ŷ = Wᵀc` from
`W⁻¹x₀`. With `W = P^{-1/2}` this is CG on `P^{-1/2} A P^{-1/2}`; with `W = L⁻ᵀ`, `P = LLᵀ`,
CG on `L⁻¹AL⁻ᵀ`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §9.2.1 (split preconditioning).
atlas: preconditioned-cg (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isPLU_luPartialPivot {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsPLU A (NLAlib.luPartialPivot A).1 (NLAlib.luPartialPivot A).2.1 (NLAlib.luPartialPivot A).2.2
name: NLAlib.isPLU_luPartialPivot
doc:
**Realisation of partial pivoting**, for every square `A` (no invertibility hypothesis):
`luPartialPivot A` is a factorization `PA = LU`. When the pivot is zero the whole column is
zero and the junk multipliers `0⁻¹ · 0 = 0` give a valid step. Proof: induction on `n`, the step
is the elimination identity for `partialPivotSwap A` conjugated by the permutation of the
trailing rows. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 21; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.4.1 (existence for
singular `A` as in the atlas note).
atlas: lu-partial-pivoting

signature:
NLAlib.isPivotedCholesky_choleskyPivoted {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) :
  NLAlib.IsPivotedCholesky A (NLAlib.choleskyPivoted A).1 (NLAlib.choleskyPivoted A).2
name: NLAlib.isPivotedCholesky_choleskyPivoted
doc:
**Pivoted Cholesky never fails on a positive semidefinite matrix**: `choleskyPivoted A` is
a pivoted Cholesky factorization. Proof: induction on `n`; `diagPivotSwap A` and its Schur
complement stay PSD (`posSemidef_pivotSchur`), a zero pivot has a zero column
(`apply_eq_zero_of_posSemidef_of_apply_self_eq_zero`), and the step is the computation of
`eq_cholesky_mul_transpose_of_pivotSchur` conjugated by the trailing permutation.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9; Higham 2002, Thm 10.9.
atlas: cholesky-algorithm

signature:

doc:
**Realisation of modified Gram–Schmidt**: when Gram–Schmidt succeeds (linearly independent
columns), MGS produces a thin QR of `A`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 8.1, Thm 7.2;
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.8.
atlas: gram-schmidt

**`A^k = Q^{(k)} R^{(k)}` is a QR factorization of `A^k`**: the unshifted QR algorithm

atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

A real normal matrix already in corrected real Schur form has opposite
off-diagonal entries. Hence the nonscalar blocks are rotation-dilations.

Joining a scalar or nonreal real Schur block to a real Schur tail gives

signature:

A nonzero eigenvector forces its eigenvalue to be a characteristic root.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Definition 1.4.6; includes no diagonalizability
assumption.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
Orthonormal form of a subspace embedding (Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7):
for `U` with orthonormal columns, `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` iff
`(1 - ε)‖x‖² ≤ ‖SUx‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖x‖²` for every coefficient vector `x`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.
atlas: ose-def

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq n] {S : Matrix p m ℝ} {U : Matrix m n ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U)
  {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε ↔
    ∀ (j : Fin (Fintype.card n)),
      √(1 - ε) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues (S * U) ↑j ∧ NLAlib.singularValues (S * U) ↑j ≤ √(1 + ε)
name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues
doc:
Complete singular-value OSE equivalence for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`: the sketch preserves the subspace
iff every domain singular value of `S U` lies in `[√(1−ε), √(1+ε)]`. Arbitrary finite index
types; includes empty dimensions. Atlas: `ose-def`, `svd`.
atlas: ose-def

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_specNorm_transpose_mul_self_sub_one_le
doc:
Complete Gram-form equivalence for an orthonormal frame, valid also in
empty dimensions. Atlas: `ose-def`.
atlas: ose-def

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_mul_right_iff
doc:
Basis independence (Woodruff 2014 §2.1): for invertible `C`, `S` is an `ε`-subspace
embedding for `range U` iff it is one for `range (U C)`. The property depends on the subspace
only.

Atlas: `ose-def`.
atlas: ose-def

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_forall_sqrt_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} [Fintype k]
  [Fintype m] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] {S : Matrix k m ℝ} {U : Matrix m d ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U)
  {ε a : ℝ} (hε : ε ≤ 1) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (haε : 3 * a ≤ ε)
  (hlo : ∀ (x : d → ℝ), (1 - a) * √(x ⬝ᵥ x) ≤ √((S * U).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (S * U).mulVec x))
  (hhi : ∀ (x : d → ℝ), √((S * U).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (S * U).mulVec x) ≤ (1 + a) * √(x ⬝ᵥ x)) :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε
name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_forall_sqrt_le
doc:
**Deterministic embedding criterion.** If `U` has orthonormal columns and every
`‖SUx‖` lies between `(1 − a)‖x‖` and `(1 + a)‖x‖`, with `0 ≤ a`, `3a ≤ ε ≤ 1`, then `S` is an
`ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` (since `(1 − a)² ≥ 1 − ε` and `(1 + a)² ≤ 1 + ε`).
Woodruff 2014, proof of Thm 2.3; atlas `gaussian-ose` (helper; uses `ose-def`).
atlas: gaussian-ose

signature:

With no coefficient directions, every sketch preserves the zero subspace.

Gram form of a subspace embedding (Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7), the
direction used in practice: for `U` with orthonormal columns, `‖(SU)ᵀ(SU) − I‖₂ ≤ ε` implies

`NLAlib.Sketching.Properties.SubspaceEmbedding.Gram`.

atlas: ose-def

name: NLAlib.isUpperHessenberg_givensQR_snd_mul_fst
doc:
**`RQ` is again Hessenberg** for the Givens factors of an upper Hessenberg `H`, with no
invertibility hypothesis (upper triangular × Hessenberg). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.2.
atlas: givens-rotation-def

signature:
NLAlib.isUpperHessenberg_hessenbergH {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.IsUpperHessenberg (NLAlib.hessenbergH A)
name: NLAlib.isUpperHessenberg_hessenbergH
doc:
SCAFFOLD: hessenberg-reduction
**The reduction produces a Hessenberg matrix**: `QᵀAQ` is upper Hessenberg for the Householder
`Q`, for every `A`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 26 (Alg. 26.1); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.3.
Proof sketch: induction on `n` (`k + 3`): with `P = diag(1, H_w)` and
`H_w (A(1:, 0)) = ρ e₀` (`householder_mulVec_householderVector`), the first column of `PAP` is
`(a₀₀, ρ, 0, …, 0)` (right multiplication by `P` does not touch column `0`); the recursive `Q'`
is `diag(1, Q'')`-shaped (`householder_vecCons_zero`), so `QᵀAQ` has first column
`(a₀₀, ρ, 0, …)` and trailing block `Q''ᵀ B' Q''`, Hessenberg by induction. Difficulty 3
(the bookkeeping of padded reflectors).
atlas: hessenberg-reduction

signature:
NLAlib.isUpperHessenberg_mul_of_isQR {n : ℕ} {H Q R : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hH : NLAlib.IsUpperHessenberg H)

name: NLAlib.isUpperHessenberg_mul_of_isQR
doc:
**`RQ` of a Hessenberg matrix is Hessenberg**: if `H` is upper Hessenberg and `H = QR` is a
QR factorization with `R` invertible, then `RQ` is upper Hessenberg. (`Q = HR⁻¹` is
Hessenberg, and so is `R · Q`.) The invertibility of `R` cannot be dropped for an arbitrary QR
(for singular `H` the factorization is not unique and `Q` need not be Hessenberg); for the
Givens factors see `isUpperHessenberg_givensQR_snd_mul_fst`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §7.4.2;
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 28.
atlas: givens-rotation-def

doc: An upper triangular matrix is upper Hessenberg.

Hessenberg, so is every `A_k`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 28–29; Golub–Van
Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §7.4.2. Deviation: for an arbitrary QR routine the invertibility of the
`R_j` cannot be dropped (see `isUpperHessenberg_mul_of_isQR`); with Givens rotations it can
(`isUpperHessenberg_qrAlgorithm_givensQR`).
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

signature: NLAlib.jacobiFraction (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.jacobiFraction
doc:
The finite Jacobi (Stieltjes) continued fraction with `m` levels starting at level `k`:
`jacobiFraction a β x 0 k = 0` and
`jacobiFraction a β x (m+1) k = 1 / (x − a k − β (k+1)² · jacobiFraction a β x m (k+1))`, so
`jacobiFraction a β x m 0 = 1/(x − a₀ − β₁²/(x − a₁ − ⋯ − β_{m−1}²/(x − a_{m−1})))`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3. Atlas: `jacobi-matrix-identities`.

doc: Shifting the start level of a Jacobi fraction shifts the coefficients.
