signature:
NLAlib.jl_distributional (k n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin n)).real
      {G | |((1 / √↑k) • G).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • G).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x| > ε * x ⬝ᵥ x} ≤
    2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6))
name: NLAlib.jl_distributional
doc:
**Distributional Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma** for the Gaussian sketch: for
`S = k^{-1/2} G` with `G` standard Gaussian `k × n`, any fixed `x : ℝⁿ` and `0 < ε < 1`,
`P[|‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²| > ε‖x‖²] ≤ 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Lem 2.2 (stated there for the projection of a random unit vector; the
Gaussian-sketch form is Woodruff 2014 §2.1). Atlas: `jl-distributional`; uses
`gaussian-matrix-mulVec-law`, `chi-square-upper-tail`, `chi-square-lower-tail`.

Proof: with `u = x/‖x‖`, `‖Sx‖² = (‖x‖²/k) ‖Gu‖²` and `Gu` is a standard Gaussian vector, so the
event lies in `{χ²_k ≥ (1+ε)k} ∪ {χ²_k ≤ (1−ε)k}`. The Chernoff tails and
`log(1+ε) ≤ ε − ε²/2 + ε³/3`, `log(1−ε) ≤ −ε − ε²/2` bound each part by `exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.
Degenerate cases: for `x = 0` the event is empty; for `k = 0` the bound is `2`.
atlas: jl-distributional

signature:
NLAlib.jl_distributional_of_hasLaw.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {k n : ℕ}
  {X : Ω → Matrix (Fin k) (Fin n) ℝ} (hX : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw X (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin n)) μ)
  (x : Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  μ.real {ω | |((1 / √↑k) • X ω).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • X ω).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x| > ε * x ⬝ᵥ x} ≤
    2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6))
name: NLAlib.jl_distributional_of_hasLaw
doc:
`jl_distributional` for a random matrix `X` with `HasLaw X (gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin n)) μ`.
Atlas: `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma (k n N : ℕ) (p : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin n)).real
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • G).mulVec (p i - p j) - (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ↑N ^ 2 * 2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6))
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, union-bound form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for a finite
family `p : Fin N → ℝⁿ`, the probability that the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` distorts some
pairwise squared distance `‖p i − p j‖²` by more than a factor `1 ± ε` is at most
`N² · 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deviation: the union is taken over all `N²` ordered pairs (not the `N(N−1)/2` unordered ones),
which costs a constant factor `2` in the bound. No measurability hypothesis is needed (the union
bound holds for the outer measure).

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists (k n N : ℕ) (p : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  ∃ S,
    ∀ (i j : Fin N),
      (1 - ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j) ≤ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ∧
        S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ≤ (1 + ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, existence form (Johnson–Lindenstrauss 1984; Dasgupta–Gupta
2003, Thm 2.1): any `N ≥ 2` points of `ℝⁿ` admit a linear map `S : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ` with
`k ≥ 48 log N / ε²` that preserves every pairwise squared distance to within `1 ± ε`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half (k n N : ℕ) (p : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin n)).real
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • G).mulVec (p i - p j) - (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    1 / 2
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, `O(ε⁻² log N)` form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for
`N ≥ 2` points, `0 < ε < 1` and `k ≥ 48 log N / ε²`, the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G`
distorts some pairwise squared distance by more than `1 ± ε` with probability at most `1/2`.

Deviation: the explicit constant `48` (from `(ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ ≤ 12/ε²` and
`log(4N²) ≤ 4 log N` for `N ≥ 2`) is not optimised; Dasgupta–Gupta's constant is `4·(1/2 − ε/3)⁻¹`
at failure probability `1 − 1/N`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le (k n N : ℕ) (p : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin n) ℝ) {ε δ : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1)
  (hδ : 0 < δ) (hk : (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)⁻¹ * Real.log (2 * ↑N ^ 2 / δ) ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin n)).real
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • G).mulVec (p i - p j) - (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    δ
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma with explicit dimension (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): if
`0 < ε < 1`, `0 < δ` and `k ≥ (ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ log(2N²/δ)`, then with probability at least
`1 − δ` the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` preserves all pairwise squared distances of
`p : Fin N → ℝⁿ` to within `1 ± ε`.

Deviation: Dasgupta–Gupta take `k ≥ 4 (ε²/2 − ε³/3)⁻¹ log N`, aiming at success probability
`1/N`; we state the general-`δ` form with the constant coming from the ordered-pair union bound
in `jl_lemma`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (Q : Matrix n k ℝ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox
doc:
The Krylov (Lanczos-FA) approximation of `f(A) b` from a basis matrix `Q`:
`Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b`, with `f(QᵀAQ) = cfc f (Qᵀ * A * Q)`. With the Lanczos basis, `Qᵀ b = ‖b‖ e₁`
and this is `‖b‖ Q f(T_q) e₁`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], eq. (3.2); Higham (2008)
[`higham08`], §13.2. Deviation: any `Q` (the theorems assume orthonormal columns and
`K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (definition).

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_congr.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype k'] [DecidableEq k']
  {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} {Q' : Matrix n k' ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q')
  (hR : Q.mulVecLin.range = Q'.mulVecLin.range) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.krylovFunApprox A f b Q = NLAlib.krylovFunApprox A f b Q'
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_congr
doc:
**Lanczos-FA depends only on the range of `Q`.** If `Q` and `Q'` have orthonormal columns
and the same range, then `Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b = Q' f(Q'ᵀAQ') Q'ᵀ b` (for `Q' = QU` with `U`
orthogonal, `f(UᵀTU) = Uᵀ f(T) U`). Source: `docs/KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS.md` §3.9; Saad (1992)
[`saad92`], §3 (basis-independence of the Krylov projection).
Deviation: `A` symmetric (for nonsymmetric `A` the real `cfc` is not the matrix function).
Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper: basis independence of the approximant).

name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eq_aeval_interpolate
doc:
**Lanczos-FA is the interpolant at the Ritz values.** If `Q` has at most `q` columns, then
`krylovFunApprox A f b Q = p(A) b` for the Lagrange interpolant `p` of `f` at the distinct
eigenvalues of `QᵀAQ`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.3.
Deviation: `Q` is any orthonormal matrix with at most `q` columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q` (the
source takes the Lanczos basis, `range Q = K_q`); the Ritz values are interpolated without
multiplicity (Lagrange, not Hermite), which suffices because `f(T)` only sees `f` on `spec T`.
Atlas: proposed id `lanczos-fa-interpolation`; uses `krylov-polynomial-exactness`.
atlas: lanczos-fa-interpolation

name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eq_aeval_of_forall_eval_eq
doc:
**Lanczos-FA interpolates at the Ritz values (general form).** If `p` has `deg p < q` and
agrees with `f` at the eigenvalues of `T = QᵀAQ` (the Ritz values), then
`krylovFunApprox A f b Q = p(A) b`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.3.
Deviation: any orthonormal `Q` with `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`; Lagrange (not Hermite)
interpolation, the agreement being only required at the Ritz values.
Atlas: proposed id `lanczos-fa-interpolation`; uses `krylov-polynomial-exactness`.
atlas: lanczos-fa-interpolation

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eval_eq_aeval.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < ↑q) :
  NLAlib.krylovFunApprox A (fun x => Polynomial.eval x p) b Q = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eval_eq_aeval
doc:
**Lanczos-FA is exact on polynomials.** For symmetric `A`, `Q` with orthonormal columns and
`K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, `krylovFunApprox A p b Q = p(A) b` for every `p` with `deg p < q`.
Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Lemma 3.1.
Deviation: the matrix-function form needs `A` symmetric (so that `QᵀAQ` is self-adjoint and
`cfc` is the polynomial calculus); `mulVec_aeval_transpose_mul_mul_mulVec_eq` is the form for
any `A`.
atlas: krylov-polynomial-exactness (partial)

signature: NLAlib.krylovGrade.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) : ℕ

doc:
The Ky Fan sums obey the triangle inequality on arbitrary finite matrix indices,
including the zero prefix and all zero-padded prefixes.

name: NLAlib.lanczosAlpha
doc:
The recursion's diagonal coefficient `α_j = q_jᵀ A q_j`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Alg. 36.1. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosAlpha_eq_alpha.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (h : q ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < q) :
  NLAlib.lanczosAlpha A b j = NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.alpha (NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp A b q h) j
name: NLAlib.lanczosAlpha_eq_alpha
doc:
**The recursion's `α` are the diagonal of the canonical Jacobi matrix**: for symmetric `A`,
`q ≤ ν(A, b)` and `j < q`, `α_j = (arnoldiDecomp A b q h).alpha j`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 36; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Alg. 4.1.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence-algorithm (partial)

signature: NLAlib.lanczosBeta.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta
doc:
The recursion's off-diagonal coefficient `β_j = ‖w_{j−1}‖` (`β_0 = 0`), the same indexing
as `LanczosDecomp.beta`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 36.1.
Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosBeta_add_two_smul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b (j + 2) • NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b (j + 2) =
    A.mulVec (NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b (j + 1)) -
        NLAlib.lanczosAlpha A b (j + 1) • NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b (j + 1) -
      NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b (j + 1) • NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b j
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_add_two_smul
doc:
**The three-term relation of the recursion**: `β_{j+2} q_{j+2} = A q_{j+1} − α_{j+1} q_{j+1}
− β_{j+1} q_j`, i.e. `A q_{j+1} = β_{j+1} q_j + α_{j+1} q_{j+1} + β_{j+2} q_{j+2}`. No hypothesis on
`A` (it is how the recursion is built). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 36.1 and
eq. (36.3). Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosBeta_eq_beta.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (h : q ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < q) :
  NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b j = NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.beta (NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp A b q h) j
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_eq_beta
doc:
**The recursion's `β` are the off-diagonal of the canonical Jacobi matrix**: for symmetric
`A`, `q ≤ ν(A, b)` and `j < q`, `β_j = (arnoldiDecomp A b q h).beta j` (both `0` at `j = 0`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Alg. 4.1.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence-algorithm (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosBeta_eq_zero_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (b : n → ℝ) {j : ℕ} (h0 : 0 < j) : NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b j = 0 ↔ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b ≤ j
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_eq_zero_iff
doc:
**Breakdown characterisation**: for symmetric `A` and `j > 0`, `β_j = 0 ↔ ν(A, b) ≤ j`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.6.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence-algorithm (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosBeta_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (b : n → ℝ) {j : ℕ} (hj : NLAlib.krylovGrade A b ≤ j) : NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b j = 0
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
**`β` vanishes from the grade on**: for symmetric `A`, `β_j = 0` for `j ≥ ν(A, b)`; with
`lanczosBeta_pos`, the recursion breaks down (`β = 0`) exactly at the grade.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.6.
Proof: `lanczosBeta_succ_eq_dotProduct` and `arnoldiBasis_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le`.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence-algorithm (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosBeta_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) :
  0 ≤ NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b j
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_nonneg
doc: `β_j = ‖w_{j−1}‖ ≥ 0`. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosBeta_one_smul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b 1 • NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b 1 =
    A.mulVec (NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b 0) - NLAlib.lanczosAlpha A b 0 • NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b 0
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_one_smul
doc:
**First step of the recursion**: `β_1 q_1 = A q_0 − α_0 q_0`. No hypothesis on `A`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 36.1. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosBeta_pos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (b : n → ℝ) {j : ℕ} (h0 : 0 < j) (hj : j < NLAlib.krylovGrade A b) : 0 < NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b j
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_pos
doc:
**`β` is positive below the grade**: for symmetric `A`, `0 < β_j` for `0 < j < ν(A, b)`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Alg. 4.1.
Proof: `lanczosBeta_succ_eq_dotProduct` and `arnoldiDecomp_H_subdiag_pos`.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence-algorithm (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosBeta_succ_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b (j + 1) =
    NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b (j + 1) ⬝ᵥ
      (A.mulVec (NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b j) - NLAlib.lanczosAlpha A b j • NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b j -
        NLAlib.lanczosBeta A b j • (NLAlib.lanczosState A b j).prev)
name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_succ_eq
doc:
The recursion's `β_{j+1}` is `q_{j+1}ᵀ w_j`, with `w_j = A q_j − α_j q_j − β_j q_{j−1}`
(`q_{−1} = 0`). No hypothesis on `A`. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

name: NLAlib.lanczosBeta_succ_eq_dotProduct
doc:
**The recursion's `β` is the subdiagonal of the Arnoldi matrix**: for symmetric `A` and every
`j`, `β_{j+1} = q_{j+1}ᵀ A q_j` with `q = arnoldiBasis A b`. Proof: `lanczosBeta_succ_eq`,
`lanczosRecurrence_eq_arnoldiBasis` and orthogonality (`arnoldiBasis_dotProduct_of_ne`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`
(partial).

name: NLAlib.lanczosInit
doc:
The initial state `(0, b/‖b‖, 0)` (`q_0 = 0` when `b = 0`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (b : ι → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError
doc:
The relative error of the largest Ritz value of `K_{q+1}(A, b)` (`q` matvecs) against the
spectral norm: `(‖A‖₂ − θ_max(K_{q+1}))/‖A‖₂` (`= (λ_max − θ_max)/λ_max` for positive
semidefinite `A`; junk value `0` at `A = 0`).
Source: Kuczyński–Woźniakowski (1992) [`kw92`], §2.
atlas: random-start-power

name: NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError_le_log_sq
doc:
**Random-start Lanczos, deterministic bound.** Let `A` be positive semidefinite with
`‖A‖₂ > 0`, `u` a unit eigenvector of the top eigenvalue `λ₀(A)`, and `u ⬝ b ≠ 0`. Then after
`q ≥ 1` matvecs the relative error of the largest Ritz value obeys the squared logarithmic-overlap
bound `(λ_max − θ_max)/λ_max ≤ 4 (1 + log(‖b‖²/(u ⬝ b)²)/log 2)²/q²`. No spectral gap or
simplicity of the top eigenvalue is required.
Source: Kuczyński–Woźniakowski (1992) [`kw92`], Thm 4.2 (deterministic step, §3).
atlas: random-start-power (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError_le_one.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {A : Matrix ι ι ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (b : ι → ℝ) (q : ℕ) : NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError A b q ≤ 1
name: NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError_le_one
doc: The Lanczos relative error is at most `1`. Helper for `random-start-power`.

NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError_nonneg.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ)
  (b : ι → ℝ) (q : ℕ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError A b q
name: NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError_nonneg

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRayleighRelativeError_zero.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : ι → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :

signature: NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence
doc:
The **Lanczos vectors** `q_j` of the three-term recursion (0-based). For symmetric `A` they
are the Arnoldi vectors (`lanczosRecurrence_eq_arnoldiBasis`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Alg. 36.1. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence_eq_arnoldiBasis.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (b : n → ℝ) (j : ℕ) : NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b j = NLAlib.arnoldiBasis A b j
name: NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence_eq_arnoldiBasis
doc:
SCAFFOLD: lanczos-recurrence-algorithm
**The three-term recursion is the Arnoldi process**: for symmetric `A`, `q_j = arnoldiBasis A b j`
for every `j` (below the grade the Gram–Schmidt vectors with positive `β`; from the grade on both
sides are `0`). Sign convention verified: the recursion has `q_0ᵀ b = ‖b‖ > 0` and
`q_{j+1}ᵀ A q_j = q_{j+1}ᵀ w_j = ‖w_j‖ ≥ 0` (`lanczosBeta_succ_eq`), the signs of the canonical
decomposition (`arnoldiBasis_zero_dotProduct_pos`, `arnoldiDecomp_H_subdiag_pos`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 36.1 and Lect. 36; Saad (2011) [`saad11`],
Alg. 6.15 and Prop. 6.14; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2.
Proof sketch: strong induction on `j`, carrying also `β_j = arnoldiBasis j ⬝ A arnoldiBasis (j−1)`.
Case `j + 1 < ν` (grade): apply `LanczosDecomp.mulVec_vec_eq` to `D = arnoldiDecomp A b (j + 2)`,
so `w_j = A q_j − α_j q_j − β_j q_{j−1} = β'_{j+1} q'_{j+1}` with `β'_{j+1} > 0`
(`beta_arnoldiDecomp_pos`) and `q'_{j+1}` a unit vector; hence `‖w_j‖ = β'_{j+1}` and
`q_{j+1} = q'_{j+1}`. Case `j + 1 = ν`: `A q_j ∈ K_ν` (`mulVec_mem_krylovSpace_krylovGrade`),
its coordinates in `arnoldiDecomp A b ν` are those of `α_j q_j + β_j q_{j−1}` (tridiagonality,
`T_apply_eq_zero_of_one_lt_dist`), so `w_j = 0` (`eq_of_forall_col_dotProduct_eq`) and
`q_ν = 0 = arnoldiBasis ν` (`arnoldiBasis_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le`). Case `j + 1 > ν`: the
state is `(0, 0, 0)` or `(q_{ν−1}, 0, 0)`, so `w_j = 0`. Base: `q_0 = b/‖b‖ = arnoldiBasis 0`
(`gramSchmidtNormed` of `b`). Uses atlas `lanczos-recurrence`, `graded-krylov-basis-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (b : n → ℝ) {j : ℕ} (hj : NLAlib.krylovGrade A b ≤ j) : NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b j = 0
name: NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
The recursion's vectors vanish from the grade on: `q_j = 0` for `j ≥ ν(A, b)` (symmetric `A`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence A b 0 = ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖⁻¹ • b
name: NLAlib.lanczosRecurrence_zero
doc: `q_0 = b/‖b‖`. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence-algorithm`.

signature: NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue
doc:
The largest eigenvalue of the canonical orthonormal Krylov compression.
Its dimension is `dim K_q(A,b)`, so breakdown never pads the spectrum with zero.
The trivial Krylov space and non-Hermitian matrices have the declared value zero.
Source: Parlett (1998), Thm 11.4.1; Kuczyński–Woźniakowski (1992), §2.
atlas: random-start-power

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue_eq_iSup_rat.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue A b q =
    if q = 0 then 0
    else
      ⨆ c,
        have v := NLAlib.krylovCoefficientVector A b fun j => ↑(c j);
        if v = 0 then NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A b else NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A v
name: NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue_eq_iSup_rat
doc:
A rational-coefficient expression for the largest Ritz value. Zero coefficient images are
replaced by the starting quotient, which belongs to the same nonzero domain when the start is
nonzero and `q > 0`. Thus negative Ritz values are retained.
Source: Kuczyński–Woźniakowski (1992), §2 (variational form) and rational density.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue_eq_lambdaMax.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue A b q =
    NLAlib.lambdaMax
      ((NLAlib.orthonormalBasisMatrix (NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q)).conjTranspose * A *
        NLAlib.orthonormalBasisMatrix (NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q))
name: NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue_eq_lambdaMax
doc: The canonical largest Krylov Ritz value is the extreme eigenvalue of its compression.

signature:
NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue_eq_ritzValues.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {r : Type u_2} [Fintype r]
  [DecidableEq r] [Nonempty r] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) {Q : Matrix n r ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hspan : Q.mulVecLin.range = NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q) :
  NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue A b q = NLAlib.ritzValues hA Q hQ ⟨0, ⋯⟩

doc:
Any orthonormal basis spanning the Krylov space gives its largest Ritz value.
The nonempty frame condition ensures there is a largest eigenvalue.
Source: Parlett (1998), Thm 11.4.1.

name: NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue_eq_sSup_rayleigh
doc:
The variational bridge for the largest Krylov Ritz value excludes the zero vector.
Source: Parlett (1998), Thm 11.4.1.

NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue_eq_zero_of_space_eq_bot.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)

Under PSD comparison with a positive definite first matrix, the relative
spectral radius is at most one exactly when the smaller matrix is below the

the absolute real spectrum, including empty dimensions.

Each PSD variance increment is bounded by the cumulative variance including it.

doc:
A continuous real-valued inequality valid on the positive definite cone
extends to every PSD matrix by adding a positive scalar identity and taking
the right-hand limit. Empty dimensions are included.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.8; helper for determinant boundary cases.

doc:
For a real PSD matrix, being bounded above by identity is equivalent to
operator norm at most one. Empty dimensions are included. Horn--Johnson

`n` (0-based: row `i` of the block is row `(i + 1)`-th smallest index of `A`). Entries with

NLAlib.leaveOneOutDeflatedTraceEstimate.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {κ : Type u_4}

doc:
The supplied leave-one-out deflated trace kernel: the average over `i` of
`tr(Qᵢᵀ A Qᵢ) + ωᵢᵀ (I − QᵢQᵢᵀ) A (I − QᵢQᵢᵀ) ωᵢ`, where `Qᵢ` is supplied. No sketch-span condition is imposed by this kernel.

NLAlib.leverageSamplingSketch_mul.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {d : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

signature: NLAlib.leverageScore.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (i : m) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.leverageScore
doc:
The **leverage score** of row `i` of `A`: `ℓᵢ(A) = (A A⁺)ᵢᵢ`, the `i`-th diagonal entry of
the orthogonal projector onto `range A`. Defined for every real matrix (any rank, empty
shapes). Drineas–Mahoney–Muthukrishnan–Woodruff 2012, Def. 1; Woodruff 2014, Def. 2.12.
Atlas `leverage-scores`.
atlas: leverage-scores

name: NLAlib.leverageScore_eq_sum_sq_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
**Leverage scores are squared row norms of any orthonormal basis.** If `U` has
orthonormal columns and is a basis of `range A` (`range A ⊆ range U`, written `U (Uᵀ A) = A`,
and `U` has at most `rank A` columns), then `ℓᵢ(A) = ∑ⱼ Uᵢⱼ² = ‖U_{i,:}‖²`. Since the left side
does not mention `U`, the row norms do not depend on the choice of basis.
Drineas–Mahoney–Muthukrishnan–Woodruff 2012, Def. 1 and the remark after it; Woodruff 2014,
Def. 2.12. Atlas `leverage-scores`. Deviation: "orthonormal basis of `range A`" is spelled as the
two hypotheses `hUA`, `hr` (together with orthonormality they force `range U = range A`).
atlas: leverage-scores

signature:
NLAlib.leverageScore_eq_sum_sq_of_self.{u_1, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {q : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq q] {U : Matrix m q ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) (i : m) :
  NLAlib.leverageScore U i = ∑ j, U i j ^ 2
name: NLAlib.leverageScore_eq_sum_sq_of_self
doc:
For a matrix `U` with orthonormal columns, `ℓᵢ(U) = ∑ⱼ Uᵢⱼ²`.
Woodruff 2014, §2.4; atlas `leverage-scores`.

signature:
NLAlib.lieb_concavity.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (H : Matrix n n ℂ) (hH : H.IsHermitian) :
  ConcaveOn ℝ {A | A.PosDef} fun A => NLAlib.traceExp (H + NLAlib.matrixLog A)
name: NLAlib.lieb_concavity
doc:
Lieb's concavity theorem: `A ↦ traceExp (H + matrixLog A)` is concave on positive definite
matrices for fixed Hermitian `H`, over any finite index type (the empty type included, where the
function is constant).

Tropp 2015, Thm 8.1.1 (= Thm 3.4.1); the source states it for `d × d` matrices, the general index
type is obtained by reindexing (`posDef_reindex_iff`, `matrixLog_reindex_of_isHermitian`,
`traceExp_reindex`). Ported from the Prove2me mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration

NLAlib.lintegral_frobSq_transpose_mul_sketch_sub_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {Ωs : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ωs]

  (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
  (hmom :
    ∀ (x : n → ℝ),
      ∫⁻ (ω : Ωs), ENNReal.ofReal (((S ω).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (S ω).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x) ^ 2) ∂μ ≤

  (A : Matrix n d₁ ℝ) (B : Matrix n d₂ ℝ) :

doc:
**Approximate matrix multiplication from the JL moment property.** If the random sketch
`S` (entrywise measurable) satisfies `E (‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²)² ≤ ε² ‖x‖⁴` for every `x`, with `ε ≥ 0`,
then for fixed `A ∈ ℝ^{n×d₁}`, `B ∈ ℝ^{n×d₂}`,
`E ‖AᵀSᵀSB − AᵀB‖_F² ≤ ε² ‖A‖_F² ‖B‖_F²`.

2014); Sarlós 2006, Lem 6. Atlas `amm-ose`. Deviations: stated with lower Lebesgue integrals
(no integrability hypothesis); the hypothesis is the second-moment property itself, not a tail
bound; constant `1`.

**Expectation from a general tail envelope, nonnegative integral form.** If `f ≥ 0`
a.e. on a probability space, `a ≥ 0`, and `P(f > t) ≤ F(t)` for `t > a`, then
`E f ≤ a + ∫ₐ^∞ F(t) dt`. No finiteness or measurability assumption on the envelope
is needed for this extended nonnegative integral inequality.

Standard layer-cake estimate; Vershynin 2018, Lemma 1.2.1; HMT 2011, proof of
Thm 10.8. Uses Mathlib's `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt`.
atlas: tail-integral

signature:

name: NLAlib.log_traceExp_cumulantSum_div_le_integral_lambdaMin_sum
doc:
**Master expectation bound for `λmin`** of an independent sum of Hermitian random matrices:
for `θ < 0`, `log traceExp (cumulantSum μ X θ) / θ ≤ 𝔼 λmin(∑ X k)`. Tropp 2015, Thm 3.6.1,
eq. (3.6.2).
atlas: matrix-laplace

name: NLAlib.lt_eigenvalues₀_of_forall_mem
doc:
A strict lower Rayleigh bound on a subspace of dimension at least
`k+1` implies a strict bound for the `k`-th largest eigenvalue.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 4.2.10.
atlas: eigenvalue-order-and-counting (partial)

signature: NLAlib.lu {n : ℕ} : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.lu
doc:
**Gaussian elimination without pivoting** (Doolittle LU) as a total recursion on the
leading pivot: with `A = [[a, rᵀ], [c, C]]`, `L = [[1, 0], [c/a, L']]`,
`U = [[a, rᵀ], [0, U']]` where `(L', U') = lu (C − c rᵀ/a)`. A zero pivot gives junk through
`x / 0 = 0`. For `n = 0` the output is `(1, A)` (both are the empty matrix).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 20.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 3.2.1 (outer-product form).
atlas: lu-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.luPartialPivot {n : ℕ} :
  Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Equiv.Perm (Fin n) × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.luPartialPivot
doc:
**Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting** as a total recursion. With
`B = partialPivotSwap A = [[a, rᵀ], [c, C]]` and `(σ', L', U') = luPartialPivot (C − c rᵀ/a)`,
the output is `σ = decomposeFin⁻¹ (p, σ')` (row `p` first, then the rows of `B` in the order
`σ'`), `L = [[1, 0], [σ'(c/a), L']]` (multipliers permuted by the later swaps, as in the
textbook's "swap the rows of `L` too"), `U = [[a, rᵀ], [0, U']]`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 21.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 3.4.1.
atlas: lu-partial-pivoting

signature:
NLAlib.luPartialPivotSucceeds_iff_isUnit_det {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LUPartialPivotSucceeds A ↔ IsUnit A.det
name: NLAlib.luPartialPivotSucceeds_iff_isUnit_det
doc:
Partial pivoting succeeds iff `A` is invertible. Proof: `det A = ± ∏ᵢ uᵢᵢ` from
`isPLU_luPartialPivot` (`Matrix.det_permute`), and the pivots are the diagonal of `U`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 21; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.4.1.
atlas: lu-partial-pivoting

signature:
NLAlib.luSucceeds_iff_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LUSucceeds A ↔ ∀ k ≤ n, NLAlib.leadingMinor A k ≠ 0
name: NLAlib.luSucceeds_iff_forall_leadingMinor_ne_zero
doc:
**Breakdown of Gaussian elimination**: elimination without pivoting succeeds iff every
leading principal minor `det A(1:k,1:k)`, `k = 1, …, n`, is nonzero. Proof: induction on `n`
with `det A(1:k+1,1:k+1) = a₁₁ det (pivotSchur A)(1:k,1:k)` (`det_eq_mul_det_pivotSchur`,
`leadingMinor_succ_eq_mul_leadingMinor_pivotSchur`); the case `k = 1` gives `a₁₁ ≠ 0`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20 (Ex. 20.1); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 3.2.1.
atlas: lu-algorithm

signature:
NLAlib.luSucceeds_iff_forall_lu_snd_apply_self_ne_zero {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LUSucceeds A ↔ ∀ (i : Fin n), (NLAlib.lu A).2 i i ≠ 0
name: NLAlib.luSucceeds_iff_forall_lu_snd_apply_self_ne_zero
doc:
The pivots are the diagonal of `U`: elimination succeeds iff `(lu A).2` has nonzero
diagonal. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20.

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_comp_perm.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x : ι → ℝ) (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) :
  NLAlib.Majorized (x ∘ ⇑σ) x
name: NLAlib.majorized_comp_perm
doc:
A coordinate permutation is majorized by the original vector, including
equality of totals. Source: a permutation matrix is doubly stochastic.

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_diagonal_eigenvalues.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) : NLAlib.Majorized (fun i => RCLike.re (A i i)) hA.eigenvalues
name: NLAlib.majorized_diagonal_eigenvalues
doc:
**Schur's theorem.** The real diagonal of a Hermitian matrix is majorized by its spectrum
(`Majorized` sorts intrinsically; arbitrary finite indices, repeated eigenvalues and empty
shapes are included). Over `ℝ` the diagonal is `Matrix.diag A` (`RCLike.re_to_real`).
Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.3.45.
atlas: schur-horn

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_eigenvalues₀_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) : NLAlib.Majorized ⋯.eigenvalues₀ (hA.eigenvalues₀ + hB.eigenvalues₀)
name: NLAlib.majorized_eigenvalues₀_add
doc:
The spectrum of a real symmetric sum is majorized by the coordinatewise
sum of the two decreasing spectra. Equality of totals follows from trace.
Fan (1949), Theorem 1; Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 4.3.39.
atlas: ky-fan-maximum-principle

name: NLAlib.majorized_eigenvalues₀_add_sub
doc:
Lidskii's ordinary majorization of the coordinatewise signed eigenvalue
increment. Bhatia 1997, Theorem III.4.1; no sorting of the increment is assumed.
atlas: lidskii

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_iff_exists_doublyStochastic.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized x y ↔ ∃ D ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ ι, D.mulVec y = x
name: NLAlib.majorized_iff_exists_doublyStochastic
doc:
Full HLP equivalence between ordinary majorization and the existence of an
doubly stochastic matrix, including empty index types and signed vectors.
Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Theorem 2.B.2.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_iff_exists_orthogonal_diagonal_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (d lam : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized d lam ↔ ∃ Q, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q ∧ (Q * Matrix.diagonal lam * Q.transpose).diag = d
name: NLAlib.majorized_iff_exists_orthogonal_diagonal_eq
doc:
Ordinary real majorization is exactly attainment as the diagonal of a real
orthogonal conjugate of the prescribed spectrum. Horn–Johnson (2013),
Theorems 4.3.45 and 4.3.48; signed and repeated spectra and dimension zero.
atlas: schur-horn

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_iff_mem_convexHull_permutations.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized x y ↔ x ∈ (convexHull ℝ) (Set.range fun σ => y ∘ ⇑σ)
name: NLAlib.majorized_iff_mem_convexHull_permutations
doc:
Full HLP equivalence with convex-hull membership in the permutation orbit.
Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Theorem 2.B.2.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_iff_sum_convex_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x y : ι → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized x y ↔ ∀ (φ : ℝ → ℝ), ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ φ → ∑ i, φ (x i) ≤ ∑ i, φ (y i)
name: NLAlib.majorized_iff_sum_convex_le
doc:
Full ordinary-majorization equivalence with all convex scalar sum tests.
The affine tests `u` and `-u` recover equality of totals.
Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Proposition 4.B.1.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_mulVec_of_doublyStochastic.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (y : ι → ℝ)
  {D : Matrix ι ι ℝ} (hD : D ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ ι) : NLAlib.Majorized (D.mulVec y) y
name: NLAlib.majorized_mulVec_of_doublyStochastic
doc:
A doubly stochastic image is majorized by its input, including equality
of totals. Marshall–Olkin–Arnold (2011), Theorem 2.B.2.
atlas: majorization-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_real_parts_eigenvalues_selfAdjointPart.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (z : n → ℂ) (hz : A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (z i))) :
  NLAlib.Majorized (fun i => (z i).re) (Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues ⋯)
name: NLAlib.majorized_real_parts_eigenvalues_selfAdjointPart
doc:
The complete real-part eigenvalue list of a complex matrix is majorized
by the Hermitian-part eigenvalues. Eigenvalue multiplicities are
specified by the characteristic factorization; the list may be in any order.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 4.3.50.
atlas: real-part-eigenvalue-majorization (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.majorized_real_parts_iff_exists_charpoly_and_selfAdjointPart_charpoly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (x : n → ℝ) (z : n → ℂ) :
  NLAlib.Majorized (fun i => (z i).re) x ↔
    ∃ A,
      A.charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (z i)) ∧
        (↑((selfAdjointPart ℝ) A)).charpoly = ∏ i, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C ↑(x i))
name: NLAlib.majorized_real_parts_iff_exists_charpoly_and_selfAdjointPart_charpoly
doc:
**Real-part majorization (Horn–Johnson Thm 4.3.50).** `Re z ≺ x` if and only if some complex
matrix has eigenvalues `z` (as a characteristic polynomial) and Hermitian part with eigenvalues
`x`; multiplicities, arbitrary orderings and empty dimensions are included.
atlas: real-part-eigenvalue-majorization

signature:
NLAlib.mapAbsCondition.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : E → F) (x : E) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.mapAbsCondition
doc:
The absolute condition number of `f` at `x`: the operator norm of the Fréchet derivative.
Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.3. Mathlib's `fderiv` is zero where `f` is not differentiable, so
the value is `0` there; the theorems about it take `DifferentiableAt ℝ f x`.

signature: NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_eq_abs_deriv (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : NLAlib.mapAbsCondition f x = |deriv f x|
name: NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_eq_abs_deriv
doc:
In one dimension the absolute condition number is the absolute derivative.
Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.5.

name: NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_eq_norm_of_hasFDerivAt
doc:
A specified Fréchet derivative computes the absolute condition number.
Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.3.

signature:
NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_toEuclideanCLM.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) : NLAlib.mapAbsCondition (⇑(Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A)) x = NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.mapAbsCondition_toEuclideanCLM
doc:
The absolute condition number of the Euclidean action of a matrix is its spectral norm.
Gautschi 2004, Definitions 2.3–2.4.

signature:
NLAlib.mapComponentRelativeCondition.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ m → EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ m) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.mapComponentRelativeCondition
doc:
The Euclidean componentwise relative condition number: the spectral norm of the relative
condition matrix. Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.4; its relative reading needs every input and
output coordinate nonzero, and `f` differentiable at `x` (the value is `0` otherwise).
atlas: condition-number-of-map-def

signature:
NLAlib.mapComponentRelativeCondition_eq_mapAbsCondition.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {f : EuclideanSpace ℝ m → EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ m}
  (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) :
  NLAlib.mapComponentRelativeCondition f x = NLAlib.mapAbsCondition (NLAlib.componentRelativeMap f x) 0
name: NLAlib.mapComponentRelativeCondition_eq_mapAbsCondition
doc:
The componentwise relative condition number is the absolute condition number of the scaled
local map at `0`. Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.4.
atlas: condition-number-of-map-def

signature:
NLAlib.mapComponentRelativeCondition_le_diagonal_scaling.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {f : EuclideanSpace ℝ m → EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ m}
  (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) :
  NLAlib.mapComponentRelativeCondition f x ≤
    NLAlib.specNorm (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ((f x).ofLp i)⁻¹) * NLAlib.mapAbsCondition f x *
      NLAlib.specNorm (Matrix.diagonal fun j => x.ofLp j)
name: NLAlib.mapComponentRelativeCondition_le_diagonal_scaling
doc:
The componentwise relative condition number of a differentiable map is bounded by the
diagonal scalings times the absolute condition number (it need not be bounded by the matrix
condition number alone). Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.4.
atlas: condition-number-of-map-def

signature:
NLAlib.mapNormRelativeCondition.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : E → F) (x : E) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.mapNormRelativeCondition
doc:
The normwise relative condition number of `f` at `x`: the absolute condition number scaled
by `‖x‖ / ‖f x‖`. Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.4 (`0` when `f x = 0`).

signature:
NLAlib.mapNormRelativeCondition_eq_abs_mul_deriv_div (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.mapNormRelativeCondition f x = |x * deriv f x / f x|
name: NLAlib.mapNormRelativeCondition_eq_abs_mul_deriv_div
doc:
In one dimension the relative condition number is the absolute logarithmic derivative
`|x f'(x) / f(x)|`. Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.6.

signature:
NLAlib.mapNormRelativeCondition_toEuclideanCLM_le_conditionNumber.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : IsUnit A) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
  NLAlib.mapNormRelativeCondition (⇑(Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A)) x ≤ (NLAlib.conditionNumber A).toReal
name: NLAlib.mapNormRelativeCondition_toEuclideanCLM_le_conditionNumber
doc:
The normwise relative condition number of an invertible linear map `x ↦ A x` is at most the
matrix condition number `κ₂(A)`. Gautschi 2004, Definitions 2.3–2.4; Trefethen–Bau 1997,
Lecture 12.
atlas: condition-number-of-map-def

signature:
NLAlib.map_add_mul_prod_gaussianReal (a b : ℝ) (hab : a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 = 1) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun p => a * p.1 + b * p.2)
      ((ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1).prod (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)) =
    ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1
name: NLAlib.map_add_mul_prod_gaussianReal
doc:
The image of `γ ⊗ γ` under `(x, y) ↦ a x + b y` is `γ = N(0,1)` when `a² + b² = 1`.
Atlas: `ornstein-uhlenbeck` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.map_comp_injective_pi.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
  [MeasurableSpace β] (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure β) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (e : ι → κ)
  (he : Function.Injective e) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x j => x (e j)) (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ν) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ν
name: NLAlib.map_comp_injective_pi
doc:
Restricting the coordinates of an i.i.d. product measure along an injection gives the
product measure on the smaller index set.

signature:
NLAlib.map_exp_le_map_exp_of_posSemidef_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hB : B.PosSemidef)
  (hBA : B ≤ A) : B.map Real.exp ≤ A.map Real.exp
name: NLAlib.map_exp_le_map_exp_of_posSemidef_le
doc:
Entrywise exponential preserves Loewner order between PSD matrices.
This is order on quadratic forms, even when scalar entries are negative.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.5; helper for exponential strictness.

signature:
NLAlib.map_ofReal_matrix_pow.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  (A ^ k).map Complex.ofReal = A.map Complex.ofReal ^ k
name: NLAlib.map_ofReal_matrix_pow
doc:
Complexification commutes with matrix powers. Source: Horn–Johnson
(2013), §5.6; this is the matrix ring-homomorphism power identity.

signature:
NLAlib.map_ofReal_srhtSketch_gram {n k d : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin d) ℝ)
  (ξ : Fin n → ℝ) (T : NLAlib.ExactRowSubset (Fin n) k) :
  ((NLAlib.srhtSketch H ξ T * U).transpose * (NLAlib.srhtSketch H ξ T * U)).map Complex.ofReal =
    (1 / ↑k) • ∑ j ∈ ↑T, NLAlib.srhtPopulationAtom (NLAlib.srhtSignedFrame H U ξ) j
name: NLAlib.map_ofReal_srhtSketch_gram
doc:
The complex Chernoff empirical mean is precisely the complex extension
of the actual real sketch Gram matrix. Source: `sh:srht-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.map_ofReal_srhtWithReplacementSketch_gram {n k d : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin d) ℝ) (ξ : Fin n → ℝ) (I : Fin k → Fin n) :
  ((NLAlib.srhtWithReplacementSketch H ξ I * U).transpose * (NLAlib.srhtWithReplacementSketch H ξ I * U)).map
      Complex.ofReal =
    (1 / ↑k) • ∑ a, NLAlib.srhtPopulationAtom (NLAlib.srhtSignedFrame H U ξ) (I a)
name: NLAlib.map_ofReal_srhtWithReplacementSketch_gram
doc:
The complex Chernoff iid population mean is exactly the extension of
the actual real sketch Gram matrix. Source: `sh:srht-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.map_pow_le_map_pow_of_posSemidef_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hB : B.PosSemidef)
  (hBA : B ≤ A) (k : ℕ) : (B.map fun t => t ^ k) ≤ A.map fun t => t ^ k
name: NLAlib.map_pow_le_map_pow_of_posSemidef_le
doc:
Every natural entrywise power preserves Loewner order between PSD
matrices. Exponent zero is the identical all-ones matrix on both sides.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.5; helper for exponential strictness.

signature:
NLAlib.matrixCompensatedTracePotential.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (θ c : ℝ)
  (X V : ℕ → Ω → Matrix n n ℂ) (k : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.matrixCompensatedTracePotential
doc:
The actual compensated matrix trace potential, with cumulative variance increments
specified explicitly. The matrix Freedman theorem supplies their genuine conditional
second-moment relation and the exact Bernstein coefficient.
Source: operator rederivations Section 3.3, `S_k`; atlas `matrix-freedman` (partial).

signature:
NLAlib.matrixCompensatedTracePotential_zero.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (θ c : ℝ) (X V : ℕ → Ω → Matrix n n ℂ) (ω : Ω) :
  NLAlib.matrixCompensatedTracePotential θ c X V 0 ω = ↑(Fintype.card n)
name: NLAlib.matrixCompensatedTracePotential_zero
doc:
The actual compensated trace potential starts at the ambient dimension.
Source: operator rederivations Section 3.3, `S_0=d`; helper for `matrix-freedman` (partial).

signature:
NLAlib.matrixExp.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {d : Type u_2} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (A : Matrix d d 𝕜) :
  Matrix d d 𝕜

The **matrix exponential** `exp A = ∑ Aᵏ/k!` (Mathlib's `NormedSpace.exp`). Tropp 2015,
§2.1.11.
atlas: matrix-calculus-def

signature:
NLAlib.matrixExp_reflection_conj.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (R A : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hR : R.conjTranspose = R) (hR2 : R * R = 1) : NLAlib.matrixExp (R * A * R) = R * NLAlib.matrixExp A * R
name: NLAlib.matrixExp_reflection_conj

signature:
NLAlib.matrixExp_reindex.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq κ] (e : ι ≃ κ) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) :
  NLAlib.matrixExp ((Matrix.reindex e e) A) = (Matrix.reindex e e) (NLAlib.matrixExp A)
name: NLAlib.matrixExp_reindex
doc:
Equivalent finite labels commute with the matrix exponential, with no
Hermitian premise. Source: continuous algebra-isomorphism transport of the
exponential; atlas `golden-thompson` (finite-index transport helper).

signature:
NLAlib.matrixExp_smul_eq_cfc.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {d : Type u_2} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]

name: NLAlib.matrixExp_smul_eq_cfc
doc:
For Hermitian `A`, `matrixExp (s • A)` is the functional calculus of `x ↦ exp (s x)` at `A`.
Tropp 2015, §2.1.11.

name: NLAlib.matrixExp_smul_le_one_add_smul_add_smul_sq_of_spectrum_le
doc:
If `exp (θ x) ≤ 1 + θ x + c x²` on the spectrum of a Hermitian `A`, then
`exp (θ A) ≼ 1 + θ A + c A²`. Tropp 2015, Lemma 6.6.2; helper for `matrix-bernstein` and
`matrix-freedman`.

signature:
NLAlib.matrixExp_smul_one_eq_exp_smul_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (t : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.matrixExp (t • 1) = Real.exp t • 1
name: NLAlib.matrixExp_smul_one_eq_exp_smul_one
doc:
A real scalar identity exponentiates exactly as a scalar identity for any finite labels.
Source: scalar continuous functional calculus; helper for `matrix-freedman` (partial).

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_chernoff_sampling_lower.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (hN : 0 < N) (M : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)
  (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (M k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun M μ)
  (hPSD : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (M k ω).PosSemidef)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.lambdaMax (M k ω) ≤ L) (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), M k ω ∂μ = 1)
  {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  μ.real {ω | NLAlib.lambdaMin ((1 / ↑N) • ∑ k, M k ω) ≤ 1 - ε} ≤ ↑d * Real.exp (-ε ^ 2 * ↑N / (2 * L))

doc:
**Matrix Chernoff for sampling, lower tail.** Let `M₁, …, M_N` be independent random
positive semidefinite `d × d` matrices with `λmax(Mₖ) ≤ L` and `𝔼 Mₖ = I`. Then for
`0 ≤ ε < 1`, `P(λmin(N⁻¹ ∑ₖ Mₖ) ≤ 1 - ε) ≤ d e^{-ε² N/(2L)}`.

Atlas `matrix-chernoff-sampling`. Deviation: the atlas's unspecified constant is the explicit
`2`; the index `Fin N` is inherited from the matrix Chernoff theorem.
atlas: matrix-chernoff-sampling

`matrix_chernoff_sampling_lower`, for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`,
`P(λmax(N⁻¹ ∑ₖ Mₖ) ≥ 1 + ε) ≤ d e^{-ε² N/(3L)}`.
Tropp 2015, Thm 5.1.1 with Tropp 2012, Rem 5.3; Tropp 2011, Thm 2.2.
Atlas `matrix-chernoff-sampling`. Deviation: the atlas's unspecified constant is the explicit
`3` (valid for `ε ≤ 1`); the index `Fin N` is inherited from the matrix Chernoff theorem.

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_freedman.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Nonempty n] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {ℱ : MeasureTheory.Filtration ℕ inst✝} {X V : ℕ → Ω → Matrix n n ℂ} (hXMeas : ∀ (j : ℕ), Measurable (X j))
  (hXInt : ∀ (j : ℕ), MeasureTheory.Integrable (X j) μ) (hXHerm : ∀ (j : ℕ), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X j ω).IsHermitian)
  (hMean : ∀ (j : ℕ), μ[X j | ↑ℱ j] =ᵐ[μ] 0)
  (hLocal : ∀ (j : ℕ), NLAlib.HasLocalMatrixSecondMoment μ (↑ℱ j) (X j) (V j)) {L t v : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) (ht : 0 ≤ t)

space. Increments are adapted integrable Hermitian matrices, actually conditionally
centered, and bounded only above by `L I`. Predictable finite PSD variance increments
satisfy the genuine extended local quadratic moment identities on every predictable
set and every deterministic complex vector. Neither unconditional square integrability
nor integrability of the original variance is assumed. The bound includes `t=0` and
`L=0` and has the exact Bernstein coefficient.
Source: Tropp 2011, Theorem 1.2; supplied operator rederivations `thm:freedman` and
Part VII audit `audit:local-moment`, `audit:combined`.

  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (hB : B.PosSemidef) : max (A.det * ∏ i, B i i) (B.det * ∏ i, A i i) ≤ (A.hadamard B).det
name: NLAlib.max_det_mul_prod_diag_le_det_hadamard
doc:
Both Oppenheim lower bounds hold simultaneously, hence their maximum
is bounded by the determinant of the Hadamard product.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.5.9.
atlas: schur-product-inequalities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.max_sInf_spectrum_mul_le_sInf_spectrum_hadamard.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.PosDef) :
  max (sInf (spectrum ℝ (A * B))) (sInf (spectrum ℝ (A * B.transpose))) ≤ sInf (spectrum ℝ (A.hadamard B))
name: NLAlib.max_sInf_spectrum_mul_le_sInf_spectrum_hadamard
doc:
The smallest eigenvalue of the Hadamard product of two real SPD matrices
is at least the smallest eigenvalue of their ordinary product. The second
source bound with the transposed second factor is identical for symmetric
real inputs; both are included by the displayed maximum.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.7.18.
atlas: schur-product-inequalities (partial)

name: NLAlib.max_specNorm_sinePrincipalAngles_le_max_perturbation_frame_div
doc:
Wedin's exact operator bound measured by the two perturbation-frame
products. Wedin (1972), Section 3; all admissible rectangular endpoints are allowed.
atlas: wedin-sin-theta (partial)

name: NLAlib.max_specNorm_sinePrincipalAngles_le_max_residual_div
doc:
Wedin's exact maximum-residual operator bound for the leading left and
right singular spaces of SVDs. Wedin (1972), Section 3. The denominator
is `σ_(k-1)(A+E)-σ_k(A)`; the endpoint `k=min(m,n)` uses the zero-padded
next value. Empty selected frames are included whenever the displayed gap is positive.
atlas: wedin-sin-theta (partial)

name: NLAlib.max_specNorm_sinePrincipalAngles_le_specNorm_div
doc:
Wedin's mixed-gap sine operator norms are both at most the perturbation
operator norm divided by the mixed gap. Wedin (1972), Section 3.
atlas: wedin-sin-theta (partial)

name: NLAlib.max_specNorm_sinePrincipalAngles_le_two_mul_specNorm_div_population_gap
doc:
The leading singular-space population-gap operator bound holds without
any smallness hypothesis on the perturbation. Wedin (1972), Section 3; Weyl
and the unit sine bound give the exact constant two. The next singular value is
zero padded at `k=min(m,n)`, including unmatched rectangular null directions.
atlas: wedin-sin-theta (partial)

signature: NLAlib.mcdiarmidTail (C t : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.mcdiarmidTail
doc:
The McDiarmid tail `exp (-2 t² / C)`, with the zero-oscillation case `C = 0` written
explicitly (`0` for a positive threshold, `1` otherwise). McDiarmid 1989, Theorem 3.1.

signature:
NLAlib.mcdiarmid_lower_tail.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : ι → Type u_3}
  [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (S i)] (X : (i : ι) → Ω → S i) (hX : ∀ (i : ι), Measurable (X i))
  (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) (f : ((i : ι) → S i) → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) (c : ι → ℝ)
  (hc : ∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ c i) (hcoord : ∀ (i : ι) (x : (j : ι) → S j) (y : S i), |f (Function.update x i y) - f x| ≤ c i)
  {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
  μ.real {ω | t ≤ ∫ (ω' : Ω), f fun i => X i ω' ∂μ - f fun i => X i ω} ≤ NLAlib.mcdiarmidTail (∑ i, c i ^ 2) t
name: NLAlib.mcdiarmid_lower_tail
doc:
**McDiarmid's matching lower tail.** The same explicit tail controls
`P(E f(X)-f(X)≥t)`, including zero total oscillation. McDiarmid 1989, Theorem 3.1, applied to
the negative centred variable.
atlas: mcdiarmid

signature:
NLAlib.mcdiarmid_upper_tail.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : ι → Type u_3}
  [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (S i)] (X : (i : ι) → Ω → S i) (hX : ∀ (i : ι), Measurable (X i))
  (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) (f : ((i : ι) → S i) → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) (c : ι → ℝ)
  (hc : ∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ c i) (hcoord : ∀ (i : ι) (x : (j : ι) → S j) (y : S i), |f (Function.update x i y) - f x| ≤ c i)
  {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
  μ.real {ω | t ≤ (f fun i => X i ω) - ∫ (ω' : Ω), f fun i => X i ω' ∂μ} ≤ NLAlib.mcdiarmidTail (∑ i, c i ^ 2) t
name: NLAlib.mcdiarmid_upper_tail
doc:
**McDiarmid's upper tail with exact constant two.** Independent measurable
coordinates and global coordinate bounds give `P(f(X)-E f(X)≥t)≤exp(-2t²/∑cᵢ²)`.
For zero total oscillation and a positive threshold the probability is zero.
No integrability assumptions are required. McDiarmid 1989, Theorem 3.1;
Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart 2013, Theorem 6.2.
atlas: mcdiarmid

  (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b) {G : Ω → Matrix n κ ℝ}
  (hG : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw G (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n κ) μ) {Q : Ω → κ → Matrix n r ℝ}
  (hQ : ∀ (ω : Ω) (k : κ), NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols (Q ω k)) {q : ℕ}
  (hK : ∀ (ω : Ω) (k : κ), NLAlib.krylovSpace A (fun i => G ω i k) q ≤ (Q ω k).mulVecLin.range) {t s : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t)

      {ω |
        t + 2 * (2 / a * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ (2 * q)) * (↑(Fintype.card n) + s) ≤
          |NLAlib.compressionQuadratureEstimate A (fun x => 1 / x) (G ω) (Q ω) - (cfc (fun x => 1 / x) A).trace|} ≤
    2 *
        Real.exp
          (-(1 / (256 * Real.exp 1 ^ 2)) *
            min (↑(Fintype.card κ) * t ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobNorm (cfc (fun x => 1 / x) A) ^ 2)
              (↑(Fintype.card κ) * t / NLAlib.specNorm (cfc (fun x => 1 / x) A))) +

doc:
**SLQ for `tr A⁻¹`, Gaussian test matrix.** Let `A` be symmetric with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, `G` a standard Gaussian `n × κ` test matrix (`m = |κ|` test vectors), and `Q(ω)_k`
orthonormal with `K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q(ω)_k`. With `E = (2/a)((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^{2q}` and
`c = 1/(256e²)`, for `t, s ≥ 0`:
`P(|SLQ − tr f(A)| ≥ t + 2E(n + s)) ≤ 2exp(−c min(m t²/‖f(A)‖_F², m t/‖f(A)‖))
  + 2exp(−c min(m s²/n, m s))`, where `f(A) = cfc (1/x) A = A⁻¹`.
Source: Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], Thm 4.1 (with Hanson–Wright in place of their
Rademacher tail). Atlas: `slq-error` (case `f = 1/x`); uses `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`,
`hutchinson-tail`, `inverse-polynomial-approx`. Constants: the Hanson–Wright constant
`1/(256 e²)` (UCS17 Thm 4.1: Rademacher probes, constant `1/8` in the exponent).
atlas: slq-error (partial)

matrix are independent and sub-Gaussian with variance proxy `K²`, then for `m = |κ| ≥ 1` and

`P(|tr_m(A) − 𝔼 tr_m(A)| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp(−(1/(256e²)) min(m t²/(K⁴‖A‖_F²), m t/(K²‖A‖)))`.

`hanson-wright`. Deviation: Hanson–Wright constant `1/(256 e²)`; any matrix `A` (not only

`P(χ²_d ≤ u) ≤ (e u / d)^{d/2}`.

the projection of a random unit vector), with the parameter `s = ε / (2(1 − ε))` in

name: NLAlib.measureReal_sum_sq_le_sub_two_sqrt_mul_le_gaussianVector
doc:
**Laurent–Massart lower tail of `χ²_d`**: for `d ≥ 1` and `x ≥ 0`,
`P(χ²_d ≤ d − 2√(d x)) ≤ e^{-x}`.

Laurent–Massart 2000, Lem 1 (second inequality, with all weights `aᵢ = 1`). Proof: with
`u = 2√(x/d)`, the event is `χ²_d ≤ (1 − u) d`; for `u ≥ 1` it is null (`χ²_d > 0` a.s.), and for
`u < 1` use `measureReal_sum_sq_le_one_sub_mul_le_gaussianVector` and `log(1 − u) ≤ −u − u²/2`.
The hypothesis `1 ≤ d` is needed: for `d = 0` the event is everything. Atlas:
`chi-square-lower-tail`.
atlas: chi-square-lower-tail

      {g | (⨅ c, √((g - B.mulVec c) ⬝ᵥ (g - B.mulVec c))) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.exp 1 * u / ↑d) ^ (↑d / 2))
name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal
doc:
**Small ball for the distance to a subspace.** Let `B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ` have
`rank B + d ≤ N` with `d ≥ 1`. For a standard Gaussian vector `g ∈ ℝᴺ` and `0 ≤ u ≤ d`,
`P(dist(g, range B)² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / d)^{d/2}`, with `dist(g, range B) = inf_c ‖g - B c‖₂`.

The squared distance dominates the sum of squares of `d` coordinates of `g` in an orthonormal
basis of `(range B)ᗮ` (Bessel), which is `χ²_d` by rotation invariance; then the chi-square lower
tail. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_dist_colspace_small_ball`.
atlas: smin-small-ball

  (hud : u ≤ ↑N - ↑n + 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n)).real {A | (⨅ x, √(A.mulVec ↑x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec ↑x)) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤
    (Real.exp 1 * u / (↑N - ↑n + 1)) ^ ((↑N - ↑n + 1) / 2)
name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_col_span_le_le_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Small ball for the distance from a column to the span of the others.** For an `N × n`
standard Gaussian matrix `A` with `n ≤ N`, any column `j` and `0 ≤ u ≤ N - n + 1`,
`P(dist(A_j, span{A_l : l ≠ j})² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / (N - n + 1))^{(N - n + 1)/2}`, the distance
being written `inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 }`.

Condition on the other columns (resample column `j`) and apply the subspace small-ball bound
with `d = N - n + 1`. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.dist_col_span_small_ball`.
atlas: smin-small-ball

signature: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtQ.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtQ
doc:
The `Q` factor of modified Gram–Schmidt (the working columns after `n` steps).
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 8.1.
atlas: gram-schmidt

signature: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtR.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtR
doc:
The `R` factor of modified Gram–Schmidt: `r_ij = q_iᵀ w_j^{(i)}` for `i < j` (the working
column `j` before step `i`), `r_ii = ‖w_i^{(i)}‖`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 8.1.
atlas: gram-schmidt

signature: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Fin n → m → ℝ
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState
doc:
The working columns of **modified Gram–Schmidt** after `k` steps (Trefethen–Bau Alg. 8.1):
start from the columns of `A`; step `k` (for `k < n`) normalises column `k` to
`q_k = w_k / ‖w_k‖` and removes its component from every later column,
`w_j ← w_j − (q_kᵀ w_j) q_k` (`j > k`); columns `< k` are left alone. After `n` steps column `j`
holds `q_j`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Alg. 8.1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, Alg. 5.2.6.
atlas: gram-schmidt

signature:
NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState_eq.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  k ≤ n →
    ∀ (j : Fin n),
      NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState A k j =
        if ↑j < k then NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A j
        else A.col j - ∑ l with ↑l < k, (NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A l ⬝ᵥ A.col j) • NLAlib.gramSchmidtCol A l
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtState_eq
doc:
The MGS invariant: after `k ≤ n` steps, working column `j` is `q_j` for `j < k` and
`a_j − ∑_{i<k} (q_iᵀ a_j) q_i` otherwise. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 8.

signature:
NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidt_eq.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtQ A = NLAlib.gramSchmidtQ A ∧ NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidtR A = NLAlib.gramSchmidtR A
name: NLAlib.modifiedGramSchmidt_eq
doc:
**MGS = CGS in exact arithmetic**: modified Gram–Schmidt computes the same `Q` and `R` as
classical Gram–Schmidt, for every `A` (breakdowns included). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 8
(MGS is a rearrangement of CGS); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.2.8. Proof: the invariant
`modifiedGramSchmidtState_eq`, with `q_kᵀ q_i = 0` for `i ≠ k`.
atlas: gram-schmidt

Retaining all possible walk frequencies recovers the monomial exactly.
Source: Sachdeva–Vishnoi, Theorem 3.3 (`monomial-chebyshev-approx`), degenerate case.

signature: NLAlib.monomialChebyshevApprox_zero (d : ℕ) : NLAlib.monomialChebyshevApprox 0 d = 1

doc:
The zero monomial is represented exactly by the constant polynomial `1`.
Source: Sachdeva–Vishnoi, Theorem 3.3, degenerate case (`monomial-chebyshev-approx`).

NLAlib.monotoneOn_eval_T_real (q : ℕ) :

NLAlib.monotone_convexOn_max_sub (a : ℝ) :

NLAlib.monotone_convexOn_rpow_max_zero {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) :

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber
doc:
The pseudoinverse condition number `‖A‖₂ ‖A⁺‖₂` of a matrix of any shape, with the
Moore–Penrose inverse: it equals `σ₁/σ_r` with `r = rank A`
(`moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_singularValues_ratio`) and is `0` at `A = 0` (every shape). For
an invertible square matrix it is the real value of `conditionNumber A`
(`conditionNumber_toReal_eq_moorePenroseConditionNumber`). Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2 and
§5.5.2 (the condition number of a full-rank rectangular matrix).
atlas: condition-number-def

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_conjTranspose
doc:
Conjugate transposition preserves the pseudoinverse condition number at every rank.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_conjTranspose_mul_self
doc:
Taking a column Gram matrix `AᴴA` squares the pseudoinverse condition number, including at
deficient rank. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_eigenvalues₀_ratio.{u_3} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A = ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨0, ⋯⟩ / ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨Fintype.card n - 1, ⋯⟩
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_eigenvalues₀_ratio
doc:
For a positive-definite real matrix on a nonempty index type, the pseudoinverse condition
number is the ratio of its largest and smallest eigenvalues. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_mul_specNorm_inv.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : IsUnit A) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A = NLAlib.specNorm A * NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_mul_specNorm_inv
doc:
On an invertible square matrix the pseudoinverse condition number uses the ordinary inverse:
`‖A‖₂ ‖A⁻¹‖₂`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, eq. (2.6.4); Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (12.13).
atlas: condition-number-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_of_qr.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [LinearOrder n] [DecidableEq m] {A Q : Matrix m n ℝ} {R : Matrix n n ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hFactor : Q * R = A) : NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber R = NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_of_qr
doc:
QR preserves the total spectral condition number built from the
Moore--Penrose inverse, including singular and zero-rank matrices.
Golub--Van Loan, Section 2.6.2; supports `qr-decomposition`.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_singularValues_ratio
doc:
At positive rank the pseudoinverse condition number is the ratio of the largest and
last positive singular values, `σ₁/σ_r` (zero-indexed: `σ 0 / σ (r-1)`), on arbitrary
finite index types. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2 and §5.5.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_specNorm_div_singularValues_last.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜)
  (hn : 0 < Fintype.card n) (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A = NLAlib.specNorm A / NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card n - 1)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_eq_specNorm_div_singularValues_last
doc:
Under full column rank (`rank A = card n ≥ 1`), `κ⁺(A) = ‖A‖₂ / σ_min(A)` with
`σ_min(A) = singularValues A (card n - 1)`; this covers invertible square `A`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.3.2 (`κ₂(A) = σ₁/σ_n`); Trefethen–Bau 1997, eq. (12.14).
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_mul_left_of_hasOrthonormalCols.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} {p : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
  [DecidableEq p] (Q : Matrix p m 𝕜) (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber (Q * A) = NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_mul_left_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
Left multiplication by a rectangular orthonormal frame (`QᴴQ = 1`) preserves the
pseudoinverse condition number. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2 and §5.3.2 (`κ(R) = κ(A)` for
`A = QR`).
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_nonneg.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_nonneg
doc:
Pseudoinverse condition numbers are nonnegative.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2; supports `condition-number-def`.

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_smul
doc:
Nonzero scalar multiplication preserves the pseudoinverse condition number.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_transpose
doc:
Transposition preserves the pseudoinverse condition number at every rank.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2.
atlas: condition-number-def

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_zero.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] : NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber 0 = 0
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber_zero
doc:
The zero matrix has pseudoinverse condition number zero, including empty shapes.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §2.6.2; supports `condition-number-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : Matrix n m 𝕜
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse
doc:
The **Moore–Penrose inverse** `A⁺` of a rectangular matrix over `ℝ` or `ℂ`: the matrix
satisfying the four Penrose identities (`isMoorePenroseInverse`), chosen by
`exists_isMoorePenroseInverse` and well defined because the identities determine it uniquely
(`IsMoorePenroseInverse.unique`). For every SVD `A = U Σ Vᴴ` it is the textbook formula
`V Σ⁺ Uᴴ`, with `Σ⁺` the reciprocals of the nonzero singular values
(`moorePenroseInverse_eq_svd`). Defined for rank-deficient and empty matrices; the full-rank
formulas `pinvL`, `pinvR` are separate definitions (`moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvL`,
`moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvR`). Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3.
atlas: pseudoinverse

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_conjTranspose
doc: Conjugate transpose commutes with the general Moore–Penrose inverse: `(Aᴴ)⁺ = (A⁺)ᴴ`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_conjTranspose_mul_self.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}
  {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A.conjTranspose * A) =
    NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_conjTranspose_mul_self
doc:
The general inverse of the column Gram matrix `Aᴴ A` is `A⁺ (A⁺)ᴴ`, including singular Gram
matrices. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_inv_of_isUnit.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (hA : IsUnit A) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = A⁻¹
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_inv_of_isUnit
doc:
On a nonsingular square matrix, the general inverse is the ordinary inverse.
Horn--Johnson 2013, Problem 7.3.P7; supports `condition-number-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_left_inverse_mul_projector.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {L : Matrix n m ℝ} (hL : L * A = 1) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = L * (A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_left_inverse_mul_projector
doc:
Any left inverse recovers the Moore–Penrose inverse after composing with
the orthogonal range projector. Penrose identities; supports least-squares perturbation.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_of_isQR.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n]
  {A Q : Matrix m n ℝ} {R : Matrix n n ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsQR A Q R) (hR : ∀ (i : n), R i i ≠ 0) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = R⁻¹ * Q.transpose
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_of_isQR
doc:
The Moore–Penrose inverse via QR: under full column rank, `A⁺ = R⁻¹ Qᵀ`.
Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 11; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.3.3.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvL.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (h : IsUnit (A.conjTranspose * A)) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = NLAlib.pinvL A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvL
doc:
The general Moore–Penrose inverse agrees with `pinvL` for full column rank.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvR.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (h : IsUnit (A * A.conjTranspose)) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = NLAlib.pinvR A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_pinvR
doc:
The general Moore–Penrose inverse agrees with `pinvR` for full row rank.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_svd.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {p q : ℕ} {A : Matrix m n 𝕜} {U : Matrix m (Fin p) 𝕜}

  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = (V * NLAlib.rectDiag fun k => (NLAlib.singularValues A k)⁻¹) * U.conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_svd
doc:
**`A⁺ = V Σ⁺ Uᴴ`**: any SVD `A = U Σ Vᴴ` computes the Moore–Penrose inverse as
`V Σ⁺ Uᴴ` with `Σ⁺ = rectDiag (σ⁻¹)` (scalar `0⁻¹ = 0`), independently of the choice of singular
vectors. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_zero_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A = 0 ↔ A = 0
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_zero_iff
doc:
A matrix has zero Moore–Penrose inverse exactly when the matrix is zero.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_eq_zero_of_rank_eq_zero
doc: At rank zero the Moore–Penrose inverse is zero. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_kronecker.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} {q : Type u_4}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [Fintype q] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (B : Matrix p q ℝ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) A B) =
    Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_kronecker
doc:
The Moore–Penrose inverse of a Kronecker product is the product of the two
Moore–Penrose inverses. Horn–Johnson 1991, Section 4.2; arbitrary finite rectangular
matrices and all zero singular values are included.
atlas: kronecker-spectral

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_moorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) = A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_moorePenroseInverse
doc:
Taking the Moore–Penrose inverse twice recovers the original matrix.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_complement_columnProjector_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) =
    NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B).transpose * (B - A).transpose *

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_complement_columnProjector_eq
doc:
The upper-right pseudoinverse block has a perturbation-adjoint
factor and a complementary column-space factor. Stewart–Sun §III.3.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_eq_one_of_rank_eq_card.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * A = 1
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_eq_one_of_rank_eq_card
doc:
Full column rank gives the literal Moore–Penrose left inverse.
Penrose identities and rank-nullity; supports least-squares perturbation.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_eq_pinvR_mul_pinvL.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq q] (M : Matrix m q ℝ) (R : Matrix q p ℝ)

doc:
Reverse order for a full-column-rank left factor and full-row-rank right
factor. This includes empty intermediate spaces. The proof checks the four
Penrose identities and uses uniqueness. Atlas: `pseudoinverse`, `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_isHermitian.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_isHermitian
doc: The row-space projector `A⁺ A` is Hermitian.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_isIdempotentElem.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : IsIdempotentElem (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * A)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_isIdempotentElem
doc: The Moore–Penrose row-space projector is idempotent at every rank.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_left_of_hasOrthonormalCols.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}

  (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (Q * A) = NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * Q.conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_left_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
The general inverse of a left-isometric product is the reverse adjoint product:
`(Q A)⁺ = A⁺ Qᴴ` when `Qᴴ Q = 1`.
Horn--Johnson 2013, Problem 7.3.P7; supports `condition-number-def` for rectangular frames.

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_moorePenroseInverse
doc: The second Penrose identity `A⁺ A A⁺ = A⁺`, at every rank.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_transpose_mul_transpose.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).transpose * A.transpose = NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_mul_transpose_mul_transpose
doc:
A Moore–Penrose inverse is fixed by its own column-range projector,
expressed using transposes. Stewart–Sun §III.3, Penrose identities.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_reindex.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}

  (en : n ≃ q) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse ((Matrix.reindex em en) A) = (Matrix.reindex en em) (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_reindex
doc:
Reindexing commutes with the general Moore–Penrose inverse (over `ℝ` or `ℂ`), reversing
row and column labels. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_self_mul_conjTranspose.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2}
  {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A * A.conjTranspose) =
    (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).conjTranspose * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_self_mul_conjTranspose
doc:
The general inverse of the row Gram matrix `A Aᴴ` is `(A⁺)ᴴ A⁺`, including singular Gram
matrices. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_singleton (a : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (Matrix.diagonal fun x => a) = Matrix.diagonal fun x => a⁻¹
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_singleton
doc:
The Moore–Penrose inverse of a `1 × 1` matrix is its scalar reciprocal, at every rank.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_smul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] (c : 𝕜) (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (c • A) = c⁻¹ • NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A
name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_smul
doc:
Scaling the Moore–Penrose inverse by the inverse scalar: `(c A)⁺ = c⁻¹ A⁺`.
Horn--Johnson 2013, Problem 7.3.P7; supports `condition-number-def`, including rank zero.

name: NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_sub_blocks
doc:
The four orthogonal blocks of the pseudoinverse difference, with the
lower-right block zero. Stewart–Sun §III.3, from the Penrose identities.

signature:
NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse_sub_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) :

        NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B).transpose * (B - A).transpose *
          (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) +

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_eq_mul_moorePenroseInverse
