**Uniqueness of the orthogonal projector onto a range.** If `Q` has orthonormal columns,
`range Y ⊆ range Q` (written `Q (Qᴴ Y) = Y`) and `rank Y` is at least the number of columns of
`Q` (so the two ranges coincide), then `QQᴴ = Y Y⁺`.

Proof: `P₁ = QQᴴ` and `P₂ = YY⁺` are Hermitian idempotents with `P₁P₂ = P₂ = P₂P₁`, so
`M = P₁ − P₂` is a Hermitian idempotent and `‖M‖_F² = re tr M = card q − rank Y ≤ 0`.
Standard (Golub–Van Loan, 4th ed., §2.5.1: the orthogonal projector onto a subspace is unique).
Atlas `leverage-scores` (basis independence), `projection-facts`.

has `UᴴU = I` and `p = card m`, then `UUᴴ = I`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_mul_add_residual

name: NLAlib.mul_conjTranspose_mul_eq_of_range_le

columns, then `Q' Q'ᴴ Q = Q`. Atlas `projection-facts`.

Atlas `projection-facts`.

whole eigenvalue projector. Parlett §11.7; all multiplicities are included.

Helper for `jackson-lipschitz` (Jackson's theorem through the sawtooth function).

atlas: sylvester-separation-bound (partial)

NLAlib.mul_specNorm_le_specNorm_sylvester_of_interval.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

doc:
Interval/complement separation without an extra endpoint-order
assumption: a nonempty interval spectrum forces it, and empty source spaces
have zero matrices. Bhatia §VII.2.

signature:
NLAlib.mul_specNorm_le_specNorm_sylvester_of_one_sided.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

doc:
One-sided spectral separation gives constant-one spectral norm control.
Bhatia §VII.2; an empty right space is discharged before choosing an eigenvalue.

signature:
NLAlib.mul_sq_le_min_hutchinson_exponent_of_posSemidef.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

The Hanson–Wright exponent at `t = ε tr A` is at least `m ε²` for positive semidefinite

Source: Cortinovis–Kressner (2021), proof of Corollary 1; helper for `hutchinson-tail`
and the relative-error stochastic Lanczos quadrature bound `slq-error`.

name: NLAlib.mul_submatrix_cols_eq_mul_diagonal
doc: Selecting any columns from an invariant diagonal frame gives the selected diagonal invariant equation. Horn–Johnson (2013), §4.3.

signature:
NLAlib.mul_topEigenframe_eq_mul_diagonal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card n) :

name: NLAlib.mul_topEigenframe_eq_mul_diagonal
doc:
Top eigenframes satisfy the invariant equation with their sorted
prefix eigenvalues. Horn–Johnson (2013), §4.3.

signature:
NLAlib.mul_trace_pow_mul_sq_le_trace_pow_mul_inversePowerHessianKernel.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {R B : Matrix ι ι ℝ} (hR : R.PosSemidef) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (n : ℕ) :

name: NLAlib.mul_trace_pow_mul_sq_le_trace_pow_mul_inversePowerHessianKernel
doc:
The inverse-power Hessian kernel dominates the square of the first
trace derivative by weighted Cauchy--Schwarz. Source: resolvent operator
proof; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (operator calculus helper).

name: NLAlib.mul_transpose_aeval_gram_mul_mul_eq_of_blockKrylovSpace_le
doc:
A frame containing the block Krylov space reproduces every filtered sketch of degree
below the Krylov order, simultaneously. Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, its final block
Krylov specialization; Musco--Musco (2015), polynomial competitor argument.

name: NLAlib.mul_transpose_eq_mul_moorePenroseInverse_of_qr_of_rank_eq_card
doc:
Under full column rank, the QR frame projector is the
Moore--Penrose orthogonal range projector. Trefethen--Bau, Theorem 7.2;
Golub--Van Loan, Theorem 5.2.3.
atlas: qr-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.mul_transpose_eq_topEigenframe_projector_of_lower_spectral_bound.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
Every width-`j` invariant frame above the positive population
boundary gap has the canonical top spectral projector, independently of its
basis; Davis--Kahan, Section 6, at zero perturbation.

signature:
NLAlib.mul_transpose_le_one_iff_specNorm_le_one.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2}
  [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] (M : Matrix n m ℝ) : M * M.transpose ≤ 1 ↔ NLAlib.specNorm M ≤ 1
name: NLAlib.mul_transpose_le_one_iff_specNorm_le_one
NLAlib.mul_vecMulVec_eq_vecMulVec_mul
doc:
A common eigenvalue produces a rank-one rectangular intertwiner.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 2.4.4.1, converse Sylvester obstruction.

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_eigenvalues_eq_of_orthogonal_diagonalization.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {T P : Matrix n n ℝ} (hT : T.IsHermitian) (d : n → ℝ) (hPo : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P)
  (hTd : T = P * Matrix.diagonal d * P.transpose) :
  Multiset.map hT.eigenvalues Finset.univ.val = Multiset.map d Finset.univ.val
name: NLAlib.multiset_eigenvalues_eq_of_orthogonal_diagonalization
doc:
An orthogonal diagonalization identifies the eigenvalue multiset, including
multiplicities and signed entries. The real spectral theorem; Kronecker helper.

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_eigenvalues_kronecker.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
  Multiset.map ⋯.eigenvalues Finset.univ.val =
    Multiset.map (fun ij => hA.eigenvalues ij.1 * hB.eigenvalues ij.2) Finset.univ.val
name: NLAlib.multiset_eigenvalues_kronecker
doc:
The Kronecker product's eigenvalues are exactly all pairwise products, as a
multiset with algebraic multiplicities. Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 4.2.12.
Empty dimensions give empty multisets; pairwise products need sorting for an ordered list.
atlas: kronecker-spectral

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_eigenvalues_kronecker_sum.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
  Multiset.map ⋯.eigenvalues Finset.univ.val =
    Multiset.map (fun ij => hA.eigenvalues ij.1 + hB.eigenvalues ij.2) Finset.univ.val
name: NLAlib.multiset_eigenvalues_kronecker_sum
doc:
The Kronecker sum's eigenvalues are exactly all pairwise sums, as a multiset.
Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 4.2.12; signed symmetric spectra and empty types are included.
atlas: kronecker-spectral

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_singularValues_eq_sqrt_eigenvalues.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  Multiset.map (fun i => NLAlib.singularValues A ↑i) Finset.univ.val =
    Multiset.map (fun i => √(⋯.eigenvalues i)) Finset.univ.val
name: NLAlib.multiset_singularValues_eq_sqrt_eigenvalues
doc:
The domain-side multiset of native singular values is the square-root Gram
spectrum, including every domain zero. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 2.6.

signature:
NLAlib.multiset_singularValues_kronecker.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}
  {q : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq q] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (B : Matrix p q ℝ) :
  Multiset.map (fun i => NLAlib.singularValues (Matrix.kroneckerMap (fun x1 x2 => x1 * x2) A B) ↑i) Finset.univ.val =
    Multiset.map (fun xy => xy.1 * xy.2)
      (Multiset.map (fun i => NLAlib.singularValues A ↑i) Finset.univ.val ×ˢ
        Multiset.map (fun i => NLAlib.singularValues B ↑i) Finset.univ.val)
name: NLAlib.multiset_singularValues_kronecker
doc:
The singular values of a rectangular Kronecker product are all pairwise
products of the two native domain-side singular-value lists, with multiplicities.
Horn–Johnson 1991, Theorem 4.2.15. Domain lists have `card n`, `card q`, and
`card n * card q` entries; each includes its full domain-side zero padding.
This covers empty dimensions and the additional rectangular zeros automatically.
atlas: kronecker-spectral

signature: NLAlib.natDegree_evenChebyshevFilter_le (k : ℕ) : (NLAlib.evenChebyshevFilter k).natDegree ≤ k
name: NLAlib.natDegree_evenChebyshevFilter_le
doc:
The even second-kind filter has degree at most `k`.
Source: Kuczyński–Woźniakowski (1992) [`kw92`], §3 (the even Chebyshev filter).

signature:
NLAlib.natDegree_inv_two_pow_mul_T (q : ℕ) :

name: NLAlib.natDegree_inv_two_pow_mul_T
doc:
The scaled Chebyshev polynomial `2^(1−q) T_q` has degree `q`.
Source: Rivlin (1990), Cor. 2.1.1; Atlas: `chebyshev-monic-minimal`.

signature:
NLAlib.nat_mul_mul_pow_le_pow_add {x y : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) {p : ℕ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
  ↑p * x * y ^ (p - 1) ≤ x ^ p + ↑(p - 1) * y ^ p
name: NLAlib.nat_mul_mul_pow_le_pow_add
doc:
Integer Young's inequality, including zero scalars and order one.
Source: operator manuscript `eq:young`; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.
The proof reuses Mathlib's convex Bernoulli inequality for positive `y`.

signature:
NLAlib.nat_mul_mul_re_trace_mul_pow_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (V H : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hV : V.PosSemidef) (hH : H.IsHermitian) {p : ℕ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
  ↑p * ↑(2 * p - 1) * (V * H ^ (2 * p - 2)).trace.re ≤
    ↑(2 * p - 1) ^ p * (V ^ p).trace.re + ↑(p - 1) * (H ^ (2 * p)).trace.re
name: NLAlib.nat_mul_mul_re_trace_mul_pow_le
doc:
**Polynomial trace Young inequality.** For PSD `V`, Hermitian `H` and
integer `p≥1`, the factor `q=2p-1` can be absorbed into the two endpoint
trace moments. No commutativity hypothesis is used. Tropp 2015, §4.8;
supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.neg_complement_rowProjector_mul_moorePenroseInverse_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  -(1 - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * B) * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A =
    (1 - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * B) * (B - A).transpose * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).transpose *
      NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A
name: NLAlib.neg_complement_rowProjector_mul_moorePenroseInverse_eq
doc:
The lower-left pseudoinverse block has the complementary row-space
factor and a perturbation-adjoint factor. Stewart–Sun §III.3.

signature:
NLAlib.neg_hadamard_le_hadamard_of_neg_le_of_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {A B C D : Matrix n n ℝ} (hAB : -A ≤ B)

doc:
**Hadamard products preserve Loewner sandwiches, lower bound.** If `-A ≤ B ≤ A` and
`-C ≤ D ≤ C` then `-(A ⊙ C) ≤ B ⊙ D`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.8.16.
atlas: schur-product-inequalities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.neg_prod_sub_div_prod_erase_nonneg_of_bordered_interlacing {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → ℝ) (b : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)
  (hd : StrictMono d) (hb : Monotone b) (h : ∀ (i : Fin n), b i.castSucc ≤ d i ∧ d i ≤ b i.succ) (j : Fin n) :
  0 ≤ (-∏ i, (d j - b i)) / ∏ l ∈ Finset.univ.erase j, (d j - d l)
name: NLAlib.neg_prod_sub_div_prod_erase_nonneg_of_bordered_interlacing
doc:
Weakly interlacing bordered targets give nonnegative interpolation
residues when the original spectrum is strictly increasing. Target
equalities, repeated target roots, and zero residues are allowed.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 4.3; helper for bordered inverse interlacing.

signature:
NLAlib.neg_prod_sub_div_prod_erase_nonneg_of_rank_one_interlacing {n : ℕ} (d b : Fin n → ℝ) (hd : StrictMono d)
  (hb : Monotone b) (hlo : ∀ (i : Fin n), d i ≤ b i) (hhi : ∀ (i j : Fin n), ↑i + 1 = ↑j → b i ≤ d j) (j : Fin n) :

name: NLAlib.neg_prod_sub_div_prod_erase_nonneg_of_rank_one_interlacing
doc:
Weakly interlacing positive rank-one targets give nonnegative residues
when the original list is strictly increasing. No strictness is required
of any target inequality. Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 4.3;
helper for positive rank-one inverse interlacing.

signature: NLAlib.neg_sub_mul_log_one_sub_le {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) : -ε - (1 - ε) * Real.log (1 - ε) ≤ -(ε ^ 2 / 2)
name: NLAlib.neg_sub_mul_log_one_sub_le

signature:
NLAlib.neumann_and_inverse_perturbation.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (F A E : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hF : NLAlib.specNorm F < 1) (hA : IsUnit A) (hE : NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E) < 1) :
  IsUnit (1 - F) ∧
    (1 - F)⁻¹ = ∑' (k : ℕ), F ^ k ∧
      NLAlib.specNorm (1 - F)⁻¹ ≤ (1 - NLAlib.specNorm F)⁻¹ ∧
        NLAlib.specNorm ((1 - F)⁻¹ - 1) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm F / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm F) ∧
          IsUnit (A + E) ∧
            NLAlib.specNorm (A + E)⁻¹ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E)) ∧
              NLAlib.specNorm ((A + E)⁻¹ - A⁻¹) ≤
                  NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ ^ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E)) ∧
                NLAlib.frobNorm ((A + E)⁻¹ - A⁻¹) ≤
                  NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ ^ 2 * NLAlib.frobNorm E / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E))
name: NLAlib.neumann_and_inverse_perturbation
doc:
Complete quantitative Neumann and inverse perturbation contract. The matrix inverses are used throughout, and both the spectral and Frobenius
difference estimates retain the product-scale denominator. Empty dimensions
are included. Golub--Van Loan, Lemma 2.3.3 and Theorem 2.3.4.
atlas: inverse-perturbation

signature:
NLAlib.nodal_chebyshevZero (q : ℕ) :

name: NLAlib.nodal_chebyshevZero
doc:
The nodal polynomial of the `q` Chebyshev zeros is the monic Chebyshev polynomial:
`∏ₖ (X − cos((2k + 1)π/(2q))) = T_q / 2^(q−1)` (both sides are `1` when `q = 0`).
Source: Trefethen, *Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice*, Ch. 2–3; Rivlin,
*Chebyshev Polynomials*, §1.2.
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error` (lemma).
Deviation: no `0 < q` hypothesis is needed (`q − 1` is truncated subtraction).
atlas: chebyshev-interpolation-error

signature:

doc: The Euclidean unit sphere of `n → 𝕜` is nonempty as soon as the index type is.

NLAlib.nonneg_of_norm_le_on_open_bernsteinEllipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)

A open-ellipse bound is necessarily nonnegative, since the ellipse contains zero.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8; helper for analytic coefficient and SLQ rates.

signature:
NLAlib.norm_add_sq_le_of_mul_conjTranspose_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

Row-orthogonal complex summands obey the exact squared operator bound.
Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, the row-Gram Pythagorean competitor argument.

signature:
NLAlib.norm_array_le_one_of_hasOrthonormalCols {n k : ℕ} {Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ}

An orthonormal frame has `L2` operator norm at most one.
Source: operator re-derivation `sh:haar`; the C⋆-identity `‖QᴴQ‖ = ‖Q‖²` with `QᴴQ = 1`.

signature:
NLAlib.norm_chebyshevComplexCoeff_le {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFc : ContinuousOn F (NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse ρ))
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (interior (NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse ρ)))
  (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.filledBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) :
  ‖NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff F k‖ ≤ 2 * M / ρ ^ k
name: NLAlib.norm_chebyshevComplexCoeff_le
doc:
Positive Chebyshev coefficients of a function holomorphic in the filled Bernstein
ellipse interior and continuous on its closure decay as `2M/ρ^k`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1. The contour coefficients are explicitly defined and no decay bound
or polynomial-approximation property is assumed.
atlas: chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.norm_chebyshevComplexCoeff_le_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)

  {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) : ‖NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff F k‖ ≤ 2 * M / ρ ^ k

doc:
Under the original holomorphy and boundedness assumptions on the open Bernstein ellipse,
positive coefficients obey the exact bound `2M/ρ^k`. No continuous extension to the outer
boundary is assumed: apply the closed-radius estimate at every `1<r<ρ` and take `r↑ρ`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1.
atlas: chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.norm_chebyshevComplexCoeff_zero_le {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)

doc:
The zeroth Chebyshev coefficient has norm at most the function bound `M`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1.
Atlas `chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay` (zeroth-coefficient endpoint).

NLAlib.norm_chebyshevComplexCoeff_zero_le_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)

The zeroth Chebyshev coefficient has the sharp norm bound on the original

doc:
**Perturbation of the right-hand side.** For invertible `A`, `A x = b ≠ 0` and
`A (x + Δx) = b + Δb`: `‖Δx‖/‖x‖ ≤ κ₂(A) ‖Δb‖/‖b‖`. Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 12.1 (condition
number of `b ↦ x` is at most `κ(A)`); Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 2.6.2 with `ΔA = 0`.
atlas: linear-system-perturbation

signature:
NLAlib.norm_div_le_of_add_mulVec_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A ΔA : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : IsUnit A) {x b Δx Δb : n → ℝ} (hx : A.mulVec x = b) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hΔ : (A + ΔA).mulVec (x + Δx) = b + Δb)
  (hsmall : (NLAlib.conditionNumber A).toReal * (NLAlib.specNorm ΔA / NLAlib.specNorm A) < 1) :
  ‖WithLp.toLp 2 Δx‖ / ‖WithLp.toLp 2 x‖ ≤
    (NLAlib.conditionNumber A).toReal /
        (1 - (NLAlib.conditionNumber A).toReal * (NLAlib.specNorm ΔA / NLAlib.specNorm A)) *
      (NLAlib.specNorm ΔA / NLAlib.specNorm A + ‖WithLp.toLp 2 Δb‖ / ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖)
name: NLAlib.norm_div_le_of_add_mulVec_add
doc:
**Perturbation of a linear system.** For invertible `A`, `A x = b ≠ 0`,
`(A + ΔA)(x + Δx) = b + Δb` and `κ₂(A) ‖ΔA‖/‖A‖ < 1`:
`‖Δx‖/‖x‖ ≤ κ₂(A)/(1 - κ₂(A)‖ΔA‖/‖A‖) · (‖ΔA‖/‖A‖ + ‖Δb‖/‖b‖)`.
Higham 2002, Thm 7.2 (normwise, with `ε = ‖ΔA‖/‖A‖`-type tolerances); Golub–Van Loan 2013,
Thm 2.6.2; the first-order content is Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 12.1–12.2. Proof: `A Δx = Δb -
ΔA (x + Δx)`, so `‖Δx‖ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖(‖Δb‖ + ‖ΔA‖‖x‖ + ‖ΔA‖‖Δx‖)`; absorb the last term, then use
`‖b‖ ≤ ‖A‖‖x‖`. (`A + ΔA` is then invertible by `isUnit_add_of_specNorm_inv_mul_lt_one`, so
`Δx` is determined.)
atlas: linear-system-perturbation

The first-order angle coefficient, with finite denominator, follows from
the fitted-vector length. Golub–Van Loan, Theorem 5.3.1.

name: NLAlib.norm_least_squares_sub_le_pinv

A direct finite perturbation estimate retaining the old residual and the

signature:
NLAlib.norm_least_squares_sub_le_relative_data.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {A E : Matrix m n ℝ} {ε : ℝ} (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) (_hε : 0 ≤ ε)
  (hE : NLAlib.specNorm E ≤ ε * NLAlib.specNorm A) (b f : EuclideanSpace ℝ m) (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ ε * ‖b‖)
  (hsmall : NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * ε < 1) :
  have x := (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) b;
  have y := (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A + E))) (b + f);
  have r := b - (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) x;
  ‖y - x‖ ≤
    NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) / (1 - NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A * ε) *
      (ε * ‖b‖ + ε * NLAlib.specNorm A * ‖x‖ +
        NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) * ε * NLAlib.specNorm A * ‖r‖)
name: NLAlib.norm_least_squares_sub_le_relative_data
doc:
The direct solution error with both relative perturbations substituted,
before dividing by the nonzero solution. Higham, Theorem 20.1; Wedin §5.

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.norm_moorePenroseInverse_sub_div_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b Δb : m → ℝ) :
  ‖WithLp.toLp 2 ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec (b + Δb) - (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b)‖ /
      ‖WithLp.toLp 2 ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b)‖ ≤
    NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A / (NLAlib.leastSquaresEta A b * NLAlib.leastSquaresCos A b) *
      (‖WithLp.toLp 2 Δb‖ / ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖)
name: NLAlib.norm_moorePenroseInverse_sub_div_le
doc:
**Least squares, `x` under perturbation of `b`.** For `x = A⁺ b` and any `Δb`:
`‖Δx‖/‖x‖ ≤ κ⁺(A)/(η cos θ) · ‖Δb‖/‖b‖`, where `Δx = A⁺ Δb` and `κ⁺ = moorePenroseConditionNumber`.
Exact, any rank (`κ/(η cos θ)` equals `‖A⁺‖‖b‖/‖x‖` when `x ≠ 0`). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 18.1
(second entry of the table).
atlas: least-squares-perturbation (partial)

name: NLAlib.norm_mulVec_sq_bounds_of_specNorm_gram_sub_one_le
doc:
A Gram error bounded by `ε`, `‖TᴴT − I‖₂ ≤ ε`, keeps every squared Euclidean norm
`‖Tx‖₂²` between `(1−ε)‖x‖₂²` and `(1+ε)‖x‖₂²`, over `ℝ` or `ℂ`. Woodruff 2014, §2.1
(subspace embeddings from Gram errors); supports `leverage-sampling-ose`.

signature:

doc:
A rank-zero range is preserved by every sketch deterministically, without
forming a normalized leverage law. Source: operator re-derivation `sa:leverage-theorem`.

Complex orthonormal columns preserve the operator norm on the left.

signature:
NLAlib.norm_mul_moorePenroseInverse_sub_div_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b Δb : m → ℝ) :

    1 / NLAlib.leastSquaresCos A b * (‖WithLp.toLp 2 Δb‖ / ‖WithLp.toLp 2 b‖)
name: NLAlib.norm_mul_moorePenroseInverse_sub_div_le
doc:
**Least squares, `y` under perturbation of `b`.** For `y = A A⁺ b` and any `Δb`:
`‖Δy‖/‖y‖ ≤ (1/cos θ) ‖Δb‖/‖b‖`, where `Δy = A A⁺ Δb`. Exact (the map `b ↦ y` is linear), any
rank, no side conditions (degenerate cases are `0 ≤ ·`). Trefethen–Bau 1997, Thm 18.1 (first
entry of the table: condition number `1/cos θ`).
atlas: least-squares-perturbation (partial)

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.norm_toLp_sq_add_norm_toLp_sq_of_isHermitian_of_isIdempotentElem.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]

signature:
NLAlib.normalized_inverse_power_laplacian_limit_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ρ w : ι → ℝ)
  (i₀ : ι) (hρ₀ : ρ i₀ = 1) (hρ : ∀ (i : ι), i ≠ i₀ → 0 ≤ ρ i ∧ ρ i < 1) (b₀ k : ℝ) (hb₀ : 0 ≤ b₀) (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w i₀)
  (hrel : ∀ (j : ι), j ≠ i₀ → b₀ * ρ j * (w j - w i₀) = 1 - ρ j) :
  (2 * k -
      2 * b₀ *
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j,
            if i = j then 0
            else w j * ρ i * ρ j * (((if j = i₀ then 1 else 0) - if i = i₀ then 1 else 0) / (ρ j - ρ i))) ≤
    2 * (k - ↑(Fintype.card ι) + 1)
name: NLAlib.normalized_inverse_power_laplacian_limit_le
doc:
The limiting Gram Laplacian is at most the hard-edge coefficient
`2(k-r+1)`. Source: operator soft minimum gap correction; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (sharp limiting coefficient helper).
The algebraic ratio identity holds for `ρj=(λmin+ε)/(λj+ε)` and
`b₀=1/(λmin+ε)`, with `w` the Gram eigenvalues.

signature:
NLAlib.normalized_inverse_power_laplacian_symmetric_limit_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (ρ w : ι → ℝ) (i₀ : ι) (hρ₀ : ρ i₀ = 1) (hρ : ∀ (i : ι), i ≠ i₀ → 0 ≤ ρ i ∧ ρ i < 1) (b₀ k : ℝ) (hb₀ : 0 ≤ b₀)
  (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w i₀) (hrel : ∀ (j : ι), j ≠ i₀ → b₀ * ρ j * (w j - w i₀) = 1 - ρ j) :
  2 * k -
      b₀ *
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
            (w i + w j) * ρ i * ρ j * (((if j = i₀ then 1 else 0) - if i = i₀ then 1 else 0) / (ρ j - ρ i)) ≤
    2 * (k - ↑(Fintype.card ι) + 1)
name: NLAlib.normalized_inverse_power_laplacian_symmetric_limit_le
doc:
The symmetric limiting Gram Laplacian is bounded by the exact
hard-edge coefficient. Source: inverse spectral gap correction; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (sharp limiting bound helper).

idempotent. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Theorem 1.4.7; nonzero pairing is
the exact side condition, without a simplicity assumption.

NLAlib.nuclearNorm.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

NLAlib.nuclearNorm_eq_of_gram_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

values of its full decreasing eigenvalue list. Empty dimensions are included.

The trace of the positive polar factor is the nuclear norm, including
singular and empty matrices. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.4.

left-polar convention. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.6.

doc:
**Numerical inequality for the inverse Wishart spectral moments.** For integers
`1 ≤ p ≤ 18` and `x ≥ 2p`,
`(1 + 2p/(x+1-2p)) · (1/Γ(x+2))^{2p/(x+1)} ≤ (e/x)^{2p}`.

signature:
NLAlib.one_sub_filter_mean_le_four_div_sq.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (d g : ι → ℝ) {H : ℝ}
  (hd : ∀ (i : ι), d i ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) (hH : 0 < H) (hHtop : H ≤ ∑ i with d i = 1, g i ^ 2) (k : ℕ) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ)
  (hLog : Real.log ((∑ i, g i ^ 2) / H) ≤ ↑ℓ * Real.log 2) :
  1 -
      (∑ i, d i * (Polynomial.eval (d i) (NLAlib.evenChebyshevFilter k) ^ ℓ) ^ 2 * g i ^ 2) /
        ∑ i, (Polynomial.eval (d i) (NLAlib.evenChebyshevFilter k) ^ ℓ) ^ 2 * g i ^ 2 ≤
    4 / ↑(2 * k + 1) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.one_sub_filter_mean_le_four_div_sq
doc:
**Finite filter means of a power of the even Chebyshev filter.** Let `d i ∈ [0, 1]` be
scaled eigenvalues with weights `g i ^ 2`, and let `H > 0` be at most the weight carried by the
positions with `d i = 1` (the top eigenvalue). If `ℓ log 2` dominates the logarithmic ratio
`log(∑ g_i²/H)`, then the relative deficiency of the filtered mean
`∑ d_i f_k(d_i)^{2ℓ} g_i² / ∑ f_k(d_i)^{2ℓ} g_i²` is at most `4/(2k+1)²`.
Source: Kuczyński–Woźniakowski (1992) [`kw92`], §3 (deterministic part).
Deviation: the top weight `H` is any lower bound on the mass at the top eigenvalue (the source
takes one eigenvector coordinate). Helper for `random-start-power`.

signature:
NLAlib.one_sub_le_measure_isSubspaceEmbedding_gaussianMatrix {k m d : ℕ} (U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin d) ℝ)
  (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) {ε δ : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1)
  (hk : 18 * (↑d + 2 * Real.log (2 / δ)) / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  1 - δ ≤ (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin k) (Fin m)).real {G | NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding ((1 / √↑k) • G) U ε}
name: NLAlib.one_sub_le_measure_isSubspaceEmbedding_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Gaussian oblivious subspace embedding.** Let `U ∈ ℝ^{m×d}` have orthonormal columns,
`0 < ε ≤ 1`, `0 < δ ≤ 1` and `k ≥ 18 (d + 2 log(2/δ)) / ε²`. Then a `k × m` standard Gaussian
matrix `G` makes `S = k^{-1/2} G` an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` with probability at least
`1 − δ`.

Woodruff 2014, Thm 2.3 (stated there with unspecified constants); Martinsson–Tropp 2020, §8.7,
§9.3. Atlas `gaussian-ose` (uses `ose-def`, `extreme-singular-values-deviation`,
`rotation-invariance`). Deviations: explicit constant `18` and `2 log(2/δ)` in place of the
atlas's `C` and `log(1/δ)`; the probability is an outer-measure lower bound (no measurability of
the embedding event is claimed); `d = 0` holds trivially.
atlas: gaussian-ose

doc:
A nonnegative spectral power ratio with one eigenvalue equal to one has error
at most the logarithmic inverse leading overlap divided by `2q+1`.
Source: manuscript `rt:power`; finite scalar power-mean Jensen. The statement
includes `q=0` and needs no gap or upper bound on the other spectral values.

signature:
NLAlib.one_sub_two_mul_mul_specNorm_le_iSup.{u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (I : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ n × EuclideanSpace ℝ m))
  (hI : ∀ t ∈ I, ‖t.2‖ = 1)
  (hcov :
    ∀ (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ m), ‖u‖ = 1 → ‖v‖ = 1 → ∃ t ∈ I, ‖u - t.1‖ ≤ ε ∧ ‖v - t.2‖ ≤ ε) :
  (1 - 2 * ε) * NLAlib.specNorm A ≤ ⨆ t, ∑ i, ∑ j, (↑t).2.ofLp i * A i j * (↑t).1.ofLp j
name: NLAlib.one_sub_two_mul_mul_specNorm_le_iSup
doc:
Net argument for the spectral norm: if every pair of unit vectors `(u, v)` is `ε`-close to a
pair in the finite set `I` (whose second components are unit vectors), then
`(1 - 2ε)‖A‖₂ ≤ max_{(u,v) ∈ I} ⟨v, A u⟩`. Vershynin 2012, Lemma 5.4 (in this form). Helper for
atlas `gordon`, `spectral-second-moment`.

signature: NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse (ρ : ℝ) : Set ℂ

doc:
The open Bernstein ellipse is the Joukowski image of the open annulus
`ρ⁻¹<|w|<ρ`, including the real segment. Its use imposes no boundary extension assumption.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`, definition).

The logarithm is operator concave on `(0, ∞)`, i.e. `-log` is operator convex there.

signature:
NLAlib.operator_jensen {d m n : ℕ} [NeZero d] [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (I : Set ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ)

doc:
The **Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup** on the standard Gaussian line (Mehler's formula):
`P_t h(x) = ∫ h(e^{-t} x + √(1 - e^{-2t}) y) dγ(y)`, `γ = N(0,1)`. Source: Bakry–Gentil–Ledoux 2014, (2.7.1).
Atlas: `ornstein-uhlenbeck`.
atlas: ornstein-uhlenbeck

signature: NLAlib.ornsteinUhlenbeckFisherIntegrand (t : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.ornsteinUhlenbeckFisherIntegrand
doc:
Fisher integrand of the Mehler operator, written using its explicit
commutation relation. The next bridge identifies it with the
spatial derivative on the polynomial-growth domain.
Source: Bakry--Gentil--Ledoux, §5.7. Atlas: `ornstein-uhlenbeck`.
atlas: ornstein-uhlenbeck

signature:
NLAlib.ornsteinUhlenbeckFisherIntegrand_eq (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (C : ℝ) (d : ℕ)
  (hValue : ∀ (y : ℝ), |f y| ≤ C * (1 + |y|) ^ d) (hDeriv : ∀ (y : ℝ), |deriv f y| ≤ C * (1 + |y|) ^ d) (t x : ℝ) :

    deriv (NLAlib.ornsteinUhlenbeck t f) x ^ 2 / NLAlib.ornsteinUhlenbeck t f x
name: NLAlib.ornsteinUhlenbeckFisherIntegrand_eq
doc:
The commutation form of the Fisher integrand equals its
derivative form. Source: the proved polynomial-growth commutation
relation. Atlas: `ornstein-uhlenbeck`.

signature:

A canonical orthonormal basis matrix for a Hilbert subspace, with no manual
coordinate transport. In particular, it applies directly to `columnSpace B`.
The empty subspace yields an empty frame. Source: Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.4.

Source-transport helper `orthonormalBasis_repr_sum_smul` for Hanson–Wright.

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
  (Q X : Matrix n k ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm
doc:
The tangent of the largest principal angle between `range Q` (`Q` orthonormal) and
`range X` (`X` any block with the same number of columns and `QᵀX` invertible):
`tan θ_max = ‖(I − QQᵀ) X (QᵀX)⁻¹‖₂`; with an orthonormal complement `Q⊥` this is
`‖Q⊥ᵀ X (QᵀX)⁻¹‖₂` (`overlapTangentNorm_eq_specNorm_transpose_mul_mul`). Junk value `0` when `QᵀX` is
singular (the angle is `π/2`). Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.2 (proof of Thm 5.2);
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.2.4. Alternative: a definition via
`tan ∘ principalAnglesFintype` would need the SVD; this one is index-free and basis-independent in `X`.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_congr_left.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {Q P : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hP : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P)
  (h : Q.mulVecLin.range = P.mulVecLin.range) (X : Matrix n k ℝ) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X = NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm P X
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_congr_left
doc:
`tan θ_max` depends only on `range Q` among orthonormal frames with the same index type:
if `range Q = range P` then `tan θ_max(Q, X) = tan θ_max(P, X)`. Proof: `P = Q W` with `W = QᵀP`
orthogonal, so the inverse picks up a right factor `W`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.2.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_of_range_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] (Q : Matrix n k ℝ) {X Y : Matrix n k ℝ} (h : X.mulVecLin.range = Y.mulVecLin.range)
  (hX : IsUnit (Q.transpose * X)) : NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X = NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q Y
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_of_range_eq
doc:
`tan θ_max` depends only on `range X`: if `range X = range Y` and `QᵀX` is invertible,
then `tan θ_max(Q, X) = tan θ_max(Q, Y)` (and `QᵀY` is invertible too). Source: Saad (2011)
[`saad11`], §5.2.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_specNorm_transpose_mul_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {r : Type u_4} [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] (Q : Matrix n k ℝ)
  {Qp : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQp : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Qp) (hc : Q * Q.transpose + Qp * Qp.transpose = 1)
  (X : Matrix n k ℝ) : NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X = NLAlib.specNorm (Qp.transpose * X * (Q.transpose * X)⁻¹)
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_specNorm_transpose_mul_mul
doc:
With an orthonormal complement `Q⊥`: `tan θ_max = ‖Q⊥ᵀ X (QᵀX)⁻¹‖₂`, the form of Saad and
Golub–Van Loan. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.2; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.2.4.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_zero_of_not_isUnit.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] (Q X : Matrix n k ℝ) (hC : ¬IsUnit (Q.transpose * X)) : NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X = 0
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_eq_zero_of_not_isUnit
doc:
Singular overlap makes the total algebraic inverse-overlap norm zero.
This is a totalization convention, not a finite tangent at a right angle.

name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_le_of_range_eq_subspaceIterate
doc:
**Convergence of subspace iteration, basis form.** Under the hypotheses of
`overlapTangentNorm_pow_mul_le`, for any `Q₀` with `range Q₀ = range Ω` and any `Q_k` with
`range Q_k = S_k = subspaceIterate A Ω k` (for instance the orthonormal bases the algorithm
carries), `tan θ_max(range U, range Q_k) ≤ (β/α)^k tan θ_max(range U, range Q₀)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 5.2; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Thm 8.2.2.
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_mul_right.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] (Q X : Matrix n k ℝ) {R : Matrix k k ℝ} (hR : IsUnit R) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q (X * R) = NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_mul_right
doc:
`tan θ_max` is invariant under a change of basis of `range X`: `tan θ_max(Q, X R) =
tan θ_max(Q, X)` for invertible `R`, since `(I − QQᵀ) X R (QᵀXR)⁻¹ = (I − QQᵀ) X (QᵀX)⁻¹`. In
particular `X` need not be orthonormalised. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.2.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] (Q X : Matrix n k ℝ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q X
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_nonneg
doc: `tan θ_max ≥ 0`. Atlas `principal-angles-def` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_pow_mul_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype s] [DecidableEq s] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {U : Matrix n s ℝ}
  {V : Matrix n r ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) (hV : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V)
  (hUV : U * U.transpose + V * V.transpose = 1) {d : s → ℝ} {e : r → ℝ} (hAU : A * U = U * Matrix.diagonal d)
  (hAV : A * V = V * Matrix.diagonal e) {α β : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hβ : 0 ≤ β) (hd : ∀ (i : s), α ≤ |d i|)
  (he : ∀ (j : r), |e j| ≤ β) {Ω : Matrix n s ℝ} (hΩ : IsUnit (U.transpose * Ω)) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm U (A ^ k * Ω) ≤ (β / α) ^ k * NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm U Ω
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm_pow_mul_le
doc:
**Convergence of subspace iteration (symmetric case).** With an invariant orthogonal
splitting `UUᵀ + VVᵀ = I`, `AU = U diag(d)`, `AV = V diag(e)`, `|dᵢ| ≥ α > 0`, `|eⱼ| ≤ β` and
`UᵀΩ` invertible:
`tan θ_max(range U, range (A^k Ω)) ≤ (β/α)^k tan θ_max(range U, range Ω)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 5.2 (symmetric case); Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`],
Thm 8.2.2. Deviation: invariant splitting `(U, V, d, e)` with bounds `α, β` instead of ordered
eigenvalues (`α = |λ_s|`, `β = |λ_{s+1}|`); the iterate is the block `A^k Ω` (any basis of `S_k`:
`overlapTangentNorm_le_of_range_eq_subspaceIterate`).
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence

signature: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (u x : n → ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq
doc:
The totalized quadratic overlap ratio of `u` and `x`,
`tan² ∠(u, x) = (‖u‖² ‖x‖² − ⟨u, x⟩²)/⟨u, x⟩²`. For a unit `u` this is
`‖(I − u uᵀ) x‖²/⟨u, x⟩²`. The algebraic value is `0` when `⟨u, x⟩ = 0` (the angle is `π/2`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1 (where `tan θ(u, x)` is used with `‖u‖ = 1`).
Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle` (the one-column case of `overlapTangentNorm`,
`sq_overlapTangentNorm_replicateCol_eq_overlapTangentSq`).

name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Eigenvector angle, polynomial form.** Let `u` be a unit eigenvector for the eigenvalue
`λ_{i₀}` at sorted position `i₀`, and `p` a polynomial with `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every other sorted
position. Then `tan² ∠(u, p(A) b) ≤ (M/p(λ_{i₀}))² tan² ∠(u, b)`. With `deg p < q`,
`p(A) b ∈ K_q(A, b)`. This algebraic quotient identity uses zero at vanishing overlap; its geometric form
`tanSqAngle_aeval_mulVec_le` requires nonzero starting overlap and nonzero `p(λ_{i₀})`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1, proof of the angle bound
(`i = 1`).
atlas: krylov-eigenvector-angle (partial)

name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_inverseIterate_le
doc:
**Inverse iteration, angle bound.** Let `A` be real symmetric, `μ` not an eigenvalue, `u` a
unit eigenvector for the eigenvalue `λ_{i₀}` at sorted position `i₀` (the one closest to `μ`),
and `d > 0` with `|λᵢ − μ| ≥ d` at every other sorted position (`d` the distance of the second
closest, T&B's `|μ − λ_K|`). Then the inverse-iteration iterates satisfy
`tan² ∠(u, (A − μI)^{-k} x₀) ≤ (|λ_{i₀} − μ|/d)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`. Source:
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 27.2; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.2.2.
Deviations: squared tangents; unnormalised iterates (normalisation is bookkeeping,
`overlapTangentSq_smul`).
atlas: inverse-iteration

name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_le_of_forall_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eq
doc:
**Angle contraction under a spectral multiplier.** Let `u` be a unit eigenvector for the
eigenvalue at sorted position `i₀`, `|g| ≤ M` at every other sorted position, and
`uᵢ ⬝ w = g(λᵢ)(uᵢ ⬝ v)` for every `i` (e.g. `w = p(A) v`, `w = (A − μI)⁻¹ v`). Then
`tan² ∠(u, w) ≤ (M/g(λ_{i₀}))² tan² ∠(u, v)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], proof of
Thm 27.1. Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`, `power-iteration`, `inverse-iteration`.

signature: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (u x : n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_nonneg
doc: `tan² ∠(u, x) ≥ 0` (Cauchy–Schwarz). Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`.

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_of_norm_eq_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {u : n → ℝ} (hu : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1)
  (x : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x = (x ⬝ᵥ x - (u ⬝ᵥ x) ^ 2) / (u ⬝ᵥ x) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_of_norm_eq_one
doc: For a unit vector `u`, `tan² ∠(u, x) = (‖x‖² − (u ⬝ x)²)/(u ⬝ x)²`. Helper.

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_powerIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₀ : Fin (Fintype.card n)} {u : n → ℝ} (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ • u)
  (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ i₀ → |hA.eigenvalues₀ i| ≤ ρ)
  (x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u (NLAlib.powerIterate A x₀ k) ≤
    (ρ / |hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀|) ^ (2 * k) * NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x₀
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_powerIterate_le
doc:
**Power iteration, angle bound.** Let `A` be real symmetric, `u` a unit eigenvector for the
eigenvalue `λ₁ = λ_{i₀}` at sorted position `i₀`, and `|λᵢ| ≤ ρ` at every other sorted
position. Then `tan² ∠(u, A^k x₀) ≤ (ρ/|λ₁|)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`. No hypothesis on `x₀` or on
the gap is needed for the inequality (a right angle has the junk value `0` on both sides); it
is informative when `ρ < |λ₁|` and `u ⬝ x₀ ≠ 0`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`],
Thm 27.1; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], Thm 8.2.1. Deviations: squared tangents; `ρ` any
bound on the other eigenvalues (T&B: `ρ = |λ₂|`); unnormalised iterates
(`overlapTangentSq_powerStep_iterate_le` for the normalised ones).
atlas: power-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_powerStep_iterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₀ : Fin (Fintype.card n)} {u : n → ℝ} (hu : A.mulVec u = hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀ • u)
  (hu1 : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : ∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)), i ≠ i₀ → |hA.eigenvalues₀ i| ≤ ρ)
  (x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u ((NLAlib.powerStep A)^[k] x₀) ≤
    (ρ / |hA.eigenvalues₀ i₀|) ^ (2 * k) * NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x₀
name: NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_powerStep_iterate_le
doc:
**Power iteration, normalised iterates.** Under the hypotheses of
`overlapTangentSq_powerIterate_le`, the textbook iterates `x_k = (powerStep A)^[k] x₀` (normalised at
every step) satisfy `tan² ∠(u, x_k) ≤ (ρ/|λ₁|)^{2k} tan² ∠(u, x₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau
(1997) [`tb97`], Thm 27.1.
atlas: power-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.overlapTangentSq_smul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (u x : n → ℝ) {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) :

signature: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) : Matrix n (Fin k) ℝ
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor
doc:
The **partial Cholesky factor** `F ∈ ℝ^{n×k}`: column `j` is `R(:, s j) / √R(s j, s j)` with
`R` the residual after the first `j` pivots. CETW 2023, Alg. 1; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_castSucc.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin (k + 1) → n) (i : n)
  (j : Fin k) : NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A s i j.castSucc = NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A (Fin.init s) i j
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_castSucc
doc:
The first `k` columns of the factor for `k + 1` pivots are the factor for the first `k`
pivots.

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_last.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin (k + 1) → n) (i : n) :
  NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A s i (Fin.last k) =
    NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A (Fin.init s) i (s (Fin.last k)) /
      √(NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A (Fin.init s) (s (Fin.last k)) (s (Fin.last k)))
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_last
doc: The last column of the factor is the scaled pivot column of the current residual.

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_mul_transpose_eq_nystrom.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) :
  NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A s * (NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor A s).transpose =
    NLAlib.nystrom A (NLAlib.selectionMatrix s)
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyFactor_mul_transpose_eq_nystrom
doc:
SCAFFOLD: partial-cholesky-nystrom
**Partial Cholesky is column Nyström**: for PSD `A` and any pivot sequence `s`,
`F Fᵀ = A(:,S) A(S,S)⁺ A(S,:)`, the Nyström approximation with the selection matrix of `S`.
CETW 2023, §2 (label to verify); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9.
Proof sketch: write `A = GᵀG` (`exists_eq_transpose_mul_of_posSemidef`). Partial Cholesky on
`A` is Gram–Schmidt on the columns `G(:, s 0), G(:, s 1), …` in order: by induction the
residual is `Gᵀ (I − Pⱼ) G` with `Pⱼ` the orthogonal projector onto the span of the first `j`
pivot columns of `G` (a zero pivot means the column is already in the span). Hence
`F Fᵀ = Gᵀ P_k G`, and `nystrom_eq_of_eq_transpose_mul` gives `nystrom A Ω = Gᵀ P G` with
`P` the projector onto `range (G Ω) = span {G(:, s j)}`.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom

signature: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {k : ℕ} : (Fin k → n) → Matrix n n ℝ
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual
doc:
The **residual of partial Cholesky** after the pivots `s 0, …, s (k−1)`, in this order.
CETW 2023, Alg. 1 (residual update); Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_left.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_left
doc:
The partial Cholesky residual of a PSD matrix vanishes on the pivot rows.
CETW 2023, §2.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_right.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) (j : Fin k) (i : n) : NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A s i (s j) = 0
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_right
doc:
The partial Cholesky residual of a PSD matrix vanishes on the pivot columns.

atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_eq_sub_nystrom.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) {k : ℕ} (s : Fin k → n) :
  NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A s =
    A - A.submatrix id s * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (A.submatrix s s) * A.submatrix s id
name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_eq_sub_nystrom
doc:
**The partial Cholesky residual is the generalized Schur complement**:
`R = A − A(:,S) A(S,S)⁺ A(S,:)`, for PSD `A` and any pivot sequence. With
`posSemidef_partialCholeskyResidual` and `partialCholeskyResidual_apply_pivot_left/right`, the
residual is PSD and zero on the rows and columns of `S`. CETW 2023, §2; Golub–Van Loan 2013,
§4.2.9.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom

name: NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual_eq_zero_of_rank_le
doc:
Every positive-probability pivot history is exact once its length reaches the
input rank. Source: manuscript `sa:rp-rank`; CETW (2025), rank-zero termination.
atlas: rpcholesky (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace {n k : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hH : H.rank = n) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun g => g ⬝ᵥ g - H.mulVec g ⬝ᵥ (H * H.transpose)⁻¹.mulVec (H.mulVec g))
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => ∑ j, x j ^ 2)
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
name: NLAlib.pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace
doc:
**Law of the residual of a Gaussian row.** Let `H` be a fixed `n × k` real matrix of rank
`n` and `g` a standard Gaussian vector in `ℝᵏ`. The squared distance from `g` to the row space of
`H`, `‖g‖² - (H g)ᵀ (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ (H g)`, has the `χ²_{k-n}` law (the law of `∑ⱼ Xⱼ²`,
`X ~ N(0, I_{k-n})`).

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 / HMT 2011, Prop A.5. Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean`
(helper). Proof ported from the Prove2me solution `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law`
(orthonormal basis of `ker H` and the block law `hasLaw_gaussianMatrix_block`, atlas
`block-law-indep`).

signature:
NLAlib.pinvL.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

Left pseudoinverse `(Gᴴ G)⁻¹ Gᴴ` (at `𝕜 = ℝ`: `(Gᵀ G)⁻¹ Gᵀ`), the Moore–Penrose inverse of a
matrix of full column rank. Junk value `0` when `Gᴴ G` is singular (Mathlib's `A⁻¹ = 0`); the
theorems take `IsUnit (Gᴴ * G)`. HMT 2011, §A.2.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.pinvL_conjTranspose.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

`((GᴴG)⁻¹Gᴴ)ᴴ = G(GᴴG)⁻¹`, i.e. `(pinvL G)ᴴ = pinvR Gᴴ`. Holds unconditionally (both sides
are `G (GᴴG)⁻¹` with Mathlib's total inverse). HMT 2011 §A.2; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

minimizers. Higham, Theorem 20.1; arbitrary finite indices.

signature:
NLAlib.pinv_solution_norm_pos.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} (hA : A.rank = Fintype.card n) (b : EuclideanSpace ℝ m)
  (hx : (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) b ≠ 0) :
  0 < ‖(Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) b)‖ ∧ 0 < ‖b‖
name: NLAlib.pinv_solution_norm_pos
doc:
A nonzero full-rank Moore–Penrose solution has nonzero fitted value and
nonzero data. Golub–Van Loan, Theorem 5.3.1.

signature: NLAlib.pivotSchur {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.pivotSchur
doc:
The **Schur complement of the leading pivot**: for `A = [[a, rᵀ], [c, C]]` on `Fin (n + 1)`,
`pivotSchur A = C − a⁻¹ c rᵀ`. This is the trailing matrix after one step of Gaussian
elimination (Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 20; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §3.2.10) and of the Cholesky
recursion (Trefethen–Bau 1997, Lect. 23). Total: for `a = 0` it is the trailing block `C`.

signature:
NLAlib.pivotSchur_apply {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) (i j : Fin n) :
  NLAlib.pivotSchur A i j = A i.succ j.succ - (A 0 0)⁻¹ * (A i.succ 0 * A 0 j.succ)
name: NLAlib.pivotSchur_apply
doc: Entrywise form of the pivot Schur complement: `Cᵢⱼ − cᵢ rⱼ / a`.

signature:
NLAlib.pivotSchur_leadingSubmatrix {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : k + 1 ≤ n + 1) :
  NLAlib.pivotSchur (NLAlib.leadingSubmatrix A (k + 1)) = NLAlib.leadingSubmatrix (NLAlib.pivotSchur A) k
name: NLAlib.pivotSchur_leadingSubmatrix
doc:
The pivot Schur complement commutes with taking leading blocks:
`pivotSchur (A(1:k+1, 1:k+1)) = (pivotSchur A)(1:k, 1:k)`.

signature: NLAlib.planeRotation.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [DecidableEq n] (u v : n → ℝ) (c s : ℝ) : Matrix n n ℝ
name: NLAlib.planeRotation
doc:
The **plane rotation** by `(c, s)` in the plane of the orthonormal pair `u, v`:
`I + (c − 1)(u uᵀ + v vᵀ) + s (u vᵀ − v uᵀ)`. For `u = eᵢ`, `v = eⱼ` this is Golub–Van Loan's
`G(i, j, θ)` with `c = cos θ`, `s = sin θ`. For a non-orthonormal pair it is just this matrix.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.8.

signature:
NLAlib.planeRotation_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (u v x : n → ℝ) (c s : ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s).mulVec x =
    x + (c - 1) • ((u ⬝ᵥ x) • u + (v ⬝ᵥ x) • v) + s • ((v ⬝ᵥ x) • u - (u ⬝ᵥ x) • v)
name: NLAlib.planeRotation_mulVec
doc:
A plane rotation acts by `x ↦ x + (c − 1)((u·x) u + (v·x) v) + s ((v·x) u − (u·x) v)`:
on the plane, `u ↦ c u − s v` and `v ↦ s u + c v`; the orthogonal complement is fixed.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, §5.1.8.

signature:
NLAlib.planeRotation_mul_mul_transpose_apply_diag_of_disjoint_eigenvectors.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hA : A.transpose = A) (u v : n → ℝ) (hu : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1)
  (hv : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 v‖ = 1) (huv : u ⬝ᵥ v = 0) (α β : ℝ) (hAu : A.mulVec u = α • u) (hAv : A.mulVec v = β • v)
  (hdisjoint : ∀ (i : n), u i * v i = 0) (c s : ℝ) (hcs : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) (i : n) :
  (NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s * A * (NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s).transpose) i i =
    A i i + s ^ 2 * (β - α) * (u i ^ 2 - v i ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.planeRotation_mul_mul_transpose_apply_diag_of_disjoint_eigenvectors
doc:
The diagonal increment from rotating eigenvectors with disjoint coordinate supports is
exactly `s²(β-α)(uᵢ²-vᵢ²)`, including repeated and negative eigenvalues. Horn–Johnson 2013,
proof of Theorem 4.3.48.

signature:
NLAlib.planeRotation_mul_mul_transpose_of_eigenvectors.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hA : A.transpose = A) (u v : n → ℝ) (hu : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) (hv : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 v‖ = 1)
  (huv : u ⬝ᵥ v = 0) (α β : ℝ) (hAu : A.mulVec u = α • u) (hAv : A.mulVec v = β • v) (c s : ℝ)
  (hcs : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) :
  NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s * A * (NLAlib.planeRotation u v c s).transpose =
    A + (s ^ 2 * (β - α)) • (Matrix.vecMulVec u u - Matrix.vecMulVec v v) +
      (c * s * (β - α)) • (Matrix.vecMulVec u v + Matrix.vecMulVec v u)
name: NLAlib.planeRotation_mul_mul_transpose_of_eigenvectors
doc:
Conjugating a symmetric matrix by a rotation of two of its eigenvectors changes only their
two-dimensional spectral block; no restriction on signed or repeated eigenvalues.
Horn–Johnson 2013, proof of Theorem 4.3.48.

signature:
NLAlib.planeRotation_single_conjugation_diag.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (hA : A.transpose = A) (i j : n) (hij : i ≠ j) (c s : ℝ) (hcs : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) (k : n) :
  have Δ := 2 * c * s * A i j + s ^ 2 * (A j j - A i i);
  (NLAlib.planeRotation (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1) c s * A *
        (NLAlib.planeRotation (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1) c s).transpose)
      k k =
    A k k + if k = i then Δ else if k = j then -Δ else 0
name: NLAlib.planeRotation_single_conjugation_diag
doc:
A coordinate plane rotation changes the two selected diagonal entries by
opposite increments and fixes every other diagonal entry. Schur–Horn variational
rederivation, equation (1).

signature:
NLAlib.polarFrame.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq q] (Y : Matrix m q ℝ) :
  Matrix m q ℝ
name: NLAlib.polarFrame

signature:
NLAlib.polarFrame_mul_transpose_mul_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {q : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq q]
  (Y : Matrix m q ℝ) (hY : IsUnit (Y.transpose * Y)) : NLAlib.polarFrame Y * ((NLAlib.polarFrame Y).transpose * Y) = Y
name: NLAlib.polarFrame_mul_transpose_mul_eq
doc:
The polar frame reproduces its input exactly under its orthogonal projector when
the column Gram matrix is invertible. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `gn-expected-error`.

signature: NLAlib.polarSingularCoefficients (r i : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.polarSingularCoefficients
doc:
The polar singular coefficients are one exactly on the positive
singular-value prefix of length equal to the matrix rank.
Bhatia (1997), §IV.2; matrix toolkit derivations, (10)–(12).

signature: NLAlib.polarSingularCoefficients_antitone (r : ℕ) : Antitone (NLAlib.polarSingularCoefficients r)
name: NLAlib.polarSingularCoefficients_antitone
doc:
Polar singular coefficients decrease with their index.
Bhatia (1997), §IV.2; matrix toolkit derivations, (10)–(12).

signature: NLAlib.polarSingularCoefficients_nonneg (r i : ℕ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.polarSingularCoefficients r i
name: NLAlib.polarSingularCoefficients_nonneg
doc:
Polar singular coefficients are nonnegative.
Bhatia (1997), §IV.2; matrix toolkit derivations, (10)–(12).

signature:
NLAlib.polar_coisometry_unique_iff_rank_eq_card.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] {A U : Matrix m n ℝ} (hU : U * U.transpose = 1) (hA : CFC.sqrt (A * A.transpose) * U = A) :
  (∀ (V : Matrix m n ℝ), V * V.transpose = 1 → CFC.sqrt (A * A.transpose) * V = A → V = U) ↔ A.rank = Fintype.card m
name: NLAlib.polar_coisometry_unique_iff_rank_eq_card
doc:
Coisometry uniqueness in the wide formulation holds exactly at full row
rank. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.3.1.
atlas: polar-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.polar_isometry_unique_iff_rank_eq_card.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A U : Matrix m n ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) (hA : U * CFC.sqrt (A.transpose * A) = A) :
  (∀ (V : Matrix m n ℝ), NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V → V * CFC.sqrt (A.transpose * A) = A → V = U) ↔
    A.rank = Fintype.card n
name: NLAlib.polar_isometry_unique_iff_rank_eq_card
doc:
Among polar isometries, uniqueness holds exactly at full column rank,
including the empty column space. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 7.3.1.
atlas: polar-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.polyIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (s : Polynomial ℝ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.polyIterate
doc:
The polynomial method with iteration polynomial `s`: `x₀ + s(A) r₀`, `r₀ = c − A x₀`. Its
residual polynomial is `1 − X s`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1 (polynomial
iterations); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.6.
atlas: polynomial-method-def

name: NLAlib.polyIterate_sub
doc:
The error of a polynomial method is `(1 − X s)(A)(x₀ − x⋆)` when `A x⋆ = c`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1.
atlas: polynomial-method-def

signature:
NLAlib.polyIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) {s : Polynomial ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hs : s.degree < ↑q) :
  NLAlib.polyIterate A c x₀ s - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q
name: NLAlib.polyIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
A polynomial method with `deg s < q` stays in the affine Krylov space `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1.

signature:
NLAlib.polynomial_eq_base_sub_residue_sum.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ι → ℝ)
  (hd : Function.Injective d) (q base : Polynomial ℝ) (hdeg : (q - base).degree < ↑(Fintype.card ι))
  (hbase : ∀ (j : ι), Polynomial.eval (d j) base = 0) :
  q =
    base -
      ∑ j,
        Polynomial.C (-Polynomial.eval (d j) q / ∏ l ∈ Finset.univ.erase j, (d j - d l)) *
          ∏ l ∈ Finset.univ.erase j, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (d l))
name: NLAlib.polynomial_eq_base_sub_residue_sum
doc:
A polynomial remainder of degree below the number of distinct nodes
equals the sum of its simple residue numerators. Horn--Johnson (2013),
Section 4.3; inverse interlacing helper.

name: NLAlib.posDef_extreme_eigenvalues_sandwich
doc:
The extreme sorted eigenvalues of a positive definite matrix are positive
spectral endpoints for a Loewner sandwich. Positive dimension is explicit.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.4.12; helper for sharp constants.

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_iff_exists_strict_sqrt_contraction_factor.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {B : Matrix m n ℝ} {C : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)
  (hC : C.PosDef) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C).PosDef ↔ ∃ X, NLAlib.specNorm X < 1 ∧ B = CFC.sqrt A * X * CFC.sqrt C
name: NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_iff_exists_strict_sqrt_contraction_factor
doc:
A block with positive definite diagonal blocks is positive definite
exactly when it has a strict square-root contraction factorization.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.7.7.
atlas: psd-block-contraction (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_iff_posDef_and_schur.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m m ℝ) (B : Matrix m n ℝ) (C : Matrix n n ℝ) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C).PosDef ↔ A.PosDef ∧ (C - B.transpose * A⁻¹ * B).PosDef
name: NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_iff_posDef_and_schur
doc:
A symmetric block matrix `[A B; Bᵀ C]` is positive definite exactly when its leading block
`A` and its Schur complement `C − BᵀA⁻¹B` are both positive definite; no invertibility
hypothesis is needed (the forward implication derives it). Horn--Johnson (2013),
Exercise 4.5.P21 and Theorem 7.7.7.
atlas: haynsworth-inertia-additivity (partial), psd-block-contraction (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_iff_specNorm_lt_one_of_sqrt_factor.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {B X : Matrix m n ℝ} {C : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)
  (hC : C.PosDef) (hB : B = CFC.sqrt A * X * CFC.sqrt C) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C).PosDef ↔ NLAlib.specNorm X < 1
name: NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_iff_specNorm_lt_one_of_sqrt_factor
doc:
For positive definite diagonal blocks, every square-root factorization
identifies positive definiteness with a strict contraction bound.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.7.7;
helper for strict PSD-block factorization.

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_iff_strict_bilinear_tests.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  {A : Matrix m m ℝ} {B : Matrix m n ℝ} {C : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) (hC : C.PosDef) :
  ((Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C).PosDef ↔
      ∀ (x : m → ℝ) (y : n → ℝ), x ≠ 0 → y ≠ 0 → (x ⬝ᵥ B.mulVec y) ^ 2 < NLAlib.quadForm A x * NLAlib.quadForm C y) ∧
    ((Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C).PosDef ↔
      ∀ (x : m → ℝ) (y : n → ℝ), x ≠ 0 ∨ y ≠ 0 → 2 * |x ⬝ᵥ B.mulVec y| < NLAlib.quadForm A x + NLAlib.quadForm C y)
name: NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_iff_strict_bilinear_tests
doc:
With positive definite diagonal blocks, strict bilinear-square tests on
two nonzero vectors and strict absolute tests on every nonzero combined
vector each characterize block positive definiteness.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.7.7.
atlas: psd-block-contraction (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_zero_iff.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m m ℝ) (C : Matrix n n ℝ) : (Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 C).PosDef ↔ A.PosDef ∧ C.PosDef
name: NLAlib.posDef_fromBlocks_zero_iff

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_hadamard_of_posDef_of_diag_pos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.PosSemidef) (hdiag : ∀ (i : n), 0 < B i i) : (A.hadamard B).PosDef
name: NLAlib.posDef_hadamard_of_posDef_of_diag_pos
doc:
The Hadamard product is positive definite when the first factor is
positive definite and the PSD second factor has strictly positive diagonal.
Empty dimensions are included. Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.5.3.
atlas: schur-product-inequalities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_identity_fromBlocks_iff_specNorm_lt_one.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (X : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  (Matrix.fromBlocks 1 X X.transpose 1).PosDef ↔ NLAlib.specNorm X < 1
name: NLAlib.posDef_identity_fromBlocks_iff_specNorm_lt_one
doc:
The identity-diagonal symmetric block is positive definite precisely
when the off-diagonal block has spectral norm strictly below one.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Lemma 7.7.6.
atlas: psd-block-contraction (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_iff_leadingMinor_pos {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
  A.PosDef ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → k ≤ n → 0 < NLAlib.leadingMinor A k
name: NLAlib.posDef_iff_leadingMinor_pos
doc:
Sylvester's leading-principal-minor criterion for a real symmetric
matrix. Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.2.5.
atlas: sylvester-criterion

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_iff_pivotSchur {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
  A.PosDef ↔ 0 < A 0 0 ∧ (NLAlib.pivotSchur A).PosDef
name: NLAlib.posDef_iff_pivotSchur
doc:
**Positive definiteness through the pivot**: a symmetric `A` on `Fin (n + 1)` is positive
definite iff its pivot is positive and its pivot Schur complement is positive definite.
Proof: complete the square, `xᵀAx = a (x₀ + cᵀy / a)² + yᵀ (pivotSchur A) y` for
`x = (x₀, y)`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.5 (proof of Thm 4.2.7); Trefethen–Bau 1997,
Lect. 23 (proof of Thm 23.1); Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.7.7. This is the step of the Cholesky
recursion (atlas `cholesky-algorithm`); special case of `generalized-schur-complement-psd`.

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_iff_trailingMinor_pos {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
  A.PosDef ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → k ≤ n → 0 < NLAlib.trailingMinor A k
name: NLAlib.posDef_iff_trailingMinor_pos
doc:
Sylvester's equivalent trailing-principal-minor criterion.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.2.5 and Corollary 7.2.4.
atlas: sylvester-criterion

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_integral_of_ae_posDef.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : ℕ} (Z : Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)
  (hInt : MeasureTheory.Integrable Z μ) (hPD : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (Z ω).PosDef) : (∫ (ω : Ω), Z ω ∂μ).PosDef
name: NLAlib.posDef_integral_of_ae_posDef
doc:
The expectation of an integrable, almost surely positive definite random matrix is positive
definite.

Tropp 2015, fact used in Corollary 3.4.2. Atlas: `matrix-laplace`. Ported from the Prove2me
mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 3*.

Auxiliary; not a numbered result in the source.

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_map_exp_iff_rows_injective.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) : (A.map Real.exp).PosDef ↔ Function.Injective A.row
name: NLAlib.posDef_map_exp_iff_rows_injective
doc:
The entrywise exponential of a PSD real matrix is positive definite
exactly when no two rows of the original matrix coincide. Singular matrices,
zero rows, and empty/singleton dimensions are included.
Horn--Johnson (2013), Theorem 7.5.9.
atlas: schur-product-inequalities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_matrixExp_and_matrixLog_matrixExp.{u_1} {d : Type u_1} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (A : Matrix d d ℂ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) : (NLAlib.matrixExp A).PosDef ∧ NLAlib.matrixLog (NLAlib.matrixExp A) = A
name: NLAlib.posDef_matrixExp_and_matrixLog_matrixExp
doc:
The exponential of a Hermitian matrix is positive definite and `matrixLog` inverts it: `(matrixExp
A).PosDef ∧ matrixLog (matrixExp A) = A`, on any finite index type (including the empty one).
The second conjunct is Mathlib's `CFC.log_exp` (`matrixLog = CFC.log`, `matrixLog_eq_log`).

Tropp 2015, §2.1.11–12, eq. (2.1.17).
atlas: matrix-calculus-def

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_of_isHermitian_of_irreducible_weak_diagonal_dominance.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hIrred : (A.map norm).IsIrreducible) (hpos : ∀ (i : n), 0 < A i i)
  (hweak : ∀ (i : n), NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i ≤ ‖A i i‖)
  (hstrict : ∃ i, NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i < ‖A i i‖) : A.PosDef
name: NLAlib.posDef_of_isHermitian_of_irreducible_weak_diagonal_dominance
doc:
An irreducible real symmetric weakly diagonally dominant matrix with
positive diagonal and at least one strict row is positive definite.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 6.2.27; the graph is that of the
entrywise absolute values and the strict-row repair is explicit.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_of_isHermitian_of_irreducible_weak_diagonal_dominance_complex.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hIrred : (A.map norm).IsIrreducible)
  (hdiag : ∀ (i : n), (A i i).im = 0) (hpos : ∀ (i : n), 0 < (A i i).re)
  (hweak : ∀ (i : n), NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i ≤ ‖A i i‖)
  (hstrict : ∃ i, NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i < ‖A i i‖) : A.PosDef
name: NLAlib.posDef_of_isHermitian_of_irreducible_weak_diagonal_dominance_complex
doc:
Irreducible weak absolute row dominance with positive real diagonal
and a strict row makes a complex Hermitian matrix positive definite.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 6.2.27; the strict-row hypothesis
is necessary and is explicit.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:
NLAlib.posDef_of_isHermitian_of_row_radius_lt_diag.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hstrict : ∀ (i : n), NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i < A i i) : A.PosDef
name: NLAlib.posDef_of_isHermitian_of_row_radius_lt_diag
doc:
A real symmetric matrix with strictly dominant positive diagonal is

doc:
**Albert's criterion**: `[[A, B], [Bᴴ, C]] ⪰ 0` iff `A ⪰ 0`, `(I − AA⁺) B = 0` (range of `B`
inside range of `A`) and `M / A = C − Bᴴ A⁺ B ⪰ 0`. No Hermitian hypotheses are needed: each
side forces `A` and `C` Hermitian. Albert 1969, Thm 1; cf. Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorems 7.7.7
and 7.7.9 for the invertible case.
Proof: (⇒) `A ⪰ 0` and `C ⪰ 0` are principal submatrices; for `z ∈ ker A`,
`(z, 0)ᴴ M (z, 0) = 0` forces `Bᴴ z = 0`, i.e. `range B ⊆ range A`, which is `(I − AA⁺)B = 0`;
then with `y = −A⁺Bx` the quadratic form is `xᴴ(M/A)x ≥ 0`. (⇐) the square completion
`dotProduct_fromBlocks_eq_generalizedSchurComplement_square`.

force every real symmetric eigenvalue to be nonnegative.

`herm:coefficient-correct`. The argument excludes negative roots directly.

doc:
The pivot Schur complement of a positive semidefinite matrix is positive semidefinite, with
no condition on the pivot (for `A₀₀ = 0` the first column vanishes and `pivotSchur A` is the
trailing block). Proof: `yᵀ (pivotSchur A) y = xᵀ A x` at `x = (−cᵀy / a, y)` (valid also for

Albert 1969, Thm 1 (atlas `generalized-schur-complement-psd`).

direction (`powerStep_iterate_succ`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 27.1 (Lect.

`A^k x₀ ∈ K_{k+1}(A, x₀)`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §4.1 and §6.1. Helper for
`power-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.powerRayleighRelativeError.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (b : ι → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : ℝ

doc:
The relative error of the Rayleigh quotient of the `q`-th power iterate `A^q b` (`q`
matvecs) against the spectral norm: `(‖A‖₂ − ρ(A^q b))/‖A‖₂` (`= (λ_max − ρ)/λ_max` for
positive semidefinite `A`; junk value `0` at `A = 0`, where `‖A‖₂ = 0`).
Source: Kuczyński–Woźniakowski (1992) [`kw92`], §2.
atlas: random-start-power

name: NLAlib.powerRayleighRelativeError_le_one
doc:
The relative error is at most `1` for positive semidefinite `A` (the Rayleigh quotient is
nonnegative). Helper for `random-start-power`.

name: NLAlib.powerRayleighRelativeError_nonneg

The relative error is nonnegative for positive semidefinite `A` (the Rayleigh quotient is at
most the spectral norm). Helper for `random-start-power`.

signature: NLAlib.powerStep.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.powerStep
doc:
The normalised power step `x ↦ A x/‖A x‖` (junk value `0` when `A x = 0`). Source:
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 27.1. Helper for `power-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.powerStep_iterate_succ.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.powerStep A)^[k + 1] x₀ =
    ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (NLAlib.powerIterate A x₀ (k + 1))‖⁻¹ • NLAlib.powerIterate A x₀ (k + 1)

doc:

`A^{k+1} x₀/‖A^{k+1} x₀‖` (both sides `0` if `A^{k+1} x₀ = 0`). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 27. Helper for `power-iteration`.

are nondecreasing in `i` (`principalAngles_monotone`). Both real and complex

is not a symmetric principal-angle list.

Principal-minor products of a PSD matrix are nonnegative.

orders throughout the PSD cone, including zero products and repeated

Principal-minor products of a positive definite matrix are positive.

Equality between consecutive principal-minor product powers for a

Horn--Johnson (2013), proof of Theorem 7.8.11;
helper for normalized Szász products.

signature:
NLAlib.principal_angle_characterizations.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq r] {P Q : Matrix m n ℝ} {R : Matrix m r ℝ}
  (hP : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hR : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols R)
  (hcomp : P * P.transpose + R * R.transpose = 1) :
  Monotone (NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q) ∧
    (∀ (i : Fin (Fintype.card n)),
        NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q i ∈ Set.Icc 0 (Real.pi / 2) ∧
          Real.cos (NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q i) =
            NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin n) (Fintype.equivFin n)) (P.transpose * Q)) ↑i) ∧
      NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * Q) ∧
        NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.projResidual P Q) ∧
          NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = NLAlib.specNorm (P * P.transpose - Q * Q.transpose) ∧
            NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = ↑(Fintype.card n) - NLAlib.frobSq (P.transpose * Q) ∧
              NLAlib.frobSq (P * P.transpose - Q * Q.transpose) = 2 * NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) ∧
                NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = NLAlib.frobNorm (R.transpose * Q) ∧
                  NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q = NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype Q P ∧
                    (∀ (P' Q' : Matrix m n ℝ),
                        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols P' →
                          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q' →
                            P.mulVecLin.range = P'.mulVecLin.range →
                              Q.mulVecLin.range = Q'.mulVecLin.range →
                                NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q = NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P' Q') ∧
                      (0 < Fintype.card n →
                          NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) =
                            √(1 -
                                NLAlib.singularValues
                                    ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin n) (Fintype.equivFin n)) (P.transpose * Q))
                                    (Fintype.card n - 1) ^
                                  2)) ∧
                        (IsUnit (P.transpose * Q) →
                            NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.tangentPrincipalAngles P Q) =
                              NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * Q * (P.transpose * Q)⁻¹)) ∧
                          (∀ (hn : 0 < Fintype.card n),
                              NLAlib.principalAnglesFintype P Q ⟨Fintype.card n - 1, ⋯⟩ < Real.pi / 2 →
                                NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.tangentPrincipalAngles P Q) =
                                  NLAlib.specNorm (R.transpose * Q * (P.transpose * Q)⁻¹)) ∧
                            (Fintype.card n = 0 →
                              NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = 0 ∧
                                NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles P Q) = 0 ∧
                                  NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.tangentPrincipalAngles P Q) = 0)
name: NLAlib.principal_angle_characterizations
doc:
Complete principal-angle characterizations for equal-width real
orthonormal frames and an orthonormal complement. Stewart–Sun §I.5,
Golub–Van Loan §2.5.3. The angle and sine/tangent matrices use the actual
singular-value list. Empty frames are explicit; a last angle is mentioned
only at positive width, and the inverse formula requires the overlap to be
invertible, derived also from the last-angle condition.
atlas: principal-angles-def

signature:
NLAlib.prod_singularValues_mul_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {p : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype p]

signature:
NLAlib.pseudoinverse_perturbation_bounds.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A =
      -NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * (B - A) * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A +

            (1 - A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) +
        (1 - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * B) * (B - A).transpose * (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).transpose *
          NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A ∧
    NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) ≤
        Real.goldenRatio *
            max (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) ^ 2)
              (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) ^ 2) *
          NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) ∧
      (A.rank = B.rank →
        NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) ≤
            Real.goldenRatio * NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) *
                NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) *
              NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) ∧
          NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) ≤
              √2 * NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) * NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) *
                NLAlib.frobNorm (B - A) ∧
            NLAlib.specNorm (A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A - B * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) ≤
                min (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A)) (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B)) *
                  NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) ∧
              NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A * A - NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B * B) ≤
                  min (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A))
                      (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B)) *
                    NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) ∧
                (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) * NLAlib.specNorm (B - A) < 1 →
                  NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse B) ≤
                    NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) /
                      (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) * NLAlib.specNorm (B - A))))
