doc:
Every advertised Moore–Penrose perturbation assertion, with the exact
golden ratio and `sqrt(2)` constants. Wedin (1973), Stewart–Sun §III.3; the proof
uses the orthogonal block argument in the supplied operator derivations.
Rank equality is imposed only on the branches that require it. All ranks and
arbitrary finite row/column types, including empty ones, are covered.
atlas: pseudoinverse-perturbation

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithm {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithm
doc:
The **shifted QR algorithm** driven by a QR routine `qr` and shifts `μ`: `A₀ = A`,
`A_{k+1} = R Q + μ_k I` where `(Q, R) = qr (A_k − μ_k I)`. Total for every `qr`; it computes the
QR algorithm when `QRAlgorithmSucceeds` holds. The unshifted algorithm is `μ = fun _ => 0`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 28.1 (unshifted), Alg. 29.1 (shifted);
Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §7.3.1, §7.5. Alternative: hypotheses on arbitrary sequences
`Q_j, R_j`; a routine argument keeps the recursion total and lets `qr` be `givensQR` or any
choice of QR.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors
doc:
The factor pair `(Q_{k+1}, R_{k+1}) = qr (A_k − μ_k I)` of step `k`. Source: Trefethen–Bau
(1997) [`tb97`], Alg. 28.1. Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors_snd_apply_self_ne_zero
doc:
If no shift is an eigenvalue (`det (A − μ_j I) ≠ 0` for `j < k`), every `R_{j+1}` has a
nonzero diagonal (`A_j − μ_j I` is orthogonally similar to `A − μ_j I`). Source: Golub–Van Loan
(2013) [`gvl13`], §7.4.2. Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithmQ {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmQ
doc:
The accumulated orthogonal factor `Q^{(k)} = Q_1 ⋯ Q_k`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 28 (eq. 28.8). Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithmR {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmR
doc:
The accumulated triangular factor `R^{(k)} = R_k ⋯ R_1`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 28 (eq. 28.8). Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithmSucceeds_givensQR {n : ℕ} {μ : ℕ → ℝ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : NLAlib.IsUpperHessenberg A)
  (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.QRAlgorithmSucceeds NLAlib.givensQR μ A k
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmSucceeds_givensQR
doc:
**Realisation for the Givens routine**: on an upper Hessenberg `A`, every factor pair of the
Givens QR algorithm is a QR factorization, so all the identities above apply
(`A_k = Q^{(k)ᵀ} A Q^{(k)}`, `∏ (A − μ_j I) = Q^{(k)} R^{(k)}`). Source: Golub–Van Loan (2013)
[`gvl13`], §7.4.2.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithmSucceeds_of_forall_isQR
doc:
A routine that returns a QR factorization of every matrix makes the algorithm succeed for
every `k` (such routines exist: `exists_isFullQR`, Householder). Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Alg. 28.1.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_eq_transpose_mul_mul
doc:
**The QR iterates are orthogonally similar to `A`**: `A_k = Q^{(k)ᵀ} A Q^{(k)}`, for any
shifts. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 28.3 (eq. 28.10); Golub–Van Loan (2013)
[`gvl13`], §7.3.1.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_succ {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.qrAlgorithm qr μ A (k + 1) =
    (NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors qr μ A k).2 * (NLAlib.qrAlgorithmFactors qr μ A k).1 + μ k • 1
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_succ
doc: `A_{k+1} = R_{k+1} Q_{k+1} + μ_k I`. Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_zero {n : ℕ} (qr : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ × Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : NLAlib.qrAlgorithm qr μ A 0 = A
name: NLAlib.qrAlgorithm_zero
doc: `A₀ = A`. Helper for `qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration`.

signature: NLAlib.qrColumnFamily {n k : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) : Fin k → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
name: NLAlib.qrColumnFamily
doc:
The Euclidean columns of a matrix, with the standard matrix column order.

signature:
NLAlib.qrColumnFamily_orthogonal_mul {n k : ℕ} (O : ↥(Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))

  NLAlib.qrColumnFamily (↑O * A) = fun j => (NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols.toLinearIsometry ⋯) (NLAlib.qrColumnFamily A j)

Orthogonal left multiplication carries each input column through its

signature: NLAlib.qrNormalizedArray {n k : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ
name: NLAlib.qrNormalizedArray
doc:
The literal positive normalized Gram–Schmidt matrix.

signature:
NLAlib.qrNormalizedArray_orthogonal_mul {n k : ℕ} (O : ↥(Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))
  (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) : NLAlib.qrNormalizedArray (↑O * A) = ↑O * NLAlib.qrNormalizedArray A

doc:
The canonical positive normalized Gram–Schmidt matrix is equivariant
under orthogonal multiplication, including zero residuals.
Source: operator re-derivation `sh:qr-equiv`.

signature:
NLAlib.qr_decomposition.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [LinearOrder n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (hCard : Fintype.card n ≤ Fintype.card m) :
  ∃ Q R,
    NLAlib.IsQR A Q R ∧
      (∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ R i i) ∧
        R.transpose * R = A.transpose * A ∧
          (∀ (k : ℕ), NLAlib.singularValues R k = NLAlib.singularValues A k) ∧
            NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber R = NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A ∧
              (∀ (e : n ↪ m),
                  ∃ W T,
                    NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols W ∧
                      W * W.transpose = 1 ∧
                        W.submatrix id ⇑e = Q ∧
                          W * T = A ∧ T.submatrix (⇑e) id = R ∧ ∀ i ∉ Set.range ⇑e, ∀ (j : n), T i j = 0) ∧
                (A.rank = Fintype.card n →
                  (∀ (i : n), 0 < R i i) ∧
                    Q * Q.transpose = A * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A ∧
                      ∀ (Q' : Matrix m n ℝ) (R' : Matrix n n ℝ),
                        NLAlib.IsQR A Q' R' → (∀ (i : n), 0 < R' i i) → Q' = Q ∧ R' = R)
name: NLAlib.qr_decomposition
doc:
Complete QR factorization for real matrices with at least as many rows
as columns, in the canonical form `IsQR A Q R`. The thin factor (existence alone is
`exists_isQR`) has nonnegative upper diagonal and the
Gram, native singular values and Moore--Penrose condition number of the
input. For every coordinate embedding the same frame and triangular factor
extend to a full orthogonal factorization with a zero-padded corner. At full
column rank the diagonal is positive, the range projector agrees
with the Moore--Penrose projector, and the pair is unique among positive
diagonal QR pairs (`IsQR.eq_of_diag_pos`). Arbitrary finite row indices, ordered finite column
indices, singular inputs and empty spaces are covered.
Trefethen--Bau, Theorems 7.1--7.2; Golub--Van Loan, Theorems 5.2.1 and 5.2.3.
atlas: qr-decomposition

signature: NLAlib.quadForm.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (z : n → 𝕜) : 𝕜
name: NLAlib.quadForm
doc:
The quadratic form `zᴴ A z = star z ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ z)` (𝕜-valued; Mathlib's `PosSemidef` form). Over
`ℝ` it is `zᵀ A z` (`rw [quadForm_def, star_trivial]`). Atlas: `hutchinson-unbiased`,
`hutchinson-variance`.
atlas: quadform-def

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_add.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (x y : n → 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (x + y) = NLAlib.quadForm A x + star x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec y + star y ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x + NLAlib.quadForm A y
name: NLAlib.quadForm_add
doc:
Expansion of the quadratic form of a sum:
`(x + y)ᴴ A (x + y) = xᴴAx + xᴴAy + yᴴAx + yᴴAy`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (g p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) =
    ∑ i,
      Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) g * Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p ^ 2 *
        ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
`(p(A)v)ᵀ g(A) (p(A)v) = ∑ᵢ g(λᵢ) p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A` and polynomials
`p`, `g`. Atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {g p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hg : ∀ x ∈ S, 0 ≤ Polynomial.eval x g) (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) ≤
    M ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) v
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Polynomial bound, weighted form.** If every eigenvalue of the real symmetric `A` lies in
`S`, the weight polynomial `g` is nonnegative on `S` and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then
`(p(A)v)ᵀ g(A) (p(A)v) ≤ M² vᵀ g(A) v`, i.e. `‖p(A) v‖_{g(A)} ≤ M ‖v‖_{g(A)}`. The weights
`g = X` (energy norm, CG), `g = X²` (residual norm, MINRES) and `g = 1` (error norm) are the
cases used by Krylov methods. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Saad (2003),
Thm 6.29 (case `g = X`). Generalises `quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le` (KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2).
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) =
    ∑ i, hA.eigenvalues i * Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p ^ 2 * ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
`(p(A)v)ᵀ A (p(A)v) = ∑ᵢ λᵢ p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A`. Audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hS : S ⊆ Set.Ici 0) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) ≤ M ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A v
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Polynomial bound, energy form.** If every eigenvalue of the real symmetric `A` lies in
`S ⊆ [0, ∞)` (so `A` is positive semidefinite) and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then
`(p(A)v)ᵀ A (p(A)v) ≤ M² vᵀ A v`, i.e. `‖p(A) v‖_A ≤ M ‖v‖_A`. This is the form used for the
CG error (Greenbaum 1997, §3.1; Saad 2003, Thm 6.29); audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`. The case `g = X` of `quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le`.
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_bounds_of_sandwich.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
  (hlo : a • 1 ≤ A) (hhi : A ≤ b • 1) (x : n → ℝ) : a * x ⬝ᵥ x ≤ NLAlib.quadForm A x ∧ NLAlib.quadForm A x ≤ b * x ⬝ᵥ x
name: NLAlib.quadForm_bounds_of_sandwich

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_chebyshevIterate_sub_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q - xs) ≤
    (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_chebyshevIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Chebyshev iteration, `A`-norm rate.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, and `A x⋆ = c`,
`‖x_q − x⋆‖²_A ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`]. Deviation: squared norms;
the iterate is defined by its residual polynomial (no recurrence).
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  {k : Type u_3} [Fintype k] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (W : Matrix n k 𝕜) (v : k → 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (W.conjTranspose * A * W) v = NLAlib.quadForm A (W.mulVec v)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_conjTranspose_mul_mul
doc:
Congruence: `quadForm (WᴴAW) v = quadForm A (Wv)` for a rectangular `W`. Helper for
`preconditioned-cg` and `ostrowski-congruence-eigenvalues` (Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.5.9).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_conjTranspose_mul_self.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  {m : Type u_3} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (y : n → 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (A.conjTranspose * A) y = star (A.mulVec y) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec y
name: NLAlib.quadForm_conjTranspose_mul_self
doc:
`(Aᴴ A y)ᴴ y = (Ay)ᴴ (Ay)`: the quadratic form of the normal-equations matrix. Helper for
`cgls-lsqr-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_def.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (z : n → 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A z = star z ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec z
name: NLAlib.quadForm_def
doc: Unfolding lemma for `quadForm` (`rfl`).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜) (z : n → 𝕜) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A z = ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * (star (z i) * z j)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum
doc: Expansion `zᴴ A z = ∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ A_ij (conj zᵢ) zⱼ`. Atlas: `hutchinson-unbiased` (helper).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum_eigenvalues

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum_mul_mul.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n 𝕜)
  (z : n → 𝕜) : NLAlib.quadForm A z = ∑ i, ∑ j, star (z i) * A i j * z j
name: NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum_mul_mul
doc:
The quadratic form as the double sum `zᴴ A z = ∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ (conj zᵢ) Aᵢⱼ zⱼ` (the order of factors
used throughout the Hanson–Wright proof). Atlas `hanson-wright` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_fromBlocks.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m m ℝ)
  (B : Matrix m n ℝ) (C : Matrix n n ℝ) (x : m → ℝ) (y : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (Matrix.fromBlocks A B B.transpose C) (Sum.elim x y) =
    NLAlib.quadForm A x + 2 * x ⬝ᵥ B.mulVec y + NLAlib.quadForm C y
name: NLAlib.quadForm_fromBlocks
doc:
The quadratic form of a symmetric block matrix is the sum of both
diagonal quadratic forms and twice the cross term. Horn--Johnson (2013),
Section 7.7; helper for PSD-block quadratic tests.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_hutchinsonBlock.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (Z : Matrix n κ ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.quadForm (NLAlib.hutchinsonBlock A) fun e => Z e.1 e.2) = NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate A Z
name: NLAlib.quadForm_hutchinsonBlock
doc:
The quadratic form of the block matrix at `vec(Z)` is the Hutchinson estimator.
Atlas: `hutchinson-tail` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_map_pow_vecMulVec_self.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (b x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Matrix.vecMulVec b b).map fun t => t ^ k) x = (∑ i, x i * b i ^ k) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_map_pow_vecMulVec_self
doc:
A natural entrywise power of a rank-one Gram matrix has the squared
scalar moment as quadratic form. Exponent zero gives the constant feature.
Horn--Johnson (2013), proof of Theorem 7.5.9;
helper for the finite Vandermonde certificate.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_mul_quadForm_inv_le_moorePenroseConditionNumber_sqrt.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) (hN : 0 < Fintype.card n) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A x * NLAlib.quadForm A⁻¹ x ≤
    1 / 4 * (√(NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A) + (√(NLAlib.moorePenroseConditionNumber A))⁻¹) ^ 2 *
      ‖WithLp.toLp 2 x‖ ^ 4
name: NLAlib.quadForm_mul_quadForm_inv_le_moorePenroseConditionNumber_sqrt
doc:
Kantorovich's condition-number formula uses the existing matrix condition
number and the Euclidean norm, with the square root and its reciprocal.
Positive dimension is required only to identify the condition number with
the extreme-eigenvalue ratio. Horn--Johnson (2013), Section 7.4.12.
atlas: kantorovich-inequality

name: NLAlib.quadForm_mul_quadForm_inv_le_of_sandwich
doc:
**Kantorovich's inequality** with spectral endpoints: if `a I ≤ A ≤ b I` with `0 < a ≤ b`,
then `(xᵀ A x)(xᵀ A⁻¹ x) ≤ ((a + b)² / 4ab) ‖x‖⁴`. Empty dimensions and `x = 0` are included.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.4.12.
atlas: kantorovich-inequality

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_nonneg_of_eigenvalues_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hpsd : ∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ hA.eigenvalues i) (x : n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.quadForm A x
name: NLAlib.quadForm_nonneg_of_eigenvalues_nonneg
doc:
A symmetric matrix with nonnegative eigenvalues has `xᵀ A x ≥ 0`. Moved from
`Krylov/CG.lean` (atlas `cg-convergence`, helper).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_polyIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Error bound for a polynomial method, weighted norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in
`S`, a weight `g ≥ 0` on `S` and `|1 − x s(x)| ≤ M` on `S`,
`‖x − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1;
Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1.
atlas: polynomial-method-def

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_reindex.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {ι : Type u_3} {κ : Type u_4} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
  (A : Matrix ι ι 𝕜) (e : ι ≃ κ) (z : ι → 𝕜) :
  (NLAlib.quadForm ((Matrix.reindex e e) A) fun k => z (e.symm k)) = NLAlib.quadForm A z
name: NLAlib.quadForm_reindex
doc:
Relabelling the coordinates by an equivalence does not change the quadratic form.
Atlas `hanson-wright` (index transport).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Richardson contraction, weighted norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
step `ω ≥ 0`, `A x⋆ = c` and a weight `g ≥ 0` on `[a, b]`,
`‖x_q − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ ρ^{2q} ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}` with `ρ = max(|1 − ωa|, |1 − ωb|)`. With
`g = X` (`0 ≤ a`) this is the `A`-norm bound of the atlas, with `g = 1` the Euclidean error.
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.
Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le_of_optimal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (NLAlib.richardsonIterate (2 / (a + b)) A c x₀ q - xs) ≤
    (((b - a) / (b + a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le_of_optimal
doc:
**Richardson with the optimal step** `ω = 2/(a + b)`: for symmetric positive definite `A`
with spectrum in `[a, b]`, `0 < a ≤ b`, `‖x_q − x⋆‖²_A ≤ ((b − a)/(b + a))^{2q} ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.1; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1.
Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimizer
doc:
**The class theorem.** Let `A` be symmetric, `A x⋆ = c`, and `g` a weight polynomial with
`g(λᵢ) ≥ 0` at every eigenvalue. If `x` minimises `‖· − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} = quadForm (g(A)) (· − x⋆)`
over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`, then for every residual polynomial `p` (`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`) with
`|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue, `‖x − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}`.
CG is `g = X` (via `cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub`), MINRES `g = X²`, the error-minimising
method `g = 1`. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1 (CG) and §3.2 (MINRES);
Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Thm 6.29; KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `cg-convergence`, `minres-bound` (the shared step; tags are on the instances).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (x - xs) ≤ (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate
doc:
**CG convergence, condition-number form.** Let `A` be symmetric with every eigenvalue in
`[a, b]`, `0 < a ≤ b`, `A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th CG iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ (2 ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²`; with `κ = b/a`,
`(√b − √a)/(√b + √a) = (√κ − 1)/(√κ + 1)`. When `a = b` (`A = aI`), CG is exact after one step
and the bound reads `0` for `q ≥ 1` and `4 ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²` for `q = 0`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.5; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8.
Atlas: `cg-convergence`; uses `chebyshev-minimax`, `polynomial-spectral-bound`,
`krylov-subspace`. Deviation: squared `A`-norms (the source states the unsquared form); the
degenerate case `a = b` is included.
atlas: cg-convergence

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_poly
doc:
**CG error bound, polynomial form.** Let `A` be symmetric positive semidefinite,
`A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th CG iterate from `x₀`. For every polynomial `p` with `deg p ≤ q`,
`p(0) = 1` and `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue,
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²` (with `‖v‖_A² = quadForm A v`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (and the inequality (38.10)); Saad (2003),
Thm 6.29. Atlas: `cg-convergence`; uses `polynomial-spectral-bound`, `krylov-subspace`,
`residual-polynomial` (the case `g = X` of `quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimizer`).
atlas: cg-convergence

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isPCGIterate
doc:
**Preconditioned CG bound under a Loewner sandwich.** Let `P` be positive definite, `A` with
`a P ≼ A ≼ b P` for `0 < a ≤ b` (so `A` is symmetric positive definite and `κ(P⁻¹A) ≤ b/a`),
`A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th PCG iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²`.
Proof: CG on `P^{-1/2} A P^{-1/2}`, whose spectrum lies in `[a, b]`
(`isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate`, `quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §9.2; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], Ch. 8.
Deviation: squared `A`-norms.
atlas: preconditioned-cg

name: NLAlib.range_qrAlgorithmQ_castLE_eq_subspaceIterate
doc:
SCAFFOLD: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration
**The leading columns of `Q^{(k)}` span the subspace iterates of the leading columns of `I`.**
For invertible `A` and `j ≤ n`, the first `j` columns of `Q^{(k)}` span
`S_k(A, I_{:, 1:j}) = range (A^k I_{:, 1:j})`: unshifted QR is simultaneous iteration on all
leading blocks at once. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 28.3 and Lect. 28 (the
"simultaneous iteration" interpretation); Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §7.3.1.
Proof sketch: `A^k E_j = Q^{(k)} R^{(k)} E_j = Q^{(k)}_{:, 1:j} R^{(k)}_{1:j, 1:j}`
(`pow_eq_qrAlgorithmQ_mul_qrAlgorithmR`, `R^{(k)}` upper triangular), and `R^{(k)}_{1:j, 1:j}`
is invertible because `R^{(k)}` is (`det A^k = det Q^{(k)} det R^{(k)} ≠ 0` and the leading
block of an invertible upper triangular matrix is invertible); then
`subspaceIterate_mul_of_isUnit`. Without invertibility only `⊇` holds. Difficulty 2.
atlas: qr-algorithm-simultaneous-iteration

name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient
doc:
The Rayleigh quotient `ρ(x) = re (xᴴAx) / re (xᴴx)` (real-valued; junk value `0` at `x = 0`).
It is the quantity of the Rayleigh–Ritz theory only for Hermitian `A` (then `xᴴAx` is real and
`λ_min ≤ ρ(x) ≤ λ_max`); for other `A` it is the real part of the numerical-range value.
Over `ℝ` it is `xᵀAx / xᵀx` (`simp only [rayleighQuotient_def, quadForm_def, star_trivial,
RCLike.re_to_real]`). Source: Trefethen–Bau
(1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 27. Helper for `power-iteration`; Mathlib's
`ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient` of `Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A` agrees with it at `ℝ`
(`rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_eq`).

NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_le_lanczosRitzValue_of_mem_ne_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) {y : n → ℝ} (hy : y ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q)
  (hy0 : y ≠ 0) : NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A y ≤ NLAlib.lanczosRitzValue A b q
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_le_lanczosRitzValue_of_mem_ne_zero
doc: Every nonzero Krylov vector has quotient at most the largest compression eigenvalue.

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_le_specNorm.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A x ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_le_specNorm
doc:
A Rayleigh quotient is at most the spectral norm: `xᵀAx/xᵀx ≤ ‖A‖₂` (any real `A`, including
`x = 0`). Helper for `random-start-lanczos`.

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_smul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) :
  NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A (c • x) = NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A x
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_smul
doc:
Scaling does not change the Rayleigh quotient: `ρ(c x) = ρ(x)` for `c ≠ 0`. Helper for
`power-iteration`.

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_bounds.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (b : n → ℝ) :
  0 ≤ (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A).rayleighQuotient (WithLp.toLp 2 b) ∧
    (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A).rayleighQuotient (WithLp.toLp 2 b) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_bounds
doc:
A PSD matrix's totalized Rayleigh quotient lies between zero and its spectral
norm, even at a zero vector. Source: the spectral theorem.

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (b : n → ℝ) : (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A).rayleighQuotient (WithLp.toLp 2 b) = NLAlib.rayleighQuotient A b
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_eq
doc:
Mathlib's Rayleigh quotient of a real matrix is the matrix Rayleigh quotient
`rayleighQuotient A b = bᵀAb / bᵀb`.
Source: Mathlib's `ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient`.
The zero-vector convention is totalized division by zero.

signature:
NLAlib.rayleigh_residual_le_shifted_residual.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {x : n → ℝ}
  (hx : x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) (μ : ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.rayleigh_residual_le_shifted_residual
doc:
The Rayleigh quotient uniquely minimizes the squared residual over real
shifts. Parlett §4.5; no nonzero-eigenvalue hypothesis is needed.
atlas: eigenvalue-residual-bounds

signature:
NLAlib.rayleigh_variance_add_mul_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {x : n → ℝ} (hx : x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) (ℓ a : ℝ)

name: NLAlib.rayleigh_variance_add_mul_nonneg
doc:
A nonnegative quadratic polynomial on the spectrum bounds the Rayleigh
residual variance. Kato–Temple finite spectral proof, Parlett §10.6.

signature: NLAlib.reTraceCLM.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] : Matrix ι ι ℂ →L[ℝ] ℝ
name: NLAlib.reTraceCLM
doc:
`M ↦ Re tr M` as a continuous real-linear map on `Matrix ι ι ℂ`.
Supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature: NLAlib.reTraceCLM_apply.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (M : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : NLAlib.reTraceCLM M = M.trace.re
name: NLAlib.reTraceCLM_apply
doc: `reTraceCLM M = Re tr M`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_diag_mem_Icc_of_isHermitian_of_isIdempotentElem.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [RCLike 𝕜] (P : Matrix ι ι 𝕜) (hs : P.IsHermitian) (hp : IsIdempotentElem P) (j : ι) : RCLike.re (P j j) ∈ Set.Icc 0 1
name: NLAlib.re_diag_mem_Icc_of_isHermitian_of_isIdempotentElem
doc:
Every diagonal capture weight of an orthogonal projector (Hermitian idempotent) over `ℝ` or
`ℂ` has real part in `[0,1]`, including zero dimensions. The proof uses the squared column
length. For a real symmetric projector this reads `P j j ∈ [0, 1]`. Atlas `eckart-young`
(foundation); `sa:volume-theorem`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_diagonal_eq_norm_sq_eigenvectorUnitary_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
  (fun i => RCLike.re (A i i)) = (Matrix.of fun i j => ‖↑hA.eigenvectorUnitary i j‖ ^ 2).mulVec hA.eigenvalues
name: NLAlib.re_diagonal_eq_norm_sq_eigenvectorUnitary_mulVec
doc:
The real diagonal `Re aᵢᵢ` of a Hermitian matrix is the doubly stochastic image of its
eigenvalues under the squared moduli of the eigenvector unitary. Horn–Johnson 2013, proof of
Theorem 4.3.45.

signature:
NLAlib.re_diagonal_mem_Icc_eigenvalues₀.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (i : n) (hcard : 0 < Fintype.card n) :
  RCLike.re (A i i) ∈ Set.Icc (hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨Fintype.card n - 1, ⋯⟩) (hA.eigenvalues₀ ⟨0, hcard⟩)
name: NLAlib.re_diagonal_mem_Icc_eigenvalues₀
doc:
Every real diagonal entry of a Hermitian matrix lies between its smallest and largest
eigenvalues. Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 4.3.46.

signature: NLAlib.re_fourier_nat_coe_eq_cos (k : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) : ((fourier ↑k) ↑θ).re = Real.cos (↑k * θ)
name: NLAlib.re_fourier_nat_coe_eq_cos
doc:
The real part of a period-`2π` Fourier monomial is the usual cosine frequency.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8; used by analytic Chebyshev approximation
and sharp Jackson. Relocated unchanged from `NLAlib.Polynomial.FunctionApproximation.AnalyticApproximation`.

signature: NLAlib.re_fourier_one_mem_Icc (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : ((fourier 1) t).re ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1
name: NLAlib.re_fourier_one_mem_Icc
doc:
Every cosine-circle argument lies in the closed unit interval.
Source: unit norm of Fourier characters; helper for `jackson-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_fourier_pair_eq_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T (F : ℂ → ℂ) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (θ : ℝ) :
  (fourierCoeff (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F) ↑k * (fourier ↑k) ↑θ +
        fourierCoeff (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F) (-↑k) * (fourier (-↑k)) ↑θ).re =

doc:
Pairing opposite Fourier frequencies gives the positive Chebyshev series term.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.re_pos_of_mem_spectrum_of_irreducible_weak_diagonal_dominance.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hIrred : (A.map norm).IsIrreducible) (hdiag : ∀ (i : n), (A i i).im = 0)
  (hpos : ∀ (i : n), 0 < (A i i).re) (hweak : ∀ (i : n), NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i ≤ ‖A i i‖)
  (hstrict : ∃ i, NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i < ‖A i i‖) {μ : ℂ} (hμ : μ ∈ spectrum ℂ A) : 0 < μ.re
name: NLAlib.re_pos_of_mem_spectrum_of_irreducible_weak_diagonal_dominance
doc:
Positive real diagonal and irreducible weak row dominance, with one
strict row, imply that every complex eigenvalue has positive real part.
Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 6.2.27; the strict-row assumption is
necessary and is retained explicitly.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:
NLAlib.re_pos_of_mem_spectrum_of_isUnit_of_weak_diagonal_dominance.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hunit : IsUnit A) (hdiag : ∀ (i : n), (A i i).im = 0)
  (hweak : ∀ (i : n), NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i ≤ (A i i).re) {μ : ℂ} (hμ : μ ∈ spectrum ℂ A) : 0 < μ.re
name: NLAlib.re_pos_of_mem_spectrum_of_isUnit_of_weak_diagonal_dominance
doc:
Weak row dominance about nonnegative real diagonal entries gives
positive real parts whenever the matrix is nonsingular.
Horn–Johnson (2013), Corollary 6.2.27; the only boundary point of a disc
on the imaginary axis is zero.

signature:
NLAlib.re_pos_of_mem_spectrum_of_row_radius_lt_re_diag.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : ∀ (i : n), NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i < (A i i).re) {μ : ℂ} (hμ : μ ∈ spectrum ℂ A) :
  0 < μ.re
name: NLAlib.re_pos_of_mem_spectrum_of_row_radius_lt_re_diag
doc:
A complex spectral point has positive real part when every row radius
is smaller than the real part of the diagonal. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013),
Corollary 6.1.8; this form also allows nonreal diagonal entries.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.re_pos_of_mem_spectrum_of_strict_diagonal_dominance.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hdiag : ∀ (i : n), (A i i).im = 0) (hpos : ∀ (i : n), 0 < (A i i).re)
  (hstrict : ∀ (i : n), NLAlib.gershgorinRowRadius A i < ‖A i i‖) {μ : ℂ} (hμ : μ ∈ spectrum ℂ A) : 0 < μ.re
name: NLAlib.re_pos_of_mem_spectrum_of_strict_diagonal_dominance
doc:
Strict absolute row dominance and positive real diagonal place every
complex eigenvalue in the open right half-plane. Source: Horn–Johnson
(2013), Corollary 6.1.8; arbitrary nonsymmetric matrices are allowed.
atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_cfc_eq_sum_eigenvalues.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc: The real part of `tr f(A)` is `∑ᵢ f(λᵢ(A))`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.5.6.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_diagonal_mul_conj_diagonal.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (U : ↥(Matrix.unitaryGroup ι ℂ)) (a b : ι → ℝ) :
  ((Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(a i)) * ((↑U * Matrix.diagonal fun j => ↑(b j)) * star ↑U)).trace.re =
    ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖↑U i j‖ ^ 2 * a i * b j
name: NLAlib.re_trace_diagonal_mul_conj_diagonal
doc:
A diagonal matrix times a conjugated diagonal matrix has trace given by
the squared unitary overlap weights (two separate eigenbases); supports
`noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_eq_zero_iff_of_posSemidef.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.re_trace_eq_zero_iff_of_posSemidef
doc: A PSD matrix with zero real trace is zero. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.1.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_matrixExp_mul_unitary_conj.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (U : ↥(unitary (Matrix ι ι ℂ))) (H A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) :
  (NLAlib.matrixExp (↑U * H * (↑U).conjTranspose) * (↑U * A * (↑U).conjTranspose)).trace.re =
    (NLAlib.matrixExp H * A).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_matrixExp_mul_unitary_conj
doc:
The real part of the trace pairing of a matrix exponential and another
matrix is invariant under simultaneous unitary conjugation. Source: operator
derivations §7; atlas `golden-thompson` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_mul_diagonal_pow_mul_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ)

    (C ^ 2 * (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(ev i)) ^ m).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_mul_diagonal_pow_mul_le

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_mul_diagonal_pow_mul_mul_diagonal_pow.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (hC : C.IsHermitian) (ev : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℕ) :
  (C * (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(ev i)) ^ a * C * (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(ev i)) ^ b).trace.re =
    ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖C i j‖ ^ 2 * ev j ^ a * ev i ^ b
name: NLAlib.re_trace_mul_diagonal_pow_mul_mul_diagonal_pow
doc:
Two powers of a real diagonal matrix, separated by a Hermitian matrix,
have real trace equal to a sum weighted by squared complex entry norms (eigenbasis
expansion).

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_mul_pow_mul_le_trace_sq_mul_pow.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (C H : Matrix ι ι ℂ)

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_nonneg_of_posSemidef.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] {R : Matrix n n 𝕜}
  (hR : R.PosSemidef) : 0 ≤ RCLike.re R.trace
name: NLAlib.re_trace_nonneg_of_posSemidef
doc: A PSD matrix has nonnegative real trace. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.1.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_pow_eq_sum_eigenvalues_pow.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (r : ℕ) : (A ^ r).trace.re = ∑ i, hA.eigenvalues i ^ r
name: NLAlib.re_trace_pow_eq_sum_eigenvalues_pow
doc:
Every natural Hermitian power has real trace equal to the corresponding
power sum of its real eigenvalues (spectral theorem); supports the integer trace method for
`noncommutative-khintchine` and the complex trace tails of `rpcholesky`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_pow_mul_pow_eq_sum_overlap.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι ℂ)

  (A ^ r * B ^ s).trace.re =

name: NLAlib.re_trace_pow_mul_pow_eq_sum_overlap
doc:
Products of natural Hermitian powers have real trace given by the
overlap weights of their two eigenbases (two spectral decompositions); supports
`noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_pow_nonneg_of_even.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {r : ℕ} (hr : Even r) : 0 ≤ (A ^ r).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_pow_nonneg_of_even
doc:
Every even natural Hermitian trace moment is nonnegative. Source:
the real eigenvalue power sum; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_pow_nonneg_of_posSemidef.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (r : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (A ^ r).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_pow_nonneg_of_posSemidef
doc:
Every natural PSD trace power is nonnegative. Source: its nonnegative
eigenvalues; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_sub_mul_sub_pow_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (H K : Matrix ι ι ℂ)

**Polynomial trace mean-value inequality.** At every odd power `m+1`,
where `m` is even, the Hermitian difference is bounded by the average of
the two endpoint quadratic traces; the matrices need not commute. Tropp 2015, §4.8;
supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_sub_sq_mul_pow.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (H K : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (m : ℕ) :
  ((H - K) ^ 2 * H ^ m).trace.re = (H ^ (m + 2)).trace.re + (H ^ m * K ^ 2).trace.re - 2 * (H ^ (m + 1) * K).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_sub_sq_mul_pow
doc:
The quadratic trace of a Hermitian difference expands into three
polynomial traces, by cyclicity of the trace; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

The real cosine pullback to the circle of period `2π`.

Evaluating the circle pullback at a real angle gives the usual cosine substitution.

The decreasing paired spectrum of the real dilation: padded positive values,

The explicit paired list decreases, including all the rectangular zeros.
Bhatia 1997, Section III.4; no positive-rank hypothesis is needed.

signature:

Entrywise extension of real matrices to `𝕜` (`ℝ` or `ℂ`) as a real star algebra

The embedding acts on each matrix entry by the canonical real scalar map.
Source: the canonical scalar embedding; supports `loewner-heinz-real`.

signature:
NLAlib.realMatrixComplexification_cfc.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {𝕜 : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [DecidableEq n]

Every scalar functional calculus of a real symmetric matrix commutes with the extension
to `𝕜`. Its finite spectrum makes every scalar function continuous on the spectrum.
Source: Mathlib `StarAlgHom.map_cfc`; supports `loewner-heinz-real`.

signature:
NLAlib.realMatrixComplexification_inv.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {𝕜 : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
The extension to `𝕜` commutes with the ordinary inverse on nonsingular matrices.
Source: preservation of the two inverse identities; supports `loewner-heinz-real`.

signature:
NLAlib.realMatrixComplexification_le_iff.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {𝕜 : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [DecidableEq n]

The extension to `𝕜` preserves and reflects Loewner inequalities.
Source: the positive-semidefinite difference criterion; supports `loewner-heinz-real`.

then `(I − QQᵀ) X = (I − PPᵀ) X`. Helper for `principal-angles-def` (belongs in

Atlas `projection-facts`.

Atlas `projection-facts`.

  {S₂ : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r') ℝ} (hA : A = U₁ * S₁ * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose)
  (hU₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂) (hV₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁) (hV₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂)
  (hV : V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0) (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t) (Ω : Ωs → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ)
  (hΩ : ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw Ω (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin n) (Fin t)) μ) (Q : Ωs → Matrix m q ℝ)

  (hQr : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, Q ω * ((Q ω).transpose * (A * Ω ω)) = A * Ω ω) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (A - Q ω * ((Q ω).transpose * A)) ∂μ ≤ (1 + ↑k / (↑t - ↑k - 1)) * NLAlib.frobSq S₂

doc:
**Randomized SVD with a Gaussian test matrix** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD`, Algorithm
RSVD; HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case): if `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix,
`t ≥ k + 2`, and `Q ω` has a.s. orthonormal columns with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then
`E‖A − QQᵀA‖_F² ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²` (`‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F² = frobSq S₂` via the block SVD).

hypothesis `hXi` is also removed: when the error is not integrable its Bochner integral is `0`
and the (nonnegative) bound holds trivially. No measurability of `Q` is required.
Deviation: `n`, `k`, `r`, `r'`, `t` are `Fin` (the Gaussian law of `Ω` and the block lemmas of
`Gaussian/Conditioning.lean` live on `Fin`); the row type `m` and the column type `q` of `Q`
are arbitrary.
Atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (uses `gaussian-conditioning`, `pinv-frob-moment`,
`gaussian-full-rank-ae`, `hmt-9-1-frobenius`).

NLAlib.semidefinite_pair_congruence_normal_form.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ}

    IsUnit S ∧
      A = S * Matrix.diagonal a * S.transpose ∧
        B = S * Matrix.diagonal b * S.transpose ∧
          (∀ (i : n), a i = 0 ∨ a i = 1) ∧
            (∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ b i) ∧

                A.rank = Fintype.card { i // a i = 1 } ∧

The first block is indexed by `a=1`, the second by `a=0,b=1`, and the third
by `a=b=0`; thus coordinate reordering gives `(I_r,0_s,0_t)` and
`(diag(beta),I_s,0_t)`. The identities identify `r=rank A`,

  have R := A * Vhat₁ - Uhat₁ * T;
  have S := A.transpose * Uhat₁ - Vhat₁ * T;
  have δ := NLAlib.singularValues (A + E) (k - 1) - NLAlib.singularValues A k;
  have g := NLAlib.singularValues A (k - 1) - NLAlib.singularValues A k;
  R = -(E * Vhat₁) ∧
    S = -(E.transpose * Uhat₁) ∧
      max (NLAlib.specNorm R) (NLAlib.specNorm S) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm E ∧
        (0 < δ →
            max (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁))
                  (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁)) ≤
                max (NLAlib.specNorm R) (NLAlib.specNorm S) / δ ∧
              max (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁))
                    (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁)) ≤
                  NLAlib.specNorm E / δ ∧
                √(NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁) ^ 2 +
                      NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁) ^ 2) ≤
                  √(NLAlib.frobNorm R ^ 2 + NLAlib.frobNorm S ^ 2) / δ) ∧
          (0 < g →
              max (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁))
                  (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁)) ≤
                2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / g) ∧
            (k = 0 →
              NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁) = 0 ∧
                NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁) = 0 ∧
                  NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles U₁ Uhat₁) = 0 ∧
                    NLAlib.frobNorm (NLAlib.sinePrincipalAngles V₁ Vhat₁) = 0)

signature:
NLAlib.slepian_inequality.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} {Ω' : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω]

  (hX : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => X t ω) P)
  (hY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => Y t ω) Q) (hX0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ∂P = 0)
  (hY0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ∂Q = 0) (hvar : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ^ 2 ∂P = ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ^ 2 ∂Q)
  (hinc : ∀ (s t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), (X s ω - X t ω) ^ 2 ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), (Y s ω - Y t ω) ^ 2 ∂Q) (τ : ℝ) :
  P {ω | τ < ⨆ t, X t ω} ≤ Q {ω | τ < ⨆ t, Y t ω}
name: NLAlib.slepian_inequality
doc:
**Slepian's inequality.** Let `X` (on `(Ω, P)`) and `Y` (on `(Ω', Q)`) be centred Gaussian
processes indexed by a finite set, with equal variances `𝔼 Xₜ² = 𝔼 Yₜ²` and dominated
increments `𝔼 (Xₛ - Xₜ)² ≤ 𝔼 (Yₛ - Yₜ)²`. Then for every `τ`,
`P(τ < maxₜ Xₜ) ≤ Q(τ < maxₜ Yₜ)`.
Source: Slepian 1962; Vershynin 2018, Thm 7.2.1. Atlas: `slepian`.
atlas: slepian

  (hinc : ∀ (s t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), (X s ω - X t ω) ^ 2 ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), (Y s ω - Y t ω) ^ 2 ∂Q) (τ : ℝ) :

doc:
**The search directions span the Krylov space**: for `A ≻ 0` and every `k`,
`span (p_0, …, p_{k−1}) = K_k(A, r₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1,
eq. (38.2). Proof: `span_cgRecurrence_p_eq_span_r` and `span_cgRecurrence_r`.
atlas: cg-recurrence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.span_cgRecurrence_p_eq_span_r.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun i => (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ ↑i).p) =
    Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun i => (NLAlib.cgRecurrence A c x₀ ↑i).r)
name: NLAlib.span_cgRecurrence_p_eq_span_r
doc:
**Search directions and residuals span the same spaces**: `span (p_0, …, p_{k−1}) =
span (r_0, …, r_{k−1})` for every `A` and `k` (no hypothesis). Induction on `k` with
`p_k − r_k = β_{k−1} p_{k−1}`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1, eq. (38.2).
Helper for `cg-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.span_cgRecurrence_r
doc:
**The residuals span the Krylov space**: for `A ≻ 0` and every `k`,
`span (r_0, …, r_{k−1}) = K_k(A, r₀)`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1,
eq. (38.2); Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Prop. 6.20. Proof: `≤` from `cgRecurrence_mem_krylovSpace`;
for `k ≤ ν` the residuals are nonzero (`cgRecurrence_r_ne_zero_of_lt_krylovGrade`) and
orthogonal (`dotProduct_cgRecurrence_r_eq_zero`), hence independent, and both sides have
dimension `k` (`finrank_krylovSpace`); for `k ≥ ν`, `K_k = K_ν`
(`krylovSpace_eq_of_krylovGrade_le`). Deviation: stated for every `k`, not only while `r_k ≠ 0`.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.specNorm
doc:
Spectral norm `‖A‖₂`, the largest singular value: Mathlib's ℓ₂ operator norm.
atlas: matrix-norms-def

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_add_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix m n 𝕜) : NLAlib.specNorm (A + B) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A + NLAlib.specNorm B
name: NLAlib.specNorm_add_le
doc:
Triangle inequality for the spectral norm: `‖A + B‖₂ ≤ ‖A‖₂ + ‖B‖₂`. Standard
(Golub–Van Loan, 4th ed. §2.3); atlas `norms-frob-spec`.
atlas: norms-frob-spec

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_add_le_max_of_projector_supports.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {P : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hs : P.IsHermitian)
  (hp : IsIdempotentElem P) {X Y : Matrix m n 𝕜} (hX : X * P = X) (hY : Y * (1 - P) = Y)
  (hXY : X.conjTranspose * Y = 0) : NLAlib.specNorm (X + Y) ≤ max (NLAlib.specNorm X) (NLAlib.specNorm Y)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_add_le_max_of_projector_supports
doc:
Two blocks with orthogonal input and output supports have norm at most
the maximum block norm. Stewart–Sun 1990, §I.5; the proof uses Pythagoras twice.

name: NLAlib.specNorm_add_sq_le_of_conjTranspose_mul_eq_zero
doc:
Block bound for column-orthogonal summands: if `XᴴY = 0` then
`‖X + Y‖₂² ≤ ‖X‖₂² + ‖Y‖₂²` (conjugate transpose of
`specNorm_add_sq_le_of_mul_conjTranspose_eq_zero`). Standard; atlas `norms-frob-spec`.

name: NLAlib.specNorm_add_sq_le_of_mul_conjTranspose_eq_zero
doc:
Block bound for row-orthogonal summands: if `XYᴴ = 0` then
`‖X + Y‖₂² ≤ ‖X‖₂² + ‖Y‖₂²`, because `(X + Y)(X + Y)ᴴ = XXᴴ + YYᴴ`. Standard (used in HMT 2011,
proof of Thm 9.1); atlas `norms-frob-spec`.
atlas: norms-frob-spec

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_aeval_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (p : Polynomial ℝ) {M : ℝ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) (h : ∀ (i : n), |Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p| ≤ M) :
  NLAlib.specNorm ((Polynomial.aeval A) p) ≤ M
name: NLAlib.specNorm_aeval_le
doc:
**Polynomial spectral-norm bound.** For real symmetric `A`, if `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every
eigenvalue then `‖p(A)‖₂ ≤ M`. Standard (Golub–Van Loan, 4th ed., §11.3.4, used for the CG
bound); audit G0 C5; atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`. The hypothesis `0 ≤ M` covers the empty
index type.
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_blockDiagonal_const_le.{u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {κ : Type u_3} [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq κ] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) : NLAlib.specNorm (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun x => A) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.specNorm_blockDiagonal_const_le
doc: `‖diag(A, …, A)‖₂ ≤ ‖A‖₂`. Atlas: `hutchinson-tail` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_complement_mul_projector_eq_of_rank_eq.{u_1, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] {P Q : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hPs : P.IsHermitian) (hPi : IsIdempotentElem P) (hQs : Q.IsHermitian)
  (hQi : IsIdempotentElem Q) (hr : P.rank = Q.rank) : NLAlib.specNorm ((1 - Q) * P) = NLAlib.specNorm ((1 - P) * Q)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_complement_mul_projector_eq_of_rank_eq
doc:
Equal-rank orthogonal projections have equal one-sided gap norms:
`‖(I − Q)P‖₂ = ‖(I − P)Q‖₂`. Stewart–Sun 1990, §I.5; rank zero is the empty frame.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_conjTranspose.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

name: NLAlib.specNorm_conjTranspose
doc: `‖Aᴴ‖₂ = ‖A‖₂`. Standard; atlas `norms-frob-spec`.

name: NLAlib.specNorm_conjTranspose_mul_of_eq_mul
doc:
Spectral isometry on the range of a matrix with orthonormal columns: if `PᴴP = I` and
`X = P (Pᴴ X)` (i.e. `range X ⊆ range P`), then `‖PᴴX‖₂ = ‖X‖₂`. Standard (used in
Chen–Persson, proof of `lem:tGN-core`, as `‖Q⊥ᵀA⊥‖ = ‖A⊥‖`); atlas `norms-frob-spec`.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_cutMatrix_le {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (s : Finset (Fin n)) :

doc:
Source-transport helper `specNorm_cutMatrix_le` for Hanson–Wright.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_diagonal_inv_le.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
  (s : k → ℝ) (p : Polynomial ℝ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hmin : ∀ (i : k), c ≤ |Polynomial.eval (s i ^ 2) p|) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(Polynomial.eval (s i ^ 2) p)⁻¹) ≤ 1 / c
name: NLAlib.specNorm_diagonal_inv_le
doc:
The diagonal of reciprocals of a filter has spectral norm at most the reciprocal of a positive
lower envelope on the filter values: `c ≤ |p(s i²)|` for all `i` gives
`‖diag (p(s i²)⁻¹)‖₂ ≤ 1 / c`. Halko–Martinsson–Tropp 2011, §10.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_diagonal_le.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {v : n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c)

name: NLAlib.specNorm_diagonal_le
doc:
`‖diag(v)‖₂ ≤ c` when every `|vᵢ| ≤ c` (`c ≥ 0`). Helper for
`subspace-iteration-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_eq_norm.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.specNorm_eq_norm
doc:
Bridge to Mathlib's ℓ₂ operator norm (`Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`). Atlas `norms-frob-spec`.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_eq_norm_eigenvalues.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {A : Matrix ι ι ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) : NLAlib.specNorm A = ‖hA.eigenvalues‖
name: NLAlib.specNorm_eq_norm_eigenvalues
doc:
The spectral norm of a real symmetric matrix is the supremum norm of

invariance. Atlas: `inverse-wishart-spectral-moment` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_euclideanJacobian.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  {f : EuclideanSpace ℝ m → EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ m} (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.euclideanJacobian f x) = NLAlib.mapAbsCondition f x

The absolute condition number of a differentiable map is the spectral norm of its
Euclidean Jacobian. Gautschi 2004, Definition 2.3.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_fromCols_sq_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq p] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (B : Matrix m p ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.specNorm_fromCols_sq_le
doc:
Concatenating column blocks bounds the squared operator norm by the sum
of squared block norms. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 5.6.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_fromRows_sq_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq p] (A : Matrix m p ℝ) (B : Matrix n p ℝ) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (A.fromRows B) ^ 2 ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A ^ 2 + NLAlib.specNorm B ^ 2
name: NLAlib.specNorm_fromRows_sq_le
doc:
Concatenating row blocks bounds the squared operator norm by the sum
of squared block norms. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 5.6.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_fromRows_zero_sq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [Fintype p] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq p] (A : Matrix m p ℝ) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (A.fromRows 0) ^ 2 = NLAlib.specNorm A ^ 2
name: NLAlib.specNorm_fromRows_zero_sq
doc:
Appending zero rows leaves the squared spectral norm unchanged.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 5.6; includes empty dimensions.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_gram_sub_one_eq_norm_singularValues_sq_sub_one {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (A.transpose * A - 1) = ‖fun j => NLAlib.singularValues A ↑j ^ 2 - 1‖
name: NLAlib.specNorm_gram_sub_one_eq_norm_singularValues_sq_sub_one
doc:
A Gram error has the norm of the list `σᵢ² − 1`, for every domain
singular value (including zero singular values and empty dimensions).
Atlas: `ose-def`, `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_gram_sub_one_le_iff_singularValues_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (A.transpose * A - 1) ≤ ε ↔
    ∀ (j : Fin (Fintype.card n)), 1 - ε ≤ NLAlib.singularValues A ↑j ^ 2 ∧ NLAlib.singularValues A ↑j ^ 2 ≤ 1 + ε
name: NLAlib.specNorm_gram_sub_one_le_iff_singularValues_sq
doc:
A Gram error bound is equivalent to bounds on every sorted squared singular value:
`‖AᵀA − I‖ ≤ ε` iff `1 − ε ≤ σⱼ(A)² ≤ 1 + ε` for every domain index `j < card n` (zero singular
values of a wide matrix included). Arbitrary finite row and column indices. Atlas: `ose-def`,
`svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_hutchinsonBlock_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq κ] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.hutchinsonBlock A) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A / ↑(Fintype.card κ)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_hutchinsonBlock_le
doc: `‖B‖₂ ≤ ‖A‖₂ / m` for the Hutchinson block matrix. Atlas: `hutchinson-tail` (helper).

name: NLAlib.specNorm_idempotent_eq_secant_of_range_frames
doc:
For any range and row-space orthonormal frames of a positive-rank
idempotent, the largest principal angle is strictly below pi/2 and its
secant equals the spectral norm. Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3;
the positive frame cardinality is essential.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_idempotent_rank_endpoints.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {P : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) :
  (P.rank = 0 → NLAlib.specNorm P = 0 ∧ NLAlib.specNorm (1 - P) = if Fintype.card n = 0 then 0 else 1) ∧
    (P.rank = Fintype.card n → (NLAlib.specNorm P = if Fintype.card n = 0 then 0 else 1) ∧ NLAlib.specNorm (1 - P) = 0)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_idempotent_rank_endpoints
doc:
At rank zero the idempotent norm is zero and the complement norm is one
in positive dimension; at full rank these roles reverse. Empty dimension
gives zero for both. Horn–Johnson 2013, Corollary 3.4.3.3.
atlas: cs-decomposition (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_inv_add_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A E : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : IsUnit A)
  (hE : NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E) < 1) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (A + E)⁻¹ ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E))
name: NLAlib.specNorm_inv_add_le
doc:
Inverse-norm bound under perturbation: for invertible `A` and `‖A⁻¹E‖₂ < 1`,
`‖(A + E)⁻¹‖₂ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖₂ / (1 - ‖A⁻¹E‖₂)`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 2.3.4; Stewart–Sun 1990,
§III.2.
atlas: inverse-perturbation (partial)

name: NLAlib.specNorm_inv_add_le_of_mul_lt_one
doc:
Inverse-norm bound under `‖A⁻¹‖₂ ‖E‖₂ < 1`:
`‖(A + E)⁻¹‖₂ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖₂ / (1 - ‖A⁻¹‖₂ ‖E‖₂)`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 2.3.4.
atlas: inverse-perturbation (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_inv_add_sub_inv_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A E : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : IsUnit A)
  (hE : NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E) < 1) :
  NLAlib.specNorm ((A + E)⁻¹ - A⁻¹) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ ^ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm (A⁻¹ * E))
name: NLAlib.specNorm_inv_add_sub_inv_le
doc:
Perturbation of the inverse in the spectral norm: for invertible `A` and `‖A⁻¹E‖₂ < 1`,
`‖(A + E)⁻¹ - A⁻¹‖₂ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖₂² ‖E‖₂ / (1 - ‖A⁻¹E‖₂)`. Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 2.3.4;
Stewart–Sun 1990, Thm III.2.5.
atlas: inverse-perturbation (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_inv_add_sub_inv_le_of_mul_lt_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A E : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : IsUnit A) (hE : NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ * NLAlib.specNorm E < 1) :
  NLAlib.specNorm ((A + E)⁻¹ - A⁻¹) ≤
    NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ ^ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm E / (1 - NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ * NLAlib.specNorm E)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_inv_add_sub_inv_le_of_mul_lt_one
doc:
Perturbation of the inverse under `‖A⁻¹‖₂ ‖E‖₂ < 1` (the form usually quoted):
`A + E` is invertible and `‖(A + E)⁻¹ - A⁻¹‖₂ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖₂² ‖E‖₂ / (1 - ‖A⁻¹‖₂ ‖E‖₂)`.
Golub–Van Loan 2013, Thm 2.3.4 with `‖A⁻¹E‖ ≤ ‖A⁻¹‖‖E‖`; Higham 2002, Problem 6.14.
atlas: inverse-perturbation (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_inv_eq_inv_singularValues_last.{u_1} {r : Type u_1} [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] (C : Matrix r r ℝ)
  (hC : IsUnit C) (hr : 0 < Fintype.card r) : NLAlib.specNorm C⁻¹ = 1 / NLAlib.singularValues C (Fintype.card r - 1)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_inv_eq_inv_singularValues_last
doc:
The operator norm of a nonempty square inverse is the reciprocal of its
least actual singular value. Horn–Johnson 2013, Section 5.6; empty domains
are excluded exactly because they have no last singular value.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_inv_le_inv_inversePowerSoftMin.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] (n : ℕ)
  (hn : 0 < n) (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (hA : A.PosDef) : NLAlib.specNorm A⁻¹ ≤ (NLAlib.inversePowerSoftMin n A)⁻¹

doc:
**Spectral norm from a net (operator form).** If `N` is an `ε`-net of the unit sphere
(`∀ y` unit, `∃ x ∈ N`, `‖x - y‖₂ ≤ ε`) with `0 ≤ ε < 1`, and `‖Ax‖₂ ≤ M` for every `x ∈ N`

(deterministic half).

**Deterministic range-finder bound, spectral form** (HMT 2011, Thm 9.1, spectral case): if
`A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`, `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀΩ` has full row rank, `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀΩ`, `QᵀQ = I` and
`range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖² ≤ ‖Σ₂‖² + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖²`.

Deviations from the printed statement: the hypotheses are those of the Frobenius form
`frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset`, verbatim (block decomposition with `U₂ᵀU₂ = I`,
`V₁ᵀV₁ = I`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`; no diagonality, no conditions on `U₁`, no completeness;
`Σ₁` need not be invertible); `P_Y` is `QQᵀ` for any orthonormal `Q` with
`range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`; index types other than the rank `Fin k` are arbitrary `Fintype`s.
Atlas `hmt-9-1-spectral` (assumed → proved).
atlas: hmt-9-1-spectral

the interval half-width. Bhatia §VII.2; empty spectra cause no exception.

doc:
Left compression by an orthonormal frame is a spectral contraction.
Stewart–Sun §I.5.

norm. Atlas: `ose-def` (the previously missing converse). The distortion is

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.spectralMeasure.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)

doc:
The spectral measure `μ_v = ∑ᵢ (uᵢ ⬝ v)² δ_{λᵢ}` of a symmetric matrix `A` and a vector `v`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 7 (the measure `α(λ)` of the Riemann–Stieltjes
integral); Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], §2. Atlas: `spectral-measure`.
Deviation: indexed by Mathlib's eigenvalue enumeration, so repeated eigenvalues give repeated
atoms (the measure is the same).
atlas: spectral-measure

signature:
NLAlib.spectralMeasure_compl_range_eigenvalues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

name: NLAlib.spectralMeasure_compl_range_eigenvalues
doc:
The spectral measure is carried by the eigenvalues: the complement of
`Set.range hA.eigenvalues` is null. Source: [`gm10`], Ch. 7. Atlas: `spectral-measure`.

signature:
NLAlib.spectralMeasure_univ.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (v : n → ℝ) : (NLAlib.spectralMeasure hA v) Set.univ = ENNReal.ofReal (v ⬝ᵥ v)
name: NLAlib.spectralMeasure_univ
doc:
The spectral measure has total mass `‖v‖² = v ⬝ v`. Source: [`gm10`], Ch. 7.
Atlas: `spectral-measure`.

atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance (partial)

atlas: gershgorin-diagonal-dominance

signature:

doc:
If the sorted spectrum of a positive semidefinite `R` is dominated by that of a
positive semidefinite `A`, then `R` has enough trace-square energy to pay the relative
trace drift above the spectral tail of `A`. The field-independent core of
`sq_max_trace_sub_spectralTraceTail_le_mul_trace_sq` (ℝ); over any `𝕜` the domination is

Chen–Epperly–Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Thm 3.1: eigenvalue monotonicity and Cauchy–Schwarz.

name: NLAlib.sq_max_sum_sub_tail_le_card_mul_sum_sq
doc:

above its complementary tail divided by the head size (scalar Cauchy–Schwarz step of
Chen–Epperly–Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 3.1).

signature:
NLAlib.sq_max_trace_sub_spectralTraceTail_le_mul_trace_sq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A R : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) (hR : R.PosSemidef) (hRA : R ≤ A) (r : ℕ) :

doc:

tail after the `r` largest eigenvalues (real case of
`sq_max_re_trace_sub_spectralTraceTail_le_of_eigenvalues₀_le`). Chen–Epperly–Tropp–Webber
2023 (RPCholesky), proof of Thm 3.1: eigenvalue monotonicity and Cauchy–Schwarz.

signature:
NLAlib.sq_overlapTangentNorm_eq_div.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {Q Q' : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q')
  (hC : IsUnit (Q.transpose * Q')) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm Q Q' ^ 2 = NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' ^ 2 / (1 - NLAlib.directedSubspaceGap Q Q' ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.sq_overlapTangentNorm_eq_div
doc:
**`tan² = sin²/(1 − sin²)`.** For `Q`, `Q'` with orthonormal columns indexed by the same `k`
and `QᵀQ'` invertible: `tan² θ_max = sin² θ_max/(1 − sin² θ_max)`. Source: Golub–Van Loan
(2013) [`gvl13`], §2.5.3 and §8.2.4; Stewart–Sun (1990) [`ss90`], §I.5. Proof sketch: with
`C = QᵀQ'` and `S = (I − QQᵀ)Q'`, `CᵀC + SᵀS = I`; for `v = Cw`,
`‖S C⁻¹ v‖²/‖v‖² = t/(1 − t)` with `t = ‖Sw‖²/‖w‖²`, which is increasing in `t`; the maximum
of `t` is `sin² θ_max`. (When `QᵀQ'` is singular, `tan` has the junk value `0`.)
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.sq_overlapTangentNorm_replicateCol_eq_overlapTangentSq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {u : n → ℝ} (hu : ‖WithLp.toLp 2 u‖ = 1) (x : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.overlapTangentNorm (Matrix.replicateCol Unit u) (Matrix.replicateCol Unit x) ^ 2 = NLAlib.overlapTangentSq u x
name: NLAlib.sq_overlapTangentNorm_replicateCol_eq_overlapTangentSq
doc:
SCAFFOLD: principal-angles-def
**`overlapTangentSq` is the one-column `tan² θ_max`.** For a unit vector `u` and any `x`,
`tan θ_max(range u, range x)² = tan² ∠(u, x)`, both sides `0` when `u ⬝ x = 0`. Source:
Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.2 and §6.6.1. Proof sketch: `uᵀx` is the `1 × 1` matrix `(u ⬝ x)`, its
inverse is `(u ⬝ x)⁻¹`; `(I − uuᵀ)x (u ⬝ x)⁻¹` is a single column whose spectral norm is its
Euclidean norm (`specNorm` of an `n × 1` matrix: `‖M‖² = ‖MᵀM‖` = the `1 × 1` entry,
`Matrix.l2_opNorm_conjTranspose_mul_self`), and `‖(I − uuᵀ)x‖² = ‖x‖² − (u ⬝ x)²`.
atlas: principal-angles-def (partial)

(`Matrix.conjTranspose_eq_transpose_of_trivial`). Atlas `svd`.

      NLAlib.singularValues A (Fintype.card (Fin n) - 1) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix (Fin N) (Fin n)

doc:
**Gordon's lower bound.** For an `N × n` standard Gaussian matrix with `n ≥ 1`,
`√N - √n ≤ 𝔼 σ_min(G)` where `σ_min(G) = inf_{‖x‖₂ = 1} ‖G x‖₂` (`NLAlib.sigmaMin`). For `N ≤ n`
the left side is `≤ 0` and the bound is trivial. Source: Vershynin 2012, Thm 5.32 (lower half);
Gordon 1985; Davidson–Szarek 2001, Thm II.13. Atlas: `gordon`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gordon_lower`.
atlas: gordon

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.sub_eq_mulVec_dotProduct_sub_of_polarization.{u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype k] [Fintype n]

signature:
NLAlib.sub_jacksonPeriodicApprox_eq_integral {g : ℝ → ℝ} {L : NNReal} (hg : LipschitzWith L g)
  (hper : Function.Periodic g (2 * Real.pi)) (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
  g x - NLAlib.jacksonPeriodicApprox n g x =
    -(2 * Real.pi)⁻¹ * ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..2 * Real.pi, NLAlib.sawtoothError n t * deriv (fun s => g (x - s)) t

doc:

The periodic endpoint contribution is `-2π g(x)` and the polynomial kernel is the

signature:
NLAlib.sub_le_of_continuous_of_subseq_difference_quotient_le (F : ℝ → ℝ) (hF : ContinuousOn F (Set.Icc 0 1)) (L : ℝ)
  (hv :
    ∀ t ∈ Set.Ico 0 1,
      ∃ c ≤ L,
        ∃ φ,
          StrictMono φ ∧
            Filter.Tendsto (fun ν => (F (t + (1 - t) / (↑(φ ν) + 2)) - F t) / ((1 - t) / (↑(φ ν) + 2))) Filter.atTop
              (nhds c)) :
  F 1 - F 0 ≤ L
name: NLAlib.sub_le_of_continuous_of_subseq_difference_quotient_le
doc:
A continuous real function on `[0,1]` grows by at most `L` if at every point
before the right endpoint its positive-step quotients admit a subsequence
converging to a value at most `L`. Scalar minimum argument, Lidskii operator route.

signature:
NLAlib.sub_mem_krylovSpace_iff_exists_sub_mulVec_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : IsUnit A) {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} :
  x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q ↔
    ∃ p, p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧ Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1 ∧ c - A.mulVec x = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.sub_mem_krylovSpace_iff_exists_sub_mulVec_eq
doc:
**Residual-polynomial characterisation of `x₀ + K_q`.** For invertible `A`,
`x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀) ↔ ∃ p, deg p ≤ q ∧ p(0) = 1 ∧ c − A x = p(A) r₀`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35.
Deviation: the converse direction needs `A` injective (`IsUnit A`); the forward direction
(`exists_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace`) holds for every `A`.
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

name: NLAlib.sub_mem_krylovSpace_krylovGrade
doc:
**Finite termination.** If `A` is invertible and `A x⋆ = c`, then for every `x₀` the error
`x⋆ − x₀` lies in `K_ν(A, r₀)`, `r₀ = c − A x₀`, `ν = ν(A, r₀)`; so every Krylov method that
minimises over `x₀ + K_q` is exact at `q = ν`. The proof: `A` maps the invariant space `K_ν`
injectively, hence onto, itself, and `r₀ = A (x⋆ − x₀)` lies in it.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.3 and §6.1 (`A⁻¹ b ∈ K_ν(A, b)`).
Atlas: `krylov-grade` (partial: finite termination).
atlas: krylov-grade (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.sub_mulVec_polyIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (s : Polynomial ℝ) :
  c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.polyIterate A c x₀ s) = ((Polynomial.aeval A) (1 - Polynomial.X * s)).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.sub_mulVec_polyIterate
doc:
The residual of a polynomial method is `(1 − X s)(A) r₀`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
§12.1.
atlas: polynomial-method-def

signature: NLAlib.sub_mul_log_one_add_le {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) : ε - (1 + ε) * Real.log (1 + ε) ≤ -(ε ^ 2 / 3)
name: NLAlib.sub_mul_log_one_add_le
doc:
`ε - (1 + ε) log(1 + ε) ≤ -ε²/3` for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`. Proof: `log(1+ε) ≥ 2ε/(ε+2)` (first
term of Mathlib's `hasSum_log_one_add`), and `(1+ε)·2ε/(ε+2) ≥ ε + ε²/3` iff `ε ≤ 1`.
Tropp 2012, Rem 5.3 (upper tail); atlas `matrix-chernoff-sampling` (helper).

signature:

name: NLAlib.sub_mul_pinvR_mul_transpose_eq
doc:
The competitor identity of the range-finder proof: `A − AΩΩ₁†V₁ᵀ = U₂(Σ₂V₂ᵀ − Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†V₁ᵀ)`
when `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`, `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀΩ` has full row rank and `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀΩ`. HMT 2011, proof of
Thm 9.1 (§9.2). Atlas `hmt-9-1-spectral`, `hmt-9-1-frobenius`.

signature:
NLAlib.sub_nystrom_eq_of_eq_transpose_mul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {t : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype t] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq r] {F : Matrix r n ℝ} {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A = F.transpose * F)
  (Ω : Matrix n t ℝ) :
  A - NLAlib.nystrom A Ω =
    ((1 - F * Ω * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (F * Ω)) * F).transpose *
      ((1 - F * Ω * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (F * Ω)) * F)
name: NLAlib.sub_nystrom_eq_of_eq_transpose_mul
doc:
**Nyström structural identity** (exact form): if `A = FᵀF` then
`A − A⟨Ω⟩ = ((I − P)F)ᵀ((I − P)F)` with `P = (FΩ)(FΩ)⁺`. Gittens–Mahoney 2016, Lemma 1;
Tropp–Webber 2023, §2. Atlas `nystrom-structural`. Deviation: stated for any Gram factor `F`
(the source uses `F = A^{1/2}`); it is an identity, not only the bound of the source.
atlas: nystrom-structural

signature:

    NLAlib.partialCholeskyResidual A s

doc:
**Partial Cholesky residual identity**: `A − F Fᵀ` is the projResidual, for PSD `A` and any pivot
sequence. Proof: induction on `k`; the new column `f` satisfies
`f fᵀ = R(:,t) R(t,:) / R(t,t)` (`√x² = x` for the PSD diagonal, symmetry of `R`).
CETW 2023, §2; Golub–Van Loan 2013, §4.2.9.
atlas: partial-cholesky-nystrom (partial)

Complementary orthogonal-projector gap decomposition `P − Q = (I − Q)P − Q(I − P)`.

signature:
NLAlib.sub_rayleighQuotient_pow_div_specNorm_le_log_overlap_div.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) (hL : 0 < NLAlib.specNorm A) (i₀ : n)

overlap divided by `2q+1`. finite concave-power Jensen.

signature:
NLAlib.sub_smul_one_eq_transpose_mul_diagonal_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

      (↑hA.eigenvectorUnitary).transpose
name: NLAlib.sub_smul_one_eq_transpose_mul_diagonal_mul
doc:
A real symmetric matrix shifted by `x` is congruent to a diagonal matrix:
`A − xI = (Uᵀ)ᵀ diag(λ − x) Uᵀ` with `U = hA.eigenvectorUnitary`. Helper for
`sylvester-inertia`.

name: NLAlib.sub_sq_dotProduct_le_of_forall_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct_eq
doc:
**Angle contraction under a spectral multiplier, numerator form.** Let `u` be a unit
eigenvector for the eigenvalue at sorted position `i₀`, let `|g| ≤ M` at every other sorted
position, and let `uᵢ ⬝ w = g(λᵢ)(uᵢ ⬝ v)` for every `i`. Then the component of `w`
orthogonal to `u` is at most `M` times that of `v`: `‖w‖² − (u ⬝ w)² ≤ M² (‖v‖² − (u ⬝ v)²)`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], proof of Thm 27.1; Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1.
Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`, `power-iteration`, `inverse-iteration`.

The paired squared-norm separation estimate from two coupled

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceIterate.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq n] [Fintype s] (A : Matrix n n K) (Ω : Matrix n s K) (k : ℕ) : Submodule K (n → K)
name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate
doc:
The `k`-th subspace iterate `S_k = range (A^k Ω)` of subspace (orthogonal, simultaneous)
iteration started from the block `Ω`, over any field `K`. Orthonormalisation is bookkeeping: any
`Q` with `range Q = S_k` is a basis the algorithm may carry (`range_mul_eq_subspaceIterate_succ`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.1; Golub–Van Loan (2013) [`gvl13`], §8.2.4.
atlas: subspace-iteration-def

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceIterate_eq_range_graph.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]
  [Fintype k] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq k] [DecidableEq r] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {U₁ : Matrix n k ℝ}
  {U₂ : Matrix n r ℝ} {L₁ Linv : Matrix k k ℝ} {L₂ : Matrix r r ℝ} (hA₁ : A * U₁ = U₁ * L₁) (hA₂ : A * U₂ = U₂ * L₂)
  {Ω : Matrix n k ℝ} {Ω₁ R : Matrix k k ℝ} {Ω₂ : Matrix r k ℝ} (hΩ : Ω = U₁ * Ω₁ + U₂ * Ω₂) (hR : Ω₁ * R = 1)
  (hL : L₁ * Linv = 1) (t : ℕ) : NLAlib.subspaceIterate A Ω t = (U₁ + U₂ * (L₂ ^ t * Ω₂ * R * Linv ^ t)).mulVecLin.range

doc:
Right normalization gives the exact graph of every subspace iterate.
Source: manuscript `sa:graph`; Saad (2011), §5.1. Right inverses are explicit data.

name: NLAlib.subspaceIterate_le_blockKrylovSpace

Subspace iteration is block Krylov with the fixed polynomial `x^k`:
`S_k = range (A^k Ω) ⊆ K_{k+1}(A, Ω)`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §5.1 and §6.3;
Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], §4.
atlas: subspace-iteration-def

signature:
NLAlib.subspaceTangent.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n] [Fintype k] [Fintype r]

doc:
The largest tangent from a subspace to the leading orthonormal block is the
largest tail-coordinate norm among vectors whose head-coordinate norm is at most one.
Source: Saad (2011), §5.1; manuscript `sa:subspace`. For transverse subspaces this is
the usual supremum of the tail/head norm ratio. This real-valued supremum
is an algebraic helper: if its defining set is unbounded above, Mathlib returns
zero. Use it under a transverse-graph or explicit boundedness hypothesis.

  (S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ))
  (h :
    ¬BddAbove
        ((fun x => ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (U₂.transpose.mulVec x)‖) ''
          {x | x ∈ S ∧ ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (U₁.transpose.mulVec x)‖ ≤ 1})) :
  NLAlib.subspaceTangent U₁ U₂ S = 0
name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent_eq_zero_of_not_bddAbove
doc:
An unbounded defining set makes the real supremum helper zero. A finite
geometric interpretation therefore requires an explicit boundedness domain.

NLAlib.subspaceTangent_nonneg_of_bddAbove.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} {r : Type u_3} [Fintype n]

  (hA₂ : A * U₂ = U₂ * L₂) {Ω : Matrix n k ℝ} {Ω₁ R : Matrix k k ℝ} {Ω₂ : Matrix r k ℝ} (hΩ : Ω = U₁ * Ω₁ + U₂ * Ω₂)

  NLAlib.subspaceTangent U₁ U₂ (NLAlib.subspaceIterate A Ω t) ≤
    (NLAlib.specNorm L₂ * NLAlib.specNorm Linv) ^ t * NLAlib.subspaceTangent U₁ U₂ Ω.mulVecLin.range
name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent_subspaceIterate_le
doc:
Largest principal-angle tangents of subspace iteration contract by the magnitude
gap factor. Source: manuscript `sa:subspace-theorem`; Saad (2011), §5.1.
For diagonal eigenvalue blocks, `specNorm L₂ * specNorm Linv` is
`max |λ_tail| / min |λ_head|`. This form allows indefinite matrices and empty tails.
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence (partial)

name: NLAlib.subspaceTangent_subspaceIterate_le_of_diagonal
doc:
The explicit magnitude-gap bound uses any positive lower bound on the absolute
leading eigenvalues. Taking their minimum gives the manuscript's `γ = ‖Λ₂‖ / α`;
for a sorted PSD spectrum this is the usual tail/head eigenvalue ratio.
Source: manuscript `sa:subspace-theorem`; Saad (2011), §5.1.
atlas: subspace-iteration-convergence (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.sudakov_fernique_inequality.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} {Ω' : Type u_3} [Fintype ι]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace Ω'] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Q : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'} (X : ι → Ω → ℝ)
  (Y : ι → Ω' → ℝ) (hX : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => X t ω) P)
  (hY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => Y t ω) Q) (hX0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ∂P = 0)
  (hY0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ∂Q = 0)
  (hinc : ∀ (s t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), (X s ω - X t ω) ^ 2 ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), (Y s ω - Y t ω) ^ 2 ∂Q) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), ⨆ t, X t ω ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), ⨆ t, Y t ω ∂Q
name: NLAlib.sudakov_fernique_inequality
doc:
**Sudakov–Fernique inequality.** Let `X` (on `(Ω, P)`) and `Y` (on `(Ω', Q)`) be centred
Gaussian processes indexed by a finite set with dominated increments
`𝔼 (Xₛ - Xₜ)² ≤ 𝔼 (Yₛ - Yₜ)²`. Then `𝔼 maxₜ Xₜ ≤ 𝔼 maxₜ Yₜ`.
Source: Sudakov 1971, Fernique 1975; Vershynin 2018, Thm 7.2.11. Atlas: `sudakov-fernique`.
atlas: sudakov-fernique

signature:
NLAlib.sum_abs_eigenvalues₀_add_sub_le_nuclearNorm.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A E : Matrix n n ℝ}

Bhatia (1997), Theorem III.4.1.

signature:

name: NLAlib.sum_abs_singularValues_add_sub_le_sum_prefix
doc:
Every selected sum of absolute rectangular singular-value increments is
bounded by the same-sized top singular-value sum of the perturbation.
Bhatia 1997, Theorem IV.3.4; includes arbitrary subsets, multiplicities, empty
shapes and zero singular values.

signature:

doc:
Every finite selection of zero-padded natural singular indices obeys Mirsky's
absolute-difference sum bound, on arbitrary finite real matrix row and column indices.
Bhatia 1997, Theorem IV.3.4; all padding indices, empty selections, empty shapes and
rank-deficient zeros are covered.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.sum_eigenvalues_eq_sum_sorted.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {𝕜 : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]

doc:
Summing a function of the sorted eigenvalues gives the same spectral sum as the
matrix-labelled eigenvalues, for real symmetric and complex Hermitian matrices alike
(`[RCLike 𝕜]`); Mathlib's sorted-eigenvalue convention.

signature:
NLAlib.sum_eigenvalues₀_add_le_sum_add_eigenvaluePrefix.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (J : Finset (Fin (Fintype.card n))) :
  ∑ j ∈ J, ⋯.eigenvalues₀ j ≤ ∑ j ∈ J, hA.eigenvalues₀ j + NLAlib.eigenvaluePrefix hB J.card
name: NLAlib.sum_eigenvalues₀_add_le_sum_add_eigenvaluePrefix
doc:
Indexed Lidskii–Wielandt: every selected decreasing eigenvalue sum of `A+B`
is at most the same selected sum of `A` plus the top `|J|` sum of `B`.
Bhatia 1997, Theorem III.4.1. Real symmetric matrices on arbitrary finite indices;
empty dimensions, repeated eigenvalues, and all negative eigenvalues are included.
atlas: lidskii

signature:
NLAlib.sum_erase_symmetric_inverse_power_limit_eq.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ρ w : ι → ℝ)
  (i₀ : ι) :
  ∑ i,
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
        (w i + w j) * ρ i * ρ j * (((if j = i₀ then 1 else 0) - if i = i₀ then 1 else 0) / (ρ j - ρ i)) =
    2 *
      ∑ i,
        ∑ j,
          if i = j then 0 else w j * ρ i * ρ j * (((if j = i₀ then 1 else 0) - if i = i₀ then 1 else 0) / (ρ j - ρ i))
name: NLAlib.sum_erase_symmetric_inverse_power_limit_eq
doc:
Symmetry combines the ordered off-diagonal gap terms into twice one
directed sum. Source: scalar divided differences of the inverse-power
Hessian; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (limit constant helper).
